in writing. ‒ multiannual recovery plan for bluefin tuna in the eastern atlantic and mediterranean i supported the proposed report because i believe it appropriately transposes into the european legal order the recommendations of the international commission for the conservation of atlantic tunas (iccat) and the regional fisheries management organisation (rfmo), which are the original competent authorities for the management of tuna and tuna-like species in the atlantic ocean and adjacent seas. scientific data show that the bluefin tuna stock in the seas under the jurisdiction of iccat and the rfmo is increasing and that restoring the stock and the tacs is the only logical step. the proposed regulation thus ensures the uniform and effective implementation of all measures of the recovery plan adopted by iccat in 2012. the proposal also includes technical measures such as those related to the transfer and rearing activities of live bluefin tuna in cages, including those related to the use of stereoscopic cameras to assess bluefin tuna quantities and releases, catch reporting requirements and the implementation of the iccat regional observer programme.
in writing. ‒ the eu is a party to the international commission for the conservation of atlantic tunas (iccat) and the regional fisheries management organisations (rfmo). these two organisations are responsible for the management of tuna and tuna-like species in the atlantic ocean and adjacent seas. iccat is thus competent to adopt recommendations for the conservation of fisheries, which are binding and need to be transposed into eu law. bluefin tuna is the most important species to be regulated by iccat. in 2006, that organisation adopted a multiannual bluefin tuna recovery plan until 2022. the total allowable catch stood at 33000 tonnes before the adoption of the recovery plan and reached a low of 12900 tonnes in 2012. this indicates the extremely positive results of the above-mentioned multiannual plan. the report examines a proposal for a regulation to ensure a uniform and effective implementation of all measures of the recovery plan throughout the eu. the commission proposal contains mainly technical measures, such as measures relating to the transfer and rearing activities of live bluefin tuna in cages, catch reporting requirements and the implementation of the iccat regional observer programme. i believe that the uniform implementation of iccat recommendations throughout the eu is of the utmost importance. for these reasons, i voted in favour of the report in the plenary.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council establishing a multiannual recovery plan for bluefin tuna in the eastern atlantic and mediterranean and repealing the regulation. the multiannual plan, which would end in 2022, sets out the quotas for the allowable catches of bluefin tuna. so far, fishermen have adjusted their catches to the allowable catch, which has also led to a positive shift in the recovery of stocks. i support a further increase in the allowable catch. this is particularly important for those fishermen who fish bluefin tuna in the traditional way with traditional traps, which have a limited impact on marine ecosystems due to low energy consumption and low incidental catch. the quota had to be exhausted, and the fishermen were at risk. i also welcome the rapporteur's clear position that regulations and restrictions must be respected in the same way everywhere.
in writing. ‒ i supported the report on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council establishing a multiannual recovery plan for bluefin tuna in the eastern atlantic and mediterranean and repealing regulation (ec) no 302/2009, as i believe that it leads to a more uniform and effective implementation of all the measures set out in this area throughout the eu.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a multiannual recovery plan for bluefin tuna in the eastern atlantic and mediterranean and repealing regulation (ec) no 302/2009, as this will allow the european union to fulfil its contractual obligations under the international agreements with the international commission for the conservation of atlantic tunas (iccat) and the regional fisheries management organisation (rfmo). the proposal for a regulation will ensure a uniform and effective implementation of all the measures of the bluefin tuna recovery plan throughout the eu, maintain the survival of this species and allow controlled fishing.
in writing. ‒ the single internal market is one of the eu's greatest achievements and the conditions for ensuring free competition in the internal market are therefore crucial to its existence and functioning. one of the conditions is the prohibition of agreements and arrangements between undertakings which impede trade between member states. this can lead to abuse of a dominant position and the work of the european commission in this area is therefore very important, since it monitors acquisitions and mergers of companies in the eu that lead or can lead to a significant concentration in the market and thus to a dominant position in the market. the fundamental objective of union competition rules is to protect competition from distortion, since competition is not an end in itself but a condition for the achievement of a free and dynamic internal market and thus for ensuring the conditions for effective economic growth. the resolution proposed, which i naturally supported, is therefore not merely parliament's response to the commission's findings, but serves as a guide for dealing with current issues and drawing up legislation in this area. the proposal implies that the commission will have to inform member states more frequently about the control of unlawful state aid and strengthen the surveillance of the digital economy. nor can issues of fair competition be separated from issues of tax avoidance, i.e. unfair tax competition, which also leads to distortions of competition.

in writing. ‒ the proposed report, which i supported, completes the european legal framework on the rights of defence of suspects or accused persons in criminal proceedings throughout the european union. the three new directives thus establish an important instrument for ensuring fair trials throughout the eu. the amendments relate mainly to the presence of the accused at trials, the scope of the directive and the protection of suspects and accused persons from hasty guilty pleas. on the latter, i agree with the rapporteur that the presumption of innocence is violated mainly by the media and the press. in the spectacular arrests we often witness in slovenia, for example, or during the trial, all the cameras are pointed at the accused, their lives are turned upside down, they are guilty before they are proven guilty. the last one can last for many years. even if the verdict is acquitted, the individual is marked for life as guilty - thanks to the media. i therefore strongly support the proposed solutions to reinforce the presumption of innocence provided for in those directives.
in writing. ‒ in november 2013, the commission presented a package of measures, the 'final package - procedural rights', containing proposals for three directives. these directives will allow the completion of a european legal framework in the field of the rights of defence of suspects or accused persons in criminal proceedings throughout the eu. these are key instruments for ensuring a fair trial throughout the eu and for fully respecting the rights of the defence. i consider it extremely important that the presumption of innocence and the right to be present at trial in criminal proceedings are strengthened in this package of measures. the presumption of innocence is a fundamental right and an essential principle to avoid arbitrariness and abuse in criminal proceedings. the principle of presumption of innocence includes the right to remain silent, transfers the burden of proof to the prosecution and includes the principle of 'in dubio pro reo' (in doubt in favour of the accused). the right to be present at one's own trial is a fundamental element of the presumption of innocence, which is currently protected in european law only under the european arrest warrant and the framework decision on the recognition of the execution of criminal judgments in absentia. i agree that it is essential to strengthen the protection provided for by those instruments and to ensure that all suspects and accused persons in criminal proceedings benefit from it. because of what you described, i supported the report.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a directive of the european parliament and of the council on the strengthening of certain aspects of the presumption of innocence and of the right to be present at trial in criminal proceedings. i support the establishment of a minimum level of protection of the principle of presumption of innocence in all member states and the strengthening of the right to be present at trial. it is also necessary to ensure a high overall level of protection for accused persons in criminal matters in a member state without prejudice to higher standards of protection that may be applicable in individual member states. i welcome the fact that the report considers the reverse burden of proof in criminal proceedings unacceptable and that it insists on the principle that the burden of proof of guilt is borne by the prosecution.
in writing. ‒ i supported the report on the proposal for a directive of the european parliament and of the council on the strengthening of certain aspects of the presumption of innocence and of the right to be present at trial in criminal proceedings, as i believe that the three directives presented entitled 'final package - procedural rights' will contribute to the completion of the european legal framework on the rights of defence of suspects or accused persons in criminal proceedings. respect for the rights of the defence and the fairness of the trial will thus be improved throughout the european union.
in writing. ‒ the proposal for a directive lays down minimum rules on certain aspects of the presumption of innocence, the principle of legality and the observance of the principle of the primacy of the interests of the parties in criminal proceedings. it points out, inter alia, that the presumption of innocence is infringed when a judicial or other public authority, by a court decision or a public statement, labels a suspect or accused person as if his or her guilt had already been established, without having previously been established in accordance with the law. i support the proposal for a directive as it aims to provide fundamental procedural guarantees in criminal proceedings and to enable the right to a fair trial without prejudice to higher standards of protection that may be applicable in each member state.
in writing. ‒ personal protective equipment is a common item of clothing for many people in europe, whether for work or leisure. the very name 'protective equipment' recalls that the production of such equipment, which protects the individual against certain dangerous influences, must be properly regulated and controlled. such equipment must therefore be properly tested and the type of production and the materials from which these products are made are also important. i therefore support the efforts of the commission and the council to improve the conditions for the use of personal protective equipment contained in the proposed report.
in writing. ‒ the report concerns a proposal for a regulation on personal protective equipment. the basic premise of the proposal for a regulation was that only very effective instruments could ensure the protection of workers in a completely unhindered way. of course, it must be borne in mind that accidents at work are not only caused by the failure to use adequate protective equipment, but also by its incorrect use. i believe that protective equipment will only be effective if it is designed and placed on the market in an appropriate form, taking into account the different users. the report on the proposal for a regulation, among other things, highlights some purely technical aspects of the regulation with a desire to include all risk categories and all possible cases. this is to avoid legal uncertainty or misinterpretation to the greatest extent possible. i agree that we need not only investment policies but also the necessary safeguards to improve the working environment. these include everything from minimum requirements for worker safety to measures to protect workers and to improve the quality of the working environment accordingly. in view of the above, i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a regulation on personal protective equipment in the plenary.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on personal protective equipment. i support the creation of a single market for personal protective equipment, which must have the consumer in mind first and foremost, to whom we must ensure a high level of protection. for each new personal protective equipment that appears on the internal market of the european union, we need to establish the essential requirements and conditions under which it can compete on the european market. i welcome the proposed amendment that appropriate measures should be taken to ensure the safety of people during demonstrations of equipment and field trials. the proposal also provides that field tests should not be designed to test the performance of ppe but to assess other aspects not related to protection such as comfort, ergonomics and design.

in writing. ‒ i myself support the new proposal for a regulation which sets out new rules on the free movement of gas appliances in the eu internal market. this is a hugely important area, with as many as 470 million gas appliances in the eu, from simple portable cookers to boilers for large buildings, and the number is growing. the proposed regulation replaces the current directive, which has proved to be highly problematic in the harmonisation procedures with the national laws of the member states. by choosing a regulation that is directly applicable in the member states, the latter will be able to save the costs associated with transposing a directive. furthermore, the form of the regulation avoids the risk of divergences in transmission which could lead to different levels of security and distortions of the internal market. it should also be noted that the proposal is in line with eu legislation governing energy supply and energy efficiency. the new equipment will also have to bear the ce marking, which will facilitate the certification of products placed on the market.

in writing. ‒ the report refers to the proposal for a regulation on wire-cable equipment, which aims to harmonise the conditions for placing on the market and ensuring the free movement of subsystems and safety components of wire-cable equipment in the eu. all safety components and subsystems will, under that regulation, have to be designed and manufactured in accordance with the essential requirements set out in the regulation. the regulation also fully harmonises the essential requirements to be met by cableway installations. this means that member states may not impose stricter or additional requirements in their national legislation. i believe that a regulation is the appropriate solution, as it will avoid unnecessary transmission costs and will also provide clear and precise rules that will be uniformly applied throughout the eu. the regulation defines more clearly, in particular, cableway installations intended for transport and leisure purposes, and also excludes those installations used for leisure purposes in fairgrounds or amusement parks. it also aligns the conformity assessment procedures available for subsystems with those already in place for safety components. i agree with the proposal for a regulation, but i am also aware of the importance of the greatest possible harmonisation within the eu in this area, which is why i supported the report in the plenary.

in writing. ‒ negotiations on a stabilisation and association agreement between the eu and kosovo were concluded in july 2014. the national assembly of the republic of kosovo subsequently ratified the agreement on 2 november 2014. the agreement establishes a contractual relationship that provides for improved political dialogue, closer trade integration and new forms of cooperation between the eu and kosovo. it covers several sectors, including respect for and promotion of democratic principles and human rights. it also contains provisions promoting european standards in areas such as competition, public procurement, intellectual property and consumer protection. the agreement sets out rights and obligations and provides a strong impetus for the implementation and institutionalisation of reforms. the recommendation calls for the approval of the conclusion of the agreement, which is the central document in the process of stabilisation and association of kosovo. the stabilisation and association agreement will create opportunities for investment, growth, business development and strengthening, while also ensuring good governance through the application of european standards and the approximation of eu legislation. the agreement should also, inter alia, open up possibilities for strengthening contacts with experts in relevant sectors (environment, fight against crime and illicit trafficking, culture, etc.) and further strengthen relations and cooperation with neighbouring countries, thus contributing to the stability of the region. as this is an important step in the process of accession and the rapprochement of the republic of kosovo with the eu, i supported the recommendation in the plenary.

in writing. ‒ i supported the report on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on a union code on the rules governing the movement of persons across borders (schengen borders code), as i considered that the necessity and proportionality of reintroducing internal border controls should be considered in the light of the threat to public policy or internal security that has created the need for such controls. however, alternative measures that could be taken at national, union or both levels and the impact of such controls on the free movement of persons within the area without internal border control should also be considered. the reintroduction of internal border control should continue to apply only exceptionally in an area where persons may move freely. the first priority must be the safety of all citizens of the union.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report, which is mainly a technical codification of existing rules that have been amended several times. specifically, the purpose of this proposal is to undertake a codification of regulation (ec) no 562/2006 of the european parliament and of the council of 15 march 2006 establishing a community code on the rules governing the movement of persons across borders (schengen borders code). the new regulation will replace the various acts incorporated in it; this proposal fully preserves the content of the acts being codified and does nothing more than bring them together with the only exception of formal amendments that are required by the codification exercise itself. the reason for such codifications is that the commission attaches great importance to simplifying and clarifying the law of the union so as to make it clearer and more accessible to citizens. this aim cannot be achieved so long as numerous provisions that have been amended several times, often quite substantially, remain scattered, so that they must be sought partly in the original instrument and partly in later amending ones.
in writing. ‒ schengen is one of the european union's greatest achievements. today it is being tested, and with it the eu. it is essential to stop or contain the wave of migration, and this requires coordinated action by all member states in controlling the external borders. i therefore supported the proposal for a regulation which brings together a set of common measures and rules on the movement of persons across borders.
in writing. ‒ as with the protocol on persistent organic pollutants, the proposal to amend the protocol on heavy metals to the 1979 convention on long-range transboundary air pollution sets out, in particular, stricter emission limit values for dust from certain major stationary sources, as well as flexible transitional arrangements that will benefit those parties that accede to the amended protocol before the end of 2019, including countries in eastern and south-eastern europe. these protocols are important because air pollution knows no national boundaries, and therefore proper cooperation and unification of protocols is the only possible option, and for this reason i support these solutions.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution, which contains a recommendation from the european parliament to accept a series of amendments to the 1998 protocol to the 1979 convention on long-range transboundary air pollution on heavy metals. the objective of this protocol is to control emissions of heavy metals caused by anthropogenic activities that are subject to long-range transboundary atmospheric transport and are likely to have significant adverse effects on human health or the environment. the parties to the protocol agreed, among other things, to reduce their total annual emissions into the atmosphere of each of the heavy metals listed in its annex, to facilitate the exchange of technologies and techniques designed to reduce emissions of heavy metals and to encourage research, development, monitoring and cooperation, primarily focusing on heavy metals.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution, which contains a recommendation from the european parliament to accept a series of amendments to the 1998 protocol to the 1979 convention on long-range transboundary air pollution on persistent organic pollutants. the 1998 aarhus protocol on persistent organic pollutants aims to control, reduce or eliminate discharges, emissions and losses of pops. it requires parties to eliminate the production and use of a series of relevant substances, as well as to restrict the use of other substances such as dichlorodiphenyltrichloroethane (ddt), hexachlorocyclohexanes (hch) and polychlorinated biphenyls (pcbs). the protocol entered into force on 23 october 2003 and was transposed into eu law through several legal instruments. the amended protocol includes seven new substances, updates implementation requirements for several substances, updates restrictions for pcdd/pcdf emissions from several sources, and adds pcbs to the list of substances affected by the total annual emission restrictions and reporting obligations. the amendments to the protocol are already largely covered by eu legislation, and will be further transposed via a new directive setting updated national emission ceilings for certain atmospheric pollutants.
in writing. ‒ i support the amendments to the protocol, which will be further transposed by a new directive, which will set updated national emission ceilings for certain air pollutants and allow the introduction of annual national emission inventories, which will cover, inter alia, emissions of certain persistent organic pollutants. the measures will make a significant contribution to the protection of the environment and human health.

in writing. ‒ the report refers to the proposal for a decision establishing a european platform to strengthen cooperation in the prevention and deterrence of undeclared work. this is one of the most worrying and complex problems, as it concerns activities which, although legal in nature, are not registered with public authorities or, in the case of virtual self-employment, are incorrectly registered. working underground has very serious negative consequences for many segments. it affects workers' rights and their social rights, as well as the municipal, state and ultimately eu budgets. i welcome the proposed establishment of the platform, but it must be followed by concrete action. i believe that there are many other frameworks in which we can properly combat undeclared work. as such, i can mention an appropriate tax policy which should be stimulating and not push workers and employers into a relationship of black-collar work. i also believe that there is a need to support activities in the field of active employment policy, social policy and, above all, the updating of data, which will allow access to accurate data on the number of people working underground. i agree that the proposed platform could provide a basis for the development of a work programme that would fully meet the urgent need for targeted action, which is why i supported the report.

respected. more and more europeans are afraid of the migrant crisis. up to 2000 asylum seekers enter the union every day. what happens when spring comes? what approach do we want to take to the transit route through the politically unstable and economically very paralysed countries of the western balkans, via slovenia and beyond? of the five hotspots in greece, only one is currently operational. there's a resettlement and repatriation plan in place, an action plan with turkey. it is high time that these policies were put into effect. even if the geneva conference brings a solution to syria, we cannot expect peace tomorrow. the latest shocking report from europol finds that it is unclear where the 10,000 unaccompanied children have gone. half of them have been lost in italy, at least 10,000 in sweden. the speculation of where and how many of them might end up is terrifying. these are children and we need to act now. the union is not in control of the migration crisis. it's not the numbers. we are talking about two and a half million refugees in a union of 500 million people. it's not that it's unmanageable, but someone in the institutions has to take political leadership. when slovenia, my country, joined schengen, it, like a number of other countries, saw the new face of europe - a europe that opened up in the most visible way. and now this europe is closing itself in the most shameful, base way with national egos.
i think we should not underestimate the awareness of people who come to europe as refugees, migrants, asylum seekers. they know they're no longer welcome here. that here, also today in the european parliament, we are having more discussions about how to deter, contain, contain and reject them. simply put, there are too many to be accepted broadly, in line with the ethics and values that we refer to in such speeches. what will happen to us in europe was not thought of when we approved and participated in the wars that drove these people from their homes and prepared them to humiliate themselves with their families on our roads and borders today, to die on overturned boats. this was not considered when we preferred violent intervention to political and diplomatic solutions. we've heard a lot of emotional speeches here today, a lot of anger at our helplessness. i'm not going to be a part of this. i would just like to stress that at this moment, all of us - high representative mogherini and all european governments - through our own fault and miscalculation, we must firmly and sincerely support the peace talks in syria, which are the only way to restore confidence that refugees will have a place to return to when the time comes. and then we'll have to find political solutions for other countries from which people are fleeing to us in europe.
i would like to make four brief comments. firstly, the issue of violence against refugees is relevant. they're vulnerable children, first and foremost. we heard that as many as 10,000 children have disappeared from european soil. europol anticipates that they are abducted or bought by organised crime and used for sexual slavery or exploitative work. on the other hand, there is at least one other vulnerable group that we should be concerned about, and that is the european girls, and we know why. the member states are therefore faced with the important question of how to fill the security vacuum in which they have been floating for two decades. secondly, turkey. the eu must engage with turkey in a credible and cautious way to stem the tide of migration, but we cannot rely 100% on them or on others. we must rely on ourselves first, and then on collective action. thirdly, the schengen area. this is one of the european union's greatest achievements. today, the european union is being put to the test. thank god the european union has offered at least part of the solution with the border and coast guard, which gives us new powers to protect our external borders. and fourthly, regardless of the future status of greece, the european union must be saved at any cost. so we need to stop or contain the migration wave as a matter of urgency. in this respect, it should adopt alternative measures. if greece cannot do this, then let us give aid to albania, macedonia and bulgaria. and finally, we must start returning economic migrants immediately.

in writing. most trade agreements with the eu include a bilateral safeguard clause allowing for the suspension of preferences in the event that their application would lead to an unexpected and substantial increase in imports that could cause economic damage to the domestic industry of the importing party (i.e. moldova). simply put, this means that further tariff liberalisation can be suspended or the mip can be reintroduced. the said instrument also contains an agreement between the eu and the european atomic energy community and their member states, of the one part, and the republic of moldova, of the other part. in addition, the agreement contains a mechanism to prevent circumvention, which allows the reintroduction of the most-favoured-nation tariff rate in the event that imports of certain agricultural products from moldova exceed a certain threshold without adequate justification of their exact origin. the effective implementation of these instruments requires the adoption of a regulation by the ep and the council in eu internal law. the commission proposal, currently under consideration, also allows for the practical implementation of the relevant provisions of the eu-moldova association agreement approved by the ep in november 2015. i consider that the adoption of the proposed regulation is necessary to implement the obligations of moldova under the agreement and to protect eu producers adequately, where appropriate. i voted for the report because of what it said.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this objection because i am against the plan to temporarily raise the nox emissions limits for diesel cars. the recent volkswagen scandal has shown how car manufacturers produce vehicles which pollute way more than they declare, and i believe that this practice has to be put to an end as quickly as possible. this is why i think that temporarily raising the emissions limits does not follow a clear, reasonable logic. nevertheless, this objection was rejected as the eu commission has promised a review clause and tabled a long-term legislative proposal to revamp the eu car approval regime. i sincerely hope that the commission will effectively tackle this issue in a reasonable timeframe.
in writing. ‒ i did not support the european parliament's resolution because i believe that the draft regulation is not yet complete and would not contribute to a substantial reduction in air pollution. we need concrete measures, such as better implementation of current legislation and effective enforcement, rather than another political gesture.
in writing. ‒ the rapporteur, ms reding, has produced a good and balanced report on a sensitive subject such as the tisa agreement. with it, parliament sent a clear message to the negotiators about what to look out for, and we demanded full transparency in the negotiations. telecommunications, transport, infrastructure services, they represent a good part of the global economy, and the world is also rapidly digitizing. twenty-three wto members are involved in the negotiations. the eu, as one of them, has much to gain from the agreement, provided that the negotiators pay sufficient attention to the most sensitive areas. i myself have focused on workers' rights and the prevention of social dumping, the maintenance of a high level of consumer rights, the protection of personal data and, of course, most importantly, public services. the latter must remain 'open' to all and not be left entirely to market forces, since it can quickly happen that the weakest sections of the population are the ones who are short-changed. i hear a lot of general opposition to the agreement these days, mainly from an ideological point of view, even though the negotiations are still actively underway. but the world is moving forward, and we can either ride this train of progress and cooperate in it with our proposals and practices, or we can be left behind. the eu as an economic superpower cannot afford to do this, and i have therefore supported the recommendations to the negotiators. but i will be watching developments closely before i decide what my final support for the agreement will be.
in writing. ‒ tisa will create fairer trade rules in the service sector and the ep is committed to giving clear understanding to negotiators on how to apply the mandate. it is clear that the eu has the biggest service sector and that tisa is necessary to upgrade previous agreements multilaterally and propel job creation in this sector, also adapting to the new opportunities technology has brought to the sector. however, i want to clearly state that tisa should contain no lazy compromises regarding the protection of our european public services, education and culture. otherwise, i will vote against, once the agreement is on the table for approval and ratification.
in writing. ‒ the ep plays a key role in the eu's trade policy. he has the right to express his views throughout the procedure, which allows him to influence its course. the ep also calls for the eu to be able to take action to prevent the spread of the virus, and for the eu to be able to take action to prevent the spread of the virus. major concerns within the framework of this agreement arise in relation to certain areas of the subject matter of the negotiations on trade in services. i agree that public and cultural services, fundamental rights to data protection and fair working conditions, and the right to regulation cannot be negotiated and must necessarily be excluded from the scope of the agreement. i believe that the negotiations on the trade in services agreement (tisa) should result in effective international rules, not inferior domestic rules. the report does not directly refer to the (non) support for the tisa agreement, but is intended primarily to make proposals to the commission on the way forward in the negotiations on the drafting of the agreement itself. the amendment to ensure that the proposals put forward by the ep are taken into account and the amendment to give the council the right to review the implementation of its mandate were not adopted in plenary, and i therefore voted against the report.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report with the european parliament's recommendations to the commission for the negotiation of the trade in services agreement (tisa). i support the clear guidance given by the european parliament to the negotiators on tisa, which i believe is balanced. it brings many benefits to large and small and medium-sized enterprises, and also provides for the rights of workers. there is a lot of misinformation on the part of the opponents of the agreement about public services such as public health, safety and the environment, and i support that, as is also very clearly stated in the european parliament's recommendations to the commission.
in writing. ‒ i supported the report with the european parliament's recommendations to the commission for the negotiation of a trade in services agreement (tisa) as i believe that such cooperation is important, necessary and beneficial. the tisa, which is negotiated between 52 countries, representing a third of the world trade organisation, will facilitate the exchange of services and create more jobs. the agreement will bring benefits to consumers, more opportunities for smes and a boost to the european economy as a whole. but by joining other large countries in the future, we could somehow achieve not only benefits and lower prices for consumers, but also higher standards. this will not be an agreement that creates new barriers, but an agreement that breaks them down.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution because i fully share the recommendations to the commission contained in the text as regards the negotiations for the trade in services agreement (tisa). one of the main issues is ensuring the protection of eu firms from unfair competition abroad, in relation to which we are recommending eu negotiators ensure: 1) reciprocity in market opening, as services in the eu are already more open to foreign competition than those of its partners; 2) curbs on third countries’ restrictive practices against eu firms, such as forced data localisation or foreign equity caps; and 3) less red tape for smes, which lack the financial and human resources needed to navigate international trade rules. likewise, i agree with the ‘red lines’ that are being set out in our recommendations, specifically the areas that should be excluded from negotiations, such as: 1) eu public services, like education, health, social services, social security systems and audiovisual services; and 2) eu citizens’ data protection, which must be up to current and future standards. also, the eu should agree to accept only highly-skilled foreign workers, on contracts and for a strictly limited period of time.
in writing. ‒ i support the recommendations on the negotiations for a trade in services agreement (tisa) as they reflect the eu's values, principles and interests. it is in the eu's vital interest to protect consumer rights, data protection and the right to privacy, and to improve social and environmental standards, including at the level of international agreements.
in writing. ‒ i did not support the motion for a resolution because i think the european commission is sufficiently active in ensuring gender equality and women's rights. the form, not the content, was the focus of the resolution's drafters. the motion for a resolution which we in the european people's party drew up and which was rejected concerned the implementation of the commission working document on the empowerment of women and also recognised the commission's progress in this area. i think we need to take an operational approach to this. a strategy as a dead letter on paper can mean much less than a concrete working document with clearly defined operational objectives.
in writing. ‒ i voted against the resolution on a new strategy for gender equality and women's rights after 2015. women in the eu earn on average less than men, are at greater risk of poverty in old age, and have a much higher burden of household chores. in the labour market, we still often see women being conditioned before entering into employment to not have children for a few years. to change this, we need political commitment at the highest level. but instead of the commission's communication on a strategy for gender equality and women's rights after 2015, we have before us a working document from the commission's services. in doing so, the president of the commission sent a message that the issue of gender equality was a minor issue, given his statement that the commission would be more ambitious on major issues and more modest and reserved on minor issues. the post-2015 strategy for gender equality and women's rights will have a lot to do.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution because with this text we urge the commission to table a communication on a new strategy for gender equality and women’s rights 2016-2020 as soon as possible, which should address gender equality issues in line with the international agenda and deliver on its political commitments. while i, along other meps, believe that the commission has a clear responsibility to launch policies on equality between women and men and to address important issues such as violence against women, the gender pay gap, and the balance between personal and working life, so far it has only presented a staff working document, which has no interinstitutional value, on a ‘strategic engagement for gender equality 2016-2019’. what we need is a proper commission communication that includes concrete benchmarks and a dedicated budget, in the framework of a new strategy which should provide new impetus and deliver concrete action to strengthen women’s rights and promote gender equality.
in writing. ‒ gender equality as a strategic objective is essential to achieve the overall objectives of the europe 2020 strategy for growth, employment and social inclusion. i did not support the new post-2015 strategies for women's rights and gender equality because i believe that the guidelines set are too low ambition and will not lead to concrete actions to strengthen women's rights and promote gender equality. this question deserves more careful attention and consideration than the political act in question.

in writing. ‒ since 2011, when rebel groups, with the help of nato, overthrew muammar gaddafi, libya has been facing a serious political, institutional and security crisis. since the summer of 2014, the country has been the scene of increasingly violent clashes between two disbanded and fragmented opposing groups (the forces of operation pride and the "libyan dawn" coalition). both opposing camps defend their aims and invoke the legitimacy of the opposing governments and parliaments, based in tripoli and tobruk. in the country, militias affiliated with the so-called islamic state have taken advantage of the civil war and the power vacuum to increase their presence. they have been carrying out terrorist attacks with increasing frequency and brutally abusing the local population. since libya's descent into civil war, the human rights situation there, as well as the humanitarian situation, has deteriorated sharply. the motion for a resolution makes some appropriate proposals for action, such as the establishment of inclusive internal institutions that could uphold the rule of law, the development of a comprehensive disarmament, demobilization and reintegration programme, the conferral of jurisdiction on the international criminal court for violations and abuses in libya, etc. however, since paragraph 12 on the deployment of eunavfor was not removed from the motion for a resolution in plenary, i abstained.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the joint motion for a resolution on the situation in libya. i support the political agreement in libya signed by the opposing parties which will complete the political divide in libya. the agreement calls for the formation of a government of national unity and a provisional government of the nine-member presidential committee, composed of the prime minister, five deputies and three ministers. i particularly welcome the fact that the agreement was adopted under the auspices of the united nations. i join the call in the resolution for the house of representatives in tobruk and the presidency to support this agreement, which is a key step in the implementation of the libyan political agreement and which is consistent with the efforts to achieve peace and stability in the country and to defend all libyan citizens.
in writing. ‒ i supported the motion for a resolution on the situation in libya because i believe that the european union's support for libya in resolving the crisis is not only necessary but also very urgent. the situation affecting the violation of human rights and fundamental freedoms and the violence and disturbance of peace in the country consequently threaten the security of the entire region, including the eu. the growing humanitarian crisis calls more than ever for the eu to call for an end to violence, new divisions and solutions through political dialogue.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution because urgent action is needed in libya, where economic disintegration and violence are worsening its fragility and enabling extremist organisations to flourish. spillovers from libya’s conflicts are also destabilising the sahel region, and could constitute a threat to the eu´s security. the libyan conflict is in fact having repercussions in egypt and particularly tunisia, but also in algeria and its oilfields, while contributing to exacerbate extremism. with this resolution we urge the eu and international community to be ready to support libyans’ efforts to implement the libyan political agreement. we urgently call for continued humanitarian, financial and political assistance from the eu and the international community to address the humanitarian situation in libya, the plight of internally displaced persons and refugees and that of civilians facing disruptions in access to basic services.
in writing. ‒ the current situation in libya requires the immediate intervention of peacekeepers and the establishment of political dialogue between the parties. military conflict worsens human rights and cripples the economy, and allows the rise of extremist groups, terrorist attacks and smuggling. i support the european parliament's resolution on the situation in libya, as i believe it will help to stabilise the situation in libya. the eu stands ready to provide support to help build the state, ensure security and peace, and uphold human rights and the rule of law.
in writing. ‒ i supported the proposed resolution on the eu's island regions, as i believe that more attention should be paid to islands, which make up a significant part of the european territory. the arguments for the preservation of island regions are similar to those i often raise in relation to the problem of hilly and mountainous areas. both islands and mountain areas face transport and information remoteness, migration, which affects the cultural and natural heritage and the ageing population. in terms of economic activity, island regions are most dependent on tourism, which is the largest employer in these regions, but the seasonality of this industry makes it difficult to provide jobs throughout the year. in the resolution we therefore called for the establishment of an eu strategic framework for island regions and for a change of approach for islands that are under the greatest pressure from migration waves.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the motion for a resolution on the question for an oral answer on the special status of the islands. i agree with the call on the commission to draw up a clear definition of the types of permanent geographical, natural and demographic handicaps that may affect island regions and to launch a thorough study/analysis of the additional costs of insularity in terms of passenger and freight transport, energy supply and market access, particularly for small and medium-sized enterprises.
in writing. ‒ motion for a resolution on the question for oral answer (b8-0106/2016) pursuant to rule 128 (5) of the rules of procedure on the special status of islands, as i believe that islands need a special policy because of their natural specificity, remoteness and sensitivity. only by giving countries a special treatment and an adapted financial framework will the union be able to exploit the potential offered by these islands, despite some limitations. in particular, by developing tourism, promoting cultural heritage, developing craft and economic activities and the potential of alternative energy, they will achieve development, growth and become more competitive within the union.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution because i believe it is important to take concrete steps to address the permanent handicaps that eu islands face and make full use of their potential. we must take into consideration the unique difficulties that southern insular regions face due to the increased migration flows. this is why we called upon the commission, among other things, to maintain special tax regimes for islands. we also ask the commission to: 1)set up a homogenous group made up of all island territories, which recognises the permanent handicaps of insular regions, 2) take account of other statistical indicators, besides gdp, which will reflect the economic and social vulnerability of these regions, 3) launch an in-depth analysis of the extra costs incurred as a result of being an island and 4) establish an “eu strategic framework for islands” which would link up instruments that could have a major territorial impact, and submit a communication on an “agenda for eu islands” and subsequently a white paper to monitor the development of islands.
in writing. ‒ the european islands are facing many challenges due to the adverse conditions arising from climate conditions, the economic crisis, migration flows and distance from the european continental shores. i therefore supported the resolution in which the european parliament calls on the commission to draw up a development programme for the eu islands. it is necessary to halt the displacement of people from island regions, to promote sustainable development on islands and to create new jobs.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the resolution on the question for oral answer on the role of local and regional authorities in the european structural and investment funds. cohesion policy is an important instrument of the european union and will play an important role in the 2014-2020 programming year as the main investment instrument covering all eu regions and as an opportunity to establish a process of sustainable growth. i particularly support the resolution as it emphasises the key role of local and regional authorities in shaping and implementing eu strategies, while recognising the role of a wide range of stakeholders, from member states to local communities. to design and implement eu strategies effectively, we need good cooperation between all stakeholders at eu level.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution, which lays out a set of recommendations concerning the role of regional and local authorities in the european structural and investment fund (esif). its main message, which i completely support, is that local and regional authorities play a key role in shaping and implementing eu strategies. the text outlines the positive synergies and complementarity between the esi funds and other eu programmes, in which local and regional authorities can play a useful role in attaining the objectives of cohesion policy. in order to fulfil these objectives, enhancing the administrative capacity and tackling the structural weaknesses of local and regional authorities are pivotal to both the programming and the implementation phases of the operational programmes and to achieving a higher absorption rate of esi funds. the resolution therefore rightly calls on the commission to ensure that support is provided for capacity building for local and regional authorities and their administrations and institutions, so that they are in a position to play a meaningful role in cohesion policy.

in writing. ‒ i supported the european parliament's proposed recommendation that austria be allowed to sign and ratify the hague convention and that malta be allowed to accede to it. the hague convention provides for a system under which documents may be served in another contracting state, but it applies only to cross-border service of documents in or from third countries. the rules governing service between eu member states are laid down in the horizontal regulation on the service of judicial documents. austria and malta were the only two eu countries that had not applied the provisions of the hague convention, but have recently expressed their wish to accede to it. but before they can be implemented, the eu must give these two countries the power to act on its behalf. i agree with the rapporteur that the field of crossborder service of documents is very useful and that it is in the interest of both the eu and the acceding countries that there is a single exchange regime.
in writing. ‒ i supported the authorisation of austria to sign and ratify the hague convention of 15 november 1965 and malta's accession to it, which will enable countries to ratify the convention. the hague convention of 1965 established a system that allowed for the service of documents between states. cross-border service of documents in or from third countries in the ec is regulated by regulation no 1393/2007, which transfers the hague convention to the ec. the convention has so far been applied by 26 of the 28 member states and it is in the interest of the ec that there is a uniform regime for the service of documents in crossborder relations with third countries.
in writing. ‒ the hague convention of 15 november 1965 established a system whereby judicial and extrajudicial documents in civil or commercial matters may also be served in another state party to the convention. the convention applies to service of documents in or from third countries and is already applied by 26 eu member states. the hague convention has proved to be very useful in the field of cross-border service of documents. austria and malta, which have not yet signed the convention, have expressed their desire to join. however, the convention does not allow for the accession of international organisations, which means that the eu must specifically authorise member states wishing to accede to the convention to act on its behalf. the existence of a uniform regime for the service of documents in cross-border relations with third countries is in the interest of both the eu and austria and malta, which wish to accede to the convention. i therefore voted in favour of the recommendation in the plenary and thereby supported it.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the recommendation on the draft council decision authorising the republic of austria, in the interest of the european union, to sign and ratify the hague convention of 15 november 1965 on the service abroad of judicial and extrajudicial documents in civil or commercial matters and the republic of malta to accede to it. austria and malta are the only countries of the 28 not yet applying the hague convention. since both have expressed a desire to join, malta has already deposited the instrument, austria will deposit it, and since this is in the interest of the union and its member states, i have supported the recommendation.
in writing. ‒ i supported the recommendation on a draft council decision authorising the republic of austria, in the interest of the european union, to sign and ratify the hague convention of 15 november 1965 on the service abroad of judicial and extrajudicial documents in civil or commercial matters and the republic of malta to accede to it, since the hague convention already allows documents to be served on other contracting states. the convention is already applied by 26 of the 28 member states, and austria and malta have expressed their wish to accede to it.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the authorisation for austria to sign and ratify, and malta to accede to, the hague convention of 15 november 1965 on the service abroad of judicial and extrajudicial documents in civil or commercial matters, in the interest of the european union. the hague convention of 15 november 1965 establishes a system whereby documents in or from third countries can be served in another signatory state. twenty-six member states already apply the convention, leaving austria and malta as the two remaining member states who are still not part of the system. these two member states have now filed a request to join and, given that the hague convention of 15 november 1965 has proven useful in the field of the cross-border service of documents, it is in the interest both of the union and of the two member states in question to have a single regime for the service of documents in cross-border relations with third countries.

in writing. ‒ the estimated size of the grey economy in the eu member states is a staggering €1 000 billion a year in uncollected taxes and contributions. although it is an estimate, there is no doubt that it is a major anomaly, which is detrimental both in terms of free competition and in terms of providing access to public services financed by taxes. the fight against tax fraud is one of the eu's priorities and is already showing results. the examples of corporate tax evasion exposures that we've seen since the luxleaks revelations are certainly steps in the right direction. if we do not punish the big offenders and build our apparent power on the backs of thieves, we will lose credibility with the citizens. to achieve these objectives, we need to strengthen the exchange of financial account data and all other relevant information concerning the cross-border activities of companies. i am therefore pleased that the eu and san marino have reached an agreement on the automatic exchange of financial account information, which is an important step in the fight against tax fraud. the agreement provides for the automatic exchange of information on residents' financial accounts, which will help to identify those residents who conceal income or capital. i therefore supported the proposed decision to conclude the agreement.
in writing. ‒ this agreement is an important step towards better international cooperation to prevent tax fraud, which was also possible due to the non-exchange of financial data between countries. the adoption of the san marino agreement will be a significant step forward in enabling the automatic exchange of information on residents' financial accounts between the ec and san marino. this will help us to prevent the concealment of money for tax evasion purposes. the commission has also taken into account the fact that the commission has not yet adopted a recommendation on the use of the term 'competent authority' in the context of the 2014 oecd guidelines on competition policy. the agreement will thus allow member states' tax administrations to exercise greater control over the accounts of their nationals in san marino, leading to a reduction in tax evasion.
in writing. ‒ on 8 december 2015, the eu and san marino signed an agreement on the automatic exchange of financial account information to improve international tax cooperation and compliance. the agreement provides for the automatic exchange of information on residents' financial accounts between the eu and san marino as from 2017. the purpose of the agreement is to resolve situations where a taxpayer attempts to conceal capital in the form of income or assets for which he has not paid tax. the agreement will enable tax administrations in the member states and in san marino to identify correctly and unambiguously the relevant taxpayers, to administer and enforce national tax legislation in cross-border situations, to assess the likelihood of tax evasion and to ensure that no unnecessary further investigations are carried out. the agreement represents an important step in the ongoing efforts to combat tax fraud and tax evasion and builds on the 2004 agreement, which resulted in san marino implementing measures equivalent to those of the eu savings tax directive. i therefore supported the report in plenary.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a council decision on the conclusion, on behalf of the european union, of the amending protocol to the agreement between the european community and the republic of san marino providing for measures equivalent to those laid down in council directive 2003/48/ec on taxation of savings income in the form of interest payments. much has been done in the past to combat tax fraud, and much more remains to be done. in particular, in the field of data exchange between countries. the eu-san marino agreement builds on the 2004 agreement and will mean enhanced measures against tax fraud and tax evasion.

in writing. ‒ the act of accession of the republic of croatia of 2011 introduces a simplified system for croatia's accession to the conventions (and protocols) concluded by the member states on the basis of article 34 of the treaty on european union (teu). to this end, the council shall adopt a decision fixing the date of entry into force of the conventions for croatia and amending them accordingly as necessary upon accession of the new member state. such a decision shall be taken by the council on the basis of a recommendation from the commission and after consulting the ep. the report in question concerns croatia's accession to the convention of 26 july 1995 on the protection of the european communities' financial interests, its protocols of 27 september 1996 and 29 november 1996 and the second protocol of 19 june 1997, adopted under title vi of the teu and designed to establish a common basis for the criminal law protection of the ec's financial interests. in this case, it is not necessary to make the adjustments which would be necessary as a result of croatia's accession to that convention and its protocols. i believe that the accession of the republic of croatia to those conventions is necessary and that is why i voted in favour of the report in the plenary.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the accession of croatia to the convention on the protection of the financial interests of the union. article 3(4) and 3(5) of the 2011 accession treaty of the republic of croatia provides that croatia accedes to conventions and protocols concluded by the member states on the basis of article 34 of the treaty on european union by virtue of the act of accession. among the conventions and protocols concerned is the convention on the protection of the european communities’ financial interests of 26 july 1995, its protocol of 27 september 1996, its protocol of 29 november 1996 and the second protocol of 19 june 1997, all adopted under title vi of the eu treaty. the convention aims at establishing a common base for the criminal-law protection of the european community’s financial interests. i voted in favour of determining the date on which the convention shall enter into force for croatia in line with a simplified system for the accession of croatia to the conventions and protocols concluded by the member states on the basis of article 34 of the treaty on european union.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of adopting a recommendation recommending that the commission should set the council the date for the entry into force for croatia of the above conventions concluded by the member states on the basis of article 34 teu, thereby allowing the further establishment of a common basis for the criminal law protection of the eu's financial interests.
in writing. ‒ with an ageing population in europe and still high unemployment rates in some eu member states or their regions, the design and direction of appropriate employment flows is of paramount importance in reversing these trends. the free choice of employment in the eu is one of the most important components of the european single market, one of the four fundamental freedoms of the european union, and thus an essential element of eu citizenship. increasing the mobility of workers within the eu, thereby increasing the employment opportunities of workers and helping employers to fill vacancies, is one of the key steps towards achieving these goals. i therefore had no hesitation in supporting the above regulation or the report by mr becker, which aims to develop the eures network into an effective instrument for all jobseekers and employers interested in finding workers within the eu. this will be achieved by providing access to a transparent and comprehensive eu-wide register of job vacancies and jobseeker profiles, including apprenticeships and traineeships. i particularly like the fact that we are bringing young jobseekers into the network, so that they can take full advantage of the benefits of the eu. i believe that the eures network will have a very positive impact on increasing intra-eu mobility and thus on a more connected europe.
in writing. ‒ i supported the rapporteur's proposal as it establishes a more in-depth and improved european network of employment services. this will increase workers' access to job vacancies in other member states, thereby increasing labour mobility and thus making a key contribution to further integration of labour markets between the member states of the european union. the european network of employment services will make available even more job vacancies in regions where workers from other regions and member states with higher unemployment rates can be employed. at the same time, the proposal provides assistance to workers and employers, increases the role of eures, clearly defines cross-border cooperation, establishes minimum common criteria to be met by all member states and ensures equal access to services.
in writing. ‒ freedom of movement is one of the four fundamental freedoms of the eu. it also includes the freedom to choose one's job, which is an essential element of eu citizenship. the rate of labour mobility within the eu is relatively low, i.e. 0.29%, in relation to the size of the labour market and the number of the active population. i agree that there is a need to increase labour mobility in the eu, thereby increasing the employment opportunities of workers and helping employers to fill vacancies better and faster. the proposed regulation aims to develop the eures network into an effective tool for all jobseekers and employers interested in labour mobility within the eu. this pan-european network would provide access to a transparent and as comprehensive as possible register of vacancies and jobseeker profiles. the network's performance will also be regularly assessed, allowing for any improvements to be made as quickly as possible and ensuring the network's continued and successful operation. i believe that the eures network represents a unique opportunity for jobseekers in the eu, as it is free, provides information on living and working conditions, connects jobseekers with employers looking for specific skills and points them to sectors and occupations where there is a shortage of skilled workers. i voted to accept the report because of what it described.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on a european network of employment services, workers' access to mobility services and the further integration of labour markets. the high unemployment rate in the european union is still crippling certain regions, and at the same time there are still some 2 million unfilled vacancies, so we need to step up efforts in this area. the new rules will help to bring jobs closer together and give the social partners, young people and crossborder regions a greater role.
in writing. ‒ i supported the report on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on a european network of employment services, access to mobility services for workers and further integration of labour markets, as the renewed eures will make a significant contribution to reducing unemployment in the eu member states and to bringing jobs closer together. in addition to public employment services, private agencies and non-governmental organisations will also be able to participate in eures. the vacancies will thus be publicly published and accessible to all. i think we'll reduce unemployment among vulnerable groups. i am convinced that eures will also have a positive impact on increasing the employment mobility of citizens within the eu.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on a european network of employment services, workers’ access to mobility services and the further integration of labour markets. the european employment service network (eures) is an eu-wide database of job-seekers and vacancies, established in 1993 as a cooperation network between the commission and the public employment services of the eu member states (plus switzerland, norway, iceland and liechtenstein), and partners: private job agencies, trade unions, employers’ associations. however, several important limitations such as an incomplete database of job vacancies and cvs, limited automated matching potential and insufficient cross-border labour information have prevented it from functioning efficiently and further integrating the member states labour markets. i voted in favour of improving the european employment services (eures) network with the aim of helping fight unemployment by better matching the labour market supply and demand and paying more attention to cross-border regions and young people.

in writing. ‒ tunisia's economy is in a bad shape, especially after the terrorist attacks last year. the eu/commission is therefore offering a hand to tunisia and its economy by proposing to introduce a duty-free quota of a total of 70,000 tonnes per year for the export of olive oil from tunisia to the eu, without increasing the total volume of imports. the measure is intended to help the tunisian economy, where the olive sector provides jobs for one million people, representing as much as one fifth of all jobs in agriculture. olive oil is also the main agricultural product exported by tunisia. i myself agree with the solidarity that the eu is showing towards tunisia, but we must be very careful not to harm our own farmers, especially those in southern europe. in the countries most affected by the economic crisis, the olive oil sector is of paramount importance for the maintenance of jobs, exports and economic stability. prices have been falling for a long time, and farmers have been plagued by rising production costs for a long time. the impact of this measure on the european agricultural sector cannot be ignored and i have therefore also supported the amendments to the proposal which make this possible in part.
in writing. ‒ following the terrorist attack in susu on 26 june 2015, the eu decided to offer more assistance to tunisia in its political and economic transition. it will do so through concrete and targeted measures that can be effective also in the short term. the commission has therefore proposed to introduce a temporary unilateral tariff-free tariff quota of 35000 tonnes per year for the export of olive oil from tunisia to the eu in the form of autonomous trade measures. the quota will be available for a period of two years (january 2016 to december 2017). i agree that the eu must contribute to the economic recovery of tunisia in this difficult period, but i believe that eu solidarity should not be at the expense of farmers in southern europe, who are in this case olive oil producers. the eu is the world leader in the olive oil sector. in the large areas of eu countries most affected by the financial and economic crisis, this sector provides thousands of jobs and contributes to a positive eu trade balance. the report contains certain proposals for amendments, the main purpose of which is to encourage the commission to assess the impact of such measures on the european agricultural sector while assessing the feasibility of the proposal. i think the proposals are appropriate, which is why i supported the report.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on the introduction of emergency autonomous trade measures for the republic of tunisia. i support the amendment proposals which include the commission's mid-term review of the impact of this regulation on the olive oil market in the union since its entry into force. however, if the review concludes that the provisions of the regulation have a negative impact on the union market, the commission shall be empowered to adopt an implementing act to propose corrective measures to address the situation on the union market. we are hereby expressing our support for the economic development of tunisia.
in writing. ‒ i supported the report on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council introducing emergency autonomous trade measures for the republic of tunisia, as it is important that the eu expresses its support through concrete actions, especially in view of tunisia's economic development, following the difficult circumstances caused by the terrorist attacks in the summer. the european commission therefore proposes to introduce a temporary unilateral duty-free tariff quota of 35000 tonnes per year, or 70.000 tonnes in total, for the export of olive oil from tunisia to the union. the measure will benefit a large part of the tunisian economy. the tunisian olive sector indirectly provides jobs for more than one million people and accounts for one fifth of all jobs in the country's agriculture. olive oil is among the main agricultural products exported by tunisia.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the introduction of emergency autonomous trade measures for tunisia. after the terrorist attacks in tunis and sousse in 2015, tourist arrivals in tunisia have decreased considerably, negatively affecting the already struggling economy. in order to help the tunisian economy, an emergency short-term trade measure is announced in the form of a two-year temporary zero-duty tariff quota of 35 000 tonnes per year for eu olive oil imports from tunisia for 2016 and 2017. the measure will not increase the overall volume of imports from tunisia as the eu will only discount duties on the current tunisian olive oil exports to the eu. in order to further protect the eu olive producers, additional precautions will be undertaken such as a mid-term assessment and updates of the measures if they turn out harmful for eu olive oil producers, as well as a ‘tracking clause’ obligation ensuring that the olive oil truly comes from tunisia. i voted in favour of this emergency measure in order to help the damaged tunisian economy.
in writing. ‒ in the wake of the terrorist attack in susu on 26 june 2015, the eu decided to offer more assistance to tunisia in its political and economic transition, through concrete and targeted measures that can be effective in the short term. i support these measures and have therefore voted in favour of the proposal for a regulation which will allow the introduction of a temporary unilateral tariff quota of 35 000 tonnes per year, i.e. a total of 70 000 tonnes, for the export of olive oil from tunisia to the union, in the form of autonomous trade measures and without increasing the total volume of imports.

in writing. ‒ according to the commission's latest autumn forecast, the economic recovery in the euro area is expected to strengthen, with real gdp expected to grow by 1.4% in 2015, 1.7% in 2016 and 1.8% in 2017. the report found that the ecb had resorted to unconventional monetary policy instruments in response to the complex environment characterised by the sovereign debt crisis, falling inflation, credit crunch and slow economic growth. the report also reflects concerns about the possible adverse effects and long-term effects of these instruments. abandoning these measures will be complex and will require careful planning. this will avoid undue market distortions, in particular as regards the proper, careful and timely organisation of the abandonment and the choice of the right moment. the high and varying levels of public and private debt in some member states, in addition to the still-present structural weaknesses in the banking sector, constitute an obstacle to the proper transmission of monetary policy. i believe that the unconventional monetary policy pursued by the ecb cannot, by itself, change this situation. a strong political commitment to implementing sustainable and socially balanced structural reforms is essential to boost economic growth. in view of the above, i voted against the adoption of the ecb annual report 2014 at the plenary session.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the european central bank annual report for 2014. the ecb’s report is composed of two chapters together with the annual accounts, a consolidated balance sheet of the eurosystem as at 31 december 2014, and a series of annexes detailing the institutional framework and human resource developments in 2014. the report, among other things, describes the economic situation in the euro area in 2014. according to the report, three important global developments have had a significant influence: 1) uneven growth developments; 2) falling prices of oil and other commodities; and 3) a weaker euro exchange rate. as the report highlights that fiscal consolidation slowed down and progress in structural reforms lost momentum, the ecb stresses that credible and decisive growth-enhancing reforms are more important than ever. the report also describes a series of actions that the ecb undertook to strengthen the stability of and confidence in the european financial sector, such as assessments of the financial system’s resilience and shock-absorbing capacity, and its links to the real economy. furthermore, the ecb’s analysis of financial stability risks in the euro area during 2014 shows there are both legacy issues from the global financial crisis and a broad set of emerging risks, linked primarily to low interest rates.
