in writing. ‒ i support the proposed regulation on the reform of port systems in europe. i am pleased that the rapporteur and the team have taken the proposal to the stage where negotiations with the council can begin. with today's decision, we have set out the rules for member states and port authorities who would like to limit the number of service providers. we also stipulated that ports will have to keep separate accounts for activities financed by public funds, while being careful in setting the fee for services performed by internal operators. these rules will have to be established in a transparent and non-discriminatory manner. in addition, the states are also required to appoint supervisory authorities in order to ensure adequate control of the level of charges for the provision of port services.
in writing. ‒ i support the proposal as it aims above all to make the ten-t system more efficient, interconnected and sustainable by seeking to build a framework that increases the productivity of ports. at the same time, this proposal also aims to help them adapt to changes in transport and logistics. i support the modernisation of port services and operations, while at the same time creating an environment that is attractive for greater investment in ports. the proposal also aims to increase competition between ports, which is now at such a low level that monopoly abuse may be common. it is also important to establish common eu rules determining when state aid to ports is allowed, which must exclude aid intended for the construction of additional port infrastructure and transport routes.
in writing. ‒ ports connect europe with the world. european ports facilitate more than one third of eu trade and play a major role in the transport sector, as well as representing the potential for new jobs and investment. in 2013, the european commission tried to introduce the liberalisation of port services. the commission is working towards a more efficient, interconnected and sustainable operation of the ten-t network by developing a framework that improves the capacity of all ports and takes into account current traffic and logistics requirements. the purpose of the regulation is to prevent unfair competition between ports and to increase the business efficiency of port services. the proposal also aims to ensure financial transparency for ports, transparency and reduce red tape for users. unemployment is a major problem today and modernising ports can create new jobs, especially in the eu's coastal regions. taking into account the diversity and advantages of european ports, the aim should be to develop them on an equal and balanced basis. it is important to support the successful operation of the ten-t network, which also includes slovenia, and to promote the development of ports and the creation of new jobs in general. in view of the above, i supported the report on the proposal for a regulation establishing a framework for market access to port services and financial transparency for ports.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council establishing a framework for market access to port services and financial transparency for ports. liberalisation means for the consumer to have a choice, and for entrepreneurs and businesses to have to work hard and do a good job. all of us who grew up under socialism know firsthand what it means to have no choice. the eu's services sector remains heavily wound up in vat, at a cost to consumers, businesses and society as a whole. i therefore welcome the liberalisation of services in ports, but at the same time i regret that the procedure for adopting the regulation has been unnecessarily prolonged. although some would like to see the changes introduced more quickly, i believe that the regulation is an appropriate compromise, giving existing and potential new suppliers adequate time to prepare for the changed working conditions.
in writing. ‒ i supported the report on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council establishing a framework for market access to port services and financial transparency for ports, as the regulation provides the much needed legal certainty for ports, increases the efficiency of port operations and reduces the prices of port services. the establishment of framework conditions and the modernisation of port service activities are key to creating a stimulating and promising environment for the development of ports, while also attracting new investment to ports. i believe that the regulation can take an important step towards a fair and level playing field for all european ports.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report that regulates market access to port services and financial transparency of ports. the report is designed to support the increase in their efficiency and the reduction in costs of services supplied at the ports. it underlines the prevention of price abuse and market distortions while boosting maritime trade flows and allows for ports to keep their current service arrangements, provided they meet minimum requirements. i voted in favour of this report as it aims for more transparent and fairly priced eu maritime port facilities.
in writing. ‒ the european network includes over 300 ports, which directly or indirectly generate more than three million jobs. they are characterized by diversity in size, management and organization. in support of the idea of advanced and balanced joint european action on ports, which would, inter alia, improve the financial transparency of port operations and maintain their competitiveness, i supported the launch of tripartite negotiations between the commission, the council and the committee responsible.
in writing. ‒ i welcome and support the proposed regulation. this is a significant update of the outdated system for setting the criteria for reporting the harmonised indices of consumer prices (hicps) and the housing price indices (hpis) at eu and member state level. the hicp is the basis for inflation, which underpins all major economic and monetary decisions. it is therefore all the more important that the system is objective and that the statistics clearly reflect the reality. the proposed regulation updates the 1995 regulation and takes account in particular of the new eu decision-making brought about by the treaty of lisbon the competence of the commission or eurostat to adopt implementing and delegated acts. the important issue raised by the rapporteur seems to me to be the requirement for monthly preparation of hicp estimates by member states, which will improve the quality of the provisional inflation data.
in writing. ‒ i support the proposal for a regulation. it provides a uniform framework for the design, compilation and presentation of harmonised indices of consumer prices (hicps) and of house price indices (hpis) at union, national and sub-national level. the hicp provides a measure of inflation, which is used, among other things, as an important input in the deflation of economic values such as wages, rents and interest rates, and therefore underpins economic and monetary decisions. it is therefore of the utmost importance that those statistics are objective, impartial and comparable across all member states and product areas. the hicp regulation in force was adopted in 1995. in view of developments in the field of consumer price statistics, it is necessary to revise this framework in order to ensure the greatest possible comparability for the main users of the hicp.
in writing. ‒ harmonised indices of consumer prices (hicps) are designed to measure inflation in a harmonised way in all member states. the commission and the european central bank use the hicp in their assessment of price stability in the member states. regulation (ec) no 2494/95 on the hicp was adopted in 1995 and circumstances have changed since then, so that it is necessary to adapt that legislation. the commission proposed to have a single framework for the development, compilation and presentation of harmonised indices of consumer prices (hicps) and of housing price indices (hpis) at union, national and sub-national level. following the trialogue negotiations, the regulation also contains a reference to the owner-occupied housing price index (ooh), as the share of owner-occupied housing varies widely between member states. the commission will carry out a study on ooh and there is a possibility that this index will be included in the context of the hicp. the regulation also recommends a study of the cost of living index, in order to complement the hicp index with additional information related to inflation. provisional inflation data are very important for the conduct of monetary policy, and i therefore believe that it is crucial to provide objective and impartial statistics with the greatest possible comparability for hicp users. i voted for the report because of what it says.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on harmonised indices of consumer prices and repealing the regulation. the last regulation in force is more than 20 years old and it is therefore necessary to adopt a new regulation which will be in line with the new developments in eu decision-making brought about by the treaty of lisbon. we need objective, impartial and accurate data to be able to compare between member states. i support the commission's contribution to the financing of pilot studies, where appropriate, and its report to the european parliament and the council every five years assessing the main findings of the pilot studies.
in writing. ‒ i supported the report on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on harmonised indices of consumer prices and repealing regulation (ec) no 2494/95, as the new regulation provides a single european framework for harmonised indices of consumer prices at both union and national level. i believe that the hicp provides a relevant criterion that allows statistics on the cost of living to be objective, unbiased and comparable across all member states. i believe that the regulation is absolutely necessary, not only to revise the 1995 hicp framework and to take account of the eu decision-making innovation of the lisbon treaty, but also to provide a benchmark for inflation, which is used, among other things, as an important indicator of the deflation of economic values. the latter is the basis for economic and monetary decisions.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report concerning the harmonisation of consumer price indices. the report suggests modernising existing rules to enable objective informing on price stability within the eu and monitor the effects of the european central bank’s monetary policy. it formulates a uniform legal framework for the creation, improvement and diffusion of harmonised indices of consumer prices (hicp) and of housing prices indices (hpi) data at the national and sub-national eu level. hicp are particularly significant as they provide the inflation measure used for deflating economic values serving as the basis for economic and monetary policy decisions. it is essential that these statistics are objective and comparable across all member states and all product areas, as quality statistics and their comparability are of fundamental importance for all eu citizens, researchers and those responsible for public policy.
in writing. ‒ the existing framework for the provision of harmonised indices of consumer prices is made up of the 1995 regulation and 20 implementing regulations, and as such is unrevised and in some cases obsolete. legislation therefore needs to be adapted and harmonised for a number of reasons, in particular to provide accurate information on price stability within the union and to monitor the effects of monetary policy pursued by the european central bank. in line with the above, i supported the report on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on harmonised indices of consumer prices and repealing regulation (ec) no 2494/95.
in writing. ‒ i supported the proposed annual report on the protection of the eu's financial interests and the fight against fraud, which analyses in depth the situation in the fight against irregularities and proposes an appropriate set of measures to intensify the fight against fraud. financial fraud is unfortunately inherent in all areas, and the eu budget is no exception. the commission notes that the commission has not yet adopted a decision on the compatibility of the aid with the internal market. this suggests that despite the eu's many efforts to combat irregularities, there are still many reservations. it is also important to distinguish between irregularities and fraud, as the former may occur unintentionally, while the latter are deliberately aimed at damaging public funds. to prevent both, therefore, there is a need for enhanced cooperation between member states and the european institutions, in particular the commission, and on the other hand, a need to simplify the system of rules governing the implementation of the system of payments from the eu budget.
in writing. ‒ i support the report because i think it covers the subject of the european investment bank, which is trying to align its policies with eu policies. i support the efforts made in the report to increase the eib's power and role, but also its transparency, which leads to greater accountability to the european parliament. transparency and accountability to parliament are essential, as the complexity of the bank's operations will increase as it develops.
in writing. ‒ the committee on budgetary control has assessed the commission's report entitled 'protection of the european union's financial interests fight against fraud annual report 2014'. two areas of concern are highlighted, tobacco smuggling and public procurement. illicit tobacco trade is a global problem that costs eu member states huge sums of public revenue every year. estimates suggest that they lose as much as 37 billion euros. this is detrimental to the well-being of european taxpayers and also has a negative impact on the functioning of the internal market, as it distorts competition and deteriorates conditions for smes. the second problem is the area of public procurement. i am aware that there are many errors and irregularities in this area. however, it would be possible to calculate the actual impact of these irregularities on the european budget and to determine how to respond. we need a european prosecutor general. in relation to the necessary anti-fraud measures, reporting and monitoring should be improved and cooperation between institutions increased. for this reason, i supported the report in plenary and voted for its adoption.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the 2014 annual report on the protection of the european union's financial interests the fight against fraud. the fight against fraud and corruption is important both from the point of view of ethical and moral principles and from the point of view of increasing the european union's competitiveness in the world economy. by spending taxpayers' money transparently, in line with the objectives of the european union and the interests of eu citizens, we make an important contribution to strengthening citizens' trust in the eu institutions, which has been gradually eroding in recent years. it's important to distinguish between fraud and irregularity. not all irregularities are frauds. to combat irregularities more effectively and to implement rules and requirements, we need transparent and simple rules, enhanced cooperation between member states and the european commission, timely provision of accurate data and a uniform approach by member states to detect and report irregularities. we need strong political will to fight fraud at both national and european level.
in writing. ‒ report on the 2014 annual report on the protection of the european union's financial interests fight against fraud i supported the report, as i consider it extremely important that eu funds are managed in accordance with the rules and principles of sound financial management. it is important to recognise that the protection of the eu's financial interests is a central element of the treaty on the functioning of the eu and that we have a shared responsibility both within the eu and in the individual member states to protect the financial interests of the union. i consider that such measures are an important step towards a better protection of the financial interests of the union against crime, while at the same time increasing efficiency in the fight against financial irregularities and fraud. i believe that by taking such action we preserve the confidence of european citizens in the european institutions.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the annual report 2014 on the protection of the eu’s financial interests – fight against fraud, which targets prevention of financial fraud and strengthening of financial transparency. according to article 325(5) of the treaty on the functioning of the european union (tfeu) the commission is mandated to report each year on its work with member states to combat fraud and ensure sound management of eu funds. in 2014, member states reported 1 649 irregularities as fraudulent (both suspected and established fraud), involving eur 538 million in eu funds. the report urges member states to make greater efforts in fraud detection and combat, ensuring that their controls are risk-based and well-targeted. it equally acclaims the progress made at national level to implement new rules and policies aimed at strengthening the fight against fraud in the near future.
in writing. ‒ report on the annual report 2014 on the protection of the european union's financial interests combating fraud, which i supported, notes that the number of irregularities reported to the commission in 2014 increased compared to 2013. public procurement and the increase in tobacco smuggling are particularly critical areas. i believe that all necessary measures should be taken to prevent irregularities to the detriment of budgetary resources, whether they result from ignorance of complex rules and requirements or fraud. the report proposes, inter alia, the establishment of a system of rigorous indicators to measure corruption in the member states, the amendment of the rules to better protect whistleblowers and the transparency of lobbying.
in writing. ‒ i also supported the report on the mainstreaming of gender equality in the work of the european parliament, prepared by ms mlinarjeva. every year on 8 march, we celebrate international women's day, or as we call it in slovenia, women's day, which recognizes the struggle of women for their equality. unfortunately, this is not guaranteed in many areas. i myself am aware that women need to be respected every day and in all areas, whether in social, professional or everyday life. many women, in addition to their professional and social and public work, also play an important role in motherhood and child rearing. the report proposed concerns the proper integration of gender equality in the work of the european parliament, but the proposals it advocates should be applied to all areas of social life. despite the great progress made in the fight for equality in europe, large gender gaps still exist in many areas and efforts need to be made at both eu and national level to reduce such anomalies.
in writing. ‒ the european union recognises equality between women and men as a fundamental right and a common value of the eu. at international level, gender mainstreaming is accepted as a strategy for achieving gender equality. in practice, this means taking gender into account in the design, implementation and evaluation of policies, regulatory measures and programmes aimed at promoting equality between women and men and at promoting the fight against discrimination. in 1996, the commission introduced a two-pronged approach: mainstreaming gender into all policies and at the same time implementing measures to tackle gender inequalities. since 2009, a gender equality network has been established in the european parliament, involving some members and some staff of the european parliament. all members of the network were given the opportunity to reply to a questionnaire, which was then used to produce a report on the mainstreaming of the principle of gender equality in the work of the european parliament. they found that there are some examples of good practice, but that coordination could be improved, both within parliament and with other institutions. on the basis of the replies, it is proposed that a procedure be introduced to incorporate the principle of gender equality into the rules of procedure of the european parliament. i believe it is important to promote activities to mainstream the principle of gender equality, which is why i voted in favour of the report.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the mainstreaming of gender equality in the work of the european parliament. the definition of gender equality is broader than equality, covering formal-legal equality as well as de facto equality in everyday life. in recent years, some progress has been made, but there are still many shortcomings. research shows that in october 2013, 17.8% of board members in leading european companies were women. without actions at eu level, such as the european strategy for gender equality and the legislative initiative on women's quotas on boards, it would have been even less than 14%. reducing the gender gap is an area where the eu must play a visible and important role, as it is not enough to act only at the end of the chain.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on gender mainstreaming in the work of the european parliament. gender mainstreaming represents the integration of a gender viewpoint into the preparation, design, implementation, monitoring and evaluation of policies, regulatory measures and spending programmes. the goal is to promote equality between women and men, and combat discrimination. the report calls for continuing expansion of the gender mainstreaming system and its regular monitoring across policy areas. it appeals for the creation of a supporting environment for women to take part in decision-making positions at all levels and underlines the importance of measures for the reconciliation of work and private and family life. particular emphasis is placed on the importance of a constant struggle and continuing work towards gender equality.

vice-president of the commission.– madam president, i am very grateful for the debate this evening. it demonstrates how serious the task ahead of us is. we have many pressing needs in europe and we will have to prioritise our resources and use the resources better. in that sense, i agree with those who have spoken about the necessity to prioritise competitiveness, growth and jobs, firstly, and then, secondly, to make sure that we are able to deal with what has been the biggest challenge for europe in our lifetime. we are extremely focused on anticipating where problems may arise and this is why we have changed the instruments in our hands, including the capacity to provide humanitarian assistance inside europe, and i can tell you that in the commission we started thinking about this long before it became a pressing need in greece. we do not know what else may come our way but we know that in a world that is more fragile, where shocks are more frequent, we have to be prepared to respond quickly and in a more agile way to protect the security of our citizens, to provide new opportunities where they are wiped out by crises, and for this i would conclude by saying that first i agree that never mind how stretched our budget is we have to have space for some flexibility for a quick response when needs arise. secondly, we do have to think in a more creative way about how we use money – can we achieve more than one objective with the same euro? i will give you a small example here. we took eur 30 million from the eur 500 million to deal with the milk crisis last year, to give it to the world food programme to buy milk from our farmers and feed children in refugee camps. we have to think in a much more creative way about the 2017 budget and those that are to follow. my last point is yes, we need money, but in this very tough time for us we need our unity even more. therefore, as we work on the budget we should be very careful not to create unnecessary clashes and battles that only undermine the unity of the european union and which do not strengthen it.
in writing. we have a tough task ahead of us this year too. taxpayers rightly expect us to allocate european funds with utmost prudence. the budget for the coming year must be even more proactive in promoting growth and job creation, while successfully addressing the challenges associated with the growing migration and refugee crisis. at this stage of preparing the budget for next year, i would like to stress above all that we must continue to work to reduce youth unemployment. the commission will continue to monitor the implementation of the union's policy on youth, and will continue to monitor the implementation of the union's policy on youth. i certainly welcome this commitment statement, but i wonder why no new commitments have been made for 2016 to provide additional funding for the youth employment initiative. according to a recent eurostat survey, youth unemployment in many member states - particularly those with the highest rates - is expected to decline. at eu level, it was as much as 1.5% lower at the end of last year. it's a sign that our past efforts have been successful. i believe that the youth employment initiative is one of the main factors for this success, and i therefore agree with the rapporteur and call on the commission to present its assessment of this initiative as soon as possible and to take it into account when preparing the draft budget for the coming year.

in writing. ‒ the proposed directive aims to reduce sulphur dioxide emissions from the combustion of certain liquid fuels and thus reduce the harmful effects of these emissions on man and the environment. this directive lays down maximum permitted sulphur content in heavy fuel oil, gas oil, marine gas oil and marine diesel oil used in the european union. it is important to reduce the sulphur content at eu level collectively, as environmental acidification is a transboundary phenomenon. the aim of the codification is to simplify and clarify eu law. in this case, the codification of council directive 1999/32/ec of 26 april 1999 relating to a reduction in the sulphur content of certain liquid fuels and amending directive 93/12/eec is appropriate. the consultative working party of the legal services of the european parliament, the council and the commission considers that the proposal constitutes a codification of existing texts without any substantial change in their content. i therefore voted in favour of the report in the plenary, thereby supporting the proposal for a directive.
in writing. ‒ i supported the report on the proposal for a european parliament and council directive on the reduction of sulphur in certain liquid fuels, as it is an important directive that addresses the issue of air pollution, which is one of the main environmental concerns facing european citizens. unfortunately, a large proportion of europe's population lives in areas where the eu's air quality objectives are still not fully met. i believe that the proposed directive represents an even greater effort to ensure better air quality and natural living conditions at union level. the latter directive will also bring us one step closer to innovative and efficient use of resources.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a directive concerning the reduction in the sulphur content of certain liquid fuels. the report demands for the reduction of emissions of sulphur dioxide resulting from the use of certain types of liquid fuels. the final aim is to reduce the harmful effects of these emissions on the population and the environment. the suggested method to achieve such a goal is to impose limits on the sulphur content of such fuels as a condition for their use within member states’ land and sea territory. the report strives towards a healthier and more ecological environment.
in writing. ‒ emissions from the combustion of fuels for high-sulphur vessels pollute the air with sulphur dioxide and particulate matter, which are harmful to human health and the environment and contribute to the formation of acidic deposits. the existing council directive 1999/32/ec, which sets maximum sulphur levels for marine fuels, has been substantially amended several times and is therefore not transposable. since i believe that air quality must be maintained in a way that does not have major negative effects on human health and the environment and does not endanger them, i supported the proposal for a new directive, which provides a transparent and clear regulatory framework.
in writing. ‒ as with the previous item on the agenda, i have no comment on this one. i supported the motion for a resolution on the proposal for a regulation to prevent the diversion of trade in certain key medicines to the european union. it is simply a codification of existing texts, which do not involve any substantive changes.
in writing. ‒ i supported the report because it is important that the world's poorest countries, which are plagued by some of the worst diseases, have the opportunity to get the medicines they need at the lowest possible price. it is necessary to prevent unfair commercial practices in the procurement and distribution of medicines, while ensuring that there is a sufficient supply of medicines for poorer countries.
in writing. ‒ for the treatment of infectious diseases, poor developing countries have a high need for affordable basic medicines. these countries are often almost entirely dependent on imported medicines because their local production is insufficient. a distinction should be made between the prices of developed countries and those of the poorest developing countries. the latter must be provided with basic pharmaceutical products at very low prices. however, these prices must not become a benchmark for the price paid for the same products in the markets of developed countries. the proposed codified regulation aims to prevent parallel pricing products from being imported into the european union, but provides for exceptions in certain circumstances. the aim of the codification is to simplify and clarify eu law. in this case, the codification of council regulation (ec) no 953/2003 of 26 may 2003 to prevent trade diversion of certain key medicinal products to the european union is appropriate. the consultative working party of the legal services of the european parliament, the council and the commission considers that the proposal constitutes a codification of existing texts without any substantial change in their content. i therefore voted in favour of the report in the plenary, thereby supporting the proposal for a regulation.
in writing. ‒ i supported the report on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council to prevent the diversion of trade in certain essential medicines to the european union, as the proposal is a meaningful codification of the texts existing so far, without any substantive changes, namely the codification of council regulation (ec) no 953/2003 of 26 may 2003 to prevent the diversion of trade in certain essential medicines to the european union.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a regulation concerning the diversion into the european union of certain key medicines. many of the poorest developing countries are dependent on imports of affordable essential medicines for the treatment of transmissible diseases. price segmentation between developed country markets and these country markets is necessary to ensure that the poorest countries are supplied with essential pharmaceutical products at significantly reduced prices. the report underlines the need to encourage pharmaceutical companies to make medicines directed to the poorest countries available at greatly reduced prices in significantly increased volumes, in line with the regulation. it equally states the need for a procedure which identifies the products, countries and diseases covered by this regulation, as well as the need to differentiate the appearance of reduced-priced medicines in order to prevent their import into the eu. the overall aim of this report is to call for greater help to be provided to those in need of essential medication as well as for preventing the abuse of such help.
in writing. ‒ i supported the legislative proposal to prevent parallel pricing of pharmaceutical products from being imported into the european union. it is necessary to ensure that these products remain on the market of the poorest developing countries and to prevent the increase of economic interest in diverting trade to high-price markets. many of the poorest developing countries urgently need access to affordable basic medicines to treat infectious diseases.
in writing. ‒ i supported the proposed decision to conclude an agreement between the eu and andorra on the exchange of financial account information as an important step in the fight against tax fraud and tax evasion. the agreement builds on the 2004 agreement, which resulted in andorra implementing measures equivalent to those of the eu savings tax directive. by some estimates, the grey economy in the eu member states represents a staggering €1 trillion a year in uncollected taxes and contributions. there is therefore no doubt that this is a major anomaly, which is detrimental both in terms of free competition and in terms of providing access to public services financed by taxation. the fight against tax fraud is one of the eu's priorities and is already showing results. the examples of corporate tax evasion exposures we've seen since the lux leaks are steps in the right direction. to achieve the objectives of reducing tax irregularities, we need to strengthen the exchange of financial account data and all other relevant information concerning cross-border business operations. that agreement will allow for just that.
in writing. ‒ on 27 february 2016, the european union and andorra signed an agreement on the automatic exchange of financial account information with the aim of improving international tax cooperation and compliance. i support the proposal as the agreement is an important step in the ongoing efforts to combat tax fraud and tax evasion and builds on the 2004 agreement that achieved that andorra implement measures equivalent to those in the eu savings tax directive. in particular, i support the provision under the new agreement that eu member states and andorra will automatically exchange data on financial accounts held by residents of one or the other opened in the territory of the other. the aim is to address cases where a taxpayer attempts to conceal capital in the form of income or assets for which he has not paid tax. the agreement thus aims to ensure that andorra implements enhanced measures equivalent to those in the eu legal framework and complies with the procedures for the automatic exchange of financial account information, which are also encouraged by the oecd global standards. this will also benefit andorra, which has recently reformed its internal tax system and introduced personal income taxation for its residents.
in writing. ‒ the european union and andorra signed an agreement on 27 february 2016 on the automatic exchange of financial account information to improve international tax cooperation and compliance. the recent agreement builds on the previous one from 2004, which provided that andorra implement measures equivalent to those in the eu savings tax directive. the new agreement will provide for the automatic exchange of financial account data between the eu member states and andorra from 2018 for data collected from 1 january 2017. the purpose is to resolve situations where a taxpayer attempts to conceal capital in the form of income or assets for which he has not paid tax. the tax administrations in the member states and andorra will be able to administer and enforce national tax legislation in cross-border situations, to identify correctly and unambiguously the relevant taxpayers and to assess the likelihood of tax evasion. they will also ensure that no unnecessary further investigation is undertaken. the agreement represents an important step in the ongoing efforts to combat tax fraud and tax evasion and enhances cooperation in the exchange of information on financial accounts. i supported the report in plenary on the basis of what you have described.
in writing. ‒ i supported the report on the proposal for a council decision on the conclusion, on behalf of the european union, of the amending protocol to the agreement between the european community and the principality of andorra providing for measures equivalent to those laid down in council directive 2003/48/ec on taxation of savings income in the form of interest payments, as an encouraging step in the current efforts to prevent tax fraud and tax evasion. the present decision is a meaningful upgrade of the 2004 agreement and introduces new elements aimed at ensuring that andorra implements enhanced measures equivalent to those in the eu legal framework, while respecting the procedures for the automatic exchange of financial account information. the 2014 oecd global standards are also a driving force behind this.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report concerning the eu-andorra agreement on the automatic exchange of financial account information. the report entails the automatic interchange of information on the bank accounts of each other’s residents, with the aim of reducing tax fraud and tax evasion. the information to be exchanged includes income, such as interest and dividends, but also account balances and earnings from the sale of financial assets. this agreement will make it more difficult for eu citizens to hide cash from the tax authorities in bank accounts in andorra, allowing for better financial transparency in the eu.
in writing. ‒ i have supported the report on the proposal for a council decision on the conclusion, on behalf of the european union, of the amending protocol to the agreement between the european community and the principality of andorra providing for measures equivalent to those laid down in council directive 2003/48/ec on taxation of savings income in the form of interest payments and establishing unconditional exchange of financial account information. i believe that the agreement will further strengthen the ongoing efforts to combat tax fraud and tax evasion and ensure that andorra respects the procedures for the automatic exchange of financial account information.

in writing. ‒ i also supported the report proposed by my colleague, ms chinnici, on the proposal for a directive on procedural guarantees for children who are suspects or accused persons in criminal proceedings. the main purpose of the proposal is to establish uniform standards across the eu for the exercise of procedural rights in criminal proceedings for persons under the age of 18. in addition, the directive also focuses on promoting the mutual recognition of judgments and judicial decisions in the field of criminal law. over a million children are involved in criminal proceedings in the eu each year, and they are treated very differently across the member states, especially in terms of the provision of rights. therefore, harmonisation of standards at eu level is essential.
in writing. ‒ i support the proposal because it is necessary to ensure that all persons under 18 years of age are effectively and more uniformly entitled to a fair trial by means of minimum common rules. this is linked to the objective of promoting the mutual recognition of judgments and judicial decisions in the field of criminal law and ensuring the necessary legal protection for children.
in writing. ‒ the commission estimates that more than one million children are involved in criminal proceedings in the eu every year. that's 12% of all cases. however, the treatment of children in criminal proceedings varies significantly between member states. in some member states, for example, children are not recognised as having a fundamental right to the assistance of a lawyer. in order to ensure that the rights of children are protected in criminal proceedings, the commission proposed in 2013 a directive on the protection of children in criminal proceedings as part of a broader legislative package on procedural rights. it is important that persons under 18 years of age are guaranteed effective and uniform exercise of the right to a fair trial at all stages of the proceedings. the right to legal aid is inalienable and is linked to the right to free legal aid. the directive puts the best interests of the child at the forefront, as it contains important elements such as the right to individual assessment and the way in which the hearing is conducted. judges, lawyers, and others dealing with children need to be specially trained to do so. where other safeguards are not possible, detention of children may only be carried out on condition that children are detained separately from adult children. i voted in favour of the proposal for a directive because it will establish good minimum rights for children who are suspects or accused in criminal proceedings and will generally improve children's rights everywhere in the eu.
in writing. ‒ i supported the report on the proposal for a european parliament and council directive on procedural safeguards for children who are suspects or accused persons in criminal proceedings, given the very worrying high number of children involved in criminal proceedings across the eu and the wide disparities in the treatment of children involved in criminal proceedings between member states. the small number of specialised child prosecution bodies is also a cause for concern. the latter directive brings many important rights and opportunities for special treatment of children, access to lawyers, free legal aid, specific provisions on deprivation of liberty and ensuring that children are detained separately from adults. the proposal also provides for specific training for judges, law enforcement authorities, lawyers and others dealing with children. i think this proposal is a good one, as it concerns one of the most vulnerable groups for which, despite numerous international instruments, there is no legal definition of the essential elements for a fair trial. it is also part of a plan to strengthen the procedural rights of suspects and accused persons in criminal proceedings.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on procedural safeguards for children suspected or accused in criminal proceedings. the report seeks to formulate a properly structured catalogue of rights for children suspected or accused in criminal proceedings with the aim of uniform protection of children’s rights across the eu. the main aim of the report is to promote children’s rights, as the legal mechanisms for children protection are not fully and uniformly applied in the member states. according to eu researchers there are major discrepancies in the way in which children involved in criminal proceedings are treated in the various member states, leading to insufficient children’s rights protection at the various stages in criminal proceedings in the eu.
in writing. ‒ i supported a legislative proposal that provides procedural guarantees for children who are suspects or accused in criminal proceedings. i consider that these specific safeguard measures are necessary to establish a uniform regime in the union, as it has been found that procedural guarantees for children are poorly regulated in some member states. children in criminal proceedings will be guaranteed, inter alia, the right to a lawyer, the right to a medical examination, the right to audio-visual recording during interrogation and special guarantees during deprivation of liberty.

in writing. ‒ in 2003, the european parliament, the council of the european union and the european commission concluded an interinstitutional agreement on better lawmaking. the legislative environment has changed over the years, in particular with the treaty of lisbon, and new negotiations were launched in 2015 to update the agreement and to incorporate existing best practices. in december 2015, the conference of presidents endorsed the provisional agreement reached by the negotiators of the three institutions on the text of the new interinstitutional agreement. they jointly committed themselves to promoting simplicity, clarity and consistency in the drafting of legislation, while advocating full transparency of the legislative process. the agreement also addresses the tools for better law-making and, in particular, impact assessments. in february 2016, the constitutional affairs committee adopted a report on the conclusion of this agreement. the report provides a balanced assessment of the agreement, which provides a good basis for further cooperation between the institutions to ensure better lawmaking in the interests of eu citizens. in any case, this new interinstitutional agreement is based on the assumption that legislation is essentially a source of burden and difficulty, and on the assumption that the main problem of the eu is over-regulation. but we should focus on the real problem: bad policy choices. i did not support the report in plenary, but i abstained.

in writing. ‒ by voting in favour, i support the amendments tabled by the negotiating colleagues in the european parliament to the regulation of the european parliament and of the european council introducing emergency autonomous trade measures for the republic of tunisia. we have thus pointed out that the emergency measures to help the tunisian economy following the two terrorist attacks last year are temporary in nature. the main export industry, olive oil production, has been in difficulty and will therefore also benefit to the greatest extent from the measures. in order to avoid fraud and to ensure that the envisaged autonomous trade measures actually benefit the tunisian economy, they should be conditional on compliance by tunisia with the relevant union rules on the origin of products and related procedures, as well as on effective administrative cooperation between tunisia and the union.
in writing. ‒ the terrorist attacks in tunisia and sousse last year had a very negative impact on the tunisian economy, which was already in serious trouble. the european union wishes to assist tunisia in its political and economic transition. the european commission has therefore proposed to introduce a temporary unilateral duty-free tariff quota of 35000 tonnes per year for a period of two years i.e. a total of 70.000 tonnes for the export of olive oil from tunisia to the union, in the form of autonomous trade measures and without increasing the total volume of imports. in these difficult circumstances, the european union supports tunisia's economic development and thereby contributes to tunisia's democratic process. the measure will support a large part of the tunisian economy, as the tunisian oil sector in total provides jobs for more than one million people, representing one fifth of all jobs in tunisian agriculture. olive oil is also the main agricultural product exported by tunisia. i believe that swift and concrete eu action is a strong political signal of support for tunisia, and thus a boost to the path to democracy. i supported the report in plenary on the basis of what you have described.

in writing. ‒ council regulation (ec) no 1528/2007, the so-called 'market access regulation', concerns arrangements for the import of goods originating in certain countries that are part of the african, caribbean and pacific (acp) group of countries. as provided for in the agreements, acp states which intend to establish or lead to the establishment of economic partnership agreements shall be taken into account. in this case, it is a matter of more favourable access to eu market rules for a number of products defined in the regulation and, in particular, of the elimination of import duties on the eu market if the products originate from the regions or countries listed in the annex to the regulation. in addition, the regulation also lays down rules for determining the origin of products from the regions or countries concerned, which may be amended in accordance with this proposal. the commission proposal concerns the codification and recasting of this regulation and aims to ensure transparency, clarity and simplification of eu legislation, as the original market access regulation has been amended nine times since its adoption in 2007. in the interests of clarity and legibility, i voted in favour of adopting the report on the proposal for a regulation on the application of the arrangements to goods originating in certain acp states, thus supporting the codification of the regulation.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on the application of the arrangements for goods originating in certain countries of the african, caribbean and pacific (acp) group of states provided for in agreements establishing, or leading to the establishment of, economic partnership agreements. i support codification, which will ensure the transparency, clarity and simplification of eu legislation. eu legislation is in dire need of updating. the market access regulation provides for duty-free and quota-free access to the eu market for products originating in african, caribbean and pacific countries that are not least developed countries.
in writing. ‒ i supported the report on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on the application of the arrangements for goods originating in certain countries in the african, caribbean and pacific (acp) group set out in agreements establishing or leading to the establishment of economic partnership agreements (recast), as the purpose of the codification is to ensure transparency, clarity and simplification of eu legislation after the original legal act has been amended several times. the market access regulation has been amended nine times since its adoption in 2007, including alignment with the treaty of lisbon under the collective trade act ii and subsequent commission delegated regulations. codification is therefore essential to ensure clarity and legibility of the regulation.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report regarding codification and modification of the ‘market access regulation’ (mar), governing imports of products originating in certain african, caribbean and pacific countries. this temporary instrument provides duty-free quota-free access to the eu market for products originating in non-ldc acp countries, leading to the conclusion and application of the respective wto-compatible economic partnership agreements (epas) before 1 october 2016. the aim of the codification application is to ensure transparency, clarity and simplification of the eu legislation after revising the original legal instrument numerous times. codification is crucial for ensuring clarity and readability of the regulation and this is why i voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ i supported the report on the proposal for the codification and revision of the regulation on the application of the arrangements for goods originating in certain countries of the african, caribbean and pacific (acp) group of states provided for in agreements establishing, or leading to the establishment of, economic partnership agreements. this temporary instrument provides for duty-free and quota-free access to the eu market for products originating in the acp states before 1 october 2016. i believe that this instrument supports and maintains smooth regional integration, promotes sustainable development and contributes to the overall efforts to eradicate poverty and improve living conditions in the acp states. the purpose of codification is also to ensure the transparency, clarity and simplification of eu legislation.
in writing. ‒ the new protocol, which is in line with the objectives of the fisheries partnership agreement between the union and greenland, strengthens and promotes cooperation and a partnership framework for the development of a sustainable fisheries policy. as the protocol is based on the responsible exploitation of fisheries resources and ecosystems in the greenland area, which is highly dependent on fisheries as its second most important economic industry, it is in the interest of both parties to focus more on the sustainable development of fisheries policy, the conservation of ecosystems and the responsible exploitation of fisheries resources. the protocol itself also provides for a pilot fisheries programme for species not covered by the protocol and for scientific cooperation in the field of sustainable exploitation of fisheries resources, which is why i supported the agreement.
in writing. ‒ through fisheries partnership agreements, the eu obtains fishing rights for a large number of fish stocks in the exclusive economic zone of a partner country, while providing financial and technical support to that country. the fisheries partnership agreement with the government of denmark and the home rule government of greenland (the eu/greenland partnership) is the third most important agreement for the eu in terms of its economic value. parliament's consent is required for the conclusion of a new protocol to the agreement, which lays down the details for its implementation over the next five years. the new protocol provides for a financial contribution from the eu of eur 17,8 million per year, representing the amount for access to the greenlandic exclusive economic zone (eur 13,17 million) and a specific amount (eur 2,931 million) to support greenland's sectoral fisheries policy. fish accounts for almost 90% of greenland's exports; the most important segments are the capelin, greenland halibut and cod fisheries. this mixed agreement will provide eu vessels with access to a large number of fish stocks in the greenland exclusive economic zone. the new protocol is consistent with the objectives of the fisheries partnership agreement, as it promotes and enhances eu-greenland cooperation and provides for the development of a sustainable fisheries policy and the responsible exploitation of fishery resources in the greenland fishing zone. i therefore voted in favour of the report and thus authorised the conclusion of the protocol.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the recommendation on the draft council decision on the conclusion, on behalf of the european union, of the protocol setting out the fishing opportunities and financial contribution provided for in the fisheries partnership agreement between the european community, of the one part, and the government of denmark and the home rule government of greenland, of the other part. the aim of the agreement is for the eu to provide financial and technical support in exchange for fishing rights. i support the conclusion of a new agreement which continues to provide significant economic benefits to the european union and greenland.
in writing. ‒ i supported the recommendation on the draft council decision on the conclusion, on behalf of the european union, of the protocol setting out the fishing opportunities and financial contribution provided for in the fisheries partnership agreement between the european community, of the one part, and the government of denmark and the home rule government of greenland, of the other part, as these two countries cover a large fishing area which is ecologically biodiverse, pristine and consequently provides the eu market with healthy seafood. the eu-greenland fisheries partnership agreement is one of the most important for the eu in terms of economic value and the only such agreement with a nordic country. almost all greenland's exports of fishery products are destined for the eu, with denmark accounting for more than 90% of imports into the eu. frozen goats, greenland halibut and cod are the main exports. the eu shall pay a fixed annual financial contribution for access, irrespective of fishing opportunities, in accordance with the protocol. the current protocol provides for a financial contribution from the eu of €17.85 million per year.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the protocol setting out the fishing opportunities and the financial contribution provided for by the fisheries partnership agreement with the government of denmark and the home rule government of greenland. recently the european union has signed a number of fisheries partnership agreements (fpas) and protocols with ‘third countries’ providing financial and technical support in exchange for fishing rights to a wide range of fish stocks in the partner country’s exclusive economic zone. the specific fpa with the government of denmark and the home rule government of greenland is particularly significant to the eu for generating substantial economic benefits through fishing opportunities. while greenland’s economy is highly dependent on the fisheries sector, its flora and fauna should be well preserved as part of the unique arctic region. the renewed protocol takes into consideration ecological and economic aspects of the agreement, which is the reason i voted in favour of its conclusion.
in writing. ‒ the fisheries partnership agreement is the third most important agreement, with strong economic value and mutual benefits for the economies of both partners. that is why i supported it, as it strengthens cooperation between the eu and greenland and promotes a partnership framework for the development of a sustainable fisheries policy and the responsible exploitation of fisheries resources.
in writing. ‒ international relations in the field of aviation between member states and third countries are normally governed by bilateral air transport agreements. the european court of justice has found that the existing agreement with macao is contrary to the eu legal order, as it allows a third country to refuse, withdraw or suspend the authorisation or privileges of an air carrier designated by a member state. since this has been found to constitute discrimination against eu carriers established in the territory of a member state, even though that carrier is not majority owned by that member state or its nationals, and since this is contrary to article 49 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union, this proposal amends or supplements existing provisions contained in bilateral agreements. i therefore voted in favour of this agreement, which also covers the right to set up a company, safety provisions, the taxation of aviation fuel and anti-competitive practices.
in writing. ‒ the european commission has concluded an agreement with the macao special administrative region of the people's republic of china on certain aspects of air transport. international relations in the field of aviation between member states and third countries are normally governed by bilateral agreements. in 2002, the european court of justice ruled that certain clauses in these bilateral air services agreements were contrary to eu law, as they could discriminate against certain eu carriers (for example, if they are based in the territory of a certain member state but are owned and controlled by nationals of other member states). in order to ensure equal treatment of nationals of member states and, in general, compliance with the eu acquis, it was decided to amend/add to the existing provisions of the bilateral agreements. the commission has negotiated an agreement with macao replacing certain provisions in the existing 15 bilateral air transport agreements concluded between eu member states and macao. the main aspects of the agreement are: an eu designation clause allowing all eu carriers to exercise the right of establishment; a safety clause; a provision on the taxation of aviation fuel; an article prohibiting anti-competitive practices. i therefore voted in favour of the recommendation and thereby gave a favourable opinion on the conclusion of this agreement.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the recommendation on the draft council decision on the conclusion of the agreement on certain aspects of air transport between the european union and the government of the macao special administrative region of the people's republic of china. the agreement will upgrade and update the existing 15 bilateral air transport agreements between the member states and the macao sar. the new agreement extends the safety provisions to cases where the prescribed control of an air carrier is not exercised by the member state that designated the air carrier and introduces a clause prohibiting anti-competitive practices.
in writing. ‒ i supported the recommendation on the draft council decision on the conclusion of the agreement on certain aspects of air transport between the european union and the government of the macao special administrative region of the people's republic of china, as the commission has thus negotiated an agreement replacing certain provisions of the existing 15 bilateral air transport agreements between the eu member states and the macao special administrative region of the people's republic of china.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the conclusion of the agreement on specific aspects of air services between the european union and the government of the macao special administrative region of the people’s republic of china. the international aviation relations between member states and third countries have traditionally been governed by bilateral air services agreements, which were found discriminatory and in breach of the eu law by the european court of justice in 2002. the commission has, hence, negotiated the agreement replacing certain provisions in the existing 15 bilateral air services agreements concluded between eu member states and macao special administrative region of the people’s republic of china with the aim of prohibiting anti-competitive practices.
in writing. i have supported the agreement on certain aspects of air transport between the european union and the government of the macao special administrative region of the people's republic of china. it will replace and complement certain provisions in the existing 15 bilateral air transport agreements between eu member states and the macao special administrative region of the people's republic of china which were in conflict with the eu legal order and the principles of free establishment of companies, the principle of equal treatment in a member state and competition provisions.
in writing. ‒ the old vat directive, which was in force from 1 january 2011 to 31 december 2015, provided that the vat rate could not be lower than 15%. such legislation is necessary to establish and operate the internal market and to prevent distortions of competition, which means that cross-border distance sales and purchases below a certain threshold are still cleared at the place of origin rather than at the place of destination. therefore, the uniform application of the minimum rate of value added tax in all member states is a useful measure to ensure the proper functioning of the internal market. the commission is already preparing an action plan which will set out the guidelines and main features of the final vat arrangements for intra-eu trade. as decisions on the final version of the scheme are yet to be taken, i voted in favour of extending and maintaining the 15% general minimum vat rate for the period until 31 december 2017, allowing for a more in-depth discussion of the vat rates in the light of the future action plan of the european commission.
in writing. ‒ a single market, with a monetary union and economic union, needs to fully converge also at fiscal level. i support the fact that the union should further undergo a harmonisation process of its tax system. even though the proposal of the commission mainly addresses the extension of the current situation, setting a minimum of 15% for vat in all member states, the adequate response calls the commission to keep on working on a proposal that could definitely put all member states under the umbrella of a common tax system, not only at the level of vat.
in writing. ‒ with the single market in place on 1 january 1993, the commission presented proposals for the introduction of a definitive tax harmonisation regime. the council decision was followed by a transitional system, whereby directive 92/77/eec introduced a system of minimum rates for vat rates and provided that the overall rate of vat could not be lower than 15% in any member state. the commission notes that the commission has not provided any evidence that the measure was granted by the state. the general minimum rate of vat in all member states is a useful provision as it ensures the proper functioning of the internal market. in addition, it also gives member states room for manoeuvre for vat reforms, since only the lowest overall rate is fixed (currently the overall vat rate in all member states is above 15%). the commission intends to publish an action plan in 2016 for the introduction of a simple and efficient final value added tax system appropriate to the single market. decisions on the final scheme have not yet been taken, so i voted in favour of the proposal to extend the current scheme for three years, i.e. until 31 december 2017.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a council directive amending the directive on the common system of value added tax as regards the duration of the obligation to comply with the general minimum rate. as the commission published its proposal so late, the general minimum vat rate of 15% will apply retroactively. however, from the beginning of 2016 until the end of 2018, the overall vat rate should not be lower than 15%, thereby giving member states room to manoeuvre for vat reforms. i expect and hope that as soon as possible this year the european commission will publish an action plan defining a vat system which, with its simplicity, efficiency and fraud-proofness, is suited to the single market.
in writing. ‒ i supported the report on the proposal for a council directive amending directive 2006/112/ec on the common system of value added tax as regards the duration of the obligation to respect a general minimum rate. with a view to establishing the internal market as from 1 january 1993, the european commission has put forward proposals designed to establish a definitive system of tax harmonization. however, when it became clear that it would be impossible for the european commission to adopt the proposals before 1 january 1993, the council decided to adopt a transitional arrangement. as regards vat rates, it has adopted directive 92/77/eec. this directive introduced a system of minimum rates. provided that from 1 january 1993 to 31 december 1996 the general rate may not be lower than 15% in any member state. this provision has been extended five times and is set to expire on 31 december 2015. the purpose of this proposal is to extend the current situation for a period of two years, so that the minimum overall vat rate in the member states is 15%.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the common system of value added tax, with regard to the duration of the obligation to respect a minimum standard rate. the vat directive provides that from 1 january 2011 until 31 december 2015, the standard rate may not be less than 15%, specifying that the council shall adopt provisions for the harmonisation of legislation concerning turnover taxes. the harmonisation is necessary to ensure the establishment and functioning of the internal market and to avoid distortion of competition.
in writing. ‒ i supported the proposal to extend the current arrangement of the system of minimum overall rates for three years, which provides that the overall rate in no member state may be less than 15%. the extended timeframe provides the necessary legal certainty for stakeholders and is appropriate to prepare quality reforms for the introduction of the definitive tax harmonisation regime, which will allow for an efficient and smooth functioning of the internal market, which will prevent fraud.
in writing. ‒ europol has the power to conclude agreements with third countries listed in the council decision on mutual cooperation in preventing and combating organised crime, terrorism and other forms of serious crime. meps voted in favour of the motion for a resolution on the proposed approval of the strategic cooperation agreement between europol and brazil. since the proposal is based on strategic cooperation and excludes the exchange of personal data, the protection of personal data is not in question, since it concerns the exchange of operational, strategic, technical or classified information. as brazil's role in the fight against organised crime, trafficking in human beings, drug trafficking, credit card fraud and other cybercrime related activities is increasingly important, such cooperation is certainly beneficial as it will help to strengthen international cooperation in the field of crime prevention, detection and investigation.
