in writing. ‒ i supported the report on fisheries aspects of the international convention on marine biodiversity. marine activities are developing rapidly and their numbers are increasing rapidly, increasing the strain on and the exploitation of marine biodiversity. the latest report of the working group highlights the need for a comprehensive global system to better address this issue and recommends the development of an internationally legally binding instrument for the conservation and sustainable use of marine biodiversity.
in writing. ‒ in june 2015, a un resolution launched the development of a new legally binding international instrument for the conservation and sustainable use of marine biodiversity in areas beyond national jurisdiction. this instrument is being developed within the framework of the united nations convention on the law of the sea (unclos). the ocean plays a vital role in many of the earth's systems, and is also the site of a large number of human activities, such as fishing, trade and transport. more than half (64%) of the seas particularly the high seas and the deep seabed are areas beyond the national jurisdiction of states and governed by international law. however, less than 1% of these areas outside national jurisdiction are protected by the establishment of marine protected areas. it is important that fishing activities are also included in this new instrument, as fishing is one of the most important activities in the waters. the new instrument should complement and not replace the existing structure (networks of international regional bodies regulating fisheries in specific marine areas). this will also take account of fisheries in areas where there is currently no international organisation. i believe that marine biodiversity should be protected and preserved, while taking into account the fisheries aspect, and i therefore supported the report.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the fisheries aspects of the international agreement on marine biodiversity in areas beyond national jurisdiction, the united nations convention on the law of the sea. i support the report which stresses the importance of the conservation and sustainable use of oceans and seas and their resources, while calling on the eu and the international community to promote the conservation and sustainable use of marine biodiversity by introducing, among other measures, modern and sustainable concepts of marine ecosystem management, the principle of ocean governance and the management of the exploitation of marine resources.
in writing. ‒ i supported the report on the fisheries aspects of the international convention on marine biodiversity in outermost areas, the united nations convention on the law of the sea. agenda 21 is a document that addresses the importance of protecting the world's waters and was released at the united nations conference on environment and development in rio de janeiro in june 1992. it demonstrated that the international community recognises the need for an international approach to control pollution and increase the sustainability threat to marine biodiversity. in the years that followed, several declarations and documents on sustainable development were issued on this topic. in january 2015, the working group presented its latest report, highlighting the need for a comprehensive global system to better address this issue and recommending the development of an international legally binding instrument, in accordance with unclos, for the conservation and sustainable use of marine biological diversity in areas beyond national jurisdiction. on the basis of that recommendation, in july 2015 the un general assembly decided to establish a preparatory commission with the aim of preparing an internationally legally binding instrument to be adopted by the end of 2017.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on fisheries aspects within the international agreement on marine biodiversity. the report emphasizes the importance of the preservation and conservation of marine biological diversity as a global concern. it praises the work of the unga and ad hoc open-ended informal working group in making the issue of marine biological diversity an international, legally binding instrument beyond areas of national jurisdiction. it equally underlines the need for the inclusion of fishing activities in this new instrument.
in writing. ‒ the conservation and sustainable use of marine biodiversity is directly linked to long-term development and therefore has social, economic and environmental implications for all countries and regions. the seas and oceans have enormous potential for renewable energy and pharmaceuticals. the eu plays a key role in the global governance of the seas and oceans and has a major international influence in the field of fisheries. i therefore support efforts to conserve and manage the long-term development of marine biodiversity.
in writing. ‒ meps unanimously supported the european commission's proposal for a draft law on zootechnical and genealogical conditions for trade in and imports into the union of breeding animals and their germinal products. the law provides for greater transparency over the breeding of breeding animals and their embryos. it covers four major areas: the structured breeding sector, rules on the keeping of breeding books/registers, rules on intra-eu trade and imports from third countries, and rules on official controls and inspections by the commission. it is a very sophisticated bill that regulates areas where various issues and many uncertainties have arisen so far.
in writing. ‒ a well-functioning sector of breeding animals is crucial for the eu's animal husbandry, generating an estimated €1.89 billion in value added. the new regulation brings together all existing zootechnical parts of the legislation and provides for a harmonised structure for breeding animals, in particular for bovine, ovine, caprine, porcine and equine animals. the new rules cover internal trade in breeding animals and germinal products, their importation into the eu and rules for eu breeders exporting to third countries. herding plays a key role in the conservation of endangered species and the protection of biodiversity. it therefore lays down zootechnical and genealogical rules for the conservation and improvement of breeding animals of the breed and rules governing the conservation and improvement of indigenous or endangered breeds. 'breeding societies' and breeding programmes will have to fulfil certain conditions to obtain recognition from national authorities; the new rules will ensure a minimum level of their rights and obligations. in addition, rules on the registration and classification of breeding animals will be harmonised and performance testing on imported animals will be strengthened to ensure compliance with eu standards. i think it is important to have specific rules to take account of the specificities of each species and also to preserve and improve indigenous or endangered breeds. that's why i endorsed the report.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on zootechnical and genealogical conditions for trade in and imports into the union of breeding animals and their germinal products. i support the amendments proposed in the report, such as the proposal for a text, that the promotion of competitiveness must not lead to the extinction of breeds whose characteristics are adapted to a particular biophysical environment. the proposal also includes a provision that all actors in the zootechnical sector, in particular in the genetic improvement of breeds, should take into account animal health and welfare, together with the conditions for the transport of live animals.
in writing. ‒ i supported the report on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on zootechnical and genealogical conditions for trade in and imports into the union of breeding animals and their germinal products. the report updates and improves existing eu zootechnical legislation covering breeding, trade and import of breeding animals, thus reducing red tape and simplifying procedures, which in this case is good for both people and animals. a well-functioning breeding sector is crucial for animal breeding in the eu. its value added is estimated at almost eur 2 billion. the european commission's proposal addresses four main issues: (1) the structuring of the breeding sector; (2) rules on the management of stud books/registers, animal breeding and performance testing and genetic value assessment; (3) rules on intra-eu trade and imports from third countries; (4) rules on official controls and inspections by the commission.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on the zootechnical and genealogical conditions for trade in and imports into the union of breeding animals and their germinal products. the proposal seeks to modernise and strengthen in one regulation a number of individual segments of species-specific legislation relating to bovine, porcine, ovine, caprine and equine species including requirements for recognition and listing of breeding organisations, classification and certification of breeding animals and official controls and zootechnical checks.
in writing. ‒ i supported the report on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on zootechnical and genealogical conditions for trade in and imports into the union of breeding animals and their germinal products, as i find that it brings greater legal certainty for all stakeholders and ensures a harmonised approach to trade in and imports into the union of breeding animals and their germinal products and to the official controls to be carried out on breeding programmes and companies. since the objective of the proposal for a regulation cannot be sufficiently achieved by the member states at national level and can therefore, by reason of its impact, complexity and cross-border and international nature, be better achieved at union level,
in writing. ‒ my colleagues and i supported the report of the committee on civil liberties, justice and home affairs on the situation in the mediterranean and the need for an eu integrated approach to migration. we agreed that the eu must take an even more active approach to saving and preventing the loss of lives of migrants at sea, while ensuring the successful integration of migrants and a high level of internal security of the member states. we strongly condemned the criminal activities of criminal groups, such as smuggling, trafficking in human beings and labour exploitation, in connection with illegal migration.
in writing. ‒ i fully support the report and agree that only the eu can provide the right answers to the migration crisis, which is not a challenge only for the countries that face the mediterranean, but also those facing the south—eastern routes. uncoordinated action from member states is highly deterring and the eu is the best frame to endeavour a truly holistic approach.
in writing. ‒ according to frontex, 1.83 million people were caught trying to cross the eu's external borders illegally in 2015, compared to 282 500 in 2014. according to the international organization for migration and unicef, 20% of all migrants arriving by sea are children. in addition, according to the international organisation for migration, more than 3771 people lost their lives or went missing in the mediterranean sea in 2015, and an eu integrated approach to migration is urgently needed. the report stresses that the union's action in the field of migration must be based on the principle of solidarity, which covers asylum, immigration and border control policies. the report highlights areas where action is needed in line with the principle of solidarity: search and rescue, combating trafficking and smuggling, relocation and resettlement, humanitarian reception, revision of the dublin iii regulation, the list of safe countries of origin, a new european border and coast guard, management and security of external borders, cooperation with third countries, additional funding in the field of migration, legal labour migration and other aspects. this is why i supported the report on the situation in the mediterranean and the need for an eu integrated approach to migration.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the situation in the mediterranean and the need for an eu integrated approach to migration. according to frontex, 1.83 million people tried to enter the eu illegally last year, a number that is several times higher than in previous years and further indicates the scale of the refugee crisis. from the perspective of the eu budget, i welcome the increase in the asylum, migration and integration fund for last year and this year, but i regret the reduction in funding for legal migration and integration and better, fairer and more effective return strategies. there is also much room for improvement in the transparency of the expenditure of member states' and third countries' operations in the areas of migration, asylum and border management, which will also provide a clearer picture of the overall expenditure of the european union on migration. the scale of the crisis and the need for rapid action must not be an excuse for the indiscriminate use of the european union budget.
in writing. ‒ i supported the report on the situation in the mediterranean and the need for an eu integrated approach to migration. the report is the result of almost a year of work in the libe committee, 8 working papers, exchanges of views with experts and a large number of stakeholders, one libe operation in lampedusa related to security and rescue and one operation related to eu-tunisia cooperation in the field of migration, asylum and border management. the report aims to assess the various sensitive aspects of migration, asylum and border management, develop a set of recommendations and reports in the form of a strategic report, initiated by a comprehensive plan, with a view to a short, medium and long-term response.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the situation in the mediterranean and the need for a holistic eu approach to migration. the report analyses the current state of affairs touching upon the matters such as trafficking and exploitation of illegal immigrants, border management and visa policy and the overall complexity and tragedy of the unsafe refugee routes. the report underlines solidarity as the principle upon which union action on migration is based, where the main priority is to save lives, calling for strengthening of the search and rescue capacities.
in writing. ‒ i supported the report on the situation in the mediterranean. in addition to the above, i would add that the eu needs a holistic approach to tackling the migration crisis, which is also linked to the security situation. the main issues to be addressed are the protection of the external borders, the acceleration of the establishment of the european border and coast guard, the financial and human resources support to frontex and europol, and the need to avoid the blackmailing of turkey. i would like to stress that i am strongly opposed to so-called dialogue or two-way integration, which presupposes the mutual acceptance of values and behaviour patterns.
in writing. ‒ meps have overwhelmingly supported the 2012 and 2013 annual reports on subsidiarity and proportionality, as they are an integral part of policy-making to assess the appropriateness of european union action in pursuing policy objectives in relation to national and regional initiatives. i therefore regard as very positive the initiative to adopt a green card, which would allow national parliaments to propose the introduction, amendment or repeal of union legislation. but there are certainly still areas where national and regional policies have more experience and a better overview of the regulation of certain things than the brussels administration.
in writing. ‒ the principles of subsidiarity and proportionality are the fundamental guiding principles of the european union and the report welcomes the fact that in 2012 and 2013 the eu institutions and national parliaments carefully reviewed the consistency of these two principles. the fact that national parliaments are more closely involved and involved in the european legislative process is a positive development, as it raises awareness of the eu's fundamental principles, including subsidiarity and proportionality, in the interinstitutional framework. in addition, national parliaments are important for their territorial influence and proximity to citizens, and all parliaments need to be more involved in the european debate. since impact assessments are important decision-making tools in the legislative process, they should also take into account issues related to subsidiarity and proportionality. thorough impact assessments could increase citizens' confidence, as the principle of subsidiarity is a key element of the democratic process, and impact assessments could provide a precise assessment of compliance with this principle. the principles of subsidiarity and proportionality, as set out in article 5 of the treaty on european union, should guide the exercise of the union's competences. that is why i voted for the report.

in writing. ‒ the regulatory fitness and performance programme (refit) is a key element of the commission's new strategy for better lawmaking. the refit programme is intended to consolidate better law-making procedures, simplify eu law and reduce administrative and regulatory burdens. the report covers a range of areas such as better regulation, transparency and consultation of stakeholders, impact assessments and the implementation of eu law in the member states. simplification of legislation (refit) may reduce the level of ambition in legislation on certain issues, namely human welfare and environmental protection, because there is no proper distinction between reducing administrative burdens and reducing regulatory burdens. reducing regulatory burdens may call into question the very existence of laws and the protection afforded by them. the report does not limit its emphasis to impact assessment and more specifically to the assessment of competitiveness, as this remains an important part of the impact assessment process. in addition, the report does not make a clear distinction between reducing administrative burdens and regulatory burdens, which is why i voted against the report on the regulatory fitness and performance programme (refit).

in writing. ‒ the report aims to express parliament's opinion on the level and type of regulation needed to improve the functioning of the single market. i do not agree that improving the functioning of the single market means more power and more subsidiarity on the part of the member states. the fact is that the member states have chosen to lose part of their sovereignty when they join the eu. therefore, in my view, the essence of a better single market is not deregulation but closer and better cooperation between member states. i believe that an efficient and well-functioning internal market can make a positive contribution to competitiveness and job creation in the eu. as regards the sovereignty of the member states, it is necessary to maintain it at a certain level and to allow the member states to decide for themselves on certain important matters. the principle of proportionality should be respected in the case of subsidiarity. this is of course important to the member states, but if they want the single market to work as planned and desired, then the member states must renounce it to a certain extent. it is also necessary to realise that improving the regulation of the single market does not mean abolishing all regulations, but the necessary regulatory environment that will not be too burdensome for businesses, but at the same time not too lax. that is why i voted against the report.

the terrorist attacks in brussels have shocked us once again. it's a despicable act, a worthless man. i offer my sincere condolences to all the victims, the injured and my sympathies to those affected. and not just with those in belgium, but with everyone in turkey, pakistan, iraq and elsewhere. terrorists, racists, and extremists spread their hatred through violence, and community relations are increasingly strained. the only way for europeans to find real solutions is to stand together against terrorism and hatred. regardless of religion, race, color, or position. more security will not only come from new and strengthened security measures, borders, walls, but also from tackling social issues at home and in third countries, fighting poverty, resolving conflicts - and from people fleeing terrorism. we have long pointed out that european countries have great difficulty in exchanging intelligence and criminal intelligence. greater security cooperation is therefore essential, both within europe and with third countries. but we must also ask ourselves the uncomfortable question: why are young europeans going to syria, iraq, why are they reaching for deadly weapons, why are they more comfortable with an ideology that advocates mass beheadings, slavery, murder? there is a very clear link between radicalisation and the hopelessness of young people, and that is something we have to fight against. and we need a strong, new push to promote interfaith dialogue around the world. question asked by raising the blue card. madam president, given your attitude to pnr, would the adoption of this important act by the european parliament be a step towards a safer europe in the future?
answer the question posed by raising the blue card. in any case, the pnr we have today and which we are voting on tomorrow is an important step towards security, greater security in europe, but we must be very clear about all these measures in terms of proportionality, privacy and efficiency. now that we have a data protection package, i think that, combined, these measures are appropriate and we are on the right track to delivering what all citizens expect from us.
the panama papers affair is certainly getting a lot of attention these days, but, let's be honest, it's not a new thing. we've known about it for a long time. although we have already taken a great deal of action at european level and concluded many agreements with third countries, this is clearly still not enough. billions of euros are still slipping through the budget. this is money that we could spend on our schools, on our education, on our children, on employment, on new jobs. of course, tax evasion and the concealment of ill-gotten wealth are unacceptable. but have we even tried to look at the other side of this story? why are tax havens so friendly and attractive? perhaps we should ask ourselves how unfriendly our domestic tax systems are. and we're gonna have to do something about that, too.
i think the commission's actions are going in the right direction. we can say that we are finally moving from words to actions. we need more transparency and more data sharing. in this way we will also achieve a better tax environment for all, better tax systems. it is unacceptable that large multinationals should enrich themselves at the expense of small and medium-sized enterprises. everyone must pay taxes proportionate to their potential. but we have to be consistent. we must not allow the measures to be reversed in such a way that europe becomes less competitive. the big multinationals also create a lot of jobs. we must therefore also require member states not only to be transparent but to adapt their tax systems to be simple and competitive.
in writing. the european commission made a statement to the european parliament at its april plenary session on the planned measures in the field of public tax transparency. the panama papers case has once again confirmed that the desired globalization is written on the skin of financial capital, which has a virtual owner without responsibility. the case, which was uncovered by the international consortium of investigative journalists with the help of 11.5 million documents, exposes the unseen scale of tax fraud and money laundering. this is a clear indication that tax havens are a widely offered and created opportunity, which has been well exploited over the last half-century and will continue to be so in the future, provided that the competent institutions of the states and the international community do not lose their edge. the tax policies of the various countries are different, but they all have in common the desire to bring as many resources as possible into the public treasury, with tax revenues representing practically the bulk of the inflows. how successful they are in doing so and how they deal with the grey economy, tax evasion and fraud is another matter. we urgently need a thorough tax reform that will tackle the root causes of the problem decisively. the key to this is greater tax transparency of companies' activities and public reporting by country, where where companies operate and pay taxes is of particular importance.

answer the question posed by raising the blue card. mr president, i agree with all those who insist today that european solidarity is not working. and i agree with all those who insist today that all the countries of the european union must take responsibility when it comes to burden-sharing. we know that the relocation and resettlement program is not working at the moment, that a number of countries in the european union are not taking responsibility at the moment. and until that happens, everything else is superfluous, all agreements are unnecessary and the european union is actually crashing into a very, very critical situation. i want everyone here, including you, to take moral responsibility.
question asked by raising the blue card. a respected colleague. i appreciate some of your colleagues in your group, who are analytical in their thinking, and i'd like to ask you to follow up on what you said in your last sentence. we are talking today about the agreement with turkey about many things. from the fact that it heralds a change in policy to the enlargement of europe and a variety of other issues. i would like to ask you, but don't you think that in this debate we should also address the causes of the crisis, the causes of this humanitarian catastrophe. we are not a humanitarian organization, we are politicians, we should honestly face who and why caused the disaster in the middle east.
on 17 december last year, this parliament adopted a resolution on the annual report on human rights and democracy and the european union's policy in this field. in chapter 78 of the resolution, we demanded respect for the fundamental rights of the sahrawi people and the release of political prisoners from moroccan prisons. we have been following with concern the hunger strike of young people who have been wrongfully sentenced to long prison terms by the moroccan military court in connection with the events in lajon. i call on the president of this parliament and on the commission to take account of this parliament's demands for the release of political prisoners and for respect for human rights in their contacts with the moroccan authorities.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a decision of the european parliament and of the council on the mobilisation of the european globalisation adjustment fund volvo trucks. the financial contribution from the egf of eur 1 793 710, representing 60% of the total cost, will be sufficient for the measures involving 500 of the 647 redundant workers. this is an area where most of the vacancies are tied to highly qualified workers and the dismissed workers have only a secondary education. we need measures for redundant workers to enable them to acquire specialised skills and thus compete more easily for jobs.
in writing. ‒ i supported the report on the proposal for a decision of the european parliament and of the council on the mobilisation of the european globalisation adjustment fund (application egf/2015/009 se/volvo trucks, sweden). the european globalisation adjustment fund was established to provide additional assistance to workers affected by the consequences of major structural changes in world trade flows. the swedish authorities have provided all necessary assurances as regards the following: the access to and implementation of the proposed measures will respect the principles of equal treatment and non-discrimination, the requirements of national and eu legislation on collective redundancies have been respected, volvo trucks has continued its activities after the redundancies, has fulfilled its legal obligations in relation to redundant workers and has provided adequate care for them, the proposed measures will not receive financial support from other union funds or financial instruments and double funding will be avoided, the proposed measures will complement measures financed by the structural funds, the financial contribution from the egf will be in line with the union's procedural and substantive rules on state aid. sweden has informed the commission that the egf measures will be co-financed by the swedish government through the budget of the swedish public employment service (arbetsförmedlingen).
in writing. ‒ i supported the report on the use of the european globalisation adjustment fund, which estimates that sweden is eligible for a financial contribution of eur 1 793 710 under the conditions laid down in the egf regulation. union financial assistance shall be intended for redundant workers with a lower level of education in order to facilitate their reintegration into the labour market and employment.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a decision of the european parliament and of the council on the mobilisation of the european globalisation adjustment fund technical assistance at the initiative of the commission. i support the commission's proposal to use the amount of eur 380,000 to cover the commission's technical assistance. these are monitoring and data collection, information, knowledge base building, administrative and technical support and evaluation. i also support the report which welcomes the inclusion of the report in the electronic data exchange system as this will reduce the administrative burden on member states and simplify the use of the reports for evaluation purposes.
in writing. ‒ i supported the report on the proposal for a decision of the european parliament and of the council on the mobilisation of the european globalisation adjustment fund (application egf/2016/000 ta 2016 technical assistance at the initiative of the commission). the european globalisation adjustment fund was established to provide additional assistance to workers affected by the consequences of major structural changes in world trade flows. on 22 february 2016, the commission adopted a new proposal for a decision on the mobilisation of the egf. it concerns an amount of eur 380.000 from the commission's technical assistance fund. the objective of the technical assistance is to finance monitoring, information, the establishment of a knowledge base interface and advice to member states on the use, follow-up and evaluation of the egf. in accordance with article 11 (1) of the egf regulation, 0,5% of the maximum annual amount of the fund (i.e. eur 828,060 in 2016) may be made available for technical assistance at the initiative of the commission each year.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the legislative resolution providing that, within the general budget of the european union for the financial year 2016, the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf) is to be mobilised to provide the sum of eur 380,000 in commitment and payment appropriations for technical assistance to finance monitoring, information, the establishment of a knowledge base interface and the provision of advice to member states on the use, follow-up and evaluation of the egf.
in writing. ‒ last week, in the epp group's plenary session, meps supported a report on the proposal to amend the european union budget to provide emergency aid in the union. at a time when the european union is facing an emergency situation with massive influxes of refugees and migrants, many people are in urgent need of humanitarian assistance. as the capacities of most member states to respond to this emergency situation have already been largely exhausted, i believe that this measure was the right decision.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the council position report on the draft amending budget of the european union no 1/2016 for the financial year 2016 new instrument for providing emergency assistance in the union. the european union is facing a massive influx of refugees and migrants, which has created an emergency and a humanitarian crisis. the european union has grown up on the basis of solidarity and must respond to the needs of the people on its territory. i support a new instrument to provide emergency assistance in the union of eur 300 million this year and eur 200 million over the next two years. i also support the creation of a more durable legal and budgetary framework for the use of humanitarian aid in the union when circumstances require it.
in writing. ‒ report on the council position on the draft amending budget no 1/2016 of the european union for the financial year 2016 i supported the new instrument for providing emergency assistance in the union because the mass influx of refugees and migrants into europe has created an emergency situation in which a large number of people are in need of urgent humanitarian assistance that exceeds the organisational capacity of one or more member states. the capacities of most member states to respond to this emergency situation have already been exhausted and there has been no adequate instrument at union level to respond to the humanitarian needs of the people affected by the disasters. the commission estimates that eur 300 million will be needed for this new instrument in 2016 for the time being (eur 200 million in 2017 and 2018) but that this amount may increase further if immigration and refugee flows do not decrease.
in writing. ‒ i supported the draft amending budget allocating emergency financial assistance to deal with the emergency situation caused by the refugee, humanitarian and security crisis in the union.

in writing. ‒ i supported the european parliament's resolution, as amended, on the draft commission implementing regulation renewing the approval of the active substance glyphosate. as a fruit grower myself, i've been using glyphosate for 25 years as one of the most widely used herbicides in fruit and wine production. it is in the best interests of those of us who use these products to get to the truth about its side effects. in the report, we therefore proactively halved the period of approval from the proposed 15 years to 7 years. at the same time, we suggested that the commission should thoroughly investigate the health effects and, if certain studies suggesting carcinogenicity were found to have a scientific basis, take immediate action and withdraw the preparation from the market. given that the herbicide has been used for the last 40 years, the establishment of scientific facts on the consequences of its use should not be a problem. as there is currently no real substitute on the market for the herbicide, an immediate ban on its use would seriously harm european agriculture, while not affecting countries outside the eu, such as the us, which is by far the largest consumer of glyphosate, especially in the production of genetically modified organisms. i trust the maturity of the european commission to look into the matter and to verify all the facts and allegations circulating today and to take appropriate action if necessary.
in writing. ‒ i did not support the resolution proposing to renew the authorisation of glyphosate for another 7 years, because i put health first. since i got over my cancer, my motto has been "health first". the international agency for research on cancer has found a strong link between glyphosate and cancer, and there are other studies linking it to harmful effects on the human hormonal and nervous systems, and that's enough for me. i also supported amendments that contained more restrictions on the ways and places of use, greater controls on the sale of products and better monitoring of health and environmental impacts, and more education for users, and these were voted on. i expect the european commission to take them into account when preparing the amended proposal for the re-approval of glyphosate.
in writing. ‒ there is public debate on the conflicting scientific aspects of different assessments of glyphosate carcinogenicity and the endocrine disrupting effect of glyphosate. the international agency for research on cancer (iarc) has classified glyphosate as a substance that is "probably carcinogenic to humans". the most widely used herbicide in the world today is the systemic herbicide glyphosate. its use has increased dramatically (by a factor of 260) over the past 40 years. globally, 76% of glyphosate is used in agriculture, and in addition, in forestry, urban and horticultural applications. the european commission has proposed to renew the approval of glyphosate for a further 15 years. the motion for a resolution adopted by the envi committee calls on the commission to reconsider its proposal. glyphosate could seriously harm our health and could also endanger animals and plants, so it is important to avoid its unwarranted use in private and its use in or near public parks, playgrounds and gardens. in the case of already existing alternatives for weed suppression, the use of glyphosate should be strictly prohibited. the motion for a resolution did not express a complete rejection of the use of glyphosate and i therefore abstained.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the resolution on the draft commission implementing regulation renewing the approval of the active substance glyphosate in accordance with the regulation of the european parliament and of the council concerning the placing of plant protection products on the market and amending the annex to the implementing regulation. the commission should withdraw the draft implementing regulation and submit a new draft, should not renew the approval of glyphosate and should set a clear deadline by which it will draw up a list of additives not approved for inclusion in plant protection products. this is necessary because of serious concerns that the herbicide glyphosate, which is widely used in agriculture, is carcinogenic and causes endocrine disruption.
in writing. ‒ objection under rule 106 of the rules of procedure: i supported the renewal of the approval of the active substance glyphosate, as did the large majority of the european parliament, which voted today on the controversial plant protection compromise on glyphosate. meps rejected the european commission's original proposal, which called for renewal at intervals of another 15 years without any essential conditions. meps also want to ban or at least restrict the use of glyphosate in the private sector and in public use, as well as all additives in formulations containing poe-tallowamine, which the commission intends to ban and withdraw from the market.
in writing. ‒ i voted against the objection pursuant to rule 106 concerning the renewal of the approval of the active substance glyphosate. there has been a quite controversial debate surrounding this objection. the mandatory renewal assessment on glyphosate was carried out by germany (bundesinstitut für risikobewertung ‘bfr’), which, on the basis of around 900 scientific publications, came to the conclusion that the available data does not give evidence for harmful effects in humans, animals or the environment. efsa peer-reviewed this assessment with all other member states and largely subscribed to their conclusions. however, the international agency for research on cancer (iarc) published their own assessment in an iarc monograph in july 2015. their evaluation, on the other hand, assesses the risk of glyphosate as being probably carcinogenic for humans. in conclusion, until there is no unanimous assessment on the harmfulness of glyphosate to humans, i believe that it is wise to stick to the findings of the german bfr, based on a vast amount of scientific evidence. the related legal provisions do mention that if new reliable evidence is found on the possible carcinogenicity of glyphosate, this assessment can be reverted and that is why in the meantime i decided to vote against the objection.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the resolution on the draft commission implementing regulation renewing the approval of the active substance glyphosate for 7 years instead of 15 years as proposed by the commission. the epp/ed also advocated many other safeguards to limit the possible harmful effects of this herbicide. i have advocated greater control of the health effects of glyphosate, more sustainable use, a restriction to professional use only, greater control of the sale of glyphosate in the member states and more education for users. the abrupt discontinuation of glyphosate would have a serious impact on european fruit and wine production, given the already heavy burden on european agriculture caused by the dairy and pig crisis.
in writing. ‒ we voted overwhelmingly in favour of the european parliament's motion for a resolution on the eu in a changing global environment, in a more connected, conflicted and complex world. it is in the interest of all members of parliament to ensure the safety of our citizens, to preserve our values and our social model. in the current situation facing the whole of europe, we must strengthen the strategic autonomy of the european union and its links with nato. at the same time, we must not forget foreign policy, where we must focus on working with global partners on common interests for our future.
in writing. ‒ it was time for the european parliament to give a strong message on how to further develop the eu project. the world needs an eu capable of delivering on global challenges and counterbalance the multipolar world. most importantly being a political project able to provide not only peace but also security to its citizens, create stable relations with its neighbours and engage citizens to actively participate in caring for the values of the eu.
in writing. ‒ europe is exposed to a number of complex and interrelated challenges and threats at a global level. the report addresses the european union's global strategy, which must be based on identifying and prioritising threats and challenges, defining responses to them and identifying the necessary means. this is a very general idea of a common defence policy, which would provide for some contributions from the eu budget and some budgetary criteria for defence, as in nato. the report does not contain many concrete hints as to specific policy areas and as to ways of linking the different foreign policy areas. the question of the integrated approach and its implementation remains unanswered. individual countries and regions are only partially mentioned. the following issues should be explored in depth: the international order (e.g. multilateral fora, relations with the un, au, asean, wto, etc.) and the role of the eu in this regard, the need to involve partners, the promotion of cooperation and the dissemination of universal norms and values. other important aspects to be taken into account are the position of human rights in the new global strategy, the importance of the criminal justice approach in the fight against terrorism and the need to develop a regional security structure similar to the csce. that is why i voted against the report.
in writing. ‒ i voted for the report on the eu in a changing global environment a more connected, conflicted and complex world. the european union today faces a number of interrelated challenges and threats. if we are to take all these challenges seriously, we need a united, decisive and effective response at european union level. i support the call for the european union to strengthen coherent and structured cooperation in defence research, industrial base and cyber defence through pooling and sharing and other cooperation projects in order to spend national defence budgets more efficiently.
in writing. ‒ report on the eu in a changing global environment i supported a more connected, conflicted and complex world, as many of the current and future challenges and threats facing the eu are complex and interconnected, emanating from state and non-state actors and originating both within and beyond our common borders. connecting the local, regional and global levels is necessary because we need strong political will and leadership for decisive joint action by the eu and its member states to respond proactively, collectively and effectively to these challenges, to safeguard the eu's values and social model and to ensure that the eu is an effective and more strategic actor and contributes to global security.
in writing. ‒ the eu's foreign and security policy is faced with a number of challenges posed by the refugee, humanitarian and security crises. i supported the report on the eu in a changing global environment a more connected, conflicted and complex world, because i agree with the need to protect european society and values, stabilise the union's wider neighbourhood and strengthen cooperation with citizens, civil society, industry and local and regional authorities in building a stronger framework for europe's security.
in writing. ‒ in supporting the motion for a resolution on the eu strategy for central asia, meps underlined the importance of the region to the eu. it is a region with great economic potential, energy richness, geostrategic and security features, with which good relations must be built. in order to achieve long-term sustainable results, we have agreed to re-establish the post of eu special representative for the strengthening of external relations in the region. it is in the eu's interest to strengthen democracy, human rights, the abolition of child and forced labour, gender equality, etc. all of this will require greater focus by the countries in the region.
in writing. ‒ i support the fact that we pay special attention to this part of the world. i would like to highlight that i truly welcome the re-establishment of the post of eu special representative for central asia, in order to ensure consistency of the external actions of the union in the region, which is necessary to avoid unnecessary pains of inconsistency.
in writing. ‒ the eu strategy for a new partnership with central asia (eu strategy for central asia) was adopted in 2007 in response to the growing importance of the region for eu security, stability, governance and energy diversity. the strategy sets the framework for the eu's relations with five countries: kazakhstan, kyrgyzstan, tajikistan, turkmenistan and uzbekistan. this is the third report by the european parliament on eu-central asia relations. the importance of this part of the world to the eu has increased in recent years, mainly because of the energy resources it contains. human rights and democracy play an important role in determining the eu's approach to these former soviet republics. the eu has strengthened and improved the structure of its relations with the five countries, as meetings of senior officials from europe and central asia have become frequent. the eu has also established regular bilateral dialogues on human rights and national water resources. however, the eu does not yet have sufficient visibility in central asia and should take steps to strengthen its efforts, focusing on those objectives and actions that address the following pressing challenges: human rights and the rule of law, water and energy, and regional security. security, development and environmental protection require close cooperation between the eu and each country, and cooperation between countries themselves. that is why i voted for the report.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the implementation and review of the eu strategy for central asia. it is in the interest of the european union to strengthen good relations with all the countries of central asia on the basis of common values. we need more progress and better regional cooperation and integration between central asian countries through the exchange of experience and the transfer of standards by the european union. i support the report which stresses that the allocation of eu funds should be clearly based on initiatives and performance, taking into account achievements in different performance measures designed for all countries, and should also be dependent on measurable progress.
in writing. ‒ report on the eu in a changing global environment i supported a more connected, conflict-ridden and complex world, as respect for democracy, the rule of law and human rights is a basic condition for closer cooperation between the eu and the five central asian countries in areas of mutual interest, in the literal sense of the word 'partnership', as stated in the partnership and cooperation agreements. the overall situation of democracy and human rights in the region remains generally poor and worrying. the foreign affairs council in june 2015 re-committed to the cause of women's rights and concluded that increasing the influence of women in the region is essential to ensure long-term stability and good governance.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on implementation and review of the eu-central asia strategy. the report suggests that european fund expenditures should be performance-based and dependent on the measurable progress in human rights, democratisation and corruption. it equally calls for a country-to-country approach and no compromise on human rights, the rule of law or corruption. the report also expresses concern regarding media freedom, the suppression of civil society and widespread human rights abuses including torture in prison in the region.
in writing. ‒ the eu has a strong strategic, political and economic interest in strengthening bilateral and multilateral relations with all central asian countries on the basis of shared values. believing that integration is important, particularly in the face of security threats and challenges, but also in the field of political, diplomatic and trade relations, i supported the report on the implementation and review of the eu strategy for central asia.
in writing. ‒ i did not support the resolution on the zika virus outbreak because it proposes measures that are outside its scope and directly violate the principle of subsidiarity for topics related to the family, health and education. it is unacceptable that a resolution that focuses on research to find out about the outbreak, carriers, care needs and vaccine development, preventive measures and public health measures in light of the identified health system deficiencies, is being used to introduce access to abortion in affected countries, in clear contradiction to the judgment of the eu court of justice in brüstle v greenpeace, which found that 'life begins after conception' and to the general declaration of human rights, article 3, which states that 'everyone has the right to life, liberty and security of person', including unborn children. this is also recognized by the international covenant on civil and political rights and other international human rights instruments.
in writing. - the zika virus was discovered in 1947 in rhesus monkeys in the zika forest in uganda. in 2007, the virus was first recorded outside known endemic boundaries (epidemic on the island of yap in the federated states of micronesia). in 2015, a major outbreak of the virus in brazil (especially in the northeast) was associated with an unusual number of babies born with microencephaly. now the zika virus, transmitted by mosquito bites, is becoming more widespread. 'introduced' cases of zika virus infection have also occurred in various european countries. a case of microencephaly was reported in a pregnant woman from slovenia who contracted a virus with symptoms similar to zika virus during a stay in brazil. the european commission has therefore allocated eur 10 million for research into the virus. the report states that the results of these studies should be free of intellectual property rights and that patients should be able to afford the products thus developed. the potential link between the larvicide pyriproxyfen and microencephalopathy needs further investigation. in addition, there is a need to ensure reproductive health services and rights for women and girls and to address social issues faced by families with children born with microencephaly. that is why i supported the motion for a resolution.
in writing. ‒ i voted against the resolution on the oral question on the zika outbreak. the resolution has some good initiatives, such as the need to establish a communication plan at the most appropriate levels to raise public awareness and encourage appropriate action to prevent mosquito bites. but there are also some points in the resolution that i cannot support. these are mainly points relating to the prevention and termination of pregnancy, sexual and reproductive health and contraception, which in my view do not fall within the resolution on the zika outbreak.
in writing. ‒ i supported the motions for resolutions on the zika outbreak. on 1 february 2016, the world health organisation declared a public health emergency of global concern due to the outbreak of the zika virus. zika virus is an increasingly common mosquito-borne virus first discovered in 1947 in rhesus monkeys in the zika forest in uganda as part of the yellow fever control network. outbreaks of the zika virus have been sporadically recorded in two european regions, martinique and french guiana, and in africa, the americas, asia and the pacific, and cases of infection have also been detected in europe, in particular in the overseas territories of guadeloupe and saint-martin. according to the european centre for disease prevention and control (ecdc), the majority of infections are still asymptomatic (approximately 80%).
in writing. ‒ i supported the report on the zika virus outbreak, which calls, inter alia, on the commission to draw up an action plan to prevent the spread of the virus in europe and to provide assistance to member states and third countries in combating this epidemic in the regions where the outbreak is most severe.

in writing. ‒ the eu pnr (passenger name record) directive, as agreed in the trilogues, would oblige airlines to hand over data on their passengers to eu member states to help law enforcement in the fight against terrorism and serious crime. this would require the systematic collection, use and storage of pnr data on air passengers, including for intra-eu flights. the pnr data would thus be stored in a disguised form for five years. this directive is in the legislative process following the recent terrorist attacks and has dangerous provisions regarding the mass surveillance of all passengers in the eu. i agree that targeted control measures should be introduced in the context of an efficient exchange of information between member states, but i think that this can be achieved by allocating the funds proposed for this directive to more targeted and effective measures for the activities of local police, joint investigation teams or greater coordination of europol. this directive will address profiling at airports which could lead to the stigmatisation of citizens on the basis of their name, origin or religion. i am against the current text of the directive because it is not necessary and the proposed system is not proportionate, but i also have concerns about data retention and the inclusion of intra-eu flights in the scope of the directive. that is why i voted against the text.

in writing. ‒ trade secrets are information of value to the company (undisclosed know-how and business information) which is treated as confidential and therefore confers a competitive advantage on the company. until now, trade secrets have been protected in various eu member states by a combination of civil law, competition law and/or labour law. the commission published a proposal for a directive in november 2013 to harmonise the protection of trade secrets at eu level in order to promote cross-border trade within the internal market. the directive would thus, for the first time, introduce a uniform and harmonised legislation on the protection of trade secrets at eu level. however, only a minimum level of harmonisation is envisaged and differences between member states could indeed arise. furthermore, the definition of a trade secret is very broad. the exceptions for freedom of expression and information, freedom of the press/media and protection of whistleblowing activities are not sufficient. trade secrets would become the rule without a satisfactory guarantee to protect citizens who disclose information in the public interest. this directive provides companies with an excessive right to secrecy, and could also lead to abuses by non-profit-making companies across europe at the expense of the public's right to information. the directive also contains a lack of balance between fundamental freedoms, which is why i voted against the adoption of the directive.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a directive of the european parliament and of the council on the protection of undisclosed know-how and business information (trade secrets) against their unlawful acquisition, use and disclosure. trade secrets constitute an important part of the intellectual capital of business entities in the economy and are often used to gain competitive advantage and to carry out research and development or innovation. this proposal will improve the competitiveness of the european economy through innovation and thus strengthen the eu's leading role in the global industrial market.
in writing. ‒ if i were to vote on the report on the proposal for a directive of the european parliament and of the council on the protection of undisclosed know-how and business information (trade secrets) against their unlawful acquisition, use and disclosure, i would support it. businesses and non-commercial research institutions invest in the acquisition, development and practical application of expertise and information, which are the currency of the knowledge-based economy and provide a competitive advantage. these investments in the creation and use of intellectual capital are crucial for their competitiveness and innovation performance in the market and therefore for the return on investment, which is the main motivation for business r&d. it is appropriate to lay down rules at union level for the approximation of national legislative systems in order to ensure a sufficient and consistent level of compensation throughout the single market in cases of unlawful acquisition, use or disclosure of a trade secret. to that end, it is necessary to establish a uniform definition of a trade secret without restricting the content to be protected against unlawful appropriation. such a definition should be designed to cover business information, technological information and expertise where there is a legitimate interest in their confidentiality and a legitimate expectation that such confidentiality is maintained.
in writing. ‒ innovative companies are increasingly exposed to unfair practices aimed at the unlawful acquisition of trade secrets through theft, unauthorised copying, economic espionage or breach of confidentiality requirements originating in or outside the union. i therefore supported the report on the proposal for a directive of the european parliament and of the council on the protection of undisclosed know-how and business information, as i believe that adequate protection of the confidentiality of business secrets should be ensured. trade secrets play an important role in generating profits and maintaining business competitiveness.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the adoption of a european parliament regulation on the european union agency for railways (era). the european railway agency will have the power to issue safety certificates to railway undertakings operating in more than one member state. the aim will not be primarily to speed up administrative procedures and reduce administrative costs, but to maintain the current high level of security and to prevent covert discrimination.
in writing. ‒ i did not support the recommendations for a second reading on the council's position at first reading with a view to adopting a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on the european union agency for railways and repealing regulation (ec) no 881/2004, as i consider that it is not constructively prepared. the three previous 'railway packages' have already brought about significant changes to make european railways more competitive and interoperable, while maintaining a high level of safety. the sector still faces barriers to competition, discrimination and a lack of a liberalised, dynamic and business-friendly environment. there are too many different national rules with procedures and standards that are not transparent enough.
in writing. ‒ i supported the recommendation for second reading on the council's position at first reading with a view to adopting a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on the european union agency for railways and repealing regulation (ec) no 881/2004. the commission is proposing a fourth railway package to improve the functioning and competitiveness of the railway sector and to improve the quality and efficiency of rail services. the objective of this pillar is to improve the technical compatibility of infrastructure, rolling stock, signalling and other parts of the railway system, as well as to simplify the authorisation procedures for rolling stock used on the european rail network.
in writing. ‒ instead of going through 26 different national approval procedures, locomotives and wagons can now be approved through the european railway agency or through the member states (for the area of use indicated in the application). this is an important step forward as it reduces the cost and time of transferring trains to the track, especially compared to other modes of transport. a european vehicle register will be created and will link existing national registers. this will increase transparency for the rail sector. that is why i voted for the report and supported it.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the recommendation on the council position at first reading with a view to adopting a directive of the european parliament and of the council on the interoperability of the rail system within the european union. the regulation on the european railway agency is the technical part of the fourth railway package, which aims to amend the existing legislation and the remaining administrative and technical obstacles. the 2004 revision of the directive focuses on removing existing administrative and technical barriers. the greatest benefits of improved interoperability of the rail system in the european union will be gained by citizens.
in writing. ‒ i supported the recommendation for second reading on the council's position at first reading with a view to adopting a directive of the european parliament and of the council on the interoperability of the rail system within the european union (recast). there are two files. i agree with the coordinator, who has done a very important job, which i took into account in the vote. this is a very sensitive issue, as intermobility is of key importance for the eu as a whole. the fourth railway package contains six proposals, three technical and three political. the reporters had a lot of work to do, but despite their differences, they were able to reach a consensus. the importance of the package is crucial to the european economy, not just in transport.
in writing. ‒ i supported the recommendation for second reading on the council's position at first reading with a view to adopting a directive of the european parliament and of the council on the interoperability of the rail system within the european union (recast). over the last decade, major changes have gradually taken place in the railway market with the introduction of three railway legislative packages aimed at opening up national markets and providing more competitive and interoperable railways at eu level. europe will move closer to the creation of a single european railway area with the system introduced by the new directive. it will reduce administrative costs and speed up procedures, while maintaining the current high level of security.
in writing. ‒ currently, more than 11,000 national regulations hinder the provision of crossborder services. in order to establish a single market for rail transport services, it is necessary to establish a common regulatory framework to ensure safety in rail transport. in the future, there will be harmonisation and national rules will be harmonised, while the different rules will be very limited. instead of having to go through 26 different national safety certification procedures, the company will be able to apply for a safety certificate valid in several member states at the same time (single european safety certificate). the european railway agency will develop an event reporting tool to enable the sharing of information on potential safety risks between companies and across borders. i therefore supported the report and voted for its adoption in plenary.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the recommendation for second reading on the council's position at first reading with a view to adopting a directive of the european parliament and of the council on railway safety, in particular to establish a framework for harmonising the content of safety rules. this is necessary to improve the safety culture and incident reporting in railway traffic and by infrastructure managers. this will motivate staff to report incidents under confidential conditions, thereby increasing the safety, interoperability and reliability of the european rail network.
in writing. ‒ i supported the recommendation for second reading on the council's position at first reading with a view to adopting a directive of the european parliament and of the council on railway safety (recast). the eu railway safety directive is a major step forward towards establishing a common regulatory framework for railway safety. the directive established a framework for harmonising the content of safety rules, the award of safety certificates to railway undertakings, the tasks and roles of safety authorities and accident investigation in order to discourage member states from further developing safety rules and standards for their national lines on the basis of national technical and operational concepts. the development and implementation of the eu single safety certificate has always been a long-term objective.
in writing. ‒ i supported the recommendation for second reading on the council's position at first reading with a view to adopting a directive of the european parliament and of the council on railway safety (recast). i believe that in order to continue the efforts to establish a single market for rail transport services, a common regulatory framework for railway safety should be established.
in writing. ‒ i also supported the european parliament resolution on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on indices used as benchmarks in financial instruments and financial contracts. the proposed regulation establishes a common framework to ensure the accuracy and integrity of indices used as benchmarks for financial instruments and financial contracts in the union. its main objectives are to improve governance and ensure that custodians avoid conflicts of interest, to improve the quality of input data and methodologies used by comparative custodians. the proposed regulation applies to all published criteria used to list financial instruments traded or admitted to trading on a regulated venue or financial contracts. the proposal exempts from its scope central banks that are members of the european system of central banks.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on indices used as benchmarks in financial instruments and financial contracts. we need accurate and comprehensive benchmarks to avoid value manipulation that causes huge losses for consumers and investors and further reduces citizens' already low level of confidence in the banking sector. the financial sector needs, inter alia, accurate and comprehensive benchmarks to best assess the performance of an investment fund for the purposes of determining profitability, determining the allocation of assets in the portfolio or calculating performance payments.
in writing. ‒ i supported the report on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on indices used as benchmarks in financial instruments and financial contracts. errors or doubts about the accuracy and integrity of the indices used as benchmarks can undermine market confidence, cause losses for consumers and investors and distort the real economy. it is therefore necessary to ensure the accuracy, robustness and integrity of the benchmarks and the procedures for their establishment.
in writing. ‒ i supported the proposal for a regulation because its fundamental objective is, among other things, to improve the management of financial instruments criteria in the eu. the new rules are of direct relevance to citizens of the european union, as they will set criteria for mortgage payments and thus improve legal certainty.
in writing. ‒ i supported the discharge report for 2014 on the general budget of the eu european commission and executive agencies. i believe that european union expenditure contributes greatly to improving the level of european values and has been used in accordance with the rules. in granting discharge to the commission, parliament checks that the funds have been used lawfully and correctly, that the objectives of the guidelines have been achieved and that the appropriate results have been obtained, and that the principles of sound financial management and a culture of efficiency have been observed. these objectives were met, and i had no reservations about supporting the discharge.
in writing. ‒ in the context of the annual budgetary procedure, which can take up to seven months, with a number of negotiations and coordination, the three main eu institutions adopt the european budget for the coming year. the european commission and the other institutions are then responsible for implementing it. as the directly elected institution representing eu taxpayers, the european parliament exercises democratic control and ensures that the commission and other institutions properly manage european funds. parliament shall decide in its annual discharge procedure whether to grant discharge and give final approval to the way the budget has been implemented in a given year. before taking a decision, parliament shall examine the recommendations of the committee on budgetary control and shall take into account the annual report of the court of auditors and the commission's replies to parliamentary questions. the report by rapporteur martina dlabajová gives good reasons for granting discharge to the european commission and the implementing agencies, and i therefore voted in favour of it.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the discharge report on the implementation of the general budget of the european union for the financial year 2014, section iii commission and executive agencies. the european commission implements the budget and manages the programmes. the court of auditors notes that the accounts for the financial year 2014 have been kept confidential and that the related transactions are legal and regular. i therefore supported the discharge to be given to the implementing agencies in respect of the implementation of the budget for the financial year 2014.
in writing. ‒ discharge report on the implementation of the general budget of the european union for the financial year 2014, section iii i supported the commission and the executive agencies. when granting discharge to the commission, parliament shall verify, on the one hand, that the appropriations have been used in a lawful and proper manner and, on the other hand, that the policy objectives and the corresponding results have been achieved and that the principles of sound financial management have been respected. the commission's discharge for 2014 focused on adopting an enhanced, performance-based and results-oriented approach that will contribute to balancing the traditional approach with the introduction of new elements in line with current and future eu financing needs.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the discharge report on the implementation of the general budget of the european union for the financial year 2014 european commission and executive agencies, as the court of auditors did not find any major irregularities.

in writing. ‒ in the context of the annual budgetary procedure, which can take up to seven months, with a number of negotiations and coordination, the three main eu institutions adopt the european budget for the coming year. the european commission and the other institutions are then responsible for implementing it. as the directly elected institution representing eu taxpayers, the european parliament exercises democratic control and ensures that the commission and other institutions properly manage european funds. parliament shall decide in its annual discharge procedure whether to grant discharge and give final approval to the way the budget has been implemented in a given year. before taking a decision, parliament shall examine the recommendations of the committee on budgetary control and shall take into account the annual report of the court of auditors and the commission's replies to parliamentary questions. the report by rapporteur derek vaughan gives good reasons for granting echa's discharge, and i therefore voted in favour of it.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the discharge report on the implementation of the budget of the european securities and markets authority for the financial year 2014. the court of auditors found that the rate of implementation of the budget in 2014 was higher than in 2013, as a result of the commitments made in due time. i welcome the fact that the european securities and markets authority has reduced the volume of reallocation related to reallocation by means of a thorough quarterly budgetary review, as well as monthly reporting to the executive director and quarterly reporting to the management board, in order to ensure better and more transparent budgetary monitoring.
