in writing. ‒ i supported the european parliament's motion for a resolution on the new energy customer agreement, the so-called third energy package. its purpose is to ensure a truly competitive, transparent and customer-friendly retail energy market. unfortunately, despite some progress, this has not yet been achieved in all eu member states, as evidenced by the persistently high levels of market concentration and also by the fact that ever-lower wholesale costs are not reflected in retail prices. i am convinced that open, transparent and competitive well-regulated markets are the most important to maintain low prices, stimulate innovation and improve customer service. by removing the barriers currently faced by innovative business models in the energy sector, we can also improve the price-to-service ratio and contribute to the prevention of energy poverty.
in writing. ‒ the report on the new energy customer agreement focuses exclusively on household energy customers in the context of the transformation of the energy system and emphasises that industrial customers should be treated separately. with the current transformation of the energy system, we are moving away from a system based on traditional centralized production towards a system that is more decentralized and flexible. the final objective of the implementation of the report is thus an economy based entirely on renewable energy sources, which can only be achieved by reducing our energy consumption, by following the principle of putting energy efficiency first, and by prioritising energy savings and demand-related measures, thus achieving climate objectives in line with the paris agreement objective, energy security, competitiveness and, in particular, reducing costs for consumers. the result of the energy system transformation should be, in principle, a more efficient energy system that benefits society as a whole, increases the involvement of citizens and local and regional actors and communities and enables them to own or participate in the production, distribution and storage of renewable energy, while protecting the most vulnerable and ensuring that they benefit from energy efficiency and renewable energy measures. the report also proposes the adoption of price comparison guidelines. for these reasons, i voted in favour of the report.

in writing. ‒ i supported the new energy customer agreement, as the current transformation of the energy system is moving away from a system based on traditional centralised production to one that is more decentralised and flexible and based mainly on renewable energy. the ultimate goal of the economy should be based entirely on renewable energy sources, which can only be achieved by reducing our energy consumption. the energy union should provide stable, affordable, efficient and sustainable high-quality energy-efficient products, services and housing; enable citizens to produce, consume, store or trade their own renewable energy, individually or collectively; take energy-saving measures; actively participate in the energy market because they have a choice as consumers; contribute to the eradication of energy poverty; protect consumers from unfair, non-competitive and unfair behaviour by market actors and enable them to fully exercise their rights; and create the right conditions to ensure a well-functioning and competitive internal energy market that provides consumers with choice and transparent and clear access to information.

in writing. ‒ in voting on the european parliament's motion for a resolution on poverty, i abstained on the gender aspect, as it contained certain solutions which i cannot support for moral reasons. moreover, statistics show that the exposure to poverty is fairly equal for both men and women. statistics on the distribution of income poverty and income inequality in the eu show that in 2015, 17.2% of women and 16.1% of men were at risk of poverty. the data clearly show that women and men are exposed to poverty at about the same rate, so in my view the gender dimension is not crucial in poverty reduction. our responsibility is to provide the conditions for increasing employment, which is key to reducing poverty. for the most vulnerable, we have a duty to ensure that social policies are such as to preserve the dignity of every individual, whatever his reasons for the situation in which he finds himself.
in writing. ‒ although gender equality is one of the eu's core values and one of the objectives of strategy 2020, it is still far from being achieved. moreover, the situation in the area of gender equality has deteriorated further since the economic crisis. following the recommendation of the european commission, member states have begun to implement austerity measures and to reduce public services, which has led to an increase in poverty, especially among women. the report is divided into three parts and addresses poverty and work-life balance, poverty and employment, as well as general recommendations, including a call for member states to reduce energy poverty, a call for social rights for victims of violence against women and a highlighted role of education in combating gender stereotypes. unfortunately, the report did not include a request to establish a minimum wage and a minimum pension at european union level, nor an extension of maternity leave from 14 to 20 weeks. the positive aspects of the report include recognition of lgbti rights and measures to reduce employment insecurity. although the report has certain shortcomings, i think it is nevertheless appropriate and i have therefore supported it and voted for its adoption.

in writing. ‒ the creation of the single market is considered one of the greatest achievements of european integration, which aims to remove trade barriers throughout the european union. further deepening the single market is crucial to improving the potential of the european economy, which is why i supported the european parliament's motion for a resolution on non-tariff barriers in the single market. tariff barriers were successfully removed almost 50 years ago, while our current single market initiatives are born of the persistent challenge of how to remove non-tariff barriers. the recently adopted single market strategy sets out a number of measures to strengthen and deepen the single market, but two main changes are needed: better and more consistent enforcement of existing rules and a change in the mindset of member states, which must move away from increasingly protectionist measures and open up their domestic markets more widely.
in writing. ‒ the creation of the single market is seen as a major achievement made possible by cooperation and the pursuit of a common goal, namely the removal of trade barriers throughout the european union. tariff barriers were successfully removed almost 50 years ago, while our current single market initiatives are born of the persistent challenge of how to remove non-tariff barriers. the report examines barriers to trade and the free movement of goods and services within the single market and possible measures to remove these barriers. unfortunately, the report does not contribute to improving the definition of non-tariff barriers, but merely reflects the provisions of the treaties and the judgments of the court of justice of the european union. moreover, the report favours mutual recognition of services and goods rather than harmonisation, which poses a risk of re-application of the country of origin principle to the services sector. moreover, the report remains focused on the exclusion of member states' requirements, which it presents as disproportionate and unjustified restrictions. the report is consistent with the deregulatory approach of the better regulation agenda and thus calls for ex ante justification by member states when introducing new regulatory measures. for these reasons, the report does not reflect my demands on non-tariff barriers, which is why i did not support it at the sitting and voted against its adoption.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on non-tariff barriers in the single market. we have been talking about the european single market for some time, we have also adopted some important reports and we all agree that it is still necessary because it contributes to the european economy. the report concludes that the full implementation of the single market in the areas of free movement of goods, services, public procurement, the digital economy and most consumer protection legislation would bring economic benefits of up to eur 1.1 billion per year, which is also 8.63% of the european union's gdp. we need to remove non-tariff barriers, including unjustified national technical regulations and regulatory or non-regulatory conditions imposed on suppliers of products.

in writing. ‒ i supported the proposed resolution to conclude a protocol to the who framework convention on tobacco control. the protocol to eliminate illicit trade in tobacco products is the only multilateral legislative initiative in this field, signed by the eu on 20 december 2013, and entering into force after 40 signatories have ratified it. the illicit trade in tobacco products is a global problem and a criminal offence, undermining tobacco control policies, facilitating access to often cheaper tobacco products and posing a major threat to human health. from an economic perspective, illicit trade causes a major loss of revenue for the eu in terms of unpaid taxes and duties, estimated by some to be worth more than eur 10 billion a year. given that tax revenues from the legal tobacco trade in the member states amount to more than eur 90 billion a year, one in ten cigarettes sold on the european market is therefore illegal. illicit trafficking must therefore be combated at global level and the said protocol is the central platform for this. it lays down a system for the traceability and detection of tobacco products, the granting of licences, registration requirements, the regulation of internet sales, sales in duty-free shops and international transit. it also identifies violations, addresses liability and payment for seizures, and deals with the destruction of seized products.

in writing. ‒ i supported the draft council decision on the conclusion of the protocol to eliminate illicit trade in tobacco products to the who framework convention on tobacco control, as ratification of the protocol to the framework convention would benefit public health and contribute to the international fight against illicit trade in tobacco, tax evasion and organised crime. the who framework convention on tobacco control has been in force since 27 february 2005 and has 180 signatories to date. the protocol to eliminate illicit trade in tobacco products is based on article 15 thereof and enters into force when 40 signatories have ratified it. the eu would contribute to the early entry into force and implementation of this protocol by swift ratification. illicit trade in tobacco products is a crime, a health hazard and a revenue drain for the eu, amounting to over €10 billion in unpaid customs duties and taxes a year.

in writing. ‒ the decision to enhance cooperation in the area of jurisdiction for the recognition and enforcement of decisions in matters of property of international couples was adopted after the breakdown of negotiations between all member states on the original proposals presented by the commission in 2011. enhanced cooperation must fulfil several conditions, namely that at least nine member states must be involved and that, where the union as a whole cannot achieve the objectives of such cooperation within a reasonable time, it must be a last resort. cooperation must respect the treaty and union law, as well as the competences, rights and obligations of non-participating member states. furthermore, cooperation must pursue the objectives of the union, protect its interests and strengthen its integration processes. at the same time, cooperation must not be detrimental to the internal market or to economic, social and territorial cohesion, and must not constitute a barrier to or discrimination in trade between member states or distort competition between them. in order to support the proposal for a council decision on enhanced cooperation in this area, i therefore voted in favour of the report.

in writing. ‒ i supported the draft council decision on the conclusion, on behalf of the european union, of the protocol to eliminate illicit trade in tobacco products to the world health organisation framework convention on tobacco control, as regards the provisions of that protocol on obligations relating to judicial cooperation in criminal matters and the definition of criminal offences. the purpose of the protocol is to eliminate all forms of illicit trade in tobacco products. the latter protocol defines as any practice or conduct associated with the manufacture, sending, receipt, possession, distribution, sale or purchase of tobacco products that is prohibited by law. the protocol identifies violations, addresses liability and payment for seizure, and disposes of seized products. its main objective is to promote and strengthen international cooperation, exchange of relevant information, technical cooperation and cooperation in the field of law enforcement, and mutual legal and administrative assistance. it also specifies that a global monitoring and tracing system should be established within 5 years of entry into force. there is an inseparable conflict between the interests of the tobacco industry and the interests of public health, which the protocol does not deny. it states that the parties must ensure that any cooperation with the tobacco industry is transparent.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a directive of the european parliament and of the council amending the markets in financial instruments directive as regards certain dates. the european securities and markets authority, together with the national competent authorities, should establish a system of reference data on financial instruments. this directive postpones by one year the date from which member states are to apply the measures transposing the directive into national law and the date from which the repeal of the directive takes effect. this is necessary to enable the competent national authorities and other stakeholders to complete the operational implementation.
in writing. ‒ i supported the proposal for a directive of the european parliament and of the council amending directive 2014/65/eu on markets in financial instruments with regard to certain dates, as regulation (eu) no 600/2014 of the european parliament and of the council and directive 2014/65/eu of the european parliament and of the council are the main financial legislation acts relating to securities markets, investment firms and trading venues that were adopted as a result of the financial crisis. they set out requirements relating to the authorisation of investment firms and their activities, regulated markets and data reporting services providers. they shall coordinate the position limitation regime for commodity derivatives in order to improve transparency, support correct pricing and prevent market abuse. they also introduce rules on high-frequency trading and improve financial market supervision by harmonising administrative sanctions. the new framework requires trading venues and systematic internalisers to provide competent authorities with reference data on financial instruments. the european securities and markets authority (esma) is required to establish a financial instruments reference data system (firds) together with the national competent authorities. in order to allow esma, national authorities and stakeholders to complete the operational implementation, it is appropriate to postpone the date from which member states are to start applying the measures transposing directive 2014/65/eu and the date from which the repeal of directive 2004/39/ec takes effect by 12 months, i.e. to 3 january 2018, and to amend the directive accordingly.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a directive of the european parliament and of the council amending directive 2014/65/eu on markets in financial instruments as regards certain dates. regulation (eu) no 600/2014 of the european parliament and of the council and directive 2014/65/eu of the european parliament and of the council establish requirements in relation to authorisation and operation of investment firms, regulated markets and data reporting services providers. moreover, the new framework strengthens the protection of investors by introducing robust organisational and conduct requirements. i believe that, in order to ensure legal certainty and avoid potential market disruption, it is necessary and justified to take urgent action to extend the entry into application of the whole framework, including all delegated and implementing acts.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a directive of the european parliament and of the council amending the markets in financial instruments directive as regards certain dates. that directive postpones by one year the date from which member states are to apply the measures transposing that directive into national law and the date from which its repeal takes effect. in order to ensure legal certainty and to avoid any disruption of the market, it is justified to take action to postpone the date of application of the entire framework, including all delegated and implementing acts. this is necessary to enable the competent national authorities and other stakeholders to complete the development of the new data collection infrastructure.
in writing. ‒ i also supported the proposed amendments to the regulations on the market in financial instruments, on market abuse and on improving the securities settlement regime. those regulations also determine the conduct and position of investment firms in relation to the execution of transactions for clients. investment firms often execute, on their own behalf or on behalf of their clients, transactions in derivatives and other financial instruments or assets consisting of a number of interconnected and conditional transactions. such package deals allow investment firms and their clients to better manage their risks, as the price of each element of the package reflects the overall risk profile of the whole package rather than the prevailing market price of the individual elements. package deals can take different forms, such as swaps for physical assets, trading strategies executed on trading venues or tailor-made packages, and it is important to take these specificities into account when calibrating the applicable transparency regime. the proposed amendments therefore explicitly specify when pre-trade transparency should not apply to package deals or to their individual elements.

in writing. ‒ i supported the eu report on policy coordination for development. the eu's coordinated programme on policy coordination for development has been in place since 2005, when it became clear that more than just providing development aid was needed to achieve development goals and that far-reaching strategies between development and other eu policies were needed. the 2009 lisbon treaty underlined the eu's legal obligation to implement policy coherence for development and put the achievement of coherence between the eu's external and internal policies even more in the spotlight. the proposed report analyses five priority areas (trade and finance, food security, climate change, migration and security) and makes concrete recommendations for them. the current refugee crisis and destabilisation in the eu's neighbourhood undermines the very foundations of the eu, such as the schengen system and the principle of solidarity, and development policy coordination should therefore focus on the field of external action. stabilising the eu's neighbourhood should be at the top of the eu's priority list. the combined role of the vice-president of the commission/high representative of the union for foreign affairs and security policy has led to significant progress in the area of policy coordination for development, which applies to the eu's external action. however, the eu's comprehensive approach still faces serious challenges.
in writing. ‒ the european commission's fifth biennial report on policy coherence for development was published in august 2015, just before the adoption of the 2030 agenda for sustainable development at the un in new york in september. the adoption of the sdgs marked a turning point in the shaping of policy coherence for development. the sustainable development goals will require a more holistic approach to policy-making, with greater emphasis on coherence. it will also have a major impact on the implementation of the 2030 agenda for sustainable development. although policy coordination for development emerged in the context of north-south relations and emphasises the responsibility of rich, developed countries towards poor developing countries, the adoption of the 2030 agenda has called this vision into question. a single and universal set of development goals has been established, which applies to all and transcends the donor-recipient paradigm. the european commission's report is a useful tool in itself to raise awareness of policy coherence for development, but it would be even more useful to take a more analytical look at its progress. i also believe that concrete recommendations on addressing the challenges of policy coherence for development should be an integral part of the report. that is why i voted to adopt the report.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the eu's 2015 report on policy coordination for development. it is important to build sustainable development through globally coordinated development policies. the resolution on policy coordination for development for 2015 analyses seven priority areas, namely the area of migration, trade and finance, food security, health, climate change, gender and security. the european council meeting on policy coordination for development would also be crucial for defining the responsibilities of individual eu institutions in achieving commitments in this area. when it comes to the sdgs, third countries should be more closely involved in eu decision-making. policy coherence for development is a key element for the implementation and achievement of the new sustainable development agenda.

in writing. ‒ i supported the report by mr czesak on unfair trading practices in the food supply chain, which after many months of coordination was only ready for approval. we need to take the fight against unfair trading practices in the food chain to the next level, because we see that voluntary agreements are not the way forward. farmers are in a subordinate position in the food chain vis-à-vis well-organised and concentrated trade, and the pressure on the purchase prices of agricultural products and the poor organisation of farmers are now contributing to the deterioration of the situation. in such circumstances, farmers are at the mercy of merchants who also own the manufacturing industry, and they often sell below production price just to keep the business going. this situation is not sustainable in the long term and it is therefore essential to start developing a legislative framework at eu level as soon as possible, which will clearly define the rules of the game. the main emphasis should be on increasing competition in the field of trade and promoting the integration of farmers to better resist the pressures of large and concentrated trade. only then will it be possible to establish appropriate conditions of competition in the markets and fair relations between farmers, suppliers and traders. this will benefit all involved.
in writing. ‒ unfair trading practices in the food supply chain between businesses and suppliers are a major problem in the eu, but unfortunately not sufficiently exposed. in general, they could be defined as those which are far from good commercial practice, contrary to good faith and fair dealing and imposed unilaterally by one trading partner on another. small and medium-sized enterprises and farmers are disadvantaged and face difficulties. many member states are taking action against such practices, while other member states are only planning to take similar measures. the rules in this area vary considerably between member states, as does the scale of the problem. member states that do not have an enforcement authority are invited to consider establishing one and to give it the powers to monitor and enforce measures necessary to eliminate unfair trading practices. the report also calls for the creation of transparent retail prices, which will better reflect the added value generated by primary producers. the report also calls on all parties in the food supply chain to consider standard contracts as well as next generation contracts where risks and benefits are shared. i think that the report is good and i have supported it.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of a report on technological solutions for sustainable agriculture in the eu. with the world's growing population, malnutrition, obesity, and various cardiovascular diseases, there is a growing need to produce more safe, healthy, and nutritious food. as in other sectors, innovation in the agricultural sector can contribute to achieving sustainable agriculture in the european union. in addition, a variety of innovative approaches can help to protect the environment, in addition to increasing farmers' incomes and using resources more efficiently. i join the call to industry, the commission and the member states to work together to improve the efficiency and adaptability of robotic and other techniques in precision agriculture, thereby increasing demand and investment by farmers and the efficient use of funds for agricultural and horticultural research.
in writing. ‒ i have supported technological solutions for sustainable agriculture in the eu. one of the biggest challenges today is how to meet the demand for healthy food, which is expected to increase by 70% by 2050. technological innovation is a key part of the solution, as agricultural technologies have the potential to increase productivity and sustainability of agriculture. the european union should become a world leader in agricultural technology, innovation and sustainability. european agriculture is lagging behind its international competitors, and this can only change if there is a sustained and prioritised investment in the research base. the starting point should be targeted investment in applied and translational research. although farmers and scientists play different roles in the innovation process, better outcomes can only be achieved if both parties work more closely together. providing the necessary knowledge and skills and attracting the right expertise to the industry will be key. it is also important to create a regulatory environment that is conducive to innovation, while ensuring that eu rules do not hamper it.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on technological solutions for sustainable agriculture in the eu. the report emphasises that the agriculture sector has always relied on new farm business models and practices that include new techniques and production methods to increase outputs and adapt to new and changing circumstances. the report equally underlines that ecosystem services, such as nutrient cycling, are of central importance to agriculture, and that some functions, such as carbon sequestration, go beyond food production. i voted in favour because i am convinced that innovation has the potential to contribute to achieving sustainable agriculture in the eu.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of a report on technological solutions for sustainable agriculture in the eu. global food demand is expected to increase by 70% by 2050. providing optimal and healthy nutrition is one of the greatest challenges facing the world. the shrinking of available land, loss of the environment, water scarcity, increased demand for energy, the emergence of new pests and diseases are putting a heavy burden on the agricultural sector. to ensure a sustainable agricultural sector in the eu, it is essential to develop a wide range of innovative technologies in all types of farming.
in writing. ‒ i supported the report by mr huiteme. the european agricultural sector is of crucial importance to the eu. in addition to its core mission of providing healthy and quality food, it is a hugely important economic pillar, employing 25 million people. these are either directly engaged in agriculture or employed in the food and retail sector. eu agriculture continues to set the standards for agricultural practices around the world that produce high added value products, providing knowledge-based solutions to feed a growing and increasingly demanding population. technological innovation can therefore make a major contribution to improving land use and saving resources. so-called precision farming will transform agriculture and help us to invest fewer resources to produce more kilograms of crops. it will also contribute to more targeted action against diseases or pests. agriculture therefore needs to be better aligned with other industrial sectors (chemicals, health and technology), and cross-sectoral knowledge integration and motivating young people to farm will play an important role in this.
in writing. ‒ changes in agricultural practices are structural or linked to production processes. they make agriculture one of the most dynamic sectors. as this sector is among the first to adopt new technology, the rural economy can thrive and keep pace with the general economic development. the food and agriculture organization of the united nations estimates that the expected increase in the world's population will require an increase in food supply. there is thus a need to increase and improve agricultural production with fewer resources, in particular due to pressure on natural resources and the related impacts on biodiversity, environmental vulnerability, climate change and land scarcity. however, i think the report is a bit ambiguous and could be interpreted as supporting innovations that are contrary to my principles. while i understand that these are necessary for progress, it is necessary to ensure that they are healthy, environmentally friendly and do not have negative consequences in other areas. i object to the mention of drones and certain sections of the report that suggest the possibility of supporting genetically modified mechanisms. although the report advocates the idea that greater transparency in the supply chain and production can help consumers make more informed purchasing decisions, which i agree with, i think the report should be improved. that's why i voted against it.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on strengthening innovation and economic development in european farm management in the future. as in other sectors, the agricultural sector is facing major advances and the development of new methods, techniques and production methods. this has increased farmers' yields while reducing production costs. the report rightly concludes that economic development and sustainable production are not mutually exclusive and can be achieved through innovation, research and development, new management and improved agronomy. this is why we need to encourage innovation in technology and management.
in writing. ‒ i supported the strengthening of innovation and economic development in european farm management in the future. the agricultural sector is one of the most dynamic economic sectors and one of the first to adopt new technologies. the ecological footprint of agricultural production should be reduced in order to alleviate the pressure on the environment. more attention should be paid to the needs of farmers without compromising the achievement of policy objectives, which means allowing sufficient flexibility to enhance innovation and competitiveness. targeted incentives in the production process and investments are of paramount importance. agriculture needs to be better aligned with other industrial sectors, knowledge integration needs to be strengthened, the use of resources needs to be integrated and the interactions better understood in order to optimise their interaction and better integrate agriculture into the market economy. the european agricultural sector is of vital importance to the whole of the european union in terms of food security and employment for 25 million people. it also sets standards for agricultural practice worldwide and enables the production of products with high added value.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on enhancing innovation and economic development in future european farm management. i am strongly committed to unleashing agriculture’s innovative potential in order to produce more quality products, ensure food supplies and fight climate change more effectively. i believe that agriculture is one of the most innovative economic sectors. however, although farmers have the capacity and the knowledge to innovate, they find themselves limited by obsolete legislation or rules. it is of crucial importance to trust farmers and to use the power of innovation and the power of nature in order to reach our common goals.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on strengthening innovation and economic development in european farm management in the future. the report highlights the importance of innovation for sustainable agricultural production and stresses the importance of introducing advanced production techniques by small and medium-sized family farms, which are an integral part of european agriculture. i agree that economic development and sustainable production are not mutually exclusive and that innovation, research and development of production techniques should be encouraged.
i welcome the european commission's proposal for a new migration deal presented today. so far, we have only put out the fire in europe with a variety of actions, short-term, that were necessary to temporarily stem the flow of migrants. with the new dublin regulation and the new migration agreement, we are moving towards a comprehensive solution and a long-term solution. the €8 billion in financial assistance will be used first of all by partner countries in africa and the middle east to improve migration management, in particular border control, asylum management, fight against corruption and so on. an important part of this proposal is the establishment of entry points in the countries of origin. in particular, i welcome the idea of a european external investment fund, which must be created with private capital and which must also be development-oriented. only investments in the real economy and in the social environment can have the effect of deterring many from the risky path to europe and beyond. we are committed to making development aid paid by european taxpayers (much more than by the us and china, by the way) more selective in the future. those countries that meet their international obligations, that are willing to take back their nationals and that cooperate in managing the flows of illegal migrants and even offer international protection to third-country nationals should be rewarded. irresponsible and uncooperative governments need to be removed from aid, trade and visa privileges. (the speaker agreed to accept the question raised by the blue card (rule 149 (8)).
answer to the question posed by raising the blue card. the fact is that this idea, this concept is meant as juncker plan 2 for countries outside the european union. and it's normal that without investment, foreign investment, especially european investment (europe also contributes the most to development aid, more than other countries, more than america and so on), without that there will be no economic recovery and no prosperity in those countries where the refugees come from. so i think this fund is the most important idea and the most important action of the european union in preventing migration in the long term.
the question asked by raising the blue card. after 23 june, it is certain that the pressure of the flow of migrants from africa and other countries will continue for years. do you think that after june 23rd, if britain leaves the european union, it will not be the country that will be partly involved in solving this humanitarian problem? and do you think that if you don't cooperate, the problems will go away on their own without the british caring about it or doing anything to help solve the problem?
the fact that we are now entering into partnerships with african countries is actually a cause for concern. poverty in africa is not a problem of yesterday. we should have done this a long time ago. but that's not a criticism of the proposal. i just wish it wasn't too late. the european union is a major player in the world economy, and the european union is the world's largest trading partner. i agree that the refugee and migration crisis is not just a european problem, and in this i support you in your global approach. but i wonder what those rewards and consequences are you're talking about when you're unveiling the compact for members who don't participate. i agree that more investment is needed and also a change in approach. but first, not in a way that simply transfers the burden to the african continent and closes europe's borders. and secondly, not in a way that european money gets into the wrong hands. we need to be very strict about who and how we allocate funds. it is essential to ensure that we have sincere and honest partners in african countries. at the same time, it is also essential to strengthen legal and safe pathways for immigration to europe, as you say. we heard that the balkan route was closed, that there were fewer deaths in the mediterranean, but that human trafficking was increasing and new migration routes were opening up. i can't get past the inconceivable fact that refugees in greece can only apply for asylum via skype. these are things that can be improved immediately and give people hope. finally, i agree that european governance of migration requires a long-term, strategic approach. but it must not be limited to curbing the flow of money from africa, but must also be directed towards establishing genuine cooperation with africa, which will strengthen the continent politically and economically, in cooperation with europe and in contacts between peoples.
i have no doubt that the successful integration of migrants into the countries of the european union, into european society, is our common goal. to do this, we need common, balanced, uniform and comprehensive european rules that all european countries will unconditionally respect. the blue card as a legal instrument for resettlement is a tool that has been used far too infrequently similar to humanitarian visas to date, although it could solve many problems. the blue card reduces black market work, which benefits only the profiteers, contributes positively to integration and reduces discrimination against migrants. equal treatment and equal pay is not only a way of ensuring the social integration of migrants, but also contributes to the fight against social dumping in general. but we need a single blue card that covers the whole european market, not just the 28 countries. working and living conditions and access to education for migrant workers and their children, irrespective of their status, are essential factors for their integration into the social and economic sphere of the host country, and measures to this end must be implemented at national, regional and local level. but the adoption of rules or measures is pointless and doomed to failure if we know that they are fragmented and left to the discretion of individual countries, and if we know that certain countries do not comply with them and even openly predict it. to mention relocation: hungary and slovakia have not yet expressed a willingness to relocate people. some countries, such as the czech republic, bulgaria, estonia, refuse resettlement requests without good reasons. poland is invoking a freeze that was never granted. this is simply unacceptable and will not bring europe back to life.
on behalf of the s&d group. for almost a decade, the european parliament has been calling on the governments of the eu member states to take serious action. a us senate report has revealed that the cia used methods of brutal interrogation and torture on european soil after the september 11 attacks. european governments must recognise that this is not just a shameful but a serious violation of fundamental rights and european values. new evidence is still coming to light. a delegation from the libe committee visited romania last autumn, but the authorities did not allow us to enter the building of the alleged detention facility. it was different in lithuania before that. the european parliament's own report on this mission has been instrumental in unlocking some of the secrets. the decisive event, as mentioned earlier, was the publication of the u.s. senate report. it revealed not only the scale of the crimes but also that torture is ineffective in the fight against terrorism. under international law, there can be no excuse for such acts. and we need to show that we're serious by prosecuting those responsible. it was the most systematic violation of human rights and humanitarian law on european soil since the second world war. individual european governments have not completed detailed investigations into alleged involvement, much less taken action against those responsible or at least assumed moral responsibility. sadly, the confidential information contained in the senate torture report seems to have been obtained only by the hollywood movie industry. whereas civil society, ngos and even advocates of detention have not achieved this. dozens of people are still being held at guantanamo bay without charge or trial. investigations in individual member states need to continue in order to establish the extent of the involvement. these violations will never go away, and no carpet is big enough to sweep them under. it is our collective responsibility to close this most shameful chapter in our european history and to ensure that it never happens again. i call on my colleagues to vote in favour of the resolution tomorrow.
mr katainen, first of all, congratulations on the first year of operation of the fund. i think he surprised me in a lot of ways. he also pointed out some shortcomings. they were mentioned here today, and i personally think that one of the key shortcomings is the lack of investment in the countries that need it most. this is not your fault. i think that this is largely the fault of the member states, which have not prepared themselves sufficiently and have not built the infrastructure for this type of investment. similar fate has befallen the cohesion funds in the previous perspective and also in the present one, where more complex projects have to be prepared. i therefore recommend that you do your utmost to help us promote this in the member states where these projects are not available and where they are urgently needed, and that in this way the countries also come to terms with their developmental backwardness, because otherwise europe will be less cohesive than it is today.

in writing. ‒ i supported the draft council decision on the conclusion, on behalf of the european union, of an agreement in the form of a declaration on the extension of the agreement on trade in information technology products (itp). the parties shall endeavour to ensure that the information technology products covered by this agreement are not subject to customs duties or other duties. the agreement covers some 200 tariff headings relating to computers and telephones, raw materials, components and machinery for the production of information technology products. the duty-free treatment has contributed significantly to the development and expansion of trade, which has quadrupled in the 20 years since the agreement entered into force. following the signature of the agreement, the signatories were required to present timetables with a gradual reduction of duties for all products over a seven-year phase-out period, which means that by 2019 imports of all products concerned will be exempt from customs duties. the eu exports €189 billion worth of products covered by the ita, and this is expected to increase. the agreement can only be fully exploited if a larger number of member states accede to it.

in writing. ‒ i supported the draft council decision on the imposition of control measures on the new psychoactive substance 1-phenyl-2- ((1-pirolidin-1-yl) pentan-1-one (α-pirolidinovalerophenone, α-pvp). α-pvp is a potent psychostimulant and there are 115 known deaths and 191 known acute poisonings in the eight member states where α-pvp has been detected. there is no information available or published studies that have comprehensively assessed the health risks associated with α-pvp, namely chronic and acute toxicity, but similar effects to those seen with other stimulants have been observed in animals. for this reason, it is necessary to introduce control measures and criminal sanctions in member states for α-pvp, as provided for by their legislation in accordance with their obligations under the united nations convention on psychotropic substances.

in writing. ‒ i supported the interim report on the draft council decision on the ratification and accession of the 2010 protocol to the international convention on liability and compensation for damage in connection with the carriage of hazardous and noxious substances by sea by member states on behalf of the union, with the exception of aspects relating to judicial cooperation in civil matters. the 2010 convention establishes the objective liability of the owner of a ship carrying dangerous and harmful substances for damage resulting from an incident related to the transport of dangerous and harmful substances by sea on board that ship. the establishment of a specialised compensation fund of approximately eur 310 million for compensation payments to persons who have suffered damage in connection with the transport of dangerous goods is important. the international arrangements in this area are more appropriate than the regional arrangements. it is in the interest of the european union to have a uniform system of liability for environmental damage.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the interim report on the draft council decision on the ratification and accession by member states, in the interest of the european union, to the protocol of 2010 to the international convention on liability and compensation for damage in connection with the carriage of hazardous and noxious substances by sea, with the exception of the aspects related to judicial cooperation in civil matters. the 2010 hns convention establishes strict liability of the owner of the ship carrying hns for any damage resulting from an incident in connection with the carriage of hns by sea and on board that ship. i believe that the conclusion of the 2010 protocol to the hns convention will ensure uniform application of rules on liability and compensation in connection with accidents caused by ships carrying hns at sea across the eu. it will also guarantee availability of sufficient funds for compensation of victims of such accidents.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the interim report on the draft council decision on the ratification and accession of the 2010 protocol to the international convention on liability and compensation for damage in connection with the carriage of hazardous and noxious substances by sea by member states, on behalf of the union, with the exception of aspects relating to judicial cooperation in civil matters. the interim report calls on the member states to ratify or accede to the 2010 hns convention within a reasonable period, which should not exceed two years from the entry into force of the council decision. the objective of the 2010 hns convention is to ensure, through the dedicated hns international compensation fund, the accountability and payment of adequate, prompt and effective compensation for damage to persons, property and the environment resulting from the carriage of dangerous and harmful substances by sea.

in writing. ‒ i supported the interim report on the draft council decision on the ratification and accession of the 2010 protocol to the international convention on liability and compensation for damage in connection with the carriage of hazardous and noxious substances by sea by member states, in the interest of the european union, as regards aspects related to judicial cooperation in civil matters. the 2010 convention establishes the objective liability of the owner of a ship carrying dangerous and harmful substances for damage resulting from an incident related to the transport of dangerous and harmful substances by sea on board that ship. the establishment of a specialised compensation fund of approximately eur 310 million for compensation payments to persons who have suffered damage in connection with the transport of dangerous goods is important. the international arrangements in this area are more appropriate than the regional arrangements. the conclusion of the 2010 protocol to the hns convention will ensure the uniform application of the rules on liability and compensation in respect of accidents caused by ships carrying dangerous and harmful substances at sea in the european union. it is in the interest of the european union to have a uniform system of liability for environmental damage.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the interim report on the draft council decision on the ratification and accession by member states, in the interest of the european union, to the protocol of 2010 to the international convention on liability and compensation for damage in connection with the carriage of hazardous and noxious substances by sea, with regard to the aspects related to judicial cooperation in civil matters. the 2010 hns convention establishes strict liability of the owner of the ship carrying hns for any damage resulting from an incident in connection with the carriage of hns by sea and on board that ship. i believe that the conclusion of the 2010 protocol to the hns convention will ensure uniform application of rules on liability and compensation in connection with accidents caused by ships carrying hns at sea across the eu. it will also guarantee availability of sufficient funds for compensation of victims of such accidents.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the interim report on the draft council decision on the ratification and accession to the 2010 protocol to the international convention on liability and compensation for damage in connection with the carriage of hazardous and noxious substances by sea by member states, in the interest of the european union, as regards aspects related to judicial cooperation in civil matters. i support the purpose of the convention, which establishes, inter alia, the objective liability of the shipowner for all damage caused by the carriage of dangerous and health-damaging substances by sea under the convention and the obligation of the shipowner to take out insurance or obtain other financial security to cover his liability under the convention.

in writing. ‒ according to a study by the organisation for economic co-operation and development (oecd), the loss to national budgets worldwide from aggressive tax planning by multinational companies is between $100 and $240 billion each year, representing 4 to 10% of global corporate tax revenue. countries lose huge amounts of revenue, reducing their ability to invest in promoting employment, eradicating poverty and establishing effective health care systems for all. the report represents a positive step in limiting tax avoidance by multinational companies. its main objective is to ensure that companies pay taxes where they make profits. thus, the company will have to prove that it is actually established in a country, since only then will it be obliged to pay taxes in a fair manner. the report reinforces the role of the european parliament, which should be responsible for monitoring the effective implementation of this directive in all 28 member states. it should also be able to carry out an independent evaluation of its effectiveness. although the report is a little weaker in substance than i would have liked, i think it is a step in the right direction and that is why i voted against it.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a council directive on the establishment of rules against tax avoidance practices which have a direct impact on the functioning of the internal market. according to oecd data, member states lose at least eur 100 billion annually in their budgets due to tax avoidance, which is a serious problem and calls for effective action. i support the clearly stated position that companies pay taxes where they make profits. a harmonised european tax system is certainly one solution, but it is not the only one. the european union must be more decisive in the fight against tax evasion and tax evasion.
in writing. ‒ i supported the proposal for a council directive laying down rules against tax avoidance practices which have a direct impact on the functioning of the internal market. the provision on limiting interest rates to 20% for tax relief is inappropriate and harmful, and at the same time it hinders investment. interest payments are costs of investment projects and should therefore be able to be claimed as such, otherwise the taxable profit would be overestimated. in this respect, the 30% threshold recommended by the oecd in its strategy against base erosion and profit shifting is also problematic. many companies with serious investment projects would be harmed. it is wrong to adopt provisions to combat inappropriate tax practices that will also harm companies that pay their taxes honestly. in addition, intra-group loans are used in particular to avoid taxation in order to shift profits to low tax jurisdictions. it would therefore be more appropriate to limit the tax relief for interest payments to intra-group loans only. however, they should not restrict the facilitation of interest payments to third parties. the envisaged option of carrying forward non-deductible interest payments for up to five years will not be of great benefit, especially to companies financing real investments. in the case of large investment projects, companies face high interest payment costs for several years, which means that there is no possibility of carrying interest.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a council directive laying down rules against tax avoidance practices that directly affect the functioning of the internal market. i strongly believe that combating fraud, tax evasion and tax avoidance are overriding political priorities, as aggressive tax planning practices are unacceptable from the point of view of the integrity of the internal market and social justice. furthermore, i am of the view that fair and effective corporate taxation must become the cornerstone of the single market.
in writing. ‒ i supported the report on the proposal for a council directive on the establishment of rules against tax avoidance practices which have a direct impact on the functioning of the internal market. the proposal for a directive provides, inter alia, for a stricter limit on the amount of interest recognised as expenditure, for greater transparency in the operation of the funds and for a pan-european list of tax havens. i agree that the fight against tax fraud and evasion and tax avoidance is a top political priority, as abuses of aggressive tax planning are unacceptable from the point of view of the integrity of the internal market and social justice.

in writing. ‒ the security situation in the european union and beyond is becoming increasingly dangerous and challenging. they are marked by terrorist attacks and mass killings, which call for the european union to strengthen its security by further developing and supporting the common security and defence policy, so that it becomes a more effective political instrument and a real guarantee for the security of the citizens of the european union. however, it is not entirely clear whether the report on space capabilities for european security and defence is intended to influence the mid-term review of the financial perspective or perhaps to establish a link between terrorism and the need to develop space programmes for national audiences or perhaps something else, which is regrettable. the report calls for the european union to finance the space programme in the same amount as the us, which is highly unrealistic given the budgetary constraints. furthermore, terrorism and migration are used to legitimize the inefficient use of large amounts of public funds, which i do not support. the report is also contradictory, calling for eu strategic autonomy on the one hand and close eu cooperation with nato and the us on the other. the report also seeks to increase the security and military dimension of space programmes, while at the same time opposing the militarisation of space. on the basis of the above, i decided that the report was not appropriate and therefore did not support it in the vote.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on space capabilities for european security and defence. with the increasingly difficult situation in the world and in our neighbourhood, i am thinking particularly of terrorist attacks, we need to act quickly at all levels. we need a common strategy and a coordinated response, especially as regards the eu's common security and defence policy, as the safety of our citizens must come first. i support the report which attributes a significant role to space capabilities and services in the field of european security and defence. i therefore join the call for further implementation of the common security and defence policy and for greater efficiency, visibility and impact.
in writing. ‒ i supported the report on space capabilities for european security and defence, as space policy is an essential element of the strategic independence that the eu needs to develop. space capability is important for european security and defence, both from a day-to-day perspective in peacetime and in cases of major challenges in wartime. in the case of more developed space capabilities, the eu could also act in the field of defence through the european defence agency (eda) and the eu satellite centre. over the past decades, european space assets have been developed through the concerted efforts of the european space agency. successful cooperation and interaction between member states is essential for the development and maintenance of space capabilities for security and defence in europe. space capabilities play an important role in the context of european security and defence.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on space capabilities for european security and defence. in the light of the security situation in the union, i support the proposal to improve access to space-based satellite communication, space monitoring, precision navigation and earth observation capabilities. the satellite capabilities would be used to better assess and detect the flows of illegal immigrants, their routes and, for those coming from north africa, to detect embarkation areas on ships in order to capture them more quickly and save more lives.
in writing. ‒ between 2014 and 2020, more than eur 12 billion is earmarked for the implementation of three initiatives: satellite navigation, earth observation and space research. in 2014, the european commission also declared that one of its priorities was the adoption of a space strategy for europe. accordingly, the resolution seeks to communicate the european parliament's opinion on the establishment of a space strategy based on the achievements of the space programmes to date and the opportunities created and enhanced by the various measures. in the area of the space market, the resolution emphasises the implementation of the copernicus and galileo programmes, which must be understood as complementary. the resolution also encourages synergies in the future. the resolution also calls on the european commission to strengthen links between existing policies on space activities. in the area of access to finance and expertise, the resolution calls for an assessment of the results and possible changes, if appropriate. the commission should also address the geographical imbalance in space activities, as the countries of central and eastern europe are currently lagging behind the rest of europe. the resolution also calls for enhanced cooperation, information exchange and best practice. in support of the substance of the resolution as described above, i voted in favour of the resolution.

in writing. ‒ the situation in venezuela is very tense due to a number of factors, such as high inflation, exchange rate liberalisation, which has had negative consequences for income and access to goods, and unprecedented drought as a result of the el niño phenomenon. the opposition's victory in the december 2015 parliamentary elections further exacerbated the tensions in the country. it called for a previously unknown division of power into executive, judicial and legislative branches. in 2015, unreported murders were also reported as a result of the unrest. this is why we in the european parliament have decided to adopt a resolution addressing the situation in venezuela and calling for an improvement. unfortunately, the greens' request that the resolution call on the eu member states not to use the situation in venezuela for political purposes in their home countries was rejected. moreover, instead of criticizing both sides in the conflict for the use of violence, the resolution unilaterally blames the venezuelan government and questions the division of power in venezuela. although i think that a resolution on the situation in venezuela would be welcome, i am not satisfied with the content of the present resolution and therefore abstained.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the joint motion for a resolution on the situation in venezuela. we need to respond to the deterioration of democracy and human rights and to the socio-economic situation in venezuela, where a climate of political and social instability is increasing. the government of venezuela must take responsibility and overcome the current critical situation in the country with a constructive approach in order to find a constitutional, peaceful and democratic solution based on dialogue. only dialogue can lead the country out of this difficult situation. above all, a dialogue between the government and the opposition must be present at all times and be conducted smoothly. i support the call on the venezuelan government to release all political prisoners immediately.
in writing. ‒ i supported the european parliament resolution on the situation in venezuela, as both the venezuelan government and the supreme court are illegally constituted. there is no separation of powers and no principle of independence in the country, which is typical of democratic states. the country is one of the most dangerous in the world because of its high crime rates and impunity. the economic and social crisis is the result of high levels of corruption, mismanagement of public funds and inefficient management. the country also has a worrying situation with regard to democracy and human rights. opponents of the government cannot peacefully express their disagreement with what is happening in the country, as in most cases they are suppressed by excessive use of force and arbitrary detention by the security authorities. the government should respect the rule of law, operate within the limits of democracy and make it a priority to reduce the high level of impunity that is fuelling the rising violence and insecurity in the country.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the joint motion for a resolution on the situation in venezuela. we need an immediate response to the deterioration of democracy and human rights and the socio-economic situation in venezuela, where a climate of political and social instability is increasing. i support the call on the venezuelan government to take a constructive approach to overcome the current critical economic and political situation in the country by seeking a constitutional, peaceful and democratic solution based on dialogue and respect for human rights.
in writing. ‒ i supported the motion for a resolution because it is unacceptable that the commission, as guardian of the treaties, should be in breach of the latter. the resolution calls on the commission to fulfil its obligations and adopt risk-based scientific criteria for the detection of endocrine disrupting properties. the court of justice of the european union has already ruled that scientific criteria can only be established objectively on the basis of scientific data on the hormonal system and that the commission does not have the power to alter the regulatory balance established by a basic act.
in writing. ‒ endocrine disruptors are substances that interfere with the normal functioning of the hormonal system to the extent that they have harmful effects on the body. as early as 2012, the world health organization declared them a global threat. endocrine disruptors are associated with a number of health problems, such as cancer, fertility problems, genital deformities, obesity and neurodevelopmental disorders. legally, endocrine disruptors are covered by the european chemicals, pesticides, water and cosmetics acts. a major disadvantage is that endocrine disruptors are not precisely defined in the legislation mentioned. in 2015, the general court ruled in sweden v european commission that the european commission had breached eu law by failing to adopt a delegated act specifying the criteria for determining endocrine disrupting properties. nevertheless, the european commission decided to continue the work as planned before the judgment. the resolution thus expresses strong criticism of the european commission and condemns its inaction. at the same time, it calls on the european commission to adopt scientific risk criteria for the determination of endocrine disrupting properties without delay. it also gives the european commission two months to act in accordance with article 265 of the treaty on european union. i agree with the above, and therefore voted in favour of the resolution.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the joint motion for a resolution on endocrine disruptors: the situation following the judgment of the general court of the european union of 16 december 2015. after two and a half years, we are still waiting for the commission to adopt delegated acts to establish scientific criteria for the detection of endocrine disrupting properties in active substances and biocidal products. the commission has also failed to fulfil its institutional obligations. i very much hope that the commission will deliver on its commitment by the summer. the general court of the european union has also held that scientific criteria can be objectively established only on the basis of scientific data on the endocrine system, independent of all other factors, in particular economic ones.
in writing. ‒ i supported the motion for a resolution on endocrine disruptors: the state of play following the judgment of the court of justice of 16 december 2015. the latest study on health costs associated with endocrine disruptors, which assessed five health conditions that could be caused by endocrine disruptors, found that the social and economic burden of the health consequences of endocrine disruptors for the eu is estimated to be significant, ranging from eur 46 to eur 288 billion per year, based on the available expert literature. the provisional criteria laid down in the regulation do not ensure an adequate level of protection. protecting citizens from health risks is one of the three strategic objectives of the european union's health policy, and we must put hormonal disruptors at the centre of prevention. in the area of health, where the link can be brought much closer to the citizen, only consistent action by the commission is necessary and admissible. action is needed because of the growing number of diseases besides cancer and diabetes. preventive action is both necessary and economically justified.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the joint motion for a resolution on endocrine disruptors: state of play following the judgement of the general court of the european union of 16 december 2015. the resolution condemns the commission not only for its failure to comply with its obligation to adopt delegated acts pursuant to regulation (eu) no 528/2012, but moreover for failing to comply with its institutional obligations. the resolution stresses that the general court ruled that the specification of scientific criteria could only be carried out in an objective manner based on scientific data related to the endocrine system, independently of any other consideration. furthermore, the resolution urges the commission to comply immediately with its obligations under article 266 tfeu and to adopt immediately hazard-based scientific criteria for the determination of endocrine-disrupting properties.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the joint motion for a resolution on endocrine disruptors: the situation following the judgment of the general court of the european union of 16 december 2015. in its judgment of 16 december 2015 in case t-521/14, the general court of the european union held that the commission had infringed eu law by failing to adopt delegated acts with scientific criteria for the detection of endocrine disrupting properties. as the commission has not yet taken action to comply with the court's judgment, but continues to violate eu law, i join the call for the commission to fulfil its institutional obligations.
in writing. ‒ there is no consensus in the scientific community on the issue of genetically modified organisms, and it is expected that meps and the public will be divided on these issues. i myself am a proponent of the precautionary principle in the case of gmos, and i think it is completely unnecessary to rush through a sensitive subject such as the registration of gm maize. we are at a delicate moment when the institutions should have more respect for each other and, above all, for the will of the people who are largely against the use of gmos in europe. i also wonder very much, personally, if we really need this kind of gmo corn seed. i understand that for various reasons we are not able to grow enough soybeans in the eu and we are obliged to import soybeans from countries where gmos are mainly used. but i can't understand why we need gmo corn seed. i'm pretty sure we can grow enough corn without that gmo seed. therefore, i supported the proposed conscientious objection.

on behalf of the s&d group. europe has always been a continent of migration. similarly, we in europe have always faced terrorist threats. for decades, we've lived with terrorism in spain, in ireland, elsewhere. recently, threats have come from outside. but the first phenomenon is not the consequence of the second, and vice versa, as many would like to believe. that is why i am concerned about the commission's plan for the future of information systems, which it has presented, together with the proposal for smart borders. the commission wants to tackle new threats and challenges by pooling databases and building a 'big brother'. the number of passengers will increase considerably in the future. probably the number of threats. technology will advance, and criminals will likely be one step ahead of it. of course, we must fight against dangers, but we must also be able to identify and prevent potential threats. but we're not going to do that by creating new super databases. first, existing systems need to be thoroughly assessed and any weaknesses addressed. above all, their use needs to be improved. the spread of information already known is a very big step. we have also learned this lesson from the recent terrorist attacks in paris, in brussels. we have repeatedly called for the exchange of information to be the priority. i am not opposed to new and effective solutions in the field of information technology. but only if you protect your personal information. a criminal suspect and a tourist are treated very differently, and so is their personal information. we do not intend to impede the work of the judicial and security authorities, but we cannot accept a completely unrestricted and systematic access to everyone's personal data. our common future also depends on today's debate, and we will all be responsible for the extent to which we encroach on the privacy of europeans.
today we are again seeing that the exchange of relevant information between the relevant security actors increases the security of all citizens. this correlation has been proven for a long time. unfortunately, it is also the case in practice, for example in the recent terrorist attacks in europe. it is therefore surprising that a political compromise on the issue of giving law enforcement access to certain data on individuals is so difficult to reach. i wonder what kind of security situation we would be living in if the european people's party had not for years pushed this issue high on the agenda of european security policy. the european people's party also recently made 10 recommendations on the fight against terrorism, including a call for improved collection, processing and exchange of information from criminal records between member states, between law enforcement authorities, between agencies (europol, frontex, eurojust, etc.) and between systems which must become compatible with each other. we therefore call on the commission to present systemic solutions to this pressing problem, which is perpetuating the weak security situation in europe, without delay. in order to combat terrorism effectively, we must also improve cooperation with third countries, not only the usa and canada, but also turkey, the countries of north africa and the middle east. better communication will also improve the effectiveness of the fight against illicit arms trafficking, radicalisation online and in prisons, and terrorist financing. the treatment of so-called foreign fighters and the protection of external borders will also be improved.
the fight against crime requires decisive and rapid action, but it must not come at the expense of unjustified interference with the lives of citizens and measures that do not achieve the desired results. of course, security and freedom are two sides of the same coin, and unfortunately, they are sometimes far from each other. the control and collection of data, the sharing of data must have its limits and we cannot give blanco menus to the sharing and processing of data, which can also lead to abuse of power. there's a fine line between tracking and processing and, of course, defining what are called potential suspects and who they really are. and so we need to be careful about the data we collect, and of course, these rules cannot be an end in themselves. it is therefore necessary to emphasise the particular importance of the data protection officers and controllers.

in writing. ‒ european union citizens are highly mobile - some 12 million of them study, work or live in another eu member state. today, when citizens and businesses of the european union are exercising their rights to free movement or the freedoms of the internal market, they may face administrative difficulties in submitting the necessary public documents to the authorities of another member state, for example in the case of cross-border mobility. the purpose of the legislative regulation is to promote the free movement of citizens and businesses by simplifying the adoption of certain public documents in the european union. this is not a question of recognising the content of authentic instruments, since it is important to preserve the sovereignty of the member states in the field of family law. unfortunately, certain regulations do not include diplomas and vocational certificates, certificates of invalidity and certain documents for businesses. moreover, multilingual standard forms cannot be submitted separately, but must be attached to the national documents, which is an unnecessary problem. nevertheless, significant progress has been made, as the regulation also contains revision clauses that allow administrative simplification to be extended in the future as national administrations adjust to the new way of working. for the reasons stated above, i voted against the amendment and thus supported the report on the council's position with a view to adopting a regulation on the promotion of the free movement of citizens.

in writing. ‒ this regulation is the fourth in the reform of the court of justice of the european union and builds on its predecessor. in parallel with the increase in the number of judges at the general court from 40 to 47, the tribunal, which has seven judges, should also be abolished. the proposal provides for the transfer of pending cases from the civil service tribunal to the general court, which will take place on 31 august 2016. for reasons of legal certainty, the rules of procedure of the general court will be applied to these cases. the report points out that the rules of procedure of the general court should be amended to take account of the special rules laid down in the applicable rules of procedure of the civil service tribunal in civil service disputes. a greater number of cases should be referred to a larger number of panels where this justifies their importance, in order to ensure the consistency and quality of case-law. they should also consider the possibility of adapting case allocation rules and practices in order to create thematic synergies. in conjunction with article 257 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union, the report stresses that it is logical to conclude that an article which allows the establishment of an institutional body also implicitly allows the abolition of that body if changed circumstances so require. the report is in line with my view on the reform of the general court of the european union, which is why i supported it.
