in writing. ‒ the european union has agreed with monaco an agreement on the automatic exchange of financial account information to improve international tax cooperation and compliance. the agreement represents an important step in the fight against tax fraud and tax evasion. the agreement builds on a previous agreement of 2004, which had achieved that monaco implemented measures equivalent to those of the eu savings tax directive. the new agreement will enable tax authorities in the member states and monaco to correctly and unambiguously identify those taxpayers, administer and enforce national tax laws in cross-border cases, assess the likelihood of tax evasion and also prevent unnecessary further investigations. for the reasons set out above, i consider the proposal for a council decision on the conclusion, on behalf of the european union, of the amending protocol to the agreement between the european community and the principality of monaco concerning measures to be taken to combat money laundering to be a good one and i also voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a decision.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a council decision on the proposal for a council decision on the conclusion, on behalf of the european union, of the amending protocol to the agreement between the european community and the principality of monaco concerning measures equivalent to those laid down in the council directive. the agreement will strengthen cooperation between the european union and monaco in the field of exchange of financial account information and in the tax field. i believe that this agreement will strengthen the fight against tax fraud and tax evasion, which we must have zero tolerance for. this is an upgrade of the 2004 agreement.
in writing. ‒ following the adoption of the savings directive and with a view to maintaining a level playing field for economic operators, the european union signed an agreement with the principality of monaco on measures equivalent to those laid down in the directive. on 17 june 2011, the commission presented recommendations for a mandate to open negotiations with the principality of monaco with a view to upgrading the european union's agreements with those countries in line with international developments and to ensure that those countries continue to apply measures equivalent to those in the european union. on the basis of that proposal, the council was invited to approve, on behalf of the european union, the amending protocol to the agreement between the european community and the principality of monaco providing for measures equivalent to those laid down in the directive on taxation of savings income in the form of interest payments. the report agrees to the conclusion of a protocol amending the agreement, and i have therefore supported it.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a council decision on the conclusion, on behalf of the european union, of the amending protocol to the agreement between the european community and the principality of monaco providing for measures equivalent to those laid down in council directive 2003/48/ec. the european union and monaco have negotiated an agreement on the automatic exchange of financial account information, aimed at improving international tax cooperation and compliance. i voted in favour because i find that this agreement represents an important step in ongoing efforts to clamp down on tax fraud and tax evasion and upgrades the 2004 agreement that ensured that monaco applied measures equivalent to those in an eu directive on the taxation of savings income. under the new agreement, the eu member states and monaco will automatically exchange information on the financial accounts held on their territories by each other’s residents. the aim is to address situations where a taxpayer seeks to hide capital representing income or assets for which taxes have not been paid.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a decision of the european parliament and of the council on the mobilisation of the european globalisation adjustment fund application from belgium hainaut machinery. the european globalisation adjustment fund is implemented as an expression of the solidarity of the european union, which is one of the foundations on which the community was built. with today's approval by the plenary, € 1 824 041 will help 488 overworked workers from three companies in the manufacture of other machinery and equipment in the belgian region of hainaut and 300 young people who are not in employment, education or training and are under 25 years of age. it is very important that training is aligned with the needs of the region and neighbouring regions and that attention is paid to the needs of older workers. older workers are at greater risk of becoming long-term unemployed and socially excluded and therefore have specific needs that need to be taken into account in support.
in writing. ‒ the european globalisation adjustment fund was established to provide additional assistance to workers affected by the consequences of major structural changes in world trade flows. i supported the proposal to use the european globalisation adjustment fund. in the case of belgium, 488 workers were made redundant during the reference period from 25 december 2014 to 25 september 2015 and 300 young unemployed persons were made redundant. in recent years, trade in construction machinery within the union has suffered serious disruptions due to a decline in public and private investment in infrastructure. this has led to a dramatic loss of market share for european producers, coupled with a significant increase in steel prices in europe. workers aged 55 to 64 years represent 35,9% of all european globalisation adjustment fund target beneficiaries, as they are at higher risk of long-term unemployment and social exclusion.

in writing. ‒ the european union is a contracting party to the international commission for the conservation of atlantic tunas (iccat) and the regional fisheries management organisation (rfmo) responsible for the management of tuna and tuna-like species in the atlantic ocean and adjacent seas. while the commission proposal broadly reflects the relevant iccat recommendations, in some cases it goes beyond iccat decisions and even eu sectoral legislation. bluefin tuna is of major economic importance to the european union, especially to the mediterranean member states. although the catch is quite small, bluefin tuna is highly prized in the japanese market, where prices are consequently astronomical. the report concerns the modified form of the iccat plan, describes the improvement of the control of stocks, restrictions and types of fishing gear. the proposal for a regulation includes technical measures such as those relating to the transfer and rearing activities of live bluefin tuna in cages, including measures relating to the use of stereoscopic cameras to assess bluefin tuna quantities and releases, catch reporting requirements and the implementation of the iccat regional observer programme. the report stresses that the european union should pay particular attention to traditional traps, which contribute to the recovery of tuna stocks, as they are highly selective in the implementation of the recovery plan. i think the report is good, which is why i supported it.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council establishing a multiannual recovery plan for bluefin tuna in the eastern atlantic and mediterranean and repealing the regulation. the report contains technical measures to ensure uniform and effective implementation of all measures of the recovery plan adopted between 2012 and 2014. for example, the proposal contains a measure concerning the transfer and rearing of live bluefin tuna in cage nets. in 2006, the international commission for the conservation of atlantic tunas adopted a multiannual bluefin tuna recovery plan, which runs until 2022.
in writing. ‒ i support the current proposal for a regulation to transpose the bluefin tuna recovery plan in the eastern atlantic and mediterranean into union law. in 2006, the international commission for the conservation of atlantic tunas adopted a multiannual recovery plan for bluefin tuna, which expires in 2022. to restore the stock, the plan provides for a gradual reduction in the total allowable catch from 2007 to 2011, fishing limits in certain areas and periods, new minimum sizes, measures relating to sport and recreational fishing activities and fishing capacity. the proposal also contains technical measures on the use of stereoscopic cameras to estimate bluefin tuna quantities. the role of traditional and craft tools and techniques in the conservation of stocks is important. in implementing the recovery plan, the european union should pay particular attention to those tools and techniques which have contributed to the recovery of bluefin tuna stocks.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of report on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on a multiannual recovery plan for bluefin tuna in the eastern atlantic and the mediterranean repealing regulation (ec) no 302/2009. the european union is contracting party to the international commission for the conservation of atlantic tunas (iccat), the regional fisheries management organisation (rfmo) responsible for the management of tuna and tuna-like species in the atlantic ocean and adjoining seas. bluefin tuna is the most important species regulated by iccat. the proposal contains technical measures such as those on transfer and caging operations of live bluefin tuna, including also measures on the use of stereoscopic cameras to estimate the quantities of bluefin tuna and releases, catch reporting requirements, and the implementation of the iccat regional observer programme.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council establishing a multiannual recovery plan for bluefin tuna in the eastern atlantic and mediterranean and repealing the regulation. the proposal for a regulation lays down general rules for the application of the recovery plan, taking into account the specific characteristics of the different types of fishing gear and paying particular attention to traditional, more sustainable and artisanal gear.
in writing. ‒ in october 2014, the european commission published a multiannual plan for the cod, herring and sprat stocks in the baltic sea and the fisheries exploiting these stocks. the proposal aims to establish a framework for the management of cod, herring and sprat stocks in the baltic sea, where fisheries are mainly directed at these three species. in recent years cod, herring and sprat have accounted for more than 94% of the catches in the baltic sea. the baltic sea is a nearly closed body of water in which these three species are ubiquitous and constantly interacting with each other. it is therefore essential that the european union has a well-regulated area to allow for interactions between the species covered by the plan, including the impact of cod on herring and sprat stocks and vice versa. the report was considerably weakened compared to the draft. for example, it allows fishing in quantities higher than those limited by the common fisheries policy, which is unacceptable. although the report explicitly mentions the good environmental status of the marine strategy framework directive and also allows for the restriction of fishing gear in order to conserve non-commercial fish species, which i support, i think the report is rather poor. that is why i voted against the adoption of this one.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council establishing a multiannual plan for the cod, herring and sprat stocks and the fisheries exploiting those stocks in the baltic sea, amending regulation no 2187/2005 and repealing regulation no 1098/2007. i support the commission's 2014 multiannual plan, which published a multiannual plan for the stocks of herring and sprat in the baltic sea and the fisheries exploiting those stocks. it has thus established a multi-species management framework for the cod, herring and sprat stocks in the baltic sea, where fisheries are mainly directed towards these three species. the baltic sea is a nearly closed body of water in which these three species are ubiquitous and constantly interacting with each other.
in writing. ‒ i supported the proposal for a regulation establishing a multiannual plan for cod, herring and sprat stocks in the baltic sea and the fisheries exploiting those stocks. multiannual plans are a fundamental tool for the sustainable management or recovery of fish stocks. such long-term approaches are not only intended to improve the conservation of stocks but also to increase predictability for fishermen in the long term. the multiannual management plan is an instrument to ensure the sustainable exploitation of fish stocks and marine ecosystems. the purpose of multiannual plans is to maintain the size of stocks within safe biological limits. they shall set out the maximum allowable catches and the type of technical measures, taking into account the characteristics of each stock and the effects of the economic measures on the fisheries concerned.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of report on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council establishing a multiannual plan for the stocks of cod, herring and sprat in the baltic sea and the fisheries exploiting those stocks, amending council regulation (ec) no 2187/2005 and repealing council regulation (ec) no 1098/2007. the aim of the plan is to establish a framework for the multispecies management of the stocks of cod, herring and sprat in the baltic sea, where fishing primarily targets these three species. cod, herring and sprat account for over 94 % of baltic catches in the recent years. the baltic sea is a virtually closed body of water in which these three species are omnipresent and interact continuously. therefore, it is of utmost importance to deliver regulation making it possible to recognize interactions between the species covered, inter alia the cod's influence on herring and sprat stocks and the other way round. i voted in favour because i believe that the plan provides for a balanced, sustainable exploitation of those stocks and the stability of fishing opportunities – and thereby of the livelihoods of fishers.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council establishing a multiannual plan for the cod, herring and sprat stocks and the fisheries exploiting those stocks in the baltic sea, amending regulation no 2187/2005 and repealing regulation no 1098/2007. the proposal for a regulation contributes to the objectives of the common sustainable fisheries policy as set out in article 2 of regulation (eu) no 1380/2013, in particular by applying the precautionary approach to fisheries management. its purpose is to ensure that, when exploiting living marine biological resources, populations of harvested species are restored and maintained above levels that allow maximum sustainable yield.
in writing. ‒ this proposal for a council regulation on jurisdiction, applicable law and the recognition and enforcement of judgments in matrimonial matters is the second in this field. the report states that the proposal for a regulation on matrimonial property regime is in the clear interest of the union and of international couples within it. the regulation will remove many instances of ambiguity and legal uncertainty. in the areas of recognition, enforceability and enforcement of decisions in matrimonial property matters, the current text is largely based on the european parliament's position of 2013. it thus summarises the very precise provisions of regulation no 650/2012 on cross-border succession. even if recognition is automatic, the decision is therefore enforceable only after a declaration of enforceability has been obtained in the member state concerned. however, a declaration of enforceability may be refused only in very specific cases, such as when enforcement is contrary to public policy. in view of the above, i welcome the report on jurisdiction, applicable law and the recognition and enforcement of judgments in matrimonial property matters, and have therefore supported it.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a council regulation on jurisdiction, applicable law and the recognition and enforcement of judgments in matrimonial matters. in the area of matrimonial property regimes, the regulation covers jurisdiction and the law applicable, as well as the recognition and enforcement of judgments, but excludes in particular matters of the legal capacity and capacity of the spouses, the existence, validity and recognition of the marriage, maintenance obligations and succession. the member states will thus continue to have autonomy as regards family law.
in writing. ‒ i supported the proposal for a regulation governing the jurisdiction of the judiciary, the applicable legislation and the recognition and enforcement of judgments in matters of matrimonial property regimes. in order to preserve the autonomy of the member states in the area of family law, the regulation does not cover areas such as the legal capacity of the spouses, the existence, validity or recognition of a marriage, maintenance obligations or the succession of the estate of a deceased spouse. nor does the regulation affect or interfere with the substantive law of the member states on matrimonial property regimes. it is provided that, if a member state does not recognise the marriage, the courts of that member state are to be given a discretion which confers jurisdiction in the matter on the courts of the other member state which recognises that marriage. the proposal also respects the principle of the unity of the law applicable to the matrimonial property regime, which applies to all immovable property under this regime regardless of where it is situated. the regulation allows the choice of the law applicable to the property consequences between spouses, but this choice is limited by the requirement that the spouses are nationals of, or at least habitually resident in, the country whose law has been chosen. the regulation also provides for means of communicating the necessary and basic legal information to international couples.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a council regulation on jurisdiction, applicable law and the recognition and enforcement of judgments in matrimonial matters. i believe that the regulation will remove many instances of ambiguity and legal uncertainty for international couples within the european union. in the area of matrimonial property regimes, it covers jurisdiction and the law applicable, as well as the recognition and enforcement of judgments. in particular, questions of the legal capacity and capacity of the spouses, the existence, validity and recognition of marriage, maintenance obligations and succession are excluded from its scope. it also preserves the autonomy of the member states in the field of family law.
in writing. ‒ this proposal for a council regulation on jurisdiction, applicable law and the recognition and enforcement of judgments in matters of property consequences of registered partnerships is the second of its kind. after the negotiations between the member states have come to a standstill, the proposal is returned to parliament in the form of enhanced cooperation. the part on the applicable law is universally applicable and thus also allows the application of the law of third countries. the principle of the unity of the applicable law, according to which the law on the property consequences of registered partnerships applies to all property within the partnership, regardless of its location, is the greatest advance in this respect. this eliminates the system of division of the legal status of the property of couples. the regulation allows for a choice of law applicable to the property consequences of a registered partnership, but the choice is limited, since citizenship or habitual residence must be held in the country chosen. the difference between this proposal and the proposal for a regulation on matrimonial property regimes is that registered partners will be able to choose the law of the country in which the partnership is registered. the report stresses that the proposed regulation on the property consequences of registered partnerships is in the interest of international couples living in the eu, as it will remove many instances of ambiguity and legal uncertainty. that is why i voted for the report.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a council regulation on jurisdiction, applicable law and the recognition and enforcement of decisions in matters of property consequences of registered partnerships. the regulation also clearly defines, inter alia, the court with jurisdiction to hear and determine claims relating to the property consequences of registered partnerships. i also supported the report because the regulation covers jurisdiction and applicable law, as well as the recognition and enforcement of judgments in matters of property consequences of registered partnerships, but excludes from its scope, in particular, questions of legal and business capacity of partners.
in writing. ‒ i supported the proposal for a regulation governing jurisdiction, applicable law and the recognition and enforcement of decisions in matters of matrimonial property regime. the scope of the regulation does not cover matters such as the legal capacity of partners, the existence, validity or recognition of a partnership, maintenance obligations or the inheritance of the estate of a deceased partner. the autonomy of the member states in the field of family law is therefore preserved. nor does the regulation affect or interfere with the substantive law of the member states on registered partnerships and property regimes. the regulation clearly defines the court with jurisdiction to rule on the property consequences of registered partnerships. moreover, it provides that, if a member state does not recognise a partnership, the courts of that member state are to be given a discretion which confers jurisdiction in the matter on the courts of the other member states which recognise that partnership. the proposal also respects the principle of the unity of the applicable legislation, whereby the law on the property consequences of registered partnerships applies to all property created during the partnership, regardless of where it is located.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a council regulation on jurisdiction, applicable law and the recognition and enforcement of decisions in matters of property consequences of registered partnerships. the regulation, inter alia, clearly defines which court has jurisdiction to rule on claims relating to the property consequences of registered partnerships and i believe that it will remove many instances of ambiguity and legal uncertainty for international couples within the european union.
in writing. ‒ in the area around the city of beni in the east of the democratic republic of the congo, more than 600 civilians have been brutally murdered with machetes, axes and knives since 2014, including women, children and even infants. at the same time, armed groups have not only used sexual violence as a weapon of war but have also recruited child soldiers. the great inability to bring human rights violators to justice has resulted in a great deal of impunity and new crimes. the fighting in eastern congo stems from multiple sources, including ethnic conflict, political discontent, and regional geopolitics. this unreliable mix is further exacerbated by the lack of resources in the impoverished region. in view of all this, we, the members of the european parliament, have decided to adopt a resolution condemning the continuing attacks by armed groups and the use of extreme violence against the population of the democratic republic of the congo in the eastern provinces and calling on all relevant authorities to take immediate action and bring the perpetrators to justice. the resolution calls on the prosecutor of the international criminal court to gather information and examine abuses to determine whether an investigation by the international criminal court into alleged crimes in the beni area is necessary. in view of all this, i welcome the resolution and have supported it.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the joint motion for a resolution on the massacres in eastern congo. i support the call in the resolution for all parties to the conflict to end violence immediately, to lay down their arms and to release all children from their families, while at the same time beginning to promote dialogue for a peaceful and lasting solution to the conflict. the security and human rights situation in the drc has recently continued to deteriorate due to the activities of dozens of armed groups. the priority of the government of the democratic republic of the congo should be to disarm armed groups and to establish lasting security and peace for all citizens.
in writing. ‒ i supported the motion for a resolution on the massacres in eastern congo. in the area around the city of beni in the east of the democratic republic of the congo, more than 600 civilians have been brutally murdered with machetes, axes and knives since 2014, including women, children and even infants. these massacres are the worst violence in the country in a decade, and neither the congolese authorities nor the monusco mission have officially investigated. in the more than ten years of conflict in eastern congo, civilians have been systematically attacked by a number of armed groups. they used sexual violence as a weapon of war and recruited child soldiers. the great inability to bring human rights violators to justice has led to a great deal of impunity and new crimes. the fighting in eastern congo stems from multiple sources, including ethnic conflict, political discontent and regional geopolitics, and this precarious mix is exacerbated by the resource shortages in the impoverished region. the informal or artisanal mining sector accounts for almost one fifth of the country's economic output and employs one million congolese, while also providing a source of profit for rebels and corrupt government soldiers, as well as for traders from neighbouring countries who trade directly or through local armed allies. the peace process is hampered by the unsuccessful efforts of the drc to demobilize thousands of rebel fighters, either by incorporating them into the national army or by assisting them in their integration into civilian life.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the resolutions on massacres in eastern congo. the resolution recalls the commitment made by the drc under the cotonou agreement to respecting democracy, the rule of law and human rights principles. the resolution condemns all attacks against humanitarian actors and impediments to humanitarian access and urges all parties to the conflict to respect the independence, neutrality and impartiality of humanitarian actors. the resolution equally calls the eu to intensify its dialogue with the drc and to focus its development cooperation on building better governance and improving the weak military, police and judicial system in the country. the resolution considers that the relevant authorities and the international community must prioritise putting an end to the phenomenon of child soldiers. i voted in favour because i strongly believe that the massacres and crimes against humanity which are still going on in eastern congo should be stopped promptly.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the joint motion for a resolution on the massacres in eastern congo. the security and human rights situation in the eastern part of the drc continues to deteriorate, with dozens of armed groups still active in the area, and with numerous reports of massacres, recruitment and use of children by armed groups, and widespread sexual and gender-based violence. i therefore support the call for all parties to the conflict to end violence immediately, to lay down their arms, to release all children from their families and to begin to promote dialogue for a peaceful and lasting solution to the conflict.
in writing. ‒ the last decade has seen a sharp increase in the number of people entering formal education, while europe is still plagued by unprecedented levels of youth unemployment, which also affect graduates. between 2011 and 2014, the average unemployment rate in the eu increased most among young people. the report on the follow-up to the strategic framework for european cooperation in education and training is divided into three parts, the strategic framework, the quality of education and training and migration and education. in this way, the report fails to take account of the main challenges in the field of education and training in europe, as it does not follow a holistic approach. moreover, despite the fact that the report has an entire chapter dedicated to migration and education, it does not even touch on the challenges associated with refugees. in addition, the report lacks a stronger link between education, entrepreneurship and research, as well as the involvement of the social partners and civil society. although the report emphasises that education is good for personal and consequently social growth over economic well-being, i believe that the recommendations are rather unbalanced and promote a traditional view of society. on the basis of the above, i consider that the report does not contribute to the further development of agenda 2020 and therefore i voted against the adoption of the report.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the further examination of the strategic framework for european cooperation in education and training. education and training should be a value in itself, not just aimed at meeting labour market needs. i agree with the report that welcomes the et 2020 status review, while stressing that the conclusions of this review should be taken into account and implemented without delay in order to increase the added value of the framework and optimise its effectiveness and enhance country-specific relevance and mutual learning. i also agree that very serious problems in the field of education and training remain unresolved in terms of quality, accessibility and socioeconomic discrimination.
in writing. ‒ at a time of high youth unemployment, which also affects graduates, the most important step is to evaluate the european et2020 framework in order to increase its added value and optimise its effectiveness. i therefore supported the motion for a resolution on the continuation of the strategic framework for european cooperation in education and training. the resolution contains a number of political priorities and positive recommendations.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on follow-up to the strategic framework for european cooperation in education and training (et2020). the stocktaking exercise on the et2020 framework was conducted in 2014 by the commission in cooperation with the member states. the report urges that greater attention be devoted to the quality of education, starting in the kindergarten and throughout life. it calls for the development of good practices in assessing qualitative progress and investment in the use of quality data with stakeholders at local, regional and national level. the report emphasises the importance of providing high-quality early childhood education and of its timely modernisation. it calls on the member states to channel investment into inclusive education that responds to societal challenges with regard to ensuring equal access and opportunities for all. i voted in favour because i believe that education and training are important in helping people to acquire the knowledge and professional skills they need to become competitive and innovative employees.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the further examination of the strategic framework for european cooperation in education and training. education and training must be adapted to labour market needs, as this is the only way to help increase the employment of young and old people and strengthen the economy. at the same time, education and training must also contribute to the development of the individual's ethical and civic competences and humanistic values. member states should focus investment on inclusive education that responds to societal challenges and enhances lifelong learning opportunities.
in writing. ‒ the development of renewable energy requires a new approach that will make it a fundamental pillar of the european union's energy model. the fight against climate change is our fundamental responsibility and a historic duty that we must fulfil. we also need to reduce our dependence on energy sources from other parts of the world if we are to consolidate our production model and create quality jobs and lead the development of strategic technologies for the energy transition. the transition to a sustainable energy production model is a social priority that cannot be addressed from a market perspective alone. for this reason, we must understand that regulation and democratic participation are necessary to prevent serious social and environmental externalities. we must prevent energy oligopolies from determining the future of europe's energy. it is important that we try to achieve the goal of having an economy based on 100% renewable energy. the report underlines the importance of binding targets at national level and the need for a stable policy framework. the report calls for more ambitious targets for 2030 and for countries that are lagging behind in renewable energy to be highlighted. at the initiative of the greens, the report also reinforces the future of energy management and clearly defines the reporting requirements of countries in this area. that's why i supported the report.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the progress report on renewable energy. the european union's 2020 renewable energy targets are ambitious and the european union as a whole is well on track to meet them, but there are still significant reservations in some member states. the commission should therefore ensure that the 2020 renewable energy directive is fully implemented, while providing a strong legal framework beyond 2020 with binding renewable energy targets that are aligned with the most effective way to achieve the union's long-term climate objectives.
in writing. ‒ i supported the progress report on renewable energy. the european union is well on track to reach its 20% green energy share target. the report demonstrates that europe is good at green energy and green energy is good for europe. renewable energy sources are one of the most effective ways of reducing dependence on fossil fuels and contribute to the creation of a low-carbon economy. in addition, renewable energy sources are cost-effective, increase market competitiveness and promote diversity. however, there is a need to improve national policies and the commission needs to strengthen its role in monitoring and supporting progress in the field of renewable energy.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the renewable energy progress report. the report stresses the importance of simple, accessible, affordable and efficient administrative procedures. the development of renewable energies calls for a new approach that entails making them the main pillar of the european union’s energy model. the report highlights the significance of an eu legislative proposal on energy market rules, as a more integrated market is key to the development of renewables and to reducing energy costs for families and industry. in addition, the report notes that increased regional cooperation on renewables is key to ensuring the further development of renewable energy sources. i voted in favour because i believe that we have a fundamental responsibility to combat climate change – a historic duty that we must fulfil.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the progress report on renewable energy. in accordance with article 194 tfeu, european energy policy is to ensure the functioning of the energy market and the security of energy supply, and to promote energy efficiency, energy saving and the development of renewable energy sources, as well as the interconnection of energy networks. i therefore agree with the conclusions of the report that future legislation and measures must be based on renewable energy, which will allow the full market representation of technologies for this energy.
in writing. ‒ in the european union, greenhouse gas emissions fell by 23% between 1990 and 2014. at the same time, eu gdp increased by 46%. businesses and citizens are increasingly generating growth, jobs and tax revenues, while at the same time reducing their climate impact, which is good news. the european union is on track to meet its 2020 targets, largely thanks to a successful emissions trading system. this not only encourages emission reductions but also investment in energy-efficient technologies. the economic and financial crisis in some countries undoubtedly contributed to the achievement of the targets. the european union's success in reducing greenhouse gases is commendable, but that does not mean that more could not be done to improve energy efficiency. the report under discussion is a good one, as it calls on the european commission to set a binding target of reducing greenhouse gases by 40% by 2030, thus following the targets agreed in paris at cop 21. that is why i voted for the report.
in writing. ‒ i voted against the report on the report on the implementation of the energy efficiency directive. this is a very important report and mr pieper has done a great job of reaching a compromise. but i voted against the report because, within the amendment vote, there were a few amendments voted on which call on the commission to set a binding 40% energy efficiency target for 2030 which will reflect the potential for cost-effective energy efficiency, which i cannot agree with. it would be much better to set a target of at least 30% of energy efficiency improvements by 2030 to achieve a higher target of 40% reflecting the full economic potential.
in writing. ‒ energy policy is of great importance to the european union. we are on track to achieve our 20% efficiency target by 2020, despite the fact that the directive has not been fully implemented in most member states. this demonstrates that energy efficiency is in the interest of businesses and households. the report contains a number of positive points such as the importance of energy efficiency in achieving our climate goals, the flexibility in article 7, the need for better monitoring and clarification of the definition of smes, and the state aid rules. i still rejected the directive. the directive places too much emphasis on energy saving rather than energy efficiency. because of the key elements that were not adopted, i cannot support this report either.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the implementation report on the energy efficiency directive. the report emphasises that improving energy efficiency is crucial to achieving our climate targets. the report stresses that this is essential to start the transition towards a more sustainable energy system based on renewables and away from fossil fuels as soon as possible. the report recalls that the transition towards a more sustainable energy is also vital to job creation and sustainable growth. i voted in favour of the report because i strongly believe that the implementation of the energy efficiency directive is a major progress towards achieving the eu’s climate and energy targets.
in writing. ‒ improving energy efficiency and energy savings are important for protecting the environment and climate, enhancing economic competitiveness, creating new jobs and ensuring energy security. this can be achieved by promoting energy efficiency through tax reductions and additional funding. the report on the implementation of the energy efficiency directive, as advocated by the left (with a binding target of 40% savings by 2030 for individual member states), is unrealistic and does not contribute to more efficient use of energy. the result of such a binding target could be a large increase in energy prices and the establishment of building quotas that neither local authorities nor residents can afford.
in writing. brexit has made a deep dent in the perception of the future of the european union. the days following the referendum paint a picture of confusion, even misunderstanding, and the question of what really happened hangs in the air. it turned out that many people did not know what they were really saying, and that by casting their votes, they were deciding the future destiny of entire generations. i believe that the main thing to do is to make room for the constructive dialogue that europe urgently needs in this situation. the resolution adopted by the european parliament calls for the early activation of article 50 of the lisbon treaty, although it is clear that only the british can do this themselves. the text should reflect the real situation and be much more forward-looking. we need clear commitments to fundamentally change the way the eu operates, which must return to citizens and put them at the heart of its actions. but it is true that britain is not going anywhere, it will still be somewhere between 20 and 20 miles, the narrowest part between the british isles and mainland europe, and it will not move an inch forward or backward. but it can go a long way towards understanding democracy, the will of the people and the concept of the referendum as the broadest instrument for taking account of the will of the people.
in writing. i regret that the british people have decided to leave the european union. of course, we all hoped it wouldn't come to that. we knew that the decision for or against would not be rational, but emotional. that's why it was impossible to predict the outcome with any certainty. this decision is not only important from an economic point of view, but it is above all a symbolic message. initial reactions in financial markets suggest that the withdrawal will not go unchallenged. not for the eu, not for the uk, which by all accounts will be the big loser of this decision. but there's no going back. it's a british decision, and we have to respect that decision. it has proved what i had pointed out before the referendum, that britain is not just the city of london and that the will of the people cannot be underestimated. what will happen to the european union? we'll see in the coming months, years. we do not need more europe, but a better europe. a europe that respects the will of the people and responds to their demands. a europe that is able to identify and respond to real problems. a europe where rights and obligations are part of the same package. the british referendum was a sobering reminder that the european union as it is is not, by definition, destined to remain forever.
in writing. ‒ brexit has made a deep dent in the perception of the future of the european union. unfortunately, there is a rhetoric of blaming, excluding and pointing fingers among members of the european parliament. i believe that the main thing to do is to make room for the constructive dialogue that europe urgently needs in this situation. at this point, nothing is clear except the great uncertainty both on the european continent and in the british isles. the resolution adopted by the european parliament calls for the early activation of article 50 of the lisbon treaty, although it is clear that only the british can do this themselves. the text should reflect the real situation and be much more forward-looking. we need clear commitments to fundamentally change the way the eu operates, which must return to citizens and put them at the heart of its actions. i regret that the resolution on brexit does not reflect this, and i therefore abstained.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the resolution on the decision to leave the eu resulting from the referendum in the united kingdom. the official data clearly shows that if only the young voters' votes were taken into account, the uk would remain in the european union, which is a very clear signal that young people, who are already struggling with unemployment, continue to want the right to live, study and work in the 27 countries. unfortunately, the populists have been much louder, pointing the finger at the european union, claiming that it is the main culprit for all the problems, which is of course not true. as soon as the results were announced, we were confronted with the negative consequences of the referendum on financial markets, most notably the fall of the pound to its lowest level since 1985 and the fall in consumption and investment. also, the rating agencies have in recent days downgraded the uk's credit rating to negative. we need a united response, not one that is judgmental, not one that is finger pointing, but one that is constructive and forward-looking. we can't just bury our heads in the sand and pretend like nothing happened, but we need to do some self-reflection.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the european parliament's joint resolution on the outcome of the referendum in the united kingdom. i deeply regret the outcome, but i believe that the decision of the people must be respected and that the process of the united kingdom's withdrawal from the european union must therefore be started as soon as possible.
in writing. ‒ i supported the resolution on the decision to leave the eu resulting from the referendum in the united kingdom. i agree that the future of the union needs to be considered and i believe that we must protect the integrity of the union and its citizens by promoting common values, ensuring stability and social security, providing jobs and effectively addressing the challenges of migration. therefore, the notification provided for in article 50 teu should be issued as soon as possible in order to avoid uncertainty to the detriment of all.
the refugee crisis is also a political crisis today, and despite the fact that a long time has passed since the first wave of refugees began, some basic questions remain unanswered. namely, how many refugees can europe help, and how many migrants can europe employ? there are no easy answers, of course, but running away from them will not bring better solutions. of course, we are a social europe and we want and want to help all those who are fleeing war, but we must also be realistic and realise that there is no single recipe for integrating refugees into the labour market. because of course the labour markets in different countries are not the same, they need new labour in one place and have problems in another because they have too many unemployed. if we are not able to separate the different situations of individual countries, i think we will not be able to achieve this goal of actually helping those who really need help.
so we're facing one of the most complex challenges of recent times, we're facing the biggest displacement since world war ii, and, of course, the integration of these people, refugees, into society also depends on their inclusion in the labor market. it is therefore necessary to support and open up new sources of funding that will encourage a greater and more active employment policy and the integration of these groups of so-called humanitarian refugees. but we cannot, of course, pass by the building of so-called educational bridges, because education is also one of the key elements for better inclusion. of course, practices vary from country to country, and i think we should support and emulate those practices that are positive, good. it is true that the unemployment situation differs across european countries, which should be taken into account. above all, the worst thing would be if refugees also became a category of the permanently unemployed.
the youth guarantee and the youth employment initiative are certainly two very useful measures implemented by the european union and can greatly help the generation that is facing the greatest problems in employment today, namely the young. we must also be aware that the employment of young people is also very much dependent on the member states, which must, through the reform of the education system, the integration of education, research and the economy, create the conditions in which these jobs will be created. i therefore fully support this directive to analyse in detail how these funds are used, but also to look at good practice and then, country by country, to identify which and how this measure will be most effective in each country. we need not only talk about the responsibility of the european union, but also, to a large extent, about the responsibility of the member states, which often fail at this level.
in writing. the youth guarantee programme was a new approach to tackling youth unemployment, which we endorsed with the aim of ensuring long-term employment for young people. however, i wonder whether the member states are actually implementing the measures of the programme as they should and whether the programme is achieving its purpose. a recent survey of young people in slovenia has produced worrying results. young people are very critical of the implementation of the programme, as less than 10% of young people actually got a job after the programme ended. they also feel that some courses are unusable, inappropriate and not tailored to the individual. i am not aware of surveys in other member states. but what can we learn from this? there is an urgent need to increase the involvement of all stakeholders and to strengthen the control of the implementation of the programmes. i also believe that, as a complement to the youth guarantee, the implementation of reforms and the improvement of education and training systems is essential.
in writing. recently, the eu youth employment rate has improved, with around 4.4 million under-25 unemployed in february 2016, up from around 5 million until recently. but it is difficult to assess whether the improvement is linked to the youth guarantee and the youth employment initiative or whether it is due to other circumstances. for example, the court of auditors' special report of the end of 2015 on measures in the field of youth employment estimates that the expenditure of funds was not sufficiently focused on results. these two mechanisms were proposed at a time when the rate of youth unemployment in the eu was extremely high and showed no signs of decreasing. as rapporteur for the els legislative opinion group, i was involved in the increase in pre-financing under the youth employment initiative last year. this represented about €1 billion for half a million young people in 20 eu countries. last year i stressed the importance of using resources efficiently. the european commission should monitor spending so that the money really benefits the end users, the unemployed young people, and not the bureaucrats and middlemen. member states must demonstrate that the activities financed by both mechanisms have actually led to an increase in youth employment.

in writing. ‒ i supported the report on the extension of the emission limit values to other motor vehicles and non-road vehicles. the proposal thus covers, for example, construction machinery, locomotives, as well as propulsion units in inland waterway transport. together, such engines produce as much as 15% of nitrogen oxides emissions and 5% of pm emissions, and therefore regulation and setting of limit values for such engines is necessary. the report strikes a balance between health and environmental issues on the one hand and the competitiveness of the eu manufacturing industry, the jobs and the knowledge it brings, on the other. the health and safety of eu citizens, especially those who work with machinery on a daily basis and are particularly exposed to pollutant emissions, are given the highest priority. i agree with the rapporteur, who is positive that the issue is being addressed in the framework of the regulation, thereby providing the industry with a more stable regulatory environment, which is essential for long-term development and production planning. the report proposal also reduces administrative obligations and guidance on the use of the existing internal market information system, which is more favourable than the introduction of a new administrative arrangement. the commission has also proposed that the european parliament and the council adopt a common position on the proposal for a regulation on the protection of the environment in the event of a natural disaster.
in writing. ‒ i supported the resolution because of the need to adopt a separate set of rules to fully take into account the specific requirements related to engines for non-road mobile machinery that followed the new regulatory approach to the type-approval of engines. the resolution lays down the basic provisions on gaseous and solid pollutant emissions and type-approval for internal combustion engines for non-road mobile machinery. in this way, harmonised rules for eu type-approval of engines for non-road mobile machinery will ensure the functioning of the internal market in this field and follow the commitments to reduce emissions and ensure air quality, thereby limiting adverse health effects.
in writing. ‒ the proposal sets conditions in relation to emission limit values and type-approval for internal combustion engines for non-road mobile machinery. the legislation covers a wide range of engines, which are major contributors to air pollution and are responsible for around 15% of nitrogen oxides and 5% of particulate matter emissions in the european union. compared with existing legislation, this proposal introduces new thresholds that better reflect technological progress as well as the european union's road policy. although the report is less ambitious than the original proposal on limiting nitrous oxide for inland waterways, it still represents a major step forward in limiting pollution from engine categories. in this context, i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on emission limit values and type-approval requirements for internal combustion engines for non-road mobile machinery.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on emission limit values and type-approval requirements for internal combustion engines for non-road mobile machinery. non-road mobile machinery is one of the factors contributing to harmful emissions in the form of gases or particulates. it is important to recognise that many urban areas in the european union today do not fully meet air quality standards. i also support the proposals for amendments to the regulation, in particular the amendment which stresses that, in addition to reducing market distortions, the purpose of this regulation is to simplify the applicable legal framework, including measures to simplify administrative procedures.
in writing. ‒ i supported the proposal for a regulation on emission limit values and type-approval requirements for internal combustion engines for non-road mobile machinery. the proposal aims to establish new requirements to reduce emissions of harmful substances from engines incorporated in non-road mobile machinery. the proposal covers a wide range of different types of internal combustion engines, which are responsible for around 15% of nitrogen oxide and 5% of particulate matter emissions in the eu, and introduces new emission limit values. these are rather severe restrictions, but still reasonable enough to allow the industry to comply with the new requirements. the regulation maintains a balanced approach between protecting the environment and safeguarding the competitiveness of eu industry. the new rules will simplify the implementation phase of the introduction of new emission limit values and type-approval procedures, with a view to reducing the burden on manufacturers. the exchange of data and information will also be facilitated through the use of the internal market information system. the proposal also allows the possibility of replacing old non-road mobile machinery engines that have failed with engines of the same type within a certain time limit, where the replacement using a new and improved engine type is incompatible with the older model.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on requirements relating to emission limits and type-approval for internal combustion engines for non-road mobile machinery. the regulation aims to help address the public health concern created by studies identifying ultra-fine particles as a carcinogenic substance, to generally improve air quality and to create a market without barriers not only within the eu but also with our main trade partners around the world. today, several eu urban areas do not fully meet the air-quality standards and the problem is growing, as more people are attracted to live in conglomerations. i voted in favour because i believe that technological progress can justify stricter regulation without putting undue pressure on the manufacturing industry.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the recommendation as the conclusion of the protocol will allow for a gradual opening-up and enhanced participation in certain union programmes for azerbaijan. this provides an opportunity to foster further cultural, educational, environmental, technical and scientific links, to strengthen people-to-people contacts and to enhance sectoral cooperation. the protocol also lays down the financial and technical rules enabling azerbaijan to participate in certain european union programmes addressed to the enp countries. currently, the situation with azerbaijan is changing for the better, as evidenced by the release of several human rights activists, and this should be used for new joint projects and cooperation. the committee on foreign affairs also gave a favourable opinion in favour of the recommendation.
in writing. ‒ the cooperation protocol between the european union and azerbaijan aims to establish financial and technical rules to enable azerbaijan to participate in certain european union programmes open to third countries. the specific conditions for the participation of azerbaijan in each programme will be laid down in an agreement between the european commission and the competent authorities of azerbaijan. the gradual opening-up of certain european union programmes to neighbourhood countries was already proposed by the european commission in 2006 and identified as one of the components of the european neighbourhood policy. the council endorsed this approach in 2007 and gave the commission guidance for negotiating a framework agreement with partner countries that will facilitate such cooperation. the approach was re-approved in the 2011 european neighbourhood policy review and is also one of the elements of the eastern partnership to enhance bilateral cooperation. we greens welcome this type of cooperation, but at the same time we want the european union's programmes to be transparent and open. human rights, the rule of law and democracy should remain the foundations on which the cooperation of both partners will be built. i think that the recommendation is generally a good one, and i supported it.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the recommendation on the draft council decision on the framework agreement between the european union and the republic of azerbaijan on the general principles for the participation of the republic of azerbaijan in union programmes. the protocol will establish financial and technical rules to enable azerbaijan to participate in european union programmes open to third countries. i support the gradual opening up of certain union programmes to neighbouring countries, as the commission presented back in 2006. however, relations with neighbouring countries and third world countries must be based on democracy, human rights and the rule of law. the european union must not deviate from this.
in writing. ‒ the draft recommendation addresses the participation of the republic of azerbaijan in union programmes. the protocol contains the framework agreement between the eu and the republic of azerbaijan on the general principles for the participation of the republic of azerbaijan in union programmes and includes the standard provisions contained in such protocols for the european neighbourhood policy countries. the conclusion of the said protocol will allow for the gradual opening up or enhanced participation in certain union programmes for the republic of azerbaijan, thus encouraging further strengthening of cultural, educational, environmental, technical and scientific links. in addition, people-to-people contacts and sectoral cooperation between the union and the republic of azerbaijan will be significantly enhanced. for the above reasons, i supported the recommendation for the conclusion of a framework agreement between the eu and the republic of azerbaijan on the general principles for the participation of the republic of azerbaijan in union programmes.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the recommendation on the draft council decision on the conclusion of a protocol to the partnership and cooperation agreement between the european communities and their member states, of the one part, and the republic of azerbaijan, of the other part, on a framework agreement between the european union and the republic of azerbaijan on the general principles for the participation of the republic of azerbaijan in union programmes. the objective of the protocol is to lay down financial and technical rules enabling azerbaijan to participate in certain european union programmes open to third countries. the specific terms and conditions for the participation of azerbaijan in each particular programme will be then determined in agreement between the commission and the competent authorities in azerbaijan. azerbaijan is also an important energy partner for the eu but the importance of eu-azerbaijan relations is not limited to energy security and the relevance of this partnership should be considered in the context of all aspects of cooperation envisaged in the framework of eastern partnership. i am in favour of this agreement because it aims to promote cooperation and foster people-to-people contacts, which should be beneficial for the society.
in writing. ‒ i supported the recommendation on the draft council decision on the conclusion of the protocol to the partnership and cooperation agreement between the european communities and their member states, of the one part, and the republic of azerbaijan, of the other part, on a framework agreement between the european union and the republic of azerbaijan on the general principles for the participation of the republic of azerbaijan in union programmes. the objective of the protocol is to establish financial and technical rules to enable azerbaijan to participate in certain european union programmes open to third countries. azerbaijan is also an important energy partner of the eu, among other things. i agree that the rule of law, human rights and democracy are key principles on which the eu's relations with third countries must be based. in this respect, the framework agreement in question seeks to promote cooperation within sectors and to foster people-to-people contacts.
in writing. ‒ i supported the above-mentioned amending budget without reservations. the amendment to the current budget includes a surplus of eur 1,349 million from the 2015 budget year, which consequently reduces the contribution of the member states to the current eu budget by the same amount. i expect member states to pay this surplus into the eu trust fund for the prevention of the refugee crisis, to which they have committed themselves for some time. in addition, the member states contributed only eur 82 million to the trust fund for africa and eur 69 million to the madad trust fund for the syrian crisis until this spring, while the union contribution was eur 1,8 billion and more than eur 500 million. in subsequent cases of surpluses in the eu budget, the latter should be used for the financial needs of the eu.

in writing. ‒ i supported the report on the examination of draft amending budget no 2/2016 concerning the surplus for the financial year 2015. the total amount of the surplus resulting from the implementation of the 2015 budget will be transferred to the 2016 budget. this will benefit the eu member states, as the national gni contributions of the member states to the eu budget will be reduced accordingly in relation to the 2015 surplus. the report also calls on the member states to take this opportunity to honour their commitments in relation to the refugee crisis and to align the union contribution to the two dedicated union trust funds. at the same time, the eu budget should be able to reuse at any time surpluses resulting from budgetary implementation failures or fines in order to meet its financing needs.
