in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the council position on the draft amending budget of the european union no 2/2016 for the financial year 2016: inclusion of the surplus from the financial year 2015. the objective of the draft amending budget no 2/2016 is to include in the 2016 budget the surplus of eur 1,349 million from the 2015 budget year. the report notes, inter alia, that the adoption of draft amending budget no 2/2016 will reduce the member states' contribution to the union budget on the basis of gni by eur 1,349 million in 2016 and calls on the member states to take this opportunity to implement their commitments in relation to the refugee crisis by contributing to the union trust fund the amount of the union contribution.
in writing. ‒ i supported the recommendation on the council position on the proposal for a directive on measures to ensure a high common level of security of network and information systems in the eu. the interinstitutional negotiations have in fact led to a compromise which should be supported. the proposal for a directive concerns specific operators, protects existing investments in network and information security and seeks to avoid as far as possible duplication of institutional structures and obligations imposed on market participants. the main objective of the proposal for a directive is to impose obligations on public administrations and market participants, with a particular focus on market participants providing services in the energy, transport, health and financial market infrastructure sectors. the public authorities are responsible for ensuring the sound management of their own networks and information systems.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the recommendation on council measures to ensure a high common level of security of network and information systems across the union. the proposal introduces obligations for member states on network and information security (nis) in a bid to create a level playing field and close existing legislative gaps. in accordance with the recommendation of the committee on the internal market and consumer protection, parliament adopted the council's position without amendments. i see the consensus in adopting the recommendation in the fact that the proposed directive is a well-defined direction towards a higher level of security of network and information systems in the european union.
in writing. ‒ the internet has made it possible to use information systems and services networks widely. in the internal market, these services play a key role in enabling the cross-border movement of goods, services and people. the 2012 public opinion survey showed that as many as 38% of internet users in the european union are concerned about the security of online payments. the proposal requires member states to establish a minimum level of national capabilities, including strategies for the security of network and information systems. at the same time, eu member states should also cooperate in the exchange of information, threats and good practices. the commission proposal has been criticised for containing a number of regulatory standards and for breaching the principle of subsidiarity. but the greens have made good progress in the negotiations on limiting its scope to critical infrastructure only and also on allowing as much flexibility as possible to member states in implementing the directive with existing structures. we also agreed that companies will be required to have security plans and will be required to report on events in network and information systems. i believe that the directive is a good start in this area, but its short-term added value for preventing cyber-attacks is questionable. i voted in favour of the recommendation despite some shortcomings.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the recommendation for second reading on the council's position at first reading with a view to adopting a directive of the european parliament and of the council on measures to ensure a high common level of security of network and information systems in the union. this directive will achieve a higher overall level of network and information security, leading to improved security of the internet and of the private networks and information systems that support the functioning of our society and economy. with greater willingness on the part of member states and better cooperation between them, we will achieve this.
in writing. ‒ the proposal for a directive on measures to ensure a high common level of security of network and information systems in the union was supported in plenary without a vote. the directive lays down measures to improve the security of network and information systems against cyber-attacks, for which national borders do not represent any obstacle. this is crucial given the current fragmented regulatory frameworks, which indicate different levels of preparedness in individual member states of the union. the newly adopted directive will harmonise these safety standards, thus contributing to a better safety of interconnected infrastructures. the rules of the directive also provide, inter alia, for the establishment of a minimum level of protection for network and information systems and the establishment of a strategic cooperation group to exchange information and provide assistance to eu member states in the fight against cyberattacks.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the recommendation for second reading on the council position at first reading with a view to the adoption of a directive of the european parliament and of the council concerning measures for a high common level of security of network and information systems across the union. the aim of the proposed directive is to ensure a high common level of network and information security, which means improving the security of the internet and the private networks and information systems underpinning the functioning of our societies and economies. this will be achieved by requiring the member states to increase their preparedness and improve their cooperation with each other, and by requiring operators of critical infrastructures as well as public administrations to adopt appropriate steps to manage security risks and report serious incidents to the national competent authorities. i voted in favour because i believe that stepping up the fight against cybercrime and building an international cybersecurity policy for the eu is of crucial importance.
in writing. ‒ i supported the recommendation for second reading on the council position at first reading with a view to the adoption of a directive of the european parliament and of the council on measures to ensure a high common level of security of network and information systems in the union. the proposal for a directive introduces additional obligations on the security of network and information networks with a view to creating a level playing field and closing existing legislative gaps.
in writing. ‒ the proposed report was very much welcomed by all. energy efficiency is the best answer to the key challenges ahead. on the one hand, it is reducing climate change, and on the other, it is reducing europe's energy dependence on third countries. i am very pleased that in these 20 years, when europe has been working intensively on this issue, the pluses at a, which indicate the energy efficiency of appliances, have actually been exhausted. this shows that we are moving in the right direction, but it also calls for changes to make such labelling more accurate or clearer for consumers. the report adopted changes, inter alia, the energy efficiency labelling scale for household appliances to a more transparent scale from a to g. it will replace the current scale, which is already becoming obscure for the consumer (a+, a++, a+++) due to the large number of pluses. these changes are expected to take place within five years. i support the proposed amendments, as they give us the opportunity to make progress on the one hand and effective control over the implementation of these measures on the other. indeed, in the past, the accuracy of the information on the labels of these products has been questioned on several occasions.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report because i think it is important for us as consumers to know the energy efficiency of each product. in this way, the consumer's interests are put first, which is reflected in particular in the fact that he can buy more safely, more transparently and more wisely. energy labelling also leads to fairer competition on the market, as price is no longer the first condition for buying a product, as people are increasingly aware of the energy consumption and there is one more mechanism for prosecuting those responsible.
in writing. ‒ energy labelling has been around since its inception, giving citizens a deeper understanding of the environmental impact of products and their life cycle. the assessment of directive 2010/30/ec has revealed a number of shortcomings which, if addressed appropriately, could lead to significant additional energy savings. the purpose of the audit is to facilitate the integration of ict developments that are on the horizon. the report welcomes the european commission's objectives, including the choice of a regulation as the best legal instrument to prevent divergent transposition in the member states. it intends to combine several balances, such as ensuring continuity while promoting development among citizens, industry, and other stakeholders, as well as between firm pragmatism and encouraged ambition and between a focus on technology and social awareness. the revision aims to simplify energy efficiency labelling to make it more understandable for consumers. it is particularly important that the simple energy efficiency labelling ag is maintained and that consumers can return and receive a refund if it is proven that the appliance does not comply with the energy efficiency requirements. unfortunately, for the largest energy consumers, the confusing plus sign remains until 2030. on the basis of the above, i have decided to abstain.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council establishing a framework for energy-efficiency labelling and repealing the directive. a while ago, we were shocked by the emissions scandal that led to a decline in public confidence. therefore, trust must be restored. i support the commission's desire to ensure continuity while promoting development: among citizens, industry and other stakeholders, and with a focus on technology and social awareness. the energy labelling will enable citizens to compare products on their energy efficiency and to make cost-effective and environmentally-conscious purchasing decisions.
in writing. ‒ i did not vote on the proposal for a regulation establishing a framework for energy labelling. i expect the motion to be referred back to the committee responsible for further discussion of the points on which we were unable to reach agreement in plenary. the eu energy label creates added value and helps consumers to find more energy-efficient products. we are able to find solutions on how to change energy efficiency labelling in the future, but we have not yet fully achieved this with this proposal for a regulation. the current energy labelling system is outdated. for household appliances, the rapid technological progress would require a revision of the standard scale from a to g. stricter requirements would encourage manufacturers to further improve the energy efficiency of their products. i regret that most members support the introduction of a mandatory energy efficiency label in visual advertising, which will make advertising more expensive and more complex, and will not add any value to consumers.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council setting a framework for energy efficiency labelling and repealing directive 2010/30/eu. energy labelling is beneficial to the environment, as it allows customers to compare products in terms of their energy efficiency and to take cost-effective and environmentally conscious purchasing decisions. the proposal replaces the current energy labelling framework and introduces a mechanism for the rescaling of energy efficiency classes. the proposal also provides for a product database and lays out the obligations of the economic operators involved. i voted in favour because i believe that a regulation is the best legal instrument to avoid different transpositions in the member states.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council establishing a framework for energy-efficiency labelling and repealing directive 2010/30/eu. energy efficiency is an essential element of the european union's 2030 climate and energy policy framework and is crucial for reducing energy demand and limiting greenhouse gas emissions. energy labelling is environmentally friendly, as it allows customers to compare products with regard to their energy efficiency and to make cost-effective and environmentally-conscious purchasing decisions. the commission proposal thus replaces the current energy labelling framework and establishes a mechanism for the re-evaluation of energy efficiency classes. it also provides for a product database and lays down the obligations of the participating economic operators.
in writing. ‒ i support the proposed regulation on the establishment of a european border and coast guard. the schengen area is one of the greatest and most visible achievements of european integration. but the refugee and migration crisis and the threat posed to this achievement have put this at risk, as many countries have made use of the possibility of border controls at their own borders, the eu's internal borders. in order to preserve the so-called schengen, the protection of the eu's external borders needs to be strengthened and in my view the establishment of a european border and coast guard is the right answer to this. the commission presented this proposal last december, and i think it should have been done earlier. but better late than never. the eu is also responding to criticism that the eu has failed to address the migrant crisis. however, it should be noted that the proposal respects the sovereignty of the member states in border protection, since it provides that the member state concerned must agree with the newly established agency on the operational plan and also issue instructions itself. in the case of return to the country of origin, the objective of the agency is to assist member states in the practical organisation of return operations, without prejudice to the content of return decisions issued by member states.
in writing. ‒ the european agency for the management of operational cooperation at the external borders of the member states of the european union, known as frontex, became operational on 1 may 2005. the basic idea behind frontex was to improve the integrated management of the external borders and the implementation of common rules to promote, coordinate and develop the concept of european border management. parliament has already discussed the future development of frontex on several occasions, including when drafting a resolution on the special report of the european ombudsman on an own-initiative inquiry into frontex. in this resolution, it proposes that provisions on an individual complaints mechanism be included in the review of frontex's mandate, which i regard as positive. on the other hand, some provisions of fundamental rights have disappeared. what bothers me most about the current report is that the agency would have the power to send a coast guard to a member state of the european union without its consent if the european commission considered that that member state had not effectively addressed the shortcomings at the external border of the european union. in addition, the report is weak in the area of fundamental rights and in the area of rescue. i have therefore decided to vote against the report.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on the european border and coast guard and repealing the regulation. the creation of a european border and coast guard will improve the security of our external borders. the migration and refugee crisis has made us realise that our external borders are weak and that we need to modernise the regulatory framework. the european border and coast guard will link the eu external border agency frontex more closely with national authorities, thus enhancing the protection of the european union's external border. this is the only way to restore the schengen system without internal borders.
in writing. ‒ i supported the proposal for a regulation establishing a european border and coast guard. the establishment of a european border and coast guard would ensure better management and protection at the eu's external borders. they could address migration challenges and potential future threats more effectively, thereby contributing to tackling serious crime with a cross-border dimension. a high level of internal security in the union would be ensured, while maintaining the free movement of persons. the european border and coast guard would focus its activities on developing an operational strategy for european integrated border management and assisting in its implementation in all relevant member states of the union. as a preventive measure, the proposal for a regulation is accompanied by a vulnerability assessment aimed at assessing the eu member states' capacity and preparedness to face upcoming challenges, including current and future threats and pressures at the union's external borders.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on the european border and coast guard and repealing regulation (ec) no 2007/2004, regulation (ec) no 863/2007 and council decision 2005/267/ec. the european border and coast guard will play a greater role than today’s frontex agency in returning migrants to their country of origin, but only where executing decisions have already been taken by national authorities. even though national authorities will still manage their borders on a day-to-day basis if their eu external borders are under pressure, they will be able to seek help from the european border and coast guard agency (ebcg), to rapidly deploy pooled border guard teams to those borders. i voted in favour because i am of the opinion that the regulation will ensure that the eu external borders are safer and better managed.
in writing. ‒ the european union is a project of peace and security based on common responses to common challenges. these include the establishment of a common border and coast guard, which will effectively protect us from external shocks so that we can live in freedom and peace within the union. in doing so, the union assumes a significant share of the co-responsibility for the security of its citizens. we want a house with doors, not without them. the european border and coast guard will be that door, but it will be open to all who want the union to do well and closed to all who want to destabilise it. in line with the above, i supported the report on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on the european border and coast guard and repealing regulation (ec) no 2007/2004, regulation (ec) no 863/2007 and council decision 2005/267/ec.

in writing. ‒ the report on the establishment of the european maritime safety agency supports the european commission's proposal and highlights the need to ensure that article 2b of the european maritime safety agency regulation is substantially consistent with the already agreed article 52 of the european border and coast guard act. the european maritime safety agency's main task is to ensure the safety of vessels, including offshore oil and gas platforms. to this end, the european maritime safety agency is responsible for several satellite navigation programmes that provide it with the necessary information. i voted in favour of the report because i agree with it.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council amending the regulation establishing the european maritime safety agency. the maritime safety agency was established to provide technical and other assistance to the institutions of the european union and the member states in the preparation and implementation of eu legislation on maritime safety, pollution from shipping and maritime security. i support the amendment of the regulation to increase the exchange of information and cooperation in the field of coast guard functions and emerging maritime risks.
in writing. ‒ the proposal aims to develop european cooperation in the field of coastguard by developing different forms of cooperation between the european border and coast guard, the european maritime safety agency and the european fisheries control agency. since the amendment of the regulation establishing the european maritime safety agency would improve synergies between the said bodies, thus contributing to more cost-effective services in the field of coast guard enforcement, i supported the proposal for a regulation. the amendment of the regulation establishing the european maritime safety agency would significantly improve and strengthen the union's surveillance capabilities at the eu's external maritime borders. one of the objectives is also to strengthen capacity at national and union level by developing guidelines, recommendations and best practices, as well as by supporting training and staff exchange in order to improve the exchange of information and cooperation in the field of coast guard functions.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council amending regulation (ec) no 1406/2002 establishing a european maritime safety agency. the agency shall, in cooperation with the european border and coast guard agency and the european fisheries control agency, support national authorities carrying out coastguard functions at national and union level, and where appropriate at international level. i voted in favour because i strongly believe that cooperation and coordination between the relevant eu agencies, in order to enhance synergies between their respective services, will allow them to provide more efficient and cost-effective multipurpose services to national authorities carrying out coastguard functions.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council amending regulation (ec) no 1406/2002 establishing a european maritime safety agency. the agency shall, in cooperation with the european border and coast guard agency and the european fisheries control agency, support national authorities carrying out coast guard functions at national and union level and, where appropriate, at international level, by providing surveillance and communication services based on state-of-the-art technology and by enhancing the exchange of information and cooperation on coast guard functions and emerging maritime risks.
in writing. ‒ i also supported this report, which is also a consequence of the establishment of the european border and coast guard agency. the proposal aims to enable the three european agencies, which also deal with maritime accidents, to coordinate their operations at sea and to exchange information useful for their work. the european fisheries control agency, the european maritime safety agency and the european border and coast guard agency should be able to cooperate and share capacities and exchange information on controls to enhance safety and security at sea. in the context of this objective, the commission proposes to add an article on cooperation in the field of coast guard functions to the mandate of the european fisheries control agency. the same text is proposed for the mandate of the european maritime safety agency and the european border and coast guard agency, which i mentioned earlier. the change of mandate for the three agencies requires a legal instrument to strengthen cooperation between them and with national authorities carrying out coast guard tasks.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report amending council regulation no 768/2005 establishing a community fisheries control agency. i am confident that the changes to the agency's remit will bring progress in cooperation with other agencies, in particular the european maritime safety agency and the european border and coastguard agency. the agency's responsibilities are now better defined, and therefore better cooperation and exchange of information in the field of coast guard functions can be expected, as well as easier planning, implementation of multi-purpose activities, sharing of resources and other capabilities, in agreement with the competent authorities of the member states concerned. like other members, i had no particular reservations about adopting the report, since it reflects the position of our group.
in writing. ‒ national authorities carrying out coast guard tasks are responsible for a large number of tasks in very diverse areas such as security, protection, rescue at sea, border control, customs control, environmental protection and general law enforcement. today, there are more than 300 such bodies in the european union. the purpose of the proposal is to enable the three european agencies, namely the european fisheries control agency, the european maritime safety agency and the european border and coast guard agency, to cooperate and share capabilities and exchange information on surveillance for better safety and security at sea. the report stresses that the coast guard function should be at the european union level only, even though the capacities are actually at national level. for all these reasons, the report proposes that the european commission's proposal be adopted under the simplified procedure in accordance with rule 50 of parliament's rules of procedure. i think the report on the establishment of a community fisheries control agency is a good one, which is why i supported it.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council amending the council regulation establishing a community fisheries control agency. the sheer volume of work and the large number of different structures cooperating with each other in the areas of security, protection, rescue at sea, border control, environmental protection mean that this cooperation is slow and often lacks information on competences and powers. i therefore welcome the commission's proposal to add cooperation in the field of coast guard functions to the mandate of the european fisheries control agency.
in writing. ‒ i support the proposal to amend the regulation establishing the community fisheries control agency. the proposal aims to provide support to national authorities in the exercise of the protective function of the coastguard at national and european level, enabling cooperation between the three european agencies (the european fisheries control agency, the european maritime safety agency and the newly established european border and coast guard). the three agencies will be able to pool their operational capabilities and exchange surveillance information with a view to improving maritime safety and security. the proposed amendment sets out the tasks of the community fisheries control agency, the aim of which is to support national authorities in the exercise of their coast guard functions. these tasks are to exchange information and set up systems for the exchange of information between all three agencies, to provide surveillance and communication services using state-of-the-art technology, to build capacity at eu and national level, and to provide training and exchange of staff. this would allow multi-dimensional operations to be planned and executed under specific conditions.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council amending the regulation on the secretariat of the supervisory committee of the european anti-fraud office (olaf). it is our duty to ensure that european citizens get the best use of their money, while at the same time ensuring that we fight fraud effectively. to achieve this, we need a strong european anti-fraud office (olaf) and a strengthened supervisory board to ensure independent oversight of olaf's activities. only then will we be able to establish a well-functioning mechanism of system and balance, something we have not seen in recent years. for all these reasons, i support the new proposed regulation which will make the secretariat of the supervisory board part of the commission rather than olaf. i believe that this will increase the independence of the supervisory board secretariat and thus create a working environment in which the supervisory board can fully fulfil its purpose.
in writing. ‒ i support the proposal to amend the regulation on the european anti-fraud office, the main objective of which is to add further guarantees to the independence of the supervisory board secretariat. the amendment is intended to facilitate certain organisational and budgetary aspects, without affecting the independent functioning of the secretariat. the head of secretariat will be responsible for the management and evaluation of his staff, and his assessment will be based on the report of the supervisory committee. the current appropriations for the budget and staff of the secretariat will also remain unaffected. the secretariat of the supervisory board will be kept in the building that is the current seat of the european anti-fraud office, thus safeguarding the independence of the supervisory board and the office, while facilitating contacts between them. furthermore, the amendment of the regulation will not affect the access of the secretariat of the supervisory board to data such as those from the information system and the database of the european anti-fraud office.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council amending regulation (eu, euratom) no 883/2013, as regards the secretariat of the supervisory committee of the european anti-fraud office (olaf). the aim of this proposal is to strengthen the independence of the olaf supervisory committee’s secretariat, thus providing for a more effective functioning of the supervisory committee. i voted in favour because i believe that in order to function independently and effectively, the supervisory committee requires an independent and adequately staffed secretariat.
in writing. ‒ the main purpose of the proposed amendment to regulation (eu, euratom) no 883/2013 is to supplement the guarantees of independence of the secretariat. the commission intends to integrate the secretariat of the supervisory board of the european anti-fraud office into the office for the administration and payment of individual entitlements (oap) from the date of application of the amended regulation. the merger will be purely administrative in nature, in order to simplify certain organisational and budgetary aspects. accession will not affect the independent functioning of the secretariat, nor will it change the number of staff or increase the budget. in line with the above, i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council amending regulation (eu, euratom) no 883/2013 as regards the secretariat of the supervisory board of the european anti-fraud office (olaf).
in writing. ‒ the multiannual financial framework is the eu's main strategic framework, as it sets the direction for the union's development and also affects the daily lives of its citizens. i supported the report proposed, as it analyses in detail the implementation of the current financial framework and contains a number of suggestions for improving the planning of expenditure or the use of funds. the fact is that the international environment has changed dramatically since the 2014-2020 financial framework came into force and has a significant impact on the use of eu budgetary resources. the refugee crisis, terrorism, the russian embargo and the agricultural crisis, the financing of the european fund for strategic investments (efsi), the high unemployment rate and the resulting social exclusion and, last but not least, brexit are just some of the events or situations that call for serious adjustments to the financial framework. the introduction of more flexible mechanisms is essential, as the ceilings of the mff have proved to be restrictive. if i limit myself to agriculture, i see that there is not much room for manoeuvre in the use of funds, since the funds are used up virtually year after year. more needs to be done to prevent the reduction of direct payments in the procurement of funds for intervention on agricultural markets, and the imminent abolition of sugar quotas, which could seriously affect the position of eu sugar beet growers, must also be borne in mind.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the preparation of the ex post revision of the mff 2014-2020: parliament's contribution before the submission of the commission's proposal. half a year on, the commission is still waiting with its proposal for the revision of the multiannual financial framework. it's probably one of the collateral casualties of the british referendum. the framework adopted in 2013 should be reviewed and adapted to the new political and economic realities, both in terms of the allocation of resources by sector and in terms of its size. security is also high on the political priority list and financial needs are high, given the scale of terrorism, as are financial needs for foreign policy to stabilise the situation in crisis countries.
in writing. ‒ i supported the motion for a resolution on the preparation of the ex post revision of the mff 2014-2020. a genuine mid-term review of the eu's multiannual financial framework is necessary if the union is to respond to the many challenges it faces today and to achieve its policy objectives. any budget surplus resulting from fines imposed on eu member states or from insufficient budget implementation should be made available to key issues such as today's response to the migration and refugee crisis. the eu budget is at the edge of its capacity. the built-in flexibility mechanism is not sufficient to meet the growing needs. additional resources are needed and the current ceiling needs to be adjusted and budgetary flexibility increased. the report also calls for simplifications to the operation of eu policies and the provisions of the multiannual financial framework, to ensure easier access to european funding for beneficiaries across europe. this requires concrete measures to prevent recurrence of payment crises in the future.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on ‘the preparation of the post-electoral revision of the mff 2014-2020: parliament’s input ahead of the commission’s proposal’. the report points out that the eu budget has to match the political and strategic priorities of the eu and ensure a balance between long-term priorities and new challenges. the report equally underlines the key role that the eu budget must play in achieving the jointly agreed europe 2020 strategy, which represents its main orientation and overarching priority. i believe that, due to new challenges that have arisen in the past two years, the mff requires rapid and thorough revision.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the preparation of the ex post revision of the mff 2014-2020: parliament's contribution before the submission of the commission's proposal. never before has the eu faced so many crises in its neighbourhood and beyond, including the refugee crisis, natural disasters, security threats and armed conflicts, which threaten fundamental values and require solidarity and enhanced external action. the eu budget must be in line with the political and strategic priorities of the eu and balance long-term priorities with new challenges, and therefore the mff review needs to carry out a qualitative analysis and evaluate the performance of the mff in the light of its implementation, new economic circumstances and other new developments.
in writing. ‒ i supported the taxe 2 special committee report because i believe that the establishment of appropriate tax systems is necessary to achieve a fairer and more equal society. the taxe 2 committee was set up last december and continued the work of the taxe special committee, which was set up to highlight harmful tax systems and practices by legal entities at both european and international level, with the aim of combating tax evasion. the reasons for the creation of the taxe committee or taxe 2 are based on the findings of the international consortium of investigative journalists, i.e. the panama papers and the lux leaks. the discovery of these documents has shown the urgent need for the european union and its member states to combat tax evasion, tax avoidance and aggressive tax planning and to work towards enhancing cooperation and transparency in order to restore fair taxation. by making our tax systems fairer and ensuring that corporate income tax is paid where value is created, not just in the member states but everywhere in the world. through the panama papers and lux leaks, we've seen how individuals and corporations fraudulently derive profits that, given fair tax treatment, should be in the national budget and thus allocated to services for citizens.
in writing. ‒ the discovery of the panama papers and luxleaks, published by the international consortium of investigative journalists, has shown the urgent need for the european union and its member states to combat tax evasion, tax avoidance and aggressive tax planning. at the same time, member states must work to strengthen cooperation and transparency in order to restore fair taxation, by making our tax systems fairer and ensuring that corporate tax is paid where value is created, not just in member states but everywhere in the world. i welcome the report, which includes many ideas from the greens, such as the intention to go beyond tax reforms, which are currently somewhat weak, or the intention to move towards a common consolidated corporate tax base at european level. the report also calls for strong european protection for whistleblowers, who play a key role in exposing tax scandals. the need for a blacklist of european tax havens and sanctions against blacklisted countries is also highlighted. in view of the above, i consider the report on tax rulings and other measures of a similar nature or effect to be a good one and have therefore supported it.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on taxation positions and other measures of a similar nature or with similar effect. the european union and the member states should work towards strengthening the fight against tax evasion and avoidance and enhancing cooperation and transparency. only then can we restore fair taxation, so that income tax is paid where value is created. i support the call for the member states and the commission to adopt additional legislative proposals on corporate tax avoidance, as member states still have sufficient room for manoeuvre to tighten the anti-abuse rules and thus prevent the erosion of the tax base.
in writing. ‒ i supported the report on taxation and other measures of a similar nature or effect. tax affairs make it imperative for eu member states to fight against tax evasion and tax avoidance. we need more cooperation between eu member states to ensure adequate control and harmonisation of eu member states' tax systems. i welcome the initiative to establish a common list of non-cooperative union jurisdictions in the framework of the external strategy for effective taxation. at eu level, we need a proposal for a common consolidated corporate tax base that will provide a comprehensive solution to harmful tax practices in the union. the work of whistleblowers is crucial for the detection of tax evasion and tax avoidance scandals and therefore protection should be provided to them. concrete legislative measures on transfer pricing are necessary, as 70% of profit shifting is through transfer pricing. the commission should draw up a blacklist of tax havens. the report also recommends the introduction of a tax credit at eu level to ensure a one-off taxation of profits generated in the union.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on tax rulings and other measures similar in nature or effect. the aim of this report is to step up to the plate on the fight against tax evasion and tax havens. the report sets clear demands for increased accountability, and effective deterrents in the form of markedly increased sanctions for tax havens, banks, tax advisors and companies. i voted in favour because i strongly believe that increased european and international cooperation on this hugely problematic issue is necessary.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on taxation and other measures of a similar nature or having similar effect. the eu and its member states must urgently fight tax evasion, tax avoidance and aggressive tax planning and work to strengthen cooperation and transparency to restore fair taxation, by making our tax systems fairer and ensuring that corporate tax is paid where value is created, not just in the member states but everywhere in the world.

in writing. ‒ i supported the joint motion for a resolution concerning japan's decision to renew the whaling fleet in 2015 and 2016. the resolution is a response to the decision by the japanese fisheries agency to inform the international whaling commission last november that it would be restoring whales under the newrep-a programme. this decision is contrary to international law relating to the whale industry. the international whaling commission maintains a global moratorium on commercial whaling and prohibits international commercial trade in whale products, and also works to abolish 'whaling for scientific purposes'. the commission has also received comments from the united kingdom and the united states on the application of the landing obligation for the 2015-2016 season. in view of all the international commitments that have been made, i fully support the resolution calling on japan to cease all whaling activities and to respect the findings of the international whaling commission.
in writing. ‒ the international whaling commission banned commercial whaling of all species of large whales in 1982, and this ban came into effect in 1986. despite this international ban, japan continued to hunt whales for so-called scientific purposes. thus, between 1986, when the ban came into force, and the 2008/2009 season, it killed more than 17000 whales. in its 2014 judgment, the international court of justice rejected japan's scientific whaling programme and found that the specific permits issued by japan for the killing, capture and processing of humpback whales, humpback whales and minke whales were not in line with its obligations under the international whaling convention. this is why we in the european parliament have decided to adopt a resolution calling on japan to respect the decision of the international court of justice and to end all whaling activities. the resolution also calls on the european commission and the council to encourage japan to commit to its international obligations regarding the protection of marine mammals in the context of the current negotiations for an eu free trade agreement. i believe that the adoption of the resolution is necessary because it will help to improve the situation in the whale sector. that's why i voted to pass the resolution.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the joint resolution on japan's decision to renew the whaling season 2015/2016. i support the continuation of the moratorium on commercial whaling, which was introduced by the international whaling commission in 1982 to protect stocks from extinction and to enable them to recover. i therefore agree with the call for japan to immediately cease all its whaling activities and to respect the findings of the international whaling commission. japan's whale recovery is in violation of international whaling commission standards and international law, and is threatening the protection of biodiversity and marine ecosystems.

in writing. ‒ i supported the proposed report on the implementation of the un convention on human rights. in december 2010, the eu was the first organisation to accede to the united nations convention on the rights of persons with disabilities. it is the first and so far the only international human rights treaty that the eu has ratified as a whole. following accession, the eu, like the other states parties, was required to submit an initial report on the state of implementation of the convention, with subsequent periodic reports to be prepared every four years. the report aims to focus on the work of the eu institutions, which are to set an example in the implementation of the convention. i agree with the rapporteur, ms stevens, that there is no hierarchy in human rights and that discrimination on the grounds of disability should be treated like any other form of discrimination. this is particularly important for women and children with disabilities, the elderly and individuals with multiple support needs, including those with special intellectual and psychosocial needs.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report because the implementation of this convention promotes, protects and ensures the full and equal enjoyment by persons with disabilities of all human rights and fundamental freedoms and helps to promote respect for their inherent dignity. a step forward is needed to enable disabled people to participate fully and effectively in society on an equal basis with others, and this is well covered in this report. my view has always been that more development projects should be set up, focusing primarily on people with special needs. i also agree with the establishment of mechanisms for capacity building and the exchange of good practice between the different institutions, both within the eu itself and among its members. i supported the report as a whole, but i did not support some of the proposed amendments relating to discrimination and the financial part, which infringes the fundamental rights of disabled people the proper use of funds and compliance with the rules of the structural funds are in the member states' domain.
in writing. ‒ in december 2010, the european union became the first regional integration organisation to accede to the united nations convention on the rights of persons with disabilities. it is the first international human rights treaty ratified by the european union as a whole. the optional protocol has not been signed or ratified. with the ratification of the convention, the european union is now under the supervision of the committee on the rights of persons with disabilities. the report focuses on recommendations falling within the competence of the european union, which may lead to implementation complications at national level. particular attention shall be paid to the institutions of the european union, which shall set an example in the implementation of the convention. this covers staff regulations and recruitment and retention practices, as well as public events organised by the european parliament or held on its premises. there is no hierarchy in human rights and discrimination on the grounds of disability must be treated like any other form of discrimination. this is particularly important for women and children with disabilities, the elderly and individuals with multiple support needs, including those with special intellectual and psychosocial needs. that is why i voted to adopt the report on the implementation of the united nations convention on the rights of persons with disabilities.

in writing. ‒ i supported the objection to the commission implementing act on permitted health claims on food, as their use must not be ambiguous or misleading. this would most likely be the case with claims on energy drinks containing caffeine. the use of health claims has been found to contribute to an increased consumption of energy drinks, which justifies the expectation that the daily intake of sugar and caffeine will exceed the recommended maximum daily intake. this would consequently lead to adverse effects on the health of humans and in particular on adolescents, who are the most massive consumers of energy drinks.
in writing. ‒ i support the objection under rule 106 of the rules of procedure to the motion for a resolution on the list of permitted health claims made on foods, other than those referring to the reduction of disease risk and to children's development and health. to date, the commission has not yet defined the specific nutrient profiles with which foods or certain categories of foods must comply in order to be able to bear nutrition and health claims and the conditions for the use of nutrition and health claims for foods or categories of foods in relation to nutrient profiles. a whopping 68% of teenagers and 18% of children regularly consume energy drinks. children and adolescents who regularly consume energy drinks have been found to experience headaches, insomnia, and behavioral problems on a regular basis. the commission should examine the possibility of introducing a restriction on the marketing of energy drinks to children and adolescents. a mere non-binding discouragement of the marketing of energy drinks to children under 12 years of age is not a sufficient measure.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the objection pursuant to rule 106: permitted health claims made on foods. energy drinks have been linked to headaches, sleep problems and behavioural problems in children and adolescents who consume them regularly. i voted in favour of the objection because i believe that the claims that caffeine helps to increase alertness and that caffeine helps to improve concentration should not be used for foods targeting children and adolescents, who are the largest group of energy-drink consumers.

we heard in an interesting debate that the g20 summit was only partially successful. leaders agreed on new measures to combat tax evasion, the united states and china agreed to ratify the paris agreement on climate change, leaders gave a yellow card to chinese dumping in the steel industry, and reiterated their commitment to global trade and free trade agreements. it also appears that the us and russia have finally taken responsibility for the ceasefire in syria. but the summit was certainly not a particularly successful one for the new prime minister of the united kingdom. in it, us president obama reiterated to the new british prime minister that the uk would not have any privileges in negotiating a new trade agreement with the us, nor did the us intend to change its traditional foreign policy priorities. he stressed that one of america's top priorities was the transatlantic partnership with the european union. soon after, even the japanese government handed may a study that found that many japanese companies would be forced to move their headquarters from the united kingdom to other european union member states if the british did not remain part of the single market. well, despite this, the g20 has brought some perhaps less visible messages. this is a stronger commitment by the twenty to free trade and, in this context, to combating various forms of protectionism. this certainly applies to china, and it also sounds like a warning of a possible change of course after the us election. the new economic momentum must be based on innovation and equity, and economic growth must be inclusive. these g20 messages are good. i hope that the outcome of this summit will encourage the european union to accelerate the adoption of free trade agreements with canada and the united states.

before voting on today's candidates for the european court of auditors, let me make two important points. first, article 286 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union provides that the council, after consulting the european parliament, is to adopt the list of members of the european court of auditors drawn up in accordance with the proposals of the member states. of course, this means strictly formally that parliament should only have a consultative role, but this does not mean that the council should not also respect and take account of the will of the european parliament. i therefore think that, as has happened in some previous cases, this time and in future too the council will take the european parliament's position on these nominations seriously and take it into account, otherwise i do not know why we are carrying out this whole procedure if the council has the final say. and i think, for a good working relationship in the future, this is important information. secondly, and of even greater concern, the list of candidates for new members of the european court of auditors today again includes only male candidates. and parliament has long stressed the importance of gender equality. the parliament's report on the role of the european court of auditors in the future states that parliament will take the issue of gender balance among the members of the court of auditors very seriously. and just for the record, the court is currently represented by only four of its 28 members. and if the pace continues as it seems, the picture will be even more defeating. i think i should add, by way of comparison, that it was this parliament that made it clear to the then candidate, mr juncker, that the number of commissioners in the current commission should not be lower than the number of commissioners in the previous college. it is time to establish the same standards in all european institutions, and i hope that this will be taken seriously in the future.
in writing. ‒ smart specialisation can help to channel investment and concentrate research and innovation in areas where regional and local competences are most present. the emerging differences between european regions in research and innovation indicate that there is a need for policies tailored to local needs. smart specialisation offers the opportunity for differentiation and economic transformation through innovation, which will be based on local resources and comparative advantages. efforts and investments will thus focus on a limited number of priorities, identified in a process in which entrepreneurs and researchers will play a leading role. smart specialisation has become the main principle and precondition for obtaining funding from the european regional development fund (erdf). the report thus re-emphasises the important role that smart specialisation plays in cohesion policy. i believe that this is the right direction to take in this area, and that is why i voted in favour of the report.

in writing. ‒ european territorial cooperation is an important instrument in cohesion policy. it is designed to transcend administrative boundaries, reduce the impact of national borders and remove barriers to cooperation and territorial integration. cross-border cooperation in the periods 2000-2006 and 2007-2013 has produced good practices in the areas of better connectivity and accessibility, transfer of knowledge and innovation, strengthening of regional identity, addressing environmental challenges and more. european territorial cooperation provides a significant added value for the european union, contributing to peace, stability and regional integration within the framework of the enlargement and neighbourhood policies. cross-border cooperation can also bring added value to managing the migration crisis. parliament analysed the implementation of european territorial cooperation as presented in the 2014-2020 programming period. parliament has always supported such a policy and has therefore also asked for more funds to this end. the report proposes some new ways of regulating this mechanism, such as thematic focus and action orientation. it is also important to note that around 41% of the european territorial cooperation budget under the european regional development fund is devoted to environmental improvement measures. for all the reasons i have mentioned, i supported the report.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the recommendation on the draft council decision on the conclusion of the agreement in the form of an exchange of letters between the european union and the people's republic of china pursuant to article xxiv:6 and article xxviii of the general agreement on tariffs and trade (gatt) 1994 relating to the modification of a benefit in the schedule of benefits of the republic of croatia in the course of its accession to the european union. the accession of croatia to the european union also led to the enlargement of the customs union. since this has increased the customs tariffs by more than the rate to which the acceding country has committed itself in the world trade organisation, we need this adjustment.
in writing. ‒ i supported the motion for a resolution on the eu-china agreement relating to the accession of croatia. following the accession of the republic of croatia, the european union has enlarged the customs union. therefore, in accordance with the rules of the world trade organisation (wto) (article xxiv:6 of the gatt 1994), it had to enter into negotiations with wto members having negotiating rights on the customs tariff of croatia in order to agree on a compensatory adjustment. such adjustment is necessary where the adoption of an eu external tariff regime results in an increase in customs tariffs above the rate to which the acceding country has committed itself in the wto.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of recommendation on the draft council decision on the conclusion of the agreement in the form of an exchange of letters between the european union and the people's republic of china pursuant to article xxiv: 6 and article xxviii of the general agreement on tariffs and trade (gatt) 1994 relating to the modification of concessions in the schedule of the republic of croatia in the course of its accession to the european union. with the accession of the republic of croatia, the european union enlarged its customs union. consequently, the european union was required under world trade organisation (wto) rules to enter into negotiations with wto members having negotiating rights related to the tariff schedule of croatia in order to eventually agree on a compensatory adjustment. such adjustment is due if the adoption of the eu’s external tariff regime results in an increase in tariff beyond the level for which the acceding country has bound itself at the wto. i believe that the people’s republic of china has the right to have its previous trading rights restored, following their slight erosion due to the enlargement of the eu customs union with croatian eu accession.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the recommendation on the draft council decision on the conclusion of the agreement in the form of an exchange of letters between the european union and the eastern republic of uruguay pursuant to article xxiv:6 and article xxviii of the general agreement on tariffs and trade (gatt) 1994 relating to the modification of concessions in the schedule of the republic of croatia in the course of its accession to the european union. with the accession of the republic of croatia, the eu enlarged its customs union and was therefore required under wto rules to enter into negotiations to the eastern republic of uruguay regarding the tariff schedule of croatia in order to eventually agree on a compensatory adjustment as the eu’s external tariff regime results in an increase of tariffs. following the negotiations, the eu will incorporate in its schedule for the customs territory of the eu 28 that of the eu 27 with modifications related to tariff rate quotas on bovine meat.

written. ‒ based on the existing directives regulating the field of data collection on natural gas and electricity prices, for household end-users, data collection is voluntary. this solution has led to certain problems in the collection of data by individual member states. this regulation now makes the collection of data compulsory for both industrial end-users and household end-users. this improves and introduces full transparency of natural gas and electricity prices for all users and allows for the sustainability of high quality data in this area. the collection of price data should not place an additional burden on reporting bodies, while the competent national authorities would continue to collect price data. the report also highlights several important points and suggests good solutions, relating to the problems of identifying the entities responsible for price discrimination, which cannot be left to suppliers, then to the preservation of confidentiality of supplier and consumer data, as well as in a segment relating to the explanation that the overall average share of transmission and distribution costs can only be differentiated at the general level of household and non-household customers. i consider that these are all imaginary solutions, which is why i am voting in favour of this report.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on european statistics on natural gas and electricity prices and repealing directive 2008/92/ec of the european parliament and of the council on a common community procedure for the enhancement of transparency of gas and electricity prices charged to industrial end-users. i support the amendments proposed in the report that member states are the ones to ensure that the data collection and management system provides comprehensible and comparable high quality representative data on natural gas and electricity prices. several member states are facing problems in collecting data, and we need this regulation to make this voluntary basis mandatory.
in writing. ‒ i supported the proposal for a regulation on gas and electricity price statistics. the purpose of this regulation is to transform the voluntary basis into a mandatory one in order to avoid problems in collecting data reported by several member states. this is necessary to ensure that the quality of the review of electricity and natural gas price data for the household sector does not deteriorate significantly and to continue to ensure broad market coverage and high quality of price data.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the proposal for a regulation on gas and electricity price statistics. i agree that a common framework for european statistics is needed to support energy policy, in particular to establish a fully integrated internal energy market for consumers. i believe that the proposed regulation will allow for greater transparency in energy costs and prices and in the level of public support.
in writing. ‒ i voted for the report that highlights that only stronger market integration can ensure more energy security for the eu. a new energy market design is strategically needed for the achievement of a true eu energy union and this report indicates directions for the commission and proposes relevant solutions for the obstacles that have been hindering a common european market for energy. in the future, more electricity will be traded across borders and that requires efficient cooperation from all market actors, therefore we have to build the capacity for cross-border cooperation to reflect the increasing variability of production so that sufficient energy can flow across the eu.
in writing. ‒ in july 2015, the european commission published a series of documents on the european single market. one of them was also aimed at the electricity market and its future development, with the aim of meeting consumer expectations, bringing the real benefits of new technologies and facilitating investments, in particular in renewable sources. the commission is due to submit a legislative proposal on electricity market design and security of supply by the end of this year. the current overcrowding of conventional power plants in the european union presents both an opportunity and a challenge to further support alternative energy sources. unfortunately, this report does not do so, but rather largely maintains the status quo, by not giving strong support to alternative energy sources and thus not contributing to the depreciation of energy from such sources, which is essential for a more environmentally friendly economy. i decided to vote against the report because it was not ambitious enough.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the way to a new energy market design. we must move towards the completion of the european internal market in electricity, thereby contributing to efficiency, security of supply and the development of renewable energy sources. i support the call to adapt the existing regulatory framework of european markets to allow for a greater share of renewable energy sources and to bridge existing cross-border regulatory gaps. we also need a holistic, forward-looking approach to the re-design of the electricity market. in this context, the report rightly calls on the commission to take the lead in a participatory process aimed at achieving a common practical definition of producers.
in writing. ‒ i supported the motion for a resolution on the new energy market design. a union-wide electricity market with clear price signals for new investments should be established. it is intended to establish a european approach to energy security and to strengthen regional cooperation in the field of energy policy, in particular in investments in new energy production facilities, in interconnectors and financing rules, and in the integration of renewable energy sources into the european internal market.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report entitled ‘towards a new energy market design’. in order to achieve the climate and energy targets, the energy system of the future will need more flexibility, which requires investment in all four flexibility solutions – flexible production, network development, demand flexibility and storage. the report calls for the new electricity market design to embrace a holistic, future-oriented approach. furthermore, it emphasises that a strengthened european internal market in electricity is possible, on the basis of stronger price signals on the wholesale market through prices that reflect actual scarcity and surplus of supplies, including price spikes. i voted in favour because i believe that energy efficiency is a core principle of the energy union strategy, since this is an effective way of reducing emissions, generating savings for consumers and reducing the eu’s dependency on fossil fuel imports.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the road to a new energy market design. i agree with the report's conclusions that the energy system will need to be more resilient in the future in order to achieve climate and energy goals. this requires investment in all four flexible solutions - flexible generation, network development, flexible demand and storage.
written. ‒ the resolution on the eu's heating and cooling strategy is a strategic part of a very important area such as the eu's energy stability and security, given that almost half of the eu's final energy demand is used for heating and cooling. the eu strategy identifies key challenges and needs for increasing energy efficiency and the deployment of renewable energy sources. the observed problems in the durability and inefficiency of residential heating systems in the eu also represent a major potential for increasing energy efficiency. investing in energy saving and energy efficiency offers the highest and fastest return on investment in the energy sector. the strategy recognises the active role that consumers can play in creating a sustainable european heating and cooling system. the need to increase recycling rates is emphasised, as waste-to-energy generation will play a very important role in the heating sector. the strategy points to an integrated approach in mobilising all key actors in relation to the use of all available european structural and investment funds which should be available to all actors, and in particular to small, medium and micro-enterprises. and, by the way, on the ballot, all my support goes to that resolution.
in writing. ‒ the report is a good start to regulating this area, which is unfortunately still dominated by fossil fuels. however, the report's language remains rather loose, giving fossil fuels the opportunity to remain the main source of heating and cooling for a long time to come. in february 2016, the eu adopted its first heating and cooling strategy, which set the objective of reducing dependence on fossil fuels in this area and shifting consumption within the agreed commitments of the recent paris agreement and moving towards more efficient and sustainable sources, while reducing the eu's dependence on imported fuels. the report also discusses, inter alia, building insulation, the use of energy from waste materials and the potential for greater synergies between the electricity market and the heating and cooling market. despite the important issues that are open in this way, i believe that this is a missed opportunity, as parliament should be much more ambitious with the great european potential for energy savings, the creation of new local jobs and the reduction of greenhouse gas emissions. that is why i abstained.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the eu's strategy for heating and cooling. i agree with the report that the eu heating and cooling strategy is an important step towards providing a holistic approach to transforming heating and cooling in the european union and identifying priority areas for action. in the eu, heating and cooling account for almost 50% of final energy consumption, of which 80% is for heating and cooling buildings. the strategy should prioritise sustainable and cost-effective solutions that enable member states to meet their climate and energy policy objectives. the heating and cooling sectors in the member states are very diverse.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on an eu strategy on heating and cooling. almost 50% of the eu’s final energy demand is used for heating and cooling, of which 80% is used in buildings. the report underlines the necessity to take along specific measures for heating and cooling when revising the energy efficiency directive (2012/27/eu), the renewable energy directive (2009/28/ec) and the energy performance of buildings directive (2010/31/eu). moreover, the report calls for specific sustainable heating and cooling strategies to be developed at national level, giving special attention to combined heat and power. i am of the opinion that the heating and cooling sector should reflect the 2015 paris agreement on climate change (cop 21).
in writing. ‒ i supported the motion for a resolution on the eu's strategy for heating and cooling. as the report highlights, a heating and cooling sector that is in line with the eu's energy and climate objectives must be based on 100% renewable energy sources by 2050 at the latest, which can only be achieved by radically reducing our energy consumption and by fully applying the principle that energy efficiency is the most important fuel. i agree that more needs to be done to reduce demand for heating in buildings and to shift the remaining demand from fuel-burning to imported fossil fuels in individual boilers to sustainable heating and cooling options in line with the eu 2050 targets.
in writing. ‒ i voted for the report because smes, which form the backbone of europe’s economy, need more financing options after the financial crisis caused banks to cut back on lending. as smes have more limited financing options and are in need of macroeconomic stability and a stable regulatory environment, this report urges the eu’s proposed capital market union to help smes gain access to other financing sources like investment capital and crowdfunding. besides, it also calls for a one-stop shop to help smes get financing and to avoid heavy regulation in getting that financing, so that smes can fulfil their job creation potential.

in writing. ‒ the eu strategy for the alpine region (eusalp) is the european union's fourth macro-regional strategy and covers 48 regions in seven countries, five of which are eu member states (italy, france, slovenia, austria, germany) and two non-members (liechtenstein and switzerland). this region is one of the largest economic regions in europe, with more than 70 million people living and working there. the commission has identified several challenges to be addressed by eusalp. these are: economic globalisation, demographic trends, climate change, energy challenges and the specific geographical location. transport and mobility are traditionally the two biggest challenges facing the alpine region, mainly due to the environmental and climatic impacts in the alps. while such a strategy is welcome, it did not take into account the proposals of the eu parliament's committee on transport and tourism, and at the same time the report does not cover the topics of environmental and climate protection, renewable energy sources, which in my opinion are increasingly crucial in this region. in view of the indecisiveness of the report and the lack of coverage of the issues mentioned, i abstained from voting.

written. ‒ the african development fund should be a european development instrument that brings together funds from a variety of donors to enable the eu to intervene efficiently, quickly, transparently and collectively in various aspects of crisis situations in africa, which continues to have very high rates of population growth, especially among young people, which on the one hand represents great social and economic potential, and on the other hand risks of instability due to increasing poverty. this is why both the european development fund and official development assistance must be allocated to clear objectives, in the economic, social and human development of the beneficiaries in africa, as stated in the report. the report also highlights the need to involve local authorities, civil society and international organisations in the planning, implementation and evaluation phases of the mutual fund. the report rightly emphasises the need for greater transparency and clarity to better achieve the objectives of this financial instrument and warns of the risk of misuse of eu development assistance. the mutual fund should create added value to existing sources of funding. the commission should also be able to use the resources of the european structural and investment funds to support the implementation of the union's macro-financial assistance. all of this leads us to support the report and that is why i supported such a report.
in writing. ‒ the eu trust fund for africa was established last year in response to migration flows to europe. it aims to use specific resources to tackle the root causes of such migration and to support all aspects of stability that can contribute to better coping with migration. the fund covers the geographical regions of the sahel, lake chad, the horn of africa and north africa, and the funding comes mainly from the budget of the european development fund (edf). possible projects that could be set up with the assistance of the fund relate to the design of economic programmes that will create employment opportunities, projects that would support basic services for the local population, projects that would support migration management, and support for general management. although the report is incomplete or repetitive in certain respects, i believe that such a fund can have a positive impact on potential migrants from these areas as well as on the lives of europeans. that is why i voted for the report.
