written. ‒ a good work-life balance simultaneously promotes economic growth, competitiveness, overall labour market participation, gender equality, reduction of the risk of poverty and intergenerational solidarity, and responds to the challenges of an ageing society and has a positive impact on eu birth rates. given that reconciliation of work, private and family life is recognised as a fundamental right, and although some initiatives have been launched in this area at european and national level, it is necessary to allow for further progress to ensure a balance between private and work life. this is very important, as the report itself states, not only for the well-being of the individual but also for the well-being of society as a whole, because people who have a satisfactory work-life balance are more productive at work. in particular, the report shall indicate what has been done and the position of the child in the context of work-life balance. the aim of the project is to develop a comprehensive strategy for the prevention of child labour, which will be implemented in the context of the european year of the child. for these reasons, i support this report in the plenary.
in writing. ‒ achieving work-life balance requires coordinated and comprehensive policies for reconciling work, care and time with family and friends, and leisure and personal development. both the eu and its member states should adopt policies that are adapted to today's realities and promote gender equality in the workplace and in other spheres of life. in particular, legislation on parental leave for mothers and fathers should be updated. there are many reasons for modernising this framework at eu level, including changes in demographics, the emergence of new ways of working and the significant negative impact of parenting on women's employment. parliament therefore decided to draw up a report to launch the debate and encourage the commission to work more quickly in this area. the report aims not only to promote gender equality in employment and other areas of life, but also to take into account the needs of an increasingly diverse society and to integrate a life-cycle approach to work-life balance. the report also seeks to speed up negotiations between european workers and trade unions on this issue. i think the report is positive and contains important points, and i have decided to support it.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on creating favourable conditions in the labour market for reconciling work and private life. to achieve a balance between work, private and family life, we need sound, coherent and comprehensive policies. i therefore support incentives and effective measures to balance work, family care and time with family, and leisure and personal development. we need to promote family-friendly working environments, reconciliation plans and re-entry programmes, as the crisis has further reduced already low fertility rates in the european union, as young people delay child-planning due to unemployment, precarious employment, uncertain futures and discrimination in the labour market.

turkey, like the european union, is at a crossroads. the country is facing so many problems that we cannot blame turkish president erdogan for trying to force certain concessions from the european union on the refugee issue. nor can we blame the leaders of the union and the member states for trying to buy peace for refugees. however, our citizens will be very angry if we completely forget that turkey has chosen, in this transition, a path which is moving further and further away from democracy and respect for human rights. if turkey does not fulfil the conditions for visa liberalisation, it cannot be granted. the rules are clear. and it's hard to understand why president erdogan is taking an authoritarian approach with little dialogue, with which he is taking away the freedom of its citizens. and while we're dealing with turkey, moves are already happening in other neighborhoods, like egypt. if we ignore them, something could happen very quickly that could cause the union to slip at the crossroads.
the social area is one of the areas where the european union has remained halfway through harmonisation. on the one hand, we have the free movement of people who can travel and work anywhere in the union. they may also work in various forms of employment. on the other hand, there are companies operating in the single market. they are put in a position where they have to ensure competitiveness, or else they may close their doors. we also have countries within the european union that cannot guarantee the same level of social rights, because of course their budgets cannot afford it. we have to distinguish between the exploitation of employees, which some employers exploit for their own greed. this is unacceptable, of course. and we have to distinguish on the other hand between ensuring equal income and equal social status. those are two different things. of course, i strongly condemn the exploitation. but i want to remind you that we must also be aware that social rights have a cost. it costs companies, it costs countries. the answer to how to ensure equal social status would be simple if there was a single european source from which to finance social rights. until that happens, of course, we're in the position we're in.
the lack of confidence is the state of affairs in the union, the loss of european identity. many europeans have forgotten it or do not know it at all. why would you do that? because too many politicians and leaders have forgotten what european values are, and because we have not consistently reacted to violations of rights and values outside or within our borders, because we do not offer, as you said, a social europe. our vision must be based on people and in no way can it contain secret it agreements of the type that lower the standard of the europeans. we cannot allow ourselves to be completely consumed by the issue of security while neglecting the concerns of europeans about privacy. the union solidarity corps, mr juncker, is a wonderful idea for engaging young people and helping people in need. with ideas like these, the union will straighten its back again. we need optimism, pessimism is not the answer. and we need to make all of us in leadership positions aware that the coming months are crucial and that we will be held accountable if europe succumbs to populism and nationalism.

in writing. wishing to improve the definition of 'social dumping', which should not be confused with dumping in the areas of trade policy and the labour sector, i supported the report on social dumping in the eu. the fact is that social rights vary considerably across the eu, as legislation is regulated by national legislation. this is of course a very different situation, and companies are naturally taking advantage of the internal market and the legislation that suits them best in this area. if we want a properly functioning internal market, including in the area of free movement of labour, we must strive to harmonise the social rights and obligations of workers, and we must also regulate specific cases such as workers at sea, posted workers, transport operators, etc. that is why i support the rapporteur's proposal for the adoption of a protocol on social policy, which would ensure that social rights take precedence over economic freedoms.
in writing. ‒ i voted for the report that sets a common definition of social dumping, as it was necessary to address the lack of a shared definition that has led to misunderstandings and misperceptions in debates across the eu member states. hence, the adopted report is of key importance to combat cases of abuse and circumvention of the existing european or national rules. i anticipate better enforcement of existing rules; more strengthened and efficient cooperation between national competent authorities as well as the identification and elimination of existing legal loopholes, which should all result in fairer conditions for workers.
in writing. ‒ social dumping is currently the biggest problem caused by deliberate exploitative practices. these are numerous examples of the abuse of european and national legislation to obtain benefits at the expense of one of the social security systems. the commission and the member states must step up their action in this area, ensure effective controls and improve the exchange of information between member states. the report links social dumping to undeclared work, hidden employment relationships and abusive cases of posting to other member states, while describing the wide range of exploitative practices that arise in relation to national legislation and european rules. the sectors most 'hit' are agriculture, construction, services, transport, health and the like. it is precisely because of the abuses which in this case take place on the territory of several countries at the same time that the member states must strengthen cooperation and organise their inspection bodies in such a way that they cooperate closely with each other in such cases. particular attention is also paid to companies which are postal mailers and serve only the purpose of exploiting certain differences between the social systems of the member states with long-term damage to employees. a special chapter is also devoted to transport, where such practices occur most frequently. i believe that such exploitative practices at the expense of our social systems and our employees must be prevented, and that is why i voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on social dumping in the european union. in the social field, the european union has not yet achieved full harmonisation, and we need to harmonise policies where possible. in recent years, we have seen an increasing trend of social dumping, which has a negative impact on the competitiveness of enterprises. however, there is still a great deal of uncertainty and confusion in the area of social dumping, as we still lack a clear and generally accepted definition. as an alternate member of the committee on transport and tourism, i support the committee's view that member states should start implementing fully, effectively and non-discriminatorily all social legislation applicable to the transport sector and should increase the number of effective controls, in particular as regards driving and rest times.
in writing. ‒ i supported the motion for a resolution on social dumping in the eu, because undeclared work and sham self-employment can distort competition, lead to precarious jobs and affect worker protection and the overall quality of jobs. in the eu, on the one hand, we have the free movement of people, who can travel and work anywhere in the union and in different forms of employment. on the other hand, we have companies operating in the single market and are put in a position where they have to ensure competitiveness. we also have countries within the european union that cannot guarantee the same level of social rights because their budgets cannot afford it. we have to distinguish between exploiting employees, on whom some employers profit because of their own greed for greater profits, and ensuring equal income and equal social status. we have to realize that social rights cost money, and that's what a lot of people don't want to see. the answer to how to ensure equal social status would be simple if there was a single european source from which to finance social rights. until that happens, we will continue to face the fact that social rights will be different within the european union. we need to help companies and design our proposals in such a way that we create an environment where the differences are as small as possible.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on the prospectus to be published when securities are offered to the public or admitted to trading. the aim of this regulation is to ensure investor protection and market efficiency, while enhancing the single market for capital. the provision of information, according to the nature of the issuer and of the securities, is necessary to enable investors to make an informed investment decision, and ensures, together with rules on the conduct of business, the protection of investors. i voted in favour because i believe that such information contributes to the proper functioning and development of securities markets.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on the prospectus to be published when securities are offered to the public or admitted to trading. i believe that the regulation is an important step towards the creation of a capital markets union, i.e. ensuring that markets work more efficiently and offering opportunities for investors and savers to invest money more efficiently to boost growth and create jobs. i also consider that disclosure in the case of offers to the public or admission of securities to trading on a regulated market is essential for the protection of investors, as it removes the mismatch between investors and issuers.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a council decision amending the council decision of 22 september 2015 establishing provisional measures in the area of international protection for the benefit of italy and greece. the proposed amendment provides for the transfer of 54000 applicants from italy and greece as a transfer of an applicant from the territory of the member state responsible for examining his or her application for international protection to the territory of the member state of relocation. relocation shall not include the transfer or reception of persons from a third country in need of international protection to the territory of a member state. the commission is also proposing to amend the proposal to make the regular review of the situation regarding the mass arrival of third-country nationals in the member states not a task of the european commission but a task of the european border and coast guard agency.
in writing. ‒ asylum proposal: i supported the provisional measures for the benefit of italy and greece. as of 26 september 2016, 54 000 asylum seekers are to be relocated from italy and greece to the territories of other member states in the proportion set out in this decision (namely 12 764 applicants from italy and 41 236 applicants from greece), unless by that date the commission proposes, in accordance with article 4 (3), to allocate those relocations to other member states to beneficiaries facing emergency situations due to a sudden inflow of persons.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a council decision amending council decision (eu) 2015/1601 of 22 september 2015 establishing provisional measures in the area of international protection for the benefit of italy and greece. the report states that eu countries must honour their pledges to accept refugees relocated from greece and italy to relieve migratory pressure on these two ‘frontline’ countries. furthermore, it underlines that the need for emergency relocation from greece and italy to other eu member states is expected to remain high, pointing to the urgent humanitarian situation in greece and the risk of deterioration in italy. i voted in favour because i believe that these measures would, at the same time, discourage irregular entries by opening up legal and safe routes to the eu.

in writing. ‒ i supported the proposal for a decision on guidelines for the employment policies of the member states, as i believe that the european union, in defining and implementing its policies and activities, must ensure a connected and inclusive labour market that can eliminate the serious effects of unemployment and ensure decent working conditions throughout the union, including adequate wages and adequate social protection, in accordance with labour regulations, collective bargaining and the principle of subsidiarity. it is also essential to ensure a high level of education and training and to prevent discrimination on grounds of sex, race or nationality, religion or belief, disability, age or sexual orientation.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the key objectives for the cites cop17 meeting in johannesburg. the conference of the parties to the convention on international trade in endangered species of wild fauna and flora (cites), to be held in johannesburg (south africa) from 24 september to 5 october 2016 is the largest global wildlife conservation agreement in existence, with 181 parties, including the eu and its 28 member states. the aim of cites is to ensure that international trade in wild animals and plants is not a threat to the survival of the species in the wild. i voted in favour because i believe that the accession to cites of the european union has rendered the union’s legal status in respect of cites more transparent vis-à-vis third parties to the convention.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the application of the postal services directive. the postal services sector in the european union has undergone a number of changes in recent years as a result of digitalisation. on the one hand, e-mail reduces the volume of letter mail, while on the other hand, online shopping increases the number of parcels and parcels. despite the different conditions in each member state, we need to promote and improve the quality and reliability of parcel delivery in the eu. in the postal services sector, we need market opening and competition to remove the many barriers to online trade in the eu that we are witnessing: high delivery costs, opacity, long delivery times and unclear liability in the event of a lost parcel.
in writing. ‒ i supported the proposal to apply the postal services directive, as the implementation of the postal services directive has helped to open up domestic letter markets and competition. the postal services sector is constantly expanding through the use of information and communication technologies, which provide opportunities for innovation and allow for market expansion.

in writing. ‒ i supported the report on the application of the postal services directive. i believe it is important to achieve the common objective of the postal services directive to ensure the sustainable implementation of the universal service, also by calling on the member states to uphold high standards of professionalism, legal protection for employees, fair and non-discriminatory access to vocational training. it is also important to ensure universal service and to enable fair competition, accessibility, quality of service and user needs.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on access to finance for smes and increasing the diversity of financing for smes in the capital markets union. small and medium-sized enterprises (smes), which account for two-thirds of private sector jobs across the european union, form the backbone of the european economy. access to finance for smes has therefore been a longstanding issue on the political agenda. the committee on budgets also stresses, inter alia, that the commission and the european central bank must recognise that access to finance is the second most serious problem facing smes. it is therefore essential that the eu budget, irrespective of their legal status, further facilitates access to finance and markets for these companies.
in writing. ‒ i supported the proposal to increase access to finance for smes and the diversity of funding for these companies in the capital markets union, because european smes are very diverse and often operate in traditional sectors. there is also a growing number of new start-ups and fast-growing innovative companies. improving access to finance for smes should not, however, lead to lowering financial standards and regulations.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on access to finance for smes and increasing the diversity of sme funding in a capital markets union. the report underlines the fact that micro enterprises, small and medium-sized enterprises and mid-caps play an important role for the european economy in terms of employment and growth. however, it acknowledges the diversity of smes, including micro-enterprises and mid-caps, in the member states. the report recognises the challenges that smes face as a result of differences between member states and regions in terms of sme financing conditions and needs. i voted in favour because i believe that a diversified, well-regulated and stable financial services sector, offering a wide range of cost-efficient tailor-made funding options, best serves the actual funding needs of smes and the real economy, enabling long-term sustainable development.
in writing. ‒ i supported the report on access to finance for smes and increasing the diversity of financing for smes in the capital markets union. i believe that smes play an important role in employment and growth in the european economy, as smes in the eu account for 67% of all employment, 71.4% of the increase in employment (year 2014). financing for smes has suffered more than financing for large companies as a result of the crisis, and the euro area has also been confronted with, and to some extent, with, tightening of bank requirements for collateral loans.
in writing. ‒ i voted for a report on how best to exploit the potential for job creation in smes. i support the view of the committee on budgets that the eu budget should be used to promote long-term quality and skilled employment and the potential of smes to create decent and sustainable jobs. the committee on budgets therefore proposes that investment in research, innovation, qualified training and development should be increased in order to promote high-quality growth and the job-creating potential of european smes. it should be remembered that smes, providing two thirds of private sector jobs across the european union, are the backbone of the european economy.

in writing. ‒ i supported a report on how best to exploit the potential for job creation in small and medium-sized enterprises (smes). i believe that smes are important for strengthening economic, social and territorial cohesion and contribute to smarter, more sustainable and inclusive growth, both in rural and urban areas. job creation in smes is influenced by a number of internal and external factors, the latter being essential conditions such as manageable competition, manageable administrative burden and total production costs, and access to finance and the availability of skilled workers. for us, the member states that joined the eu after 2004, in particular, there is a brain drain, creating peripheral regions with a shortage of skilled workers.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the application of the council directive on the general framework for equal treatment in employment and occupation (employment equality directive). we welcome the fact that almost all member states have incorporated into their constitutions the general principle of equal treatment for different forms of discrimination. member states should remove the natural, social and political obstacles which effectively prevent the implementation of the principle of equality and restrict the freedom of european citizens. the concept of the universality, indivisibility and interconnectedness of human rights cannot be a mere legal principle, valid in theory rather than in practice, since the various aspects of human identity are treated separately in the existing legal instruments of the european union.
in writing. ‒ i supported the motion for a resolution on the application of the employment equality directive, as i believe that discrimination in employment is still present in the eu, which negatively affects all aspects of life and also has negative consequences for the individual. member states are required to ensure systematic harmonisation of legislation and the implementation of the principle of equal treatment.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the application of council directive 2000/78/ec of 27 november 2000 establishing a general framework for equal treatment in employment and occupation (‘employment equality directive’). the report stipulates that in defining and implementing its policies and activities, the union shall aim to combat discrimination based on sex, racial or ethnic origin, religion or belief, disability, age or sexual orientation. moreover, it points out that, according to the eu agency for fundamental rights, all forms of discrimination, including multiple and intersectional discrimination, to a great extent hinder the deployment of human capital and constitute a barrier to career development. i voted in favour because i am of the opinion that non-discrimination in the field of occupation and employment is only effective if discrimination is comprehensively combated in all areas of life.
in writing. ‒ i supported the report on the application of council directive 2000/78/ec of 27 november 2000 on general frameworks for equal treatment in employment and occupation (employment equality directive). i believe it is important that the european union should strive to combat discrimination in defining and implementing its policies and activities. non-discrimination in the field of occupations and employment is effective only if discrimination is combated comprehensively in all areas of life, by removing the obstacles which restrict freedom and equality and prevent the integral development of the human person and the effective participation of all workers in the political, social and economic fabric of the individual member states.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the activities, impact and added value of the european globalisation adjustment fund between 2007 and 2014. i support the initiative of the committee on budgets, which notes that the european globalisation adjustment fund can support or complement member states' employment and social policy measures, but cannot replace the basic measures and competences of national authorities and should therefore not replace national workers' income schemes. it also recalls that the member states are responsible for co-financing the egf measures in accordance with the provisions of national law and are obliged to implement the egf budget effectively.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the activities, impact and added value of the european globalisation adjustment fund between 2007 and 2014. the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf) was set up to provide support for, and express its solidarity with, workers made redundant as a result of major structural changes in world trade patterns. the report emphasises the relevance of strong social dialogue based on mutual trust and shared responsibility as the best instrument with which to seek consensual solutions and common outlooks when predicting, preventing and managing restructuring processes. furthermore, it highlights that this would help to prevent job losses and therefore egf cases. i voted in favour because i believe that the current egf aims not only to support redundant workers but also to demonstrate solidarity towards those workers.
in writing. ‒ i supported the motion for a resolution on the activities, impact and added value of the european globalisation adjustment fund for the period 2007-2014. restructuring has become an increasingly common phenomenon over the past few years, with a strengthening in some sectors and a widening in others. i therefore support the european globalisation adjustment fund, which provides support for workers made redundant by major structural changes in world trade flows, and contributes to smart, sustainable and inclusive economic growth and promotes sustainable employment by supporting redundant workers and preparing them for the new job.
we are talking about the european union's relations with the largest group of countries in the world. we have a tremendous amount of important work ahead of us, and brexit, if it happens, will not make it financially stronger. the current relations and cooperation between the acp states and the european union have been and remain focused on strengthening universal values and objectives such as the promotion of human rights, democracy and sustainable development. we made the deal in coutonou in 2000 and we've revised it twice. developments in the years since the last review have shown, as has my experience on the ground in leading two european election observation missions in support of democracy in nigeria and kenya, that the starting points we share with our acp partners need to be concretised through more specific regional strategies and regional agreements that take better account of the changed political, economic and security situation. on the other hand, i very much agree with the emphasis in the report that cooperation should be in areas of common interest where mutual benefit could be expected, not only from an economic point of view, but also and above all in relation to peace and security, human rights, the rule of law, good governance, democracy, migration, the environment and so on. peace is a value that, in my view, remains the first development priority. we cannot successfully tackle poverty unless we have peace. it therefore seems to me that it makes sense for the acp and the european union to work together as a whole on this and other supporting values. in this context, i propose that in the future we devote even more energy to intercultural dialogue, which is still an underestimated opportunity for added value in polarized societies that need a higher level of internal cohesion for sustainable development. i'm grateful to colleague neuser and the shadow reporters for a job well done.

member of the commission. – mr president, if we want to achieve the sustainable development goals we must pursue our efforts to eradicate undernutrition. the commission spent almost eur 500 million per year on nutrition interventions, representing 3.1% of its development aid in 2014. the european union is also addressing undernutrition through its humanitarian assistance. we had eur 700 million spent between 2011 and 2015. but we all must do more. we will continue keeping our development policy focus on nutrition and food security issues, as well as advocating further investment in nutrition by other donors and partner countries. we will explore with a strong movement the possible pledging conference on nutrition. we will continue also to explore other interventions, such as the social safety nets, as well as reflecting on the balance between nutrition-sensitive and nutrition-specific interventions. we will continue to coordinate with donors who focus on nutrition-specific interventions, as well as maximising the synergies and complementarities of our development and humanitarian responses. this development humanitarian collaboration has been further confirmed by the commission’s response to the food crisis generated by el niño climate change phenomenon. the commission allocated an additional eur 543 million this year, almost equally shared between humanitarian and development interventions. this is coherent with the resilience approach, which aims at meeting the more immediate needs of populations in food crisis while addressing the root causes of partner countries’ fragility and vulnerability. i am confident that the proposed resolution on nutrition of the european parliament, the nutrition action plan of the commission and the council conclusions on nutrition can help the european union improve nutrition and make undernutrition history, as foreseen in sustainable development goals agenda by 2030.
member of the commission. – mr president, i have to start by saying and reconfirming that the eu is strongly committed to the fight against illegal logging and the associated trade. the flegt action plan has built an effective global coalition against it, tackling both the supply and demand sides through trade measures, through development cooperation and through broad stakeholder engagement. our action plan tackles some of the real drivers of deforestation and forest degradation. but deforestation continues and its consequences are potentially catastrophic at many levels – for the local communities that depend on forests, for the ecosystems that they support and at the global level as we deplete one of the most effective carbon sinks that we have. we must continue this fight both through our own actions and in the new global dynamic of the 2030 agenda and the paris agreement. the honourable members are right to raise their concerns, and i welcome the interest of the parliament in the follow-up to the european court of auditors report. flegt has been the subject of two reviews in the past two years. eu support to timber production countries under flegt was reviewed by the european court of auditors, while the overall performance of the action plan was also independently evaluated. a basic finding is that flegt remains highly relevant and that the work carried out so far under the action plan is delivering significant results. forest governance has improved, particularly in targeted countries, while demand for illegal timber in the eu has been reduced. the design of flegt has also been found to be future proof. that being said, things have changed since the inception of the action plan. imports of tropical timber in the eu have fallen, whilst china has become the world’s largest market and global political attention has shifted to other drivers of deforestation such as the competition for land and to other drivers of climate change. the evaluation stressed that such changes may have an impact on the relevance of the action plan if not sufficiently addressed. that is why the commission has been considering opportunities to scale up efforts to combat deforestation through flegt but also through other instruments such as redd+ and the eu timber regulation. we have now commissioned a study to consider the feasibility of a comprehensive eu action plan on deforestation. the review of the court and of the independent evaluation have highlighted important implementation challenges and areas for improvement in the way the flegt action plan has been managed, particularly in relation to the support to the countries concerned, and have recommended adjustments. we are working to address these findings to a multiannual work plan with clear objectives, targets, timeframes and budget. this will redefine priorities geographically and thematically and will ensure more effective monitoring of progress, achievements and impact. flegt is our flagship priority under the global public goods and challenges programme of the european development cooperation instrument, but we should remember that the action plan is a joint initiative. it must draw on the combined strengths and capacities of the eu and of its member states. according to the evaluation, stronger commitment and more active support by more member states is needed. finally, the honourable members also asked about voluntary partnership agreements (vpas). as mentioned by paavo väyrynen, vpas are a central flegt element, and the commission has invested intensely in their negotiation and implementation through political dialogue, through stakeholder engagement and through capacity building. our colleague david martin also mentioned indonesia and yes, soon we will be launching indonesia’s flegt licensing, and hopefully ghana will follow soon after, hopefully next year. these efforts are yielding good results in those countries where there is willingness to implement the necessary reforms. the difficulty of putting in place these reforms should not be underestimated. there are often strong vested interests, benefiting from the status quo. we will, of course, continue to make all possible efforts to maintain political momentum in vpas and address the challenges with our partner countries.

the honourable commissioner, the honourable mr president. i congratulate the rapporteur and the shadow rapporteurs on a job well done. the directive on the right to temporary legal aid for persons deprived of liberty in criminal proceedings was presented by the commission years ago, as the commissioner has already said. after difficult negotiations, an agreement was reached between the european parliament and the council only during the dutch presidency in june this year. as has been said, this is not the first eu directive on procedural rights, the area of personal security is gradually expanding in the european union and this is a good thing. i support the report as it provides common and minimum standards on the right to free legal aid for suspects and accused persons in criminal proceedings where they are deprived of liberty and free legal aid for persons against whom european arrest warrant proceedings have been initiated. in my view, the text originally proposed by the european parliament was too optimistic, since it envisaged that the scope of that directive would be extended to cases where the persons concerned were not deprived of liberty. however, not all member states could shoulder this burden. the text now provides a more realistic scope and is therefore certainly better. on the other hand, i support extending this directive to the provision of regular, not just temporary, free legal aid, as this will at least attempt to ensure a fair trial throughout the criminal proceedings. this will strengthen mutual trust between member states in the justice systems. the provision providing for the possibility of recovery in cases of abuse by persons not entitled to regular free legal aid is also appropriate. this procedural rights directive is a step towards a fair trial in the european union, but the implementation of common minimum standards of the rule of law should also be given greater attention by the eu when it comes to questionable judicial, sometimes politically motivated, processes in some transition countries where even normal rule of law standards have not yet been reached.
in writing. i support the amendment of the proposal for a directive to recognise the right to free legal aid under the european convention for the protection of human rights and fundamental freedoms and the international covenant on civil and political rights for those who do not have sufficient means to pay for legal aid themselves, where the interests of justice so require. the commission proposal will thus bring about a minimum level of free legal aid in all member states.
in writing. ‒ i was very pleased to support the proposed decision to conclude the paris agreement, which is a historic milestone in the fight against climate change. the entry into force and implementation of the agreement will mean an accelerated transition to a cleaner global economy, which recognises the importance of limited natural resources. but the final entry into force of the agreement means that we must finally move from words to action in mitigating the effects of climate change. the agreement calls for a halt to global greenhouse gas emissions and for climate neutrality beyond 2050. the key long-term objective of the agreement is to limit global warming to well below 2 °c compared to pre-industrial levels and to work towards limiting warming to 1,5 °c. at the same time, the agreement clearly emphasises the transition from fossil fuels to other sources, which in my view represents a great potential for the european, as well as for the slovenian, economy and for new jobs, especially in the field of the bioeconomy and the circular economy. the eu has been a leader in the fight against climate change for many years and in 2014 set itself an ambitious target of reducing greenhouse gas emissions by at least 40% by 2030 compared to 1990, to which eu member states have already formally committed themselves. this agreement only builds on those objectives.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the recommendation on the draft council decision on the conclusion, on behalf of the european union, of the paris agreement adopted under the united nations framework convention on climate change. the paris agreement is a historically significant landmark achievement for combating climate change and for multilateralism. it represents an ambitious, balanced, equitable and legally binding agreement. this global action aims to put the world on track to avoid dangerous climate change. moreover, the agreement acknowledges that a global peaking of greenhouse gas emissions should be reached as quickly as possible and climate neutrality should be achieved in the second half of this century. i voted in favour because i believe that the implementation of the paris agreement will play a crucial contribution to global efforts to tackle climate change.

in writing. ‒ i supported the proposed decision to use the eu solidarity fund to provide aid to greece following last year's earthquake. the adoption of the decision will make available to greece a good eur 1,6 million in funds to deal with the aftermath of the earthquake which damaged 120 residential buildings and caused the death of two people. the remaining infrastructure and cultural facilities were also extensively damaged, and some of the most important tourist beaches on lefkada were destroyed. the total amount of damage was estimated at eur 66 million, which exceeds the threshold of 1,5% of regional gdp and thus meets the criterion for aid from the solidarity fund. it is also noted that the region concerned belongs to the category of less developed regions. as greece has already received eur 164.798 in march this year, 10% of the total, the remaining amount of the solidarity fund assistance to be paid amounts to eur 1.487.036.
in writing. ‒ the report on the proposal for a decision on the mobilisation of the european union solidarity fund provides for the mobilisation of part of the fund's resources for the purpose of addressing the consequences of several earthquakes that struck the ionian islands region in greece on 17 november 2015, in particular the island of lefkada, the northern parts of ithaca and kefalonia. the european union solidarity fund is designed to help a member state or a candidate country affected by a major disaster. the cost of the emergency activities, as defined in article 3 of the solidarity fund regulation, is estimated by the greek authorities at eur 52,374 million, of which eur 38 million relates to the transport sector and eur 7 million to the protection of cultural heritage. the commission has decided to grant the aid in the amount of eur 164,798 or 10% of the expected aid from the fund, as requested by greece, on 18 march 2016. the total amount of the proposed aid is eur 1 651 834. i support the idea of solidarity in cases like this, which is why i voted for it.

in writing. ‒ i also supported the decision to use the globalisation adjustment fund, which finland had requested a few months ago, in order to reintegrate workers who had become redundant in microsoft, or formerly nokia, and its suppliers, into the labour market. the application concerns 1441 of the 2161 workers made redundant and amounts to eur 1 365 000. the redundancies were linked to large structural flows in information and communication trade, which result in increased employment in asia. nokia dominated the mobile phone market in the first decade of the 21st century, but was driven out by asian manufacturers using the android and ios operating systems. finland has been facing these problems for some time, as the nokia case affected the entire finnish electronics industry. in fact, following the sale of nokia to microsoft, the number of employees in finland alone decreased by 1100 in 2014 and a further 2300 people are expected to lose their jobs in 2015 and 2016 due to the restructuring of the phone production. eu assistance is therefore very important for re-employment and for helping displaced workers.
in writing. ‒ the globalisation adjustment fund has an annual budget of eur 150 million and provides assistance in cases where more than 500 workers are made redundant in a single company, in a single sector and in a single region, as a result of major structural changes in world trade. the assistance is reflected in job search, career guidance, education, retraining, mobility and the like. on 29 july 2016, the european commission adopted a proposal to activate the said fund for the benefit of finland to support the reintegration of workers made redundant in finland by microsoft and eight suppliers and related producers. the finnish government stated that the main reason for the above-mentioned redundancies was the declining share of microsoft in the mobile device market. the decrease in the number of employees is linked to the greater movements in world trade, with the number of employees in the it sector decreasing in the eu and increasing in the usa and china. support for finnish workers will take the form of six different services ranging from training to start-up capital for start-up companies. since the fund is working well and this is the situation for which it was set up, i supported the report.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a decision of the european parliament and of the council on the mobilisation of the european globalisation adjustment fund for the application submitted by finland microsoft. at microsoft mobile oy and eight suppliers and manufacturers in the post-production phase in finland, 2161 workers were made redundant as a result of the negative effects of globalisation, as reflected in the consequences of major structural changes in world trade flows or the consequences of the global financial and economic crisis. since the application was complete and therefore microsoft mobile oy met all the conditions, i supported the report.

in writing. ‒ i supported the report on the right to free legal aid. free legal aid is a sensitive subject, as there is no uniform interpretation of the right to a fair trial between member states and their judicial systems, and consequently no free legal aid. despite the longer time taken by the commission to prepare a proposal for a directive in this area, the proposal allows for a minimum level of free legal aid in all eu member states, which is reinforced by the amendments adopted by the european parliament. i also welcome the eligibility criteria for free legal aid, as they provide some clarity on the whole procedure. however, differences in the cost of legal proceedings between member states must also be borne in mind.
in writing. ‒ the directive on temporary legal aid for suspects or accused persons deprived of liberty and persons in european arrest warrant proceedings contains minimum harmonised rules on when and how member states are obliged to pay for legal representation in these situations. the report mentions in particular situations in which the member state will provide for the payment of legal representation when an individual cannot afford it and sets out minimum rules for such situations. this directive will harmonise the rules for determining cases in which an individual is entitled to legal aid throughout the eu. at the same time, exceptions are provided for covering minor offences, alcohol testing procedures and the like. the directive to which this report refers will be part of the wider context of legislative proposals by the european commission aimed at strengthening the procedural rights of suspects or accused persons. since the report envisages the harmonisation of rules and the introduction of common standards in this area, i have decided to support it.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a directive of the european parliament and of the council on temporary legal aid for suspects or accused persons deprived of liberty and persons in proceedings following a european arrest warrant. i support the amendment of the proposal for a directive to recognise the right to free legal aid under the european convention for the protection of human rights and fundamental freedoms and the international covenant on civil and political rights for those who do not have sufficient means to pay for legal aid themselves, where the interests of justice so require. the commission proposal will thus bring about a minimum level of free legal aid in all member states.
in writing. ‒ i supported the proposal for a directive of the european parliament and of the council on temporary legal aid free of charge for suspects or accused persons deprived of their liberty and for persons in proceedings based on a european arrest warrant. the commission proposal is a welcome step towards ensuring a minimum level of free legal aid in all member states. the proposal is limited to the right to temporary legal aid for suspects or accused persons in criminal proceedings in which they are deprived of liberty and to the right to temporary legal aid and legal aid for requested persons in proceedings based on a european arrest warrant. the inclusion in the directive of a specific provision to take utmost account of the preferences and wishes of suspects or accused persons and requested persons in the choice of a lawyer providing free legal aid is particularly deserved.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a directive of the european parliament and of the council on provisional legal aid for suspects or accused persons deprived of liberty and legal aid in european arrest warrant proceedings. according to article 82 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union (tfeu), judicial cooperation in criminal matters in the union shall be based on the principle of mutual recognition of judgements and judicial decisions. the implementation of this principle presupposes that member states put trust in each other’s criminal justice systems, including in the manner in which the rights of suspects of accused persons are safeguarded. in practice, however, national practices vary in this respect. for those who are lacking the necessary financial means, only legal aid can make the right to access to a lawyer effective. i voted in favour because i believe that the proposal of the commission is a welcome step in ensuring a minimum level of legal aid in all member states.
in writing. ‒ the proposal for a directive of the european parliament and of the council on temporary legal aid establishes common minimum rules on the right to legal aid for suspects and accused persons in criminal proceedings and persons subject to european arrest warrant proceedings (wanted persons), irrespective of their legal status, nationality or citizenship. the proposal for a directive supports the fundamental rights and principles recognised by the charter and the echr, in particular the right to an effective remedy and the right to a fair trial, the presumption of innocence and the right of defence. in the light of the above, i believe that the proposal for a european parliament and council directive on temporary legal aid will strengthen the procedural rights of suspects, accused persons or requested persons in criminal proceedings and i therefore supported it.
in writing. ‒ the control of trade in torture products has been needed for a long time and i am pleased that we have finally voted on the proposal for a regulation which seeks to regulate this area in the most appropriate way. i supported the motion without reservation. the manufacture and sale of torture equipment and its use are among the most reprehensible things that must be strictly controlled and severely punished. i am therefore convinced that consistency must be ensured in eu export controls for military equipment, firearms and equipment for torture. i also welcome the commission's proposals to prevent the use of proven medical products for lethal injection. in order to ensure effective control of this area, it is also necessary to monitor adequately the implementation of the commitments of the member states, including the obligation to report and exchange information through a secure encrypted system.
in writing. ‒ the export control mechanism was first established at european level in 2005 by regulation no 1236/2005 and has contributed to the respect of human rights in third countries. the new regulation will further extend this control mechanism, while filling major gaps in the existing controls on exports of products that could be used for capital punishment, torture or other similar treatment and punishment. the report also includes a ban on the transit of the products in question and a ban on the advertising and promotion of products prohibited for export. under the new regulation, member states will be required to provide information on the controls they have carried out on trade in these products, using national preventive mechanisms established under the un convention against torture and other cruel, inhuman or degrading treatment or punishment. i support the report and the proposed regulation, which is why i voted in favour.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council amending council regulation (ec) no 1236/2005 concerning trade in certain goods which could be used for capital punishment, torture or other cruel, inhuman or degrading treatment or punishment. the ‘anti-torture regulation’ (ec) no 1236/2005 is a unique instrument that contributes to protection of human rights via controls on items and activities that are used for or could be misused for capital punishment, torture or other cruel, inhuman or degrading treatment or punishment. the ‘anti-torture regulation’ contributes to the long-standing eu policy of eliminating the death penalty worldwide, and of preventing torture. it helps achieve these goals by combining prohibitions with licensing requirements for trade in listed goods. i voted in favour because i believe that it is of crucial importance to ensure a right mix of the eu legislative, administrative, judicial and external measures to prevent and prohibit the production, trade and use of torture goods and effectively control items with potential lethal and inhumane uses.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council amending council regulation (ec) no 1236/2005 concerning trade in certain goods which could be used for capital punishment, torture or other cruel, inhuman or degrading treatment or punishment. i consider it important to control trade with third countries in goods that could be used for capital punishment or for torture or other cruel, inhuman or degrading treatment or punishment. the warnings of undertakings that controls should not impede legitimate trade are also justified. it is therefore necessary to maintain a balance in the implementation of the regulation between the interest of undertakings in the smooth flow of legitimate trade and the control of the possible use of certain products for capital punishment, torture or other cruel treatment or punishment.

in writing. ‒ europol assists eu member states in the fight against organised crime. as organised crime simply does not stop at eu borders, cooperation with other countries around the world and international organisations is of paramount importance. while such cooperation is welcome, agreements need to take into account the partner country's criminal law enforcement practices and the related respect for human rights. the parliament's report proposing the conclusion of such an agreement with china provides for the exchange of operational and technical information, including personal and confidential information. according to europol, china is becoming increasingly relevant for the prosecution of organised crime, as in many cases it is a country of origin, destination or transit for various criminal activities. the problem with the proposed agreement is that china does not respect human rights in the area of crime prosecution, but at the same time defines criminals and terrorists differently. recently, china has detained as many as 280 human rights activists and lawyers, and some 40 are still being held on suspicion of representing an organized criminal group. at the same time, there are laws being passed that require all online companies in china to have a chinese cyber policeman in their company to monitor the "spread of rumors". because of the controversial chinese methods of prosecuting organised crime, i have decided to vote against the report.

in writing. ‒ i supported the resolution on strengthening relations between the african, caribbean and pacific group of states on the one hand and the eu on the other, as this is an important partnership in which the eu has a key role to play. europe must continue to provide a wide range of assistance to these countries, as 80% of the world's least developed countries are located in these regions. development aid to reduce migratory pressures from these countries, especially african ones, to the eu is, in my view, crucial both to create more favourable and safer living conditions in these countries and to sustain the flow of economic migrants to europe. the partners of the partnership agreement between the members of the african, caribbean and pacific group of states and the eu must devote all their energies to combating and eradicating poverty and inequality, and must also commit to strengthening sustainable development. cooperation should be based primarily on mutual benefits for the partners, in particular with regard to peace and security, human rights and the rule of law, migration, the environment and climate change. i sincerely hope that cooperation will bring results and thus greater prosperity to countries that have been struggling for many years with poverty, hunger and political instability.
in writing. ‒ the acp-eu relations and cooperation so far have been and remain geared to strengthening universal values and objectives such as the promotion of human rights, democracy and sustainable development. my experience on the ground, leading two european election observation missions in support of democracy in nigeria and kenya, suggests that the starting point needs to be concretised through more specific regional strategies and regional agreements that take better account of the changed political, economic and security situation. cooperation should take place in areas of common interest where mutual benefit can be expected, not only from an economic point of view, but also and in particular in relation to peace and security, human rights and the rule of law, good governance and democracy, migration, the environment, climate change and other areas related to the well-being of the population. peace is a value that, in my view, remains the first development priority. we cannot successfully tackle the problem of poverty unless we have peace. it therefore seems to me that it makes sense for the acp and the eu to work together as a whole in support of this and other universal values. in this context, i propose that we devote even more energy to intercultural dialogue in the future.
in writing. ‒ the report deals with the partnership agreement between the members of the african, caribbean and pacific group of states, on the one hand, and the european community and its member states, on the other. it is the most comprehensive partnership agreement between developed and developing countries in the world and expires in 2020. for this reason, this report advocates the continuation of this agreement under a new structure, which is simply too low-ambition in line with the report's guidelines. the african, caribbean and pacific (acp) group of states is dysfunctional in terms of decision-making, as decisions must be taken by consensus, which is rare. also politically, the group exists almost exclusively because of eu funding, political dialogue between the group's countries is often very limited, and the partnership between the eu and the members of the african, caribbean and pacific group of states is unbalanced, as the eu can exert pressure on this group of countries due to its political coherence. the greens are therefore seeking a more open approach to partnership. it would also be good to consider replacing the existing agreement with individual agreements between the eu and each of the three regions involved. for all the reasons i have outlined, i did not support the report.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the future of acp-eu relations after 2020. cooperation between african, caribbean and pacific countries has so far proved very welcome and necessary. a partnership based on fundamental values and principles such as respect for human rights and fundamental freedoms, democracy based on the rule of law, and transparent and accountable governance. i support the opinion of the committee on budgets, which points out that the european development fund should finally be included in the budget, but only with clear guarantees for the targeting of funds for acp-eu cooperation and the maintenance of the level of financing.
in writing. ‒ i supported the motion for a resolution on the future of acp-eu relations after 2020. acp-eu cooperation is a valuable and unique achievement that has strengthened the ties between the peoples, countries and parliaments of the acp and the eu over the past 40 years. the acp states have clearly demonstrated their desire to take joint action, we stress that a new structure is essential to enhance cooperation and adapt to new challenges, preserving those parts of the acp-eu legal order that are inherently universal, such as the commitment to human rights and gender equality, human development, good governance and democracy, respect for the rule of law and the exchange of best practice within a common framework, while the bulk of the work must be done in accordance with the principle of subsidiarity, which means that it must be done through regional agreements tailored to specific regional needs and the mutual interests of the eu and individual regions.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the future of acp-eu relations beyond 2020. the overarching objective of the cotonou agreement is reducing and eventually eradicating poverty, consistent with the objectives of sustainable development and the gradual integration of the acp countries into the world economy. over 80% of the world’s least developed countries (ldcs) are from acp regions, which gives particular relevance to the eu-acp partnership. however, the numerical strength of the acp and eu member states has not sufficiently translated into joint action in global fora. the report underlines that acp-eu cooperation is a valuable and unique achievement that has strengthened bonds between acp and eu peoples and countries and their parliaments throughout the last 40 years. it equally emphasises that the future of acp-eu relations should be based on a new reflection on the potential and obstacles ahead for eu-acp cooperation. i voted in favour because i believe that in order to improve the effectiveness of cooperation and adapt it to new challenges, a new structure must be adopted that maintains those parts of the acp-eu acquis that are universal in nature, such as a commitment to human rights and gender equality, human development, good governance and democracy.

in writing. ‒ i welcome peru's accession to the hague convention and therefore had no reservations about supporting the proposed decision. the 1980 hague convention on the civil aspects of international child abduction is a very important instrument that provides for a system of cooperation in finding solutions to cases of international child abduction. the convention has long been ratified by all eu member states. the most common problem is the breakdown of the union between parents who come from different countries. there is a danger that one of the parents may wish to take advantage of the lack of cooperation between the two countries and thus gain exclusive custody of the children. in such cases, the main problem is the national bias of the legal systems in individual countries, and judgments often end up with each national court entrusting the child to the care and upbringing of a parent who is a national of that country. the convention, however, provides for the jurisdiction of the courts and the law of the country in which the child is domiciled, as well as a system to ensure the prompt return of the child wrongfully removed. in the event of peru's accession to the convention, this will mean that children associated with the peruvian community in eu member states will be protected against unlawful removal.
in writing. ‒ i supported the proposal for a council decision authorising the republic of austria and romania to accept, in the interest of the european union, peru's accession to the 1980 hague convention on the civil aspects of international child abduction. often, problems arise when a couple's relationship ends. if the parents are from different countries, there is a risk that one of them will try to take advantage of the lack of cooperation between these countries and gain exclusive custody of the children. the purpose of this convention is to resolve such cases at the international level by determining the courts and the law of the state in which the child is domiciled as the courts having jurisdiction and the law applicable. the convention also provides for a system to ensure the prompt return of a child wrongfully removed.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a council decision authorising the republic of austria and romania to accept, in the interest of the european union, the accession of peru to the 1980 hague convention on the civil aspects of international child abduction. the hague convention of 25 october 1980 on the civil aspects of international child abduction is a vitally important instrument that has been ratified by all eu member states. the convention introduces a system of cooperation between the contracting states aimed at settling cases of international child abduction. in many instances, these problems arise when a couple has separated. if the mother and father are from different states, there is a temptation to exploit the lack of cooperation between those states in order to secure custody of the child. the biggest problem in such cases is the national bias of the legal systems of individual states. the purpose of the convention is to resolve such situations at an international level, by establishing that the competent courts and applicable laws are those of the state of residence of the child. i believe that the accession of peru to the convention is to be welcomed, especially as many eu citizens are of peruvian origin.
