in writing. ‒ resolution on international accounting standards: i supported ifrs 9. ifrs 9 will enter into force on 1 january 2018 and will replace ias 39, and is a set of financial instruments that will be able to respond to some aspects of the financial crisis and its impact on the banking sector. ifrs 9 provides improvements over ias 39 by changing the impairment model based on incurred losses to the impairment model based on expected losses, thereby addressing the issue of 'too little and too late' in the process of recognising loan losses. however, the opinions of auditors in this area vary widely and it is therefore necessary for the esas, the commission and the european accounting advisory group to work together to develop guidelines to prevent misuse of management discretion.
in writing. ‒ if we would like to achieve a more industrialised europe, with high potential for generating jobs and growth, it is essential to support that aim with a properly functioning and efficient capital market. standardising companies’ financial reporting is one more building block towards that goal.
in writing. ‒ the international accounting standards board has issued international accounting reporting standards 9 which relate to financial instruments. this was in response to some aspects of the financial crisis and its impact on the banking sector. these standards will replace the older ones and will enter into force on 1 january 2018. parliament considered these accounting standards to be an important response to the crisis by the international accounting standards board, but also to be improvements, particularly in the area of impairment models. the resolution also calls on the european commission, in cooperation with the european supervisory authorities, to closely monitor the implementation of the new standards in the eu and to prepare an ex post impact assessment by june 2019 at the latest and submit it to the european parliament. a similar call is also made to the international accounting standards board to carry out a post-implementation review to identify and assess adverse effects. i believe that the revision of accounting standards is an important step in the fight against financial crises and i therefore supported the resolution.
in writing. ‒ motion for a european parliament resolution on international accounting standards: i supported ifrs 9. ifrs 9 financial instruments is one of the iasb's (the international accounting standards board) most important responses to the financial crisis. ifrs 9 provides improvements over ias 39 by changing the impairment model based on incurred losses to the impairment model based on expected losses, thereby addressing the issue of 'too little and too late' in the process of recognising loan losses. ifrs 9 will become effective on 1 january 2018 and will replace ias 39.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the motion for a resolution on international financial reporting standards: ifrs 9. the global financial crisis brought the role played by international financial reporting standards (ifrs) in financial stability and growth onto the g20 and eu agendas. the resolution notes that ifrs 9 – financial instruments constitutes one of the major responses of the international accounting standards board to the financial crisis. moreover, the resolution notes the importance of fully understanding the interaction of ifrs 9 with other regulatory requirements. i voted in favour because i believe that the principle of prudence must be the key guiding principle for any accounting standard.
in writing. ‒ i supported the european parliament resolution on international accounting standards. in the wake of the global financial crisis, the role of international accounting standards, in particular the rules on the recognition of losses in the banking system, is crucial for financial stability and growth. i therefore support the call on the commission, in cooperation with the esas, the european central bank, the esrb and efrag, to closely monitor the implementation of ifrs 9 in the eu, to prepare an ex post impact assessment by june 2019 at the latest and to submit it to the european parliament and to act on its views.
in writing. - so many words have been said about syria that any one is unnecessary. actions are essential, but they are very different from words and international agreements . meanwhile, children, women and many other innocent civilians are dying, and survivors are heading in large numbers to safety and onward to europe. i supported the resolution because, from a human point of view, i have no reason to oppose it. more to the point, i wonder what the passage of the resolution will change. i'm afraid not much. the recent attacks on hospitals and humanitarian convoys are undoubtedly worthy of condemnation as a serious violation of international humanitarian law and a war crime. russia and the assad regime must immediately cease attacks on civilians and infrastructure, and the siege of cities must end. the key to beginning to resolve the dire situation in syria is to resume negotiations for a lasting ceasefire and to step up efforts to achieve a lasting political solution in the country. the eu must be more actively involved in the rescue effort. the latter have remained in a subordinate position throughout the years of the conflict, while they are the ones most affected by the waves of migrants and terrorism.
in writing. ‒ the epp group members believe that a lasting solution in syria requires a political transition through a syrian-led inclusive process with the support of the international community. all parties in the conflict should ensure the protection of the civilian population and honour their obligations under international humanitarian law and human rights law. definitely, peace in syria will not be achieved by an externally lead, non-inclusive approach. it is a matter for syria, with syrians.
in writing. ‒ despite negotiations and a brief ceasefire, the war in syria is by no means over and the situation is getting worse. the european parliament therefore strongly condemned in its resolution, in the light of recent events, all attacks on civilians and civilian infrastructure, the continuation of sieges and the lack of humanitarian aid. it also strongly condemned the recent attack on a humanitarian convoy and a red cross warehouse near aleppo and called on all parties involved, in particular russia and the assad regime, to cease attacks on civilians. parliament called on all parties involved in the international syria support group to continue negotiations to establish a stable ceasefire and to accelerate work towards a lasting political solution. i believe that a peaceful solution to the conflict in syria is essential for peace in the wider region and in the world, and that is why i supported the resolution.
in writing. ‒ i supported the european parliament's motion for a resolution on syria. violence in syria is escalating, particularly in aleppo, which is the target of heavy aerial bombardment and where health facilities are also attacked. the situation has become dramatic and is deteriorating rapidly, despite efforts by the international community to end hostilities. it calls on all parties to immediately cease attacks on the civilian population and infrastructure, including water and electricity infrastructure, to take measures to end all sieges and to allow humanitarian agencies unhindered and safe access. strongly supports the demands of the un special envoy for an end to the violence and protection of civilians and infrastructure, and for a weekly 48-hour ceasefire to allow at least humanitarian access to aleppo for the un and its partners, and for the evacuation of the wounded and sick.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the motion for a resolution on syria. the conflict in syria is well into its sixth year and has claimed the lives of more than a quarter of a million people. up to 14 million people are thought to be in need of humanitarian assistance within syria, while almost five million are in hard-to-reach or besieged areas. despite international efforts to reach a ceasefire, violence has escalated in recent weeks, with aleppo in particular facing heavy bombardments. the resolution urges all parties to the conflict immediately to stop all attacks on civilians and civilian infrastructure, including water and electrical infrastructure, to lift all sieges and to grant unhindered and safe access to international aid workers. i voted in favour because i believe that the eu must do everything in its power to work against terrorism in syria.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the european parliament resolution of 6 october 2016 on syria. reports indicate that violence is escalating in syria, particularly in aleppo, which is the target of heavy aerial bombardment and where health facilities are being attacked. the civilian population in besieged areas in aleppo and elsewhere in syria, including women and children, lack access to basic humanitarian assistance and are in dire need of food, clean water and medical supplies. i therefore join the call for all parties concerned to cease attacks on civilians and infrastructure, to take immediate and decisive action to end hostilities and sieges, and to allow humanitarian agencies rapid, safe and unhindered access to all people in need.
in writing. ‒ just as i was pleased to support the decision to conclude the paris agreement, i also supported the above-mentioned resolution on the guidelines for the 2016 un climate change conference to be held in marrakech in november. i hope that the conference will chart a clear path towards an operational plan for implementing the key elements of the paris agreement an enhanced transparency framework, details of the global stocktake, further guidance on planned nationally determined contributions, an agreement on differentiation, loss and damage, climate finance and support for capacity purposes, etc. as in the past, the eu must continue to set an example for others and should immediately start aligning its climate and energy objectives with the agreed international target of limiting the global average temperature increase to below 2 °c, while also working towards limiting the increase to 1,5 °c, as also defined in the paris agreement. i am confident that the formal entry into force of the agreement during the marrakesh conference will increase the motivation to implement the objectives of the agreement and will also make it easier to find solutions to save our planet.
in writing. ‒ the resolution contains the european parliament's position for the next conference of the parties to the paris agreement to combat climate change, which will take place from 7 to 18 november 2016. the resolution describes an ambitious approach and calls on member states to take an even more active role in the fight against climate change. the resolution calls on the developed countries to further accelerate the dialogue to achieve more comprehensive reductions in greenhouse gas emissions and to implement the paris agreement as soon as possible. parliament expressed disappointment at the current proposal by the international civil aviation organisation on the current legislation. it is very important to me that the resolution also contains a serious acknowledgement of the existence of the so-called climate refugees. population movements due to climate change are a real problem of our time, and we must not turn a blind eye to the problems associated with such migrations. at the same time, it is important that the resolution calls on countries to increase the creation of financial levers that will be dedicated solely to combating climate change. i supported the resolution because of the extremely important subject it addresses.
in writing. ‒ i supported the european parliament resolution on the implementation of the paris agreement and the 2016 un climate change conference in marrakech, morocco (cop 22). the paris agreement on climate change is an important milestone in the fight against climate change. the agreement is ambitious, balanced, fair and legally binding. the adoption of the agreement and the joint declaration of the 187 parties' planned nationally determined contributions before the end of cop 21 represent a significant milestone for comprehensive and joint global action, and the agreement, when implemented, will definitively and irreversibly accelerate the transition to a climate-neutral, climate-resilient global economy. the eu is on track to exceed its greenhouse gas emission reduction targets by 2020 and to meet its renewable energy target by 2020.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the motion for a resolution on the implementation of the paris agreement and the 2016 un climate change conference in marrakesh, morocco. the paris agreement is to enter into force on the thirtieth day after the date on which at least 55 parties to the convention, accounting in total for at least an estimated 55% of the total global ghg emissions, have deposited their instruments of ratification, acceptance, approval or accession to the un. the most serious effects of climate change will be felt in developing countries, particularly in those least developed countries and developing small island states that have insufficient resources to prepare for and adjust to the changes. the resolution underlines that the eu has both the capacity and responsibility to lead by example and to start work immediately on aligning its climate and energy targets with the agreed international goal of limiting the increase in global average temperature to below 2°c, while pursuing efforts to limit that increase to 1.5°c. i voted in favour because i believe that combating climate change is the priority and should be pursued worldwide while ensuring energy security and the development of sustainable economic growth and jobs.
in writing. ‒ i supported the european parliament resolution on the implementation of the paris agreement and the 2016 un climate change conference in marrakech, morocco (cop 22). the resolution concludes that the emissions reduction plan is not ambitious enough to meet the paris agreement objectives and calls on eu member states to reduce emissions under current commitments and encourages politically and financially coordinated efforts for sustainable development. i believe that the calls are justified, as the consequences of climate change are often irreversible and cause economic, ecological and social losses. it is important that the eu maintains its leadership role in preventing climate change and actively participates in climate forums such as the forthcoming one in marrakech to achieve global performance of the paris agreement commitments with partner countries.
in writing. ‒ i also supported the report by ms schaldemos on the implementation of the regulation on materials intended to come into contact with food. this report is a response to a survey by the european parliament's research department and a study by the european food safety authority, which found that many substances present in food contact materials are not evaluated. this is particularly the case for so-called 'unintentional additives', such as impurities in intentionally added substances or substances resulting from chemical reactions present in the final material. it is therefore of the utmost importance that the manufacturers of these materials provide complete information and that scientific institutions and laboratories in all member states cooperate well. the report concludes that legislation in this area also needs to improve traceability, along the entire supply chain. in particular, it is important that the same standards of traceability and compliance apply to food contact materials imported from third countries.
in writing. ‒ i supported the report, whose key contribution is to encourage the necessary action at ec level to fill the gaps resulting from the lack of specific measures for certain materials and the shortcomings in compliance and control. the debate in parliament has shown that the subject of food packaging materials is one that undoubtedly deserves more attention. we have verified the implementation of the relevant regulation and have identified concerns. our aim is to promote the development of materials and products that are safe, reusable and recyclable, thus contributing to the union's efforts to establish a more efficient circular economy.
in writing. ‒ food contact materials are something we encounter on a daily basis. they can be found in food packaging, kitchen utensils, and the like. different materials may behave very differently when in contact with food and leave traces or particles in the food. it is therefore important that the rules on the main standards are regulated at european union level. the report recommends in particular that action be taken at eu level on materials that are regulated in each country separately. these materials are mainly paper (also recycled), cardboard, various coatings, inks and accessories. the main point of this report is the need to address rapidly the current shortcomings in the implementation of the regulation of materials intended to come into contact with food. i believe that in the case of exposed materials, the most important issues are risk assessment, traceability, enforcement and control. i supported the report because food safety is crucial to our health and a healthy environment.
in writing. ‒ i supported the proposal for a regulation implementing the regulation on materials intended to come into contact with foodstuffs (regulation (ec) no 1935/2004). materials intended to come into contact with food are often used in everyday life in the form of food packaging, kitchen utensils, tableware and accessories, etc. chemicals from materials intended to come into contact with food endanger human health or adversely affect the composition of food. as food is considered to be one of the main routes of human exposure to chemicals, these materials are subject to legally binding rules at eu level, currently set out in the framework regulation. the regulation lays down general safety requirements applicable to all possible materials and articles intended to come into contact with food.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the implementation of the food contact materials regulation ((ec) no 1935/2004). food contact materials (fcms) are largely used in everyday life in the form of food packaging, kitchen utensils, tableware, etc. when put in contact with food, and depending on their composition and properties, the different materials may behave differently, transferring their constituents to the food. in such cases, chemicals emanating from fcms may endanger human health or adversely change the composition of the foodstuffs. the regulation sets out general safety requirements that are applicable to all possible food contact materials and articles. i voted in favour because i believe that further harmonisation at eu level for non-harmonised materials through specific measures based on scientific evidence would be a step in the right direction, giving priority to those materials that constitute a particular risk to human health and are in bigger demand on the eu market.
in writing. ‒ individual materials and articles intended to come into contact with food may, due to their specific composition, pose a risk to public health and the environment. therefore, effective monitoring of safety requirements for all materials and articles intended to come into direct or indirect contact with food is important to prevent the entry of substances into food in quantities that could endanger human health or cause unacceptable changes in the composition of food. i believe that the implementation report on the regulation on materials intended to come into contact with foodstuffs (regulation (ec) no 1935/2004) comprehensively presents the shortcomings in the field of enforcement of the existing regulation and sets out appropriate measures to improve the situation, and i therefore supported it.
in writing. ‒ i also supported the 2014 annual report on monitoring the application of eu law, which contains a lot of interesting information on the actual implementation and practical application of eu law. the report shows that the areas of environment, transport, internal market and services were the most affected by infringement procedures in 2014. if i translate this to the national level of the country i come from, the situation is similar. i am very pleased that the number of procedures is decreasing, which is an indication of the improvement in the dialogue between the commission and the member states.
in writing. ‒ european union law is of paramount importance to the very functioning of this common union of states. it is therefore important that its implementation and use are monitored. the 2014 annual report on the monitoring of the application of union law states that the enforcement of eu law is still not sufficiently transparent and open. it calls for respect for the principles of legal clarity, transparency and openness and for the correct and timely application of eu law. although enforcing eu law is supposed to be one of the priorities of the current european commission, this goal is far from being achieved. i believe that the commission should be more active in this area, and at the same time the european parliament could play a greater role in analysing the enforcement of eu law. the eu should also offer wider support to the most recent and future members in their own implementation and enforcement of eu law. i support efforts to improve in this area and have therefore supported the report.
in writing. ‒ i supported the proposal on monitoring the application of union law annual report 2014. the 32nd annual report on the monitoring of the application of eu law by the commission shows that the areas of environment, transport, internal market and services were the most affected by infringement procedures in 2014. it also highlights that the number of formal infringement procedures has decreased over the past five years. parliament still has very limited access to information on procedures and open cases in eu pilot. the report therefore concludes that the enforcement of eu law is still not sufficiently transparent.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on monitoring the application of union law: 2014 annual report. the commission’s 32nd annual report on monitoring the application of eu law shows that environment, transport and internal market and services remained the policy areas in which most infringement cases were open in 2014. the annual report also stresses that the number of formal infringement procedures has decreased in the last five years. i voted in favour because i believe that the european parliament should play a more structured role in the analysis of how accession countries and countries with association agreements with the european union comply with eu law and in developing appropriate support in this respect to those countries.
in writing. ‒ in a european union based on the rule of law and legal certainty and predictability, monitoring the application of eu law in the member states is essential for the credibility of the institutions and citizens' confidence in the effective functioning of the eu. the report on monitoring the application of union law, in my view, rightly calls on the commission to improve the preparation of legislation, to set more realistic deadlines for the transposition and enforcement of legislation in the member states and to effectively monitor the timely and correct transposition of eu law into national law, and i therefore supported it.
in writing. ‒ like all objections to the placing on the market of genetically engineered seeds for cultivation, i supported this objection, which relates to gm maize bt11. there is also no consensus amongst the scientific community on the issue of gmos, and it is expected that members of parliament and the general public will share our views on these issues. i myself am a proponent of the precautionary principle in the case of gmos, and i think it is completely unnecessary to rush through a sensitive subject such as the registration of gmo maize. we are at a delicate moment when the institutions should have more respect for each other and, above all, for the will of the people who are largely against the use of gmos in europe. i also wonder very much, personally, if we really need this kind of gmo corn seed. the genetically modified bt11 maize treated contains the pat protein which confers resistance to the herbicide glufosinate-ammonium, the use of which is only authorised in the eu until 2017. that herbicide is toxic to reproduction and the use of genetically modified maize would lead to an increase in its use and thus an increase in the risk to human health.

in writing. ‒ the european parliament successfully objected to the authorisation of five food and feed products derived from genetically modified organisms. these include the seeds of the genetically modified maize bt11 covered by this resolution. at the same time, the european commission rejected the call for a change in the procedure for authorising the use of individual genetically modified organisms, as the european parliament considers that the procedure is currently undemocratic, as decisions are now taken by the commission. there is also a certain lack of data on the use and import of genetically modified organisms, as the commission rarely shares data with the european parliament in such cases. the european food safety authority is also currently reviewing genetically modified organisms that the commission intends to authorise for research use. i believe that we need to keep our food safe and healthy, and i voted in favour of a resolution by parliament seeking to reject the authorisation of the genetically modified bt11 maize seeds.
in writing. ‒ objection under rule 106: i supported the placing on the market for cultivation of genetically modified maize bt11. in 1996, syngenta seeds sas (formerly novartis seeds) (the notifier) submitted to the competent authority of france a request for the placing on the market of genetically modified maize bt11 in accordance with council directive 90/220/eec (8). the draft implementing decision is not in line with union law and the objective of directive 2001/18/ec of the european parliament and of the council, namely to approximate the laws, regulations and administrative provisions of the member states in accordance with the precautionary principle and to protect human health and the environment, where gmos are deliberately released into the environment for any reason other than placing on the market in the community or when gmos are placed on the market as or in products in the community.

in writing. organized crime, corruption and money laundering threaten not only freedom of economic activity and competitiveness, but above all the security and freedom of all citizens. if we are to successfully counter these paralysing threats at both european and national level, we must not delay any longer in taking appropriate action. the cross-border dimension of criminal organisations requires a uniform definition of criminal offences and close cooperation between national authorities and european union agencies. the establishment of a european public prosecutor's office, independent of national governments and eu institutions, is a real step towards a more effective fight against corruption.

madam president, first of all i would also like to thank sophia in ‘t veld and the other shadow rapporteurs. i agree with the first vice-president that it is a very political process, and the rule of law is the key fundamental framework of our union. if that fails, our democracy is seriously threatened. i very much agree with my colleagues that we need to kick off by finding institutional agreement on establishing a mechanism like this that is in fact a manifestation of our common european values. let me remind you, commissioner timmermans, that in 2013 you, together with your colleagues, wrote to the former president of the commission, mr barroso, asking him for the establishment of such a mechanism that would protect our fundamental values. we have today an excellent chance to make it happen. in general, i do not support the idea of duplicating mechanisms with tools that already exist, but i do not feel that today we have such mechanisms that are effective. looking at the situation in poland or hungary, socialists and democrats have for a long time been pushing for the establishment of a democracy scoreboard. today we ask the accession countries to meet the copenhagen criteria, but the member states can simply do whatever they want. so i very much support the idea of establishing such a mechanism on democracy that would stop various violations of the treaties, for example freedom of the media, which we heard mentioned several times. so this mechanism is really needed.
i have long advocated the establishment of an effective mechanism to monitor the functioning of democracy, the rule of law and fundamental rights in the member states. i believe that a politically independent mechanism is one of the key measures for the rule of law in the european union, so that abuses are no longer abused, especially in transition, post-socialist countries. it is known that in slovenia, for example, opposition champion janez janša was arrested without evidence three weeks before the parliamentary elections, but after the elections and six months in prison he was cleared of all charges. and that's the end of the story. in cases of such serious abuse, the union should react immediately, but it does not, because it does not have the appropriate mechanism. with this proposal, it will probably get it, but care must be taken that it is not used for political purposes, as has already happened in the past in the case of hungary and elsewhere. if we fail to ensure the impartiality of the use of this mechanism, the citizens of the european union will reject such intervention by the european union and euroscepticism will continue to grow.

in writing. ‒ i supported this eu-china visa agreement because visas are unnecessary for people with diplomatic passports and hamper migration from the eu to china and vice versa. just a year ago, i had a rather bad experience in obtaining a visa, although i would not have needed it as a holder of a slovenian diplomatic passport. unfortunately, the procedure was much longer and more complicated than one would wish. the removal of visa barriers will increase the efficiency of mutual cooperation between eu member states and china, where economic cooperation is already strong. visa waiver will reduce the waiting time at consulates and all related costs. direct contacts between people in diplomatic circles will also be discouraged.
in writing. ‒ chinese diplomats will be able to travel to the schengen area without a visa, and european union diplomats will also be able to travel to china without a visa. although human rights concerns remain in china, this agreement marks the first step towards a visa-free regime with china in the future. the agreement provides for visa-free travel for all citizens of the european union and citizens of the people's republic of china holding diplomatic passports. in both cases, this shall apply for a period of up to 90 days in any 180-day period. the visa waiver for diplomats will reduce certain costs and facilitate the exercise of their functions. i welcome the change and see it as a step towards an easier visa regime for all eu citizens and have therefore supported the recommendation.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the recommendation on the draft council decision on the conclusion, on behalf of the european union, of the agreement between the european union and the people's republic of china on the short-stay visa waiver for holders of diplomatic passports. the agreement will upgrade the strategic partnership with china and enable bilateral exchanges and closer cooperation. the agreement thus allows eu and chinese nationals to travel to the territory of the other party for a maximum of 90 days in any 180-day period.
in writing. ‒ i supported the draft council decision on the conclusion, on behalf of the european union, of the agreement between the european union and the people's republic of china on the short-stay visa waiver for holders of diplomatic passports. eu citizens need a visa to enter china. the agreement allows citizens of the union holding a valid eu diplomatic passport or pass and citizens of china holding a valid diplomatic passport to travel without a visa to the territory of the other party for a maximum of 90 days in any 180-day period. the agreement is accompanied by a joint statement on the interpretation of this 90-day period in any 180-day period. the agreement establishes a joint committee of experts to manage it. visa waiver will reduce waiting times at consulates and travel-related costs. direct contacts between people, which are essential for the stable development of economic, cultural, scientific and other links, will be facilitated and strengthened.

in writing. ‒ the case concerns mep jean-marie le pen and concerns a request for waiver of immunity submitted by the french prosecutor general to the paris court of appeal on 14 march 2016. thus, in paris, two trials are under way before the investigating judge of the district court for incitement to racial hatred. in accordance with article 8 of the protocol on the privileges and immunities of the european union, a member of the european parliament may not be subject to investigation, detention or legal proceedings for an opinion or vote he or she expresses in the performance of his or her duties. such absolute immunity of members applies to opinions expressed by them at official sittings of parliament and also to opinions expressed elsewhere, provided, of course, that there is a link between the opinion expressed and the duties of members. there is no connection between the statement in question and mr le pen's parliamentary duties, and the report therefore proposes to waive his immunity. the european parliament's conclusion in this report seems to me to be entirely correct. i believe that this kind of hate speech should not be covered by parliamentary immunity, and i therefore supported the report.

in writing. ‒ mario borghezio, member of the european parliament, requested the protection of his parliamentary immunity under articles 8 and 9 of protocol no 7 on criminal proceedings before the court of milan, on the ground that the member of parliament had, in a radio programme, advocated ideas of supremacy and racial or ethnic hatred, which are criminal offences in italy. the court held that this was not a situation in which a member expressed an opinion in the course of his duties, nor was there any link between his opinions and the parliamentary duties he performs in the european parliament. in particular, such statements do not have the tone that can be found in political debates in the european parliament and, moreover, are by their very nature completely contrary to what the representatives of the european citizens should be advocating. as i believe that mr borghezio has clearly not acted within the framework of his duties as a member of the european parliament, i voted in favour of the report which proposes that his immunities and privileges should not be protected.

in writing. ‒ the european commission has recently proposed an amendment to regulation 91/2003/ec, while at the same time establishing common rules for the management of rail transport statistics. the aim of the amendment of the regulation is to simplify the collection and transmission of data (by member states) on goods and passengers travelling by rail. accident statistics are to be maintained by the european railway agency in accordance with the regulation. the regulation extends the obligations of the member states to provide information on the types of locomotives running on certain services, on passenger flows and also on the accessibility of railway infrastructure for disabled persons and persons with reduced mobility. in the future, the commission should step up its work on passenger data on specific routes in order to integrate rail routes in regional and cross-border areas where there are missing links in the future. i believe that progress is needed in this area and that the potential offered by railways should be better exploited within the european union, which is why i supported the recommendation.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the recommendation for second reading on the council position at first reading with a view to the adoption of a regulation of the european parliament and of the council amending the regulation of the european parliament and of the council on rail transport statistics as regards the collection of data on goods, passengers and accidents. i support the proposed compromise between the commission and the european parliament, which will avoid duplication of work between eurostat, the commission and the european railway agency, while at the same time strengthening cooperation between them and bringing statistics on eu policies closer to eu citizens.
in writing. ‒ i supported the draft legislative resolution on the council position at first reading with a view to adopting a regulation of the european parliament and of the council amending regulation (ec) no 91/2003 of the european parliament and of the council of 16 december 2002 on rail transport statistics as regards the collection of data on goods, passengers and accidents. the scope of the regulation on rail transport statistics needs to be extended to infrastructure data, in particular the establishment of a european rail traffic management system (ertms), which is one of the priorities of the trans-european transport network (ten-t). it is of the utmost importance that eu citizens have easy access to information on the implementation of eu policies, through an 'all in one' system. after lengthy negotiations, the council and parliament agreed that the most effective and cost-effective way to avoid duplication of work between eurostat, the commission and the european railway agency is to strengthen cooperation between these institutions and to ensure easy access to eu policy statistics for eu citizens and stakeholders.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the recommendation for second reading on the council position at first reading with a view to the adoption of a regulation of the european parliament and of the council amending regulation (ec) no 91/2003 on rail transport statistics, as regards the collection of data on goods, passengers and accidents. at first reading parliament decided that the scope of the regulation on rail transport statistics should be extended to cover data on infrastructure. parliament stressed that it was of the utmost importance to have a clear view on the development of ertms in the union, as the eu has spent millions of euros to fund this type of infrastructure without any concrete result so far in terms of operability of the system. parliament was also of the opinion that eurostat and the european railway agency should closely cooperate in improving statistics on rail accidents and in particular ensure the methodological consistency with regard to accident data on other modes of transport. i voted in favour because i believe that it is very important that eu citizens have easy access to data related to the implementation of eu policies.
in writing. ‒ i supported the european parliament's legislative resolution on the council's position at first reading with a view to adopting a regulation of the european parliament and of the council amending regulation (ec) no 91/2003 of the european parliament and of the council on rail transport statistics as regards the collection of data on goods, passengers and accidents. i agree with parliament that eu citizens should have easy access to information on the implementation of eu policies, all in one place. the proposed regulation on rail transport statistics will make it possible for all user groups to have easily accessible data and reliable information on the progress of european policies in the rail sector, including statistics on barrier-free stations accessible to persons with reduced mobility and disabled persons and on the use of cross-border railway infrastructure.
in writing. ‒ the commission has proposed to amend regulation 1365/2006/ec concerning statistics on inland waterways and the transport of goods by them. at the first reading in the european parliament, the proposal was accompanied by the idea of monitoring passenger traffic statistics on the mentioned routes (in particular on river ferries). the amended regulation also provides for the collection of data on the cleanliness of waterways, ships and cross-border traffic on waterways. the european parliament recommends that the commission carry out a study on the usefulness of passenger data (for ships and ferries) and on cross-border traffic in general. the commission will first develop a methodology for collecting passenger statistics in cooperation with the member states and then start pilot studies on the feasibility of collecting all passenger data. the final results of the studies will be forwarded by the european commission to the european parliament and the council, which will propose amendments. i think that the commission has put forward a good plan for the future management of statistics and possible future changes in this area, and i therefore supported the recommendation.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the recommendation for second reading on the council position at first reading with a view to the adoption of a regulation of the european parliament and of the council amending the regulation on statistics relating to the carriage of goods by inland waterway, as regards the delegation of delegated and implementing powers to the commission to adopt certain measures. following a first reading in which the european parliament achieved an extension of the scope of the regulation on statistics on inland waterway passenger transport of goods, the parliament and the council set out the first steps towards the incorporation of statistics on passenger transport into the regulation. the commission will thus develop a methodology for data collection and launch pilot studies on the feasibility of the new databases.
in writing. ‒ i supported the draft legislative resolution on the council position at first reading with a view to adopting a regulation of the european parliament and of the council amending regulation (ec) no 1365/2006 on statistics relating to the inland waterway transport of goods, as regards the delegation of delegated and implementing powers to the commission to adopt certain measures. parliament extended the scope of the regulation on statistics on inland waterway freight to passenger transport. parliament considered that a successful policy to strengthen the role of inland navigation in the transport sector must be based on reliable statistics covering the transport of goods and passengers. the extension of the scope of the existing regulation would bring inland waterway transport on a par with the maritime, air and road transport sectors for which statistics are collected for both goods and passengers. parliament and the council agreed that inland waterway passenger transport falls within the scope of the regulation. parliament and the council agreed to limit the powers of the commission to adopt delegated acts. delegated acts should only be adopted to adapt the regulation to international coding and nomenclature changes and to increase the thresholds. the duration of the delegation of power shall be limited to five years.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the recommendation for second reading on the council position at first reading with a view to the adoption of a regulation of the european parliament and of the council amending regulation (ec) no 1365/2006 on statistics of goods transport by inland waterways as regards the conferral of delegated and implementing powers on the commission for the adoption of certain measures. at first reading parliament extended the scope of the regulation on statistics on goods transport by inland waterway to include passenger transport. broadening the scope of the existing regulation would put inland waterway transport on an equal footing with the maritime, air and road transport sectors, for which statistical data are collected both for goods and passengers. parliament and the council have agreed to limit the powers of the commission to adopt delegated acts, which should be adopted only to adapt the regulation to changes in coding and nomenclature at international level and to increase thresholds. i voted in favour because i believe that a successful policy to enhance the role of inland navigation within the transport sector should be based on reliable statistics encompassing both goods and passenger transport.
in writing. ‒ i agree that a successful policy to strengthen the role of inland navigation in the transport sector must be based on reliable statistics covering the transport of goods and passengers. the extension of the scope of the existing regulation would bring inland waterway transport on a par with the maritime, air and road transport sectors for which statistics are collected for both goods and passengers.
in writing. ‒ the report on the proposal for a directive on the union legal framework for customs infringements and sanctions aims to harmonise administrative charges and fines in relation to customs in the eu. the report aims to achieve maximum harmonisation in this area, as the regulation of customs infringements and sanctions differs widely from the point of view of national regimes, with infringements being treated as criminal sanctions or as infringements in different member states. the proposal for a directive calls for the establishment of a scale of sanctions reflecting the gravity of customs infringements. the general objective of the directive advocated by the report is to ensure the effective enforcement of the customs legislation of the european union, and the report therefore calls on the commission to present a report on the aspects of customs legislation at union level. the purpose of the directive is to strengthen the proper functioning of the internal market, to provide a framework for customs infringements and to provide for the imposition of non-criminal sanctions for such infringements by approximating the provisions laid down by the laws, regulations and administrative provisions of the member states. as the report highlights some important points of the customs regime, which i welcome, i supported the report.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a directive of the european parliament and of the council on the legal framework of the union for customs infringements and sanctions. in addition to the same rules on the enforcement of customs legislation, we also need the same sanctions, which must be uniform in the event of infringements. despite the great efforts made by member states to improve the cooperation and efficiency of customs administrations and to ensure equivalent results in controls, we will not achieve the progress that we would have achieved with a comprehensive approach to enforcement, including sanctions. i believe that this directive will make a significant contribution to the harmonisation of penalties for infringements of customs legislation.
in writing. ‒ i supported the proposal to refer back to committee the european parliament and council directive on the union legal framework for customs infringements and sanctions. the customs union is considered one of the foundations of the european union and the backbone of the single market, but we still lack a coherent approach to customs enforcement, including sanctions. this means that the rules are the same, but the sanctions for their violation are very different. the customs union and trade policy are the exclusive competence of the european union and therefore only the eu can develop a common approach to the enforcement of customs legislation. if differences between the sanctioning systems in the member states were to persist, this would ultimately mean that an undertaking in one member state could lose the status of authorised economic operator as a result of an infringement, while another undertaking operating in another member state would not lose it as a result of the same infringement. in order to ensure a proportionate system of penalties, the level of penalties cannot be based on the value of the goods. the penalties should be based on the amount of the hidden charges, as they should be linked to the financial consequences of the infringement. the objective of this directive should be to harmonise non-criminal sanctions for breaches of customs legislation as the most appropriate framework for improving compliance and reducing the number of infringements.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a directive of the european parliament and of the council on the union legal framework for customs infringements and sanctions. the european commission published a proposal for a directive on the union legal framework for customs infringements and sanctions on 13 december 2013. although the customs union is considered as one of the foundations of the european union, and the backbone of the single market, there is still no integrated approach for the enforcement of customs legislation. this means that the rules are the same but when those rules are infringed, the sanctions applied significantly differ, which creates a lack of mutual trust between administrations and undermines a level playing field for economic operators in the european union. should the differences remain, it will eventually mean that a company might lose the aeo status in one country whereas for the same infringement, another company operating in another member state would not lose it. i voted in favour because i believe that member states should ensure that persons dealing with customs and trade are actively informed on how to comply and how to maintain compliance with customs legislation.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a directive of the european parliament and of the council on the legal framework of the union for customs infringements and sanctions. i support the proposal for a directive containing measures to harmonise legal measures in the event of customs infringements of the internal market, as differences between the legal systems of the member states lead to a lack of transparency on how infringements are sanctioned or not sanctioned, which jeopardises the functioning of the internal market.

in writing. ‒ draft amending budget no 3/2016 proposes an increase in the security budget of eur 15,8 million for the european schools, the european parliament, the commission, the court of justice of the eu, the european court of auditors, the european economic and social committee, the committee of the regions and the european external action service. the draft in the european parliament focuses on the creation of 35 new armed security jobs, with one of the main and pressing issues being the legal status of the assigned security guards. the security guards are expected to remain employed in the parliament in the years to come, despite the fact that a plan to reduce the staff of the european parliament by 5% was adopted some time ago. as this is a new activity, it is not a breach of the 5% reduction statement. as i do not think there is a need for armed security guards in the european parliament, i voted against the report.

in writing. ‒ the report is the first real attempt to contribute to the very heated debate on migration in the european union. it focuses on the rights of migrants in third countries and the means of enforcing these rights in the context of european union policies and wider international efforts. the report represents progress in this area, focusing on a human rights-based approach, while stressing that migration is a positive phenomenon in general, as mobility drives development in both the countries from which migrants leave and the countries to which they arrive. migration is a complex and multifaceted phenomenon requiring a holistic approach by the competent authorities and the majority of society. the report stresses that member states must respect their international obligations towards migrants and put their dignity at the forefront of migration policy. the european parliament calls for greater involvement in the review of european policies in this area and stresses the importance of involving civil society in the implementation of the policies themselves. because i believe that migration is both a major challenge and an opportunity for the european union, and because it is a very balanced and progressive report, i have decided to support it.
in writing. ‒ i did not support the motion for a resolution on human rights and migration in third countries. migration is a global and multidimensional phenomenon, driven by a wide range of factors, such as economic, social and political conditions, working conditions, violence and security, environmental degradation and the frequency of natural disasters. today, nearly 244 million people are considered international migrants, and an increasing number of refugees are women and children. international migration can help to overcome labour market shortages. appropriate reception and integration policies ensure that migrants do not suffer the excessive or prolonged effects of the traumas many have experienced. socio-cultural development depends on inclusion, which requires the determined efforts of both migrants, who must be willing to adapt to the host society without necessarily abandoning their original cultural identity, and of institutions and communities in the host countries, which must be prepared to welcome migrants and meet their needs. opening safe and legal migration routes is the best way to combat smuggling and trafficking in human beings, and development strategies should recognise migration and mobility as drivers of development, as remittances and investments promote development in both host and source countries.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on human rights and migration in third countries. migration is a global, multidimensional phenomenon caused by a wide variety of factors, such as economic conditions (including changes in wealth distribution and regional and global economic integration), social and political conditions, labour conditions, the situation with regard to violence and security, the gradual deterioration of the environment and the aggravation of natural disasters. therefore, this phenomenon must be addressed in a coherent, balanced manner, on the basis of a comprehensive approach which takes account of its human dimension, including the positive impact it has on demographic trends and economic development. the report calls for the eu and its member states to ensure efficient and effective policy coherence for development and to prioritise respect for human rights in their migration policy in relation to third countries. the report equally underlines that migration and development are linked and that development cooperation in the field of education, health, labour law, poverty reduction, human rights, democratisation and post-conflict reconstruction are key factors in preventing forced migration. i voted in favour because i believe that development assistance programmes should not be used for purely migration and border management purposes.

in writing. ‒ human rights are often overlooked in the global business of large corporations. it is important that the european union should join the efforts of the united nations, which has already issued a number of recommendations and commitments in this area. the report highlights the legal obligations of corporations to respect human rights in their operations, regardless of their location. the text identifies a growing number of serious corporate responsibility challenges and sets out a number of european union recommendations and requirements, in particular in the area of access to justice for victims of corporate abuse. the report mentions that non-binding initiatives in this area do not represent activities that would produce sufficient results. with the acceleration of globalisation, it is becoming increasingly important to ensure respect for human rights also in the context of extraterritorial dimensions, where new and new problems arise from the point of view of the legal order. the report also calls on corporations to raise their own standards of oversight. it also expressed regret at the obstructive behaviour of some member states in relation to the pursuit of a binding un convention on entrepreneurship and human rights. i'm satisfied with the report and i've endorsed it.

in writing. ‒ the management of natural resources, especially fuels, is of great importance for the environment. the report largely ignores reality and does not contribute to the planned phase-out of fossil fuels. on the contrary, it encourages the expansion of the use and storage of gas and associated infrastructure, which represents a major financial burden for public treasuries throughout the european union. in the spirit of the recently signed paris climate agreement, europe as a whole should take a step forward and focus on environmentally sustainable resources and consequently invest in the 'european energy transition'. the eu strategy on lng and gas storage is part of the so-called gas package published by the european commission in february 2015. the report focuses more or less on the commission's plan to treat gas as an environmentally sustainable and sustainable resource, but does not mention the paris climate agreement and the european union's energy and environment goals. that is why i voted against the report.

in writing. ‒ i supported the motion for a resolution on the eu strategy for liquefied natural gas and gas storage. the internal energy market will fully integrate liquefied natural gas and gas storage and will play an important role in achieving the ultimate goal of a strong energy union. the eu lng strategy should be consistent with the framework strategy for a sustainable energy union and should therefore support greater security of energy supply, decarbonisation, long-term economic sustainability and the provision of affordable and competitive energy prices. the eu gas system needs to become more diverse and flexible, contributing to the key objective of the energy union, namely a reliable, resilient and competitive gas supply. parliament called on the commission to develop a strategy for the long-term reduction of the eu's dependence on gas imports, reflecting its commitment to reduce greenhouse gas emissions by 80-95% by 2050 compared to 1990 levels. lng has the potential to be an alternative fuel in road and maritime transport and the wider use of lng in freight transport, in particular the wider use of lng engines in maritime transport, could contribute to reducing global co2, sox and nox emissions.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the eu strategy for liquefied natural gas and gas storage. as the report concludes, the eu is still unable to fully reap the benefits of an integrated internal energy market, both because of insufficient connections and coordination and because of incomplete implementation of the third energy package. the eu strategy on liquefied natural gas and gas storage is one element of the energy union, which aims at a rapid transition of the eu to a sustainable, reliable and competitive energy system. the report calls, inter alia, for smart investment in the energy sector, the optimal use of existing lng terminals and the upgrading of missing infrastructure.
in writing. ‒ the report focuses on the inconsistencies in the frequency, duration, severity, thoroughness, effectiveness and methods of fisheries control in the european union and the need for equal and non-discriminatory treatment in all member states. the fisheries sector represents a huge part of the sustainable management of the seas and oceans and is therefore of great importance for the future of our environment. it is for this reason that effective control of fishing activities should be ensured with a view to the sustainable use of living marine resources and to maintaining the same conditions of control. the report calls on the member states to ensure the effective implementation of the control regulation and stresses that the european union's fight against illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing worldwide should be more ambitious and coincide with the effective implementation of the control regulation in its waters. fishermen themselves also adopt rules if they consider them to be fair, reasonable and compatible with fishing practices. it is in this context that the european union must ensure that the rules are compatible with the fishing community and sustainable fishing. i believe that the report represents a step forward in this area and i have therefore supported it.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of a report on how to harmonise fisheries controls in europe. we need controls on fishing activities to ensure the sustainable use of living marine resources and to maintain a level playing field for all fleets in the european union. it is the member states that are responsible for the effective implementation of the control regulation. the report rightly notes that the european union's ambitious fight against illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing around the world should coincide with the effective implementation of the control regulation in its waters, while clarifying, classifying and setting standards for fisheries in different marine areas.
in writing. ‒ i supported the motion for a resolution on how to unify fisheries control in europe. fishermen often complain that their fishing controls are much stricter than those of their neighbours, whether in another member state or another fishing zone. furthermore, they claim to have the most regulated profession of all. this feeling of unfairness raises the question of the uniform application of the rules and their effectiveness. the existing union legislation should be simplified, starting with a revision of council regulation (ec) no 1224/2009 planned for 2017. the structure of the current regulation is too complex.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on how to make fisheries controls in europe uniform. the fisheries sector is a major stakeholder in the sustainable management of the seas and oceans. however, there is a need for stricter checks on products coming into the eu from illegal, unreported and unregulated fisheries and a need to guarantee an equivalent level of control on such fishing in all member states. the report stresses the importance of ensuring effective control of fisheries activities in order to guarantee sustainable exploitation of living marine resources and maintain a level playing field among eu fleets. i voted in favour because i believe that it is necessary to clarify, classify and establish standards for fishing in the different maritime areas.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report 'how to harmonise fisheries control in europe?' the report stresses the importance of ensuring effective control of fishing activities to ensure the sustainable exploitation of living marine resources and maintain a level playing field for the eu fleet, and calls on the member states to ensure the effective implementation of the control regulation. i agree that the coherence of the single market should be ensured in all member states by establishing the same control requirements, with a uniform quality level of internal and external controls in the member states, irrespective of the border at which products enter the eu.
in writing. ‒ i supported the report because connectivity and accessibility of transport infrastructure have a strong impact on economic growth and competitiveness of the economy, as well as on employment and territorial cohesion in the eu and its regions. the system of transport links, however, in certain cases causes a stop and causes restrictions. by continuing to invest and develop transport infrastructure, we can significantly help the people and businesses in these regions. however, the effective use of these funds will require transparency and well-prepared projects. eastern europe in particular is experiencing serious difficulties in the transition to rail, as it is lagging behind in the establishment of modern railway infrastructure. here the european commission should continue to provide incentives and assistance to the lagging countries, otherwise we cannot expect to establish an efficient european rail network in the next two decades.
in writing. ‒ the report focuses on the co-financing of transport projects in the member states located in central and eastern europe. the emphasis is on projects that are not sustainable, such as the alemania project, a road corridor that would link north-east italy to northern europe, or the via carpatica project in south-east bulgaria, which is opposed by local communities, and the increase in funding for regional airports. i believe that the connectivity and accessibility of transport infrastructure in the central and eastern parts of the european union needs to be improved, but in a better and different way than the report suggests. local communities, the environment and sustainable development must be taken into account. the development of transport hubs at any cost should not be the objective of the european union, but rather the need to design transport infrastructure in a sustainable way, which also has positive long-term financial implications. for these reasons, i voted against the report.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on better connectivity and accessibility of transport infrastructure in central and eastern europe. the need for economic and sustainable development principles must not be overlooked when improving the connectivity and accessibility of transport infrastructure in central and eastern europe. poor connectivity and accessibility of transport infrastructure have a negative impact on economic growth and competitiveness, as well as on employment and territorial cohesion in the european union and its regions. i welcome the recommendation that existing regional cooperation policies and instruments be better used to boost cross-border traffic between regions and to eliminate bottlenecks.
in writing. ‒ i supported the motion for a resolution on better connectivity and accessibility of transport infrastructure in central and eastern europe. high-quality transport links are fundamental to economic activities in europe and to the quality of life of our citizens. easily accessible and well-connected transport networks with a local, regional, national and cross-border dimension in passenger and freight transport are the basis for promoting economic, social and territorial cohesion within and between eu member states. at eu level, the trans-european transport network (ten-t) aims to develop an integrated trans-european multimodal transport network and to promote the interconnection and interoperability of national networks, as well as access to them. the ten-t guidelines and the connecting europe facility (cef) established in 2013 have already set out the main pillars for the implementation of the eu transport infrastructure policy by the mid-2020s. member states and the eu will need to pool their resources and work closely together to set up and implement projects to finalise the strategic core network by 2030 and the comprehensive network by 2050.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on better connectivity and accessibility of transport infrastructure in central and eastern europe. transport infrastructure is still less developed in most regions of the central and eastern part of the eu compared to other european regions. as the connectivity and accessibility of transport infrastructure have a strong impact on economic growth and competitiveness, and on employment and territorial cohesion in the eu and its regions, there is a need to improve the connectivity and accessibility of transport infrastructure to, from and within the central and eastern parts of the eu. at the same time, the needs of the economy and the principles of sustainable development must be taken into account, and missing links must be established, bottlenecks eliminated and smooth links for long-distance and regional transport ensured.

in writing. ‒ the european union is founded on the values of respect for human dignity, freedom, democracy, equality, the rule of law and respect for human rights, including the rights of persons belonging to minorities, which are included among its core principles. the union institutions and bodies and the member states should respect and lead by example in fulfilling their obligations and should strive for a common culture of the rule of law. the european parliament recommends the establishment of a comprehensive union mechanism for democracy, the rule of law and fundamental rights, involving all relevant stakeholders, pending a corresponding amendment of the treaties. in its report, parliament therefore asks the commission to submit by september 2017, on the basis of article 295 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union, a proposal for the conclusion of an eu pact for democracy, the rule of law and fundamental rights in the form of an interinstitutional agreement setting out the arrangements to facilitate cooperation between the institutions of the union and its member states in this area. in view of recent developments in hungary and poland, where there is a persistent regression of certain fundamental freedoms and a lack of respect for the rule of law, i supported the report.

in writing. ‒ i supported the motion for a resolution with recommendations to the commission on the establishment of an eu mechanism for democracy, the rule of law and fundamental rights. the european union has included democracy, the rule of law and fundamental rights among its core principles and objectives in the first articles of the treaties and in the eu membership criteria. the union has a wide range of instruments to enforce its legislation and the treaties on important issues. although the eu has several instruments at its disposal to ensure respect for the principles of democracy, the rule of law and fundamental rights, significant gaps remain and in practice these instruments are often limited in scope, inadequate and ineffective or unlikely to be used. in some cases, their unequal use is considered by many to be politically motivated, arbitrary and unfairly targeted at certain countries. there is no comprehensive mechanism for systematic, impartial and complete monitoring of all member states and their institutions. the proposed interinstitutional agreement aims to establish arrangements to facilitate cooperation between the eu institutions and the member states under article 7 teu and to link, harmonise and complement existing mechanisms. in addition, the agreement will provide for a comprehensive review mechanism applicable to all member states and the three main eu institutions.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report with recommendations to the commission on the establishment of an eu mechanism on democracy, the rule of law and fundamental rights. europe has a long tradition in the area of democracy, the rule of law and citizens’ rights. the european union has a wide range of instruments for the enforcement of its laws and treaties when it comes to material issues. while the eu has several existing instruments at its disposal to ensure the principles of democracy, the rule of law and fundamental rights are upheld, substantial gaps remain, and in practice such instruments are often limited in scope, inadequate and ineffective, or they are unlikely to be used. in some cases, their uneven application is perceived by many as politically motivated, arbitrary and unfairly targeting certain countries. there is no integrated mechanism for the systematic, impartial and complete monitoring of all eu member states and institutions. therefore, i believe, it is imperative to adopt a framework that enables the eu to address not only infringements to specific eu laws, but also (risk of) serious threats to democracy, the rule of law and fundamental rights.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report with recommendations to the commission on the establishment of an eu mechanism for democracy, the rule of law and fundamental rights. i have long advocated the establishment of an effective mechanism to monitor the functioning of democracy, the rule of law and fundamental rights in the member states. i believe that a politically independent mechanism is one of the key measures for the rule of law in the european union, so that abuses are no longer abused, especially in transition, post-socialist countries. but care must be taken that it is not used for political purposes, as has happened in the past in the case of hungary and elsewhere. if we fail to ensure the impartiality of the use of this mechanism, the citizens of the european union will reject such intervention by the european union and euroscepticism will continue to grow. ensuring the rule of law and effective independent judicial systems play a key role in creating a positive political environment that can restore confidence in the institutions and thus a friendly environment for investment and ensure greater regulatory predictability and sustainable growth.
in writing. the european commission's work programme presents the policies to which the european commission will devote particular attention in the coming year. it is certainly an important set of issues which i myself believe should be addressed in 2017. however, i would like to point out that the programme is not ambitious enough in the areas of demographic change, intergenerational cooperation and the rights of older people. these are areas that are hardly mentioned in the programme or are given far too little importance. it seems unacceptable to me that, at a time when europe is facing major demographic changes, the european institutions are not prepared to pay more attention to the ageing of the population and to take measures that will help ensure and preserve the basic dignity of older generations. we still lack a strategy to respond to demographic change at the level of europe, or the european union. this is despite experts warning that without appropriate policies on intergenerational cooperation, we can expect a constant conflict between the young and the old. in view of the above, i believe that the institutions of the european union are lagging behind in taking the necessary action in the field of demographic change. i therefore expect the european commission to devote more attention to this area in 2017 than envisaged in the 2017 work programme, as this is a problem of strategic importance.

in writing. ‒ i supported the draft legislative resolution on the council position at first reading with a view to adopting a directive of the european parliament and of the council on the accessibility of the websites and mobile applications of public sector bodies. online accessibility is very important for public sector bodies as it enables them to extend their reach and fulfil their public responsibilities. the number of websites providing egovernment services (approximately 380 500 in the eu) and public sector websites (over 761 000 in the eu) is growing rapidly. most member states have already adopted legislation or other measures for online accessibility. however, there are major differences between these laws and measures. non-harmonised national approaches to online accessibility create barriers in the internal market. the proposed harmonisation of national public sector measures at eu level is a necessary condition to address the fragmentation of the framework and the lack of confidence in the online accessibility market. harmonisation will create better market conditions, more jobs, cheaper internet access and more accessible websites: a triple benefit for the public sector, businesses and citizens.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the recommendation for second reading on the council position at first reading with a view to the adoption of a directive of the european parliament and of the council on the accessibility of the websites and mobile applications of public sector bodies. the new directive aims at the approximation of the laws, regulations and administrative provisions of the member states on the accessibility of websites from public sector bodies. the directive supports member states to achieve their national commitments regarding web-accessibility as well as their commitment to the united nations convention on the rights of persons with disabilities regarding websites of public sector bodies. web-accessibility refers to principles and techniques to be observed when constructing websites, in order to render the content of these websites accessible to all users, in particular those with disabilities. i voted in favour because i believe that in a harmonised framework, the web-developers industry should face fewer barriers to operate in the internal market, while costs for governments and others procuring web-accessibility products and services should be reduced.
