in writing. ‒ the recommendation contains a proposal for strict rules on protection against the spread of pests. the problem with such rules is, of course, the link between pests and seeds, as the spread of pests can also limit the storage and exchange of seeds. outbreaks of diseases and pests affecting individual plant species and crops are likely to be contained by new rules, currently under negotiation, which will provide for strict controls. this raises concerns about the adverse consequences for seed storage and the conservation of certain plant species, which are based on the diversity of domestic seeds and the exchange of seeds between farmers. although certain exceptions should be provided for in the implementation of the new rules, discussions with the directorate-general for health and food safety (dg sante) have shown that these exceptions will be provided for only in the years 2020 to 2025. the main concerns related to the proposed scheme relate in particular to the registration of seed producers who could endanger small growers, the registration of plant species and the introduction of so-called plant and seed passports. at the same time, the commission has hardly consulted ngos working in this field on the challenges. for all the reasons mentioned and the many problems associated with the proposal, despite the good intentions behind the regulation of this area, i abstained.
in writing. ‒ i voted against the alde group's proposal to reject the recommendation for a second reading on the council's position at first reading with a view to adopting a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on plant protection measures, amending regulations of the european parliament and of the council and repealing council directives. the regulation has a very clear objective to protect european production from harmful organisms imported from other countries. we should be careful about what one country imports, because importing plants into one country could cause problems in other countries. we must combat the risks posed by unknown plants, particularly in view of their potential harmfulness.
in writing. ‒ i supported the draft legislative resolution on the council position at first reading with a view to adopting a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on plant protection measures. plant health is a key factor in ensuring sustainable and competitive agriculture, horticulture and forestry. healthy seeds and propagating material are needed to ensure the profitability of agricultural crops, jobs, innovation in crop production and food security. the unique feature of the eu plant health regime (phs) is its openness: movements of plants and plant products into and through the union are allowed, provided that specific restrictions and requirements are respected. nevertheless, due to the high volume of imports from other continents, there is a high likelihood of future outbreaks of non-indigenous harmful organisms. the assessment of the regime (2010) showed that changes to the basic legislation will be necessary to address such increased risks in a comprehensive manner. this regulation is part of a package of audits related to plant health, the quality of plant reproductive material, animal health, official controls on plants, animals, food and feed and union expenditure related to those policies.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the recommendation for second reading on the council position at first reading with a view to the adoption of a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on protective measures against pests of plants, amending regulations (eu) no 228/2013, (eu) no 652/2014 and (eu) no 1143/2014 of the european parliament and of the council and repealing council directives 69/464/eec, 74/647/eec, 93/85/eec, 98/57/ec, 2000/29/ec, 2006/91/ec and 2007/33/ec. the aim of the regulation is to curb the growing influx into the eu of plant pests, such as olive grove killer xylella fastidiosa, and better equip member states to tackle their spread. the new regulation introduces preventive and rapid response mechanisms for suspect plant imports, steps up pest surveillance efforts in the eu and requires all member states to draw up outbreak contingency plans. i voted in favour because i strongly believe that all member states must establish multi-annual survey programmes to ensure timely detection of dangerous pests and contingency plans for each pest capable of entering their territory.

in writing. ‒ the motion for a resolution on trans-fatty acids has my support. in fact, frequent consumption of trans fats is associated with an increased risk of cardiovascular disease, infertility, gallstones, alzheimer' s disease and diabetes, obesity, and some cancers. further research shows that only one in three consumers in the eu are aware of trans-fatty acids and that measures to label the content of these fatty acids are ineffective. eu legislation does not regulate the content of trans-fatty acids in food and does not require their labelling. the effectiveness of these restrictions is demonstrated by danish legislation, which tightened the permitted content of trans-fatty acids in oils and fats to 2% in 2003. as a result, the number of deaths from cardiovascular disease has decreased significantly.
in writing. ‒ trans-fatty acids are unsaturated fats that can be found in food made from ruminants and in industrially produced food that has been partially hydrogenated. consumption of oils containing such fats is associated with increased risks of cardiovascular disease. high intakes of such foods are risk factors for developing coronary heart disease, which is responsible for around 660,000 deaths per year or otherwise - as much as 14% of all deaths in the european union each year. trans-fatty acids lower the price of the final product and are therefore mainly used in the preparation of fast food, certain snack foods and other highly processed foods. denmark was the first country to restrict the use of trans-fatty acids back in 2003 and has already achieved a reduction in cardiovascular disease. in a report published in december 2015, the european commission took note of the situation and indicated that it would seek to limit the use of trans-fatty acids in the european union and announced its expected results. to date, the european commission has not taken any action in this area, and the european parliament has therefore prepared a proposal to restrict its application. as these are substances with a high long-term impact on health, i supported the motion for a resolution.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the motion for a resolution on the oral questions on trans-fatty acids. the content of trans fatty acids in food has already been significantly reduced at voluntary level, but unfortunately not everywhere. and even where this content has been reduced, consumption in certain groups of the population, in young people, in people with low incomes, is still too high. when we talk about staple foods like milk and meat, we can't talk about the trans fatty acid content being harmful because it's contained in such small amounts that it's not harmful to health. the resolution states that we know of some negative effects of trans fatty acids and that it is time to act.
in writing. ‒ i supported the motion for a resolution on trans-fatty acids. trans-fatty acids are a specific type of unsaturated fat naturally present in ruminant-derived foods such as dairy products and meat, certain plants and plant products, and are found in particular in industrially produced partially hydrogenated vegetable oils. in 2010, the european food safety authority concluded that trans-fatty acids derived from ruminants have similar effects to those of the industrial products covered by this resolution. it has been shown that limiting the content of trans-fatty acids can have rapid and significant health benefits. unfortunately, only one in three consumers in the eu are aware of trans-fatty acids, which shows that measures to label the content of these acids have not been effective and that measures to raise awareness in the education system and media campaigns are needed.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the motion for a resolution on trans fats (tfas). trans fats or trans-fatty acids (tfas) are a type of unsaturated fatty acid that have been widely used in the food industry since the 1950s. foods that may be high in trans fats include ready-made meals, frying fat for industrial use, margarine used in pastry, pre-packed bakery products, cakes, biscuits and wafers, microwave popcorn, deep-fried foods and soups and sauces. international studies show that policies aimed at restricting the tfa content of food entailing reducing tfa levels without increasing total fat content are feasible, achievable and likely to have a positive effect on public health. the european union does not currently have legislation regulating the content of trans fats in food products or requiring their labelling. i voted in favour because i believe that the eu should introduce legal limits on the amount of industrial trans fats in processed food what would reduce exposure to the biggest sources of trans fats and save lives.

president-in-office of the council. – madam president, i am grateful to have the opportunity to intervene in this debate on behalf of the council. the divergence between our two institutions on how to organise the discharge in relation to the council’s budget is not new. however, i believe that there are a number of recent developments which, at least in the medium term, would allow us to move forward. according to article 319 of the treaty, ‘the european parliament, acting on a recommendation from the council, shall give a discharge to the commission in respect of the implementation of the budget’. the treaty and the financial regulation enumerate the documents to be examined during the discharge procedure. the council has always rigorously respected these provisions. the treaty procedure is specific to the eu institutional system. nevertheless, in keeping with procedures in member states, discharge is not given between the different arms of a budgetary authority. the parliament has over the years developed a political practice of voting separate discharge resolutions for individual institutions and organs. in 2010 the council proposed a memorandum of understanding between the two institutions in order to organise our cooperation. this standing invitation to a discussion has not been taken up by parliament so far. let me turn to the more positive and encouraging recent developments. this year we have made a big step towards increased transparency of the financially-relevant activities of all eu institutions. since june, the annual activity reports of all authorising officers by delegation are publicly available on each institution’s website, including, of course, the council. this is the result of last year’s agreement between parliament and the council to amend the financial regulation. everybody now has access to core documents, which analyse the activities on which the institutions spend money. that is why the council was a bit surprised to see, in your draft resolution, the reference to parliament not having received the council’s annual activity report. i guess that this is probably left over from previous years. a number of other suggestions formulated in parliament’s draft resolution have also already become reality, for example the existence of rules concerning whistleblowing, integrity and ethics of officials in the general secretariat of the council. i would like to underline that, in the spirit of the proposed memorandum of understanding between our institutions that i mentioned before, the council is open to dialogue with parliament on concrete issues. i hear that in the area of building policy there have already been some contacts in the past. let us work together on these positive experiences. allow me a word on budget scrutiny. your report says that the expenditure of the council must be scrutinised in the same way as other institutions, and on occasion, statements made by some members of the european parliament have created the impression that the council budget would escape all control. this is not true. it is as if the treaty procedure, the court of auditors’ scrutiny and all the other documents and reports i mentioned before, did not exist. this is not helpful. it is even misleading. european citizens expect us to ensure the regularity, legality and efficiency of eu finances, and in this we either succeed together or we fail together. citizens are not interested in quarrels between the eu institutions. i am confident that we are going in the right direction. as far as the implementation of the council budget 2014 is concerned, the court of auditors has once again confirmed that no significant weaknesses were detected. the council’s accounts did not give rise to any observations. i think it is important to have that in mind in this debate and when you cast your vote.

on budgetary control to the plenary to grant discharge to the joint technology initiative and embedded computing system artemis joint undertaking. the joint technology initiative on nan electronics eniac joint undertaking, the international thermonuclear experimental reactor fusion for energy joint undertaking and to refuse discharge to the european council and council for the financial year 2014. as for the discharge to the european council and council, the commission notes with regret this dispute between the two arms of the budgetary authorities, which has lasted for seven years now, thus preventing a suitable solution from being reached. the commission can only encourage them to cooperate with a view to ironing out all their difficulties and to work towards a smooth functioning of the discharge procedure in full respect of the relevant provisions in the treaty and in related secondary law. the commission is happy to note that parliament’s committee on budgetary control agrees that the ecsel joint undertaking, which is the successor of artemis and eniac, as mr marinescu just said, has in a satisfactory manner implemented actions to address the remarks of the budgetary authorities and therefore proposes to grant discharge for the year 2014. the commission reiterates that in the ecsel joint undertaking a structural solution is found for verification and ex post audit of any new expenditure related to horizon 2020. in fact, parliament already granted discharge to ecsel on 28 april 2016. the commission will, as a member of the governing board of ecsel, continue to closely monitor the actions undertaken by the joint undertaking, inter alia to gain sufficient data on the quality of the control systems in place by the member states and on the individual transactions. the commission will also continue to share its experience in audit matters. finally, the commission reiterates that the public-private partnership, using a tripartite model that pools member state and eu funding with industrial investments, as implemented in artemis and eniac and now in ecsel, gives europe a competitive edge in the domain of electronic components and systems. the commission also welcomes the proposal to grant discharge to the joint undertaking fusion for energy. iter is a major international scientific collaboration in the energy field, in which the european union has assumed a strategic leading role. looking back at developments since 2006, when the iter organisation was set up to jointly implement this project at international level, it should be recognised that iter has faced many challenges, in particular in terms of technology, iter being the first of a kind, project management, and risk of schedule slippage and cost increase. but, these challenges aside, iter is one of the most promising solutions to future energy demand that can contribute to addressing global warming and climate change. it is for this very significant reason that the international partners, with the major thrust of the european union, have spared no efforts to change the way the project has been managed and implemented. during recent years radical changes have been jointly decided and successfully applied to stabilise the project and address the concerns on delays and cost overruns. a new management has been put in place in the iter organisation and in fusion for energy and coordinated action plans have been endorsed to ensure a closer corporation. progress is now evident on the site, in particular in the construction of buildings under european responsibility. in addition and following the initiative of the european union, this progress is now reviewed against a set of identified milestones for the activities with clear deadlines. a robust risk management system is also in place to reduce risk and address possible problems. one of the partners’ main efforts has been the revision of the project’s schedule and its associated costs in june 2016. this revision set up solid and reliable grounds to complete the iter construction successfully and enable the european union to respect the budget for the construction phase of iter until 2020, eur 6.6 billion in 2008 values. the improvements brought to the project are now reversing the project’s past trend. they enable iter to remain one of the major international energy research projects and allow the european union to keep its support and leadership of this project. these improvements, in particular since 2015, have also been confirmed by a different independent review in mid-2016. at european level fusion for energy is now also in a better shape to deliver the eu contribution to the project. let me add that through its contracts and grants european industry is fully involved in designing, building and delivering thousands of first of a kind technological components and carrying out research projects in support of the construction of this unique device. already in its current construction phase iter is therefore creating jobs and growth for european industry. with your favourable vote on the discharge you will enable the joint undertaking to continue providing, on behalf of europe, a key contribution to the success of iter. i thank you for your support and look forward to the continued dialogue between the commission and parliament to make iter a success and a win for securing a sustainable energy source for the future.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the joint motion for a resolution on the situation in northern iraq/mosul. the people of mosul, iraq's second largest city, are suffering under the brutal rule of isis, starving and desperate for liberation. i support the resolution which strongly supports the operation to liberate monsul, which will play a crucial role in the current global effort to permanently defeat isis. in doing so, the resolution does not deprive iraq of the right to take the measures necessary to preserve its independence, territorial integrity and sovereignty. the priority of the iraqi government should be to implement the right of return of the displaced indigenous population displaced in iraq.
in writing. ‒ i supported the motion for a resolution on the situation in northern iraq/mosul. the iraqi army, supported by the global coalition to fight isis/daesh, kurdish regional government (krg) infantry and forces of the paramilitary organisation popular mobilization, has launched an operation to liberate mosul, iraq's second largest city, and numerous towns and villages in the mosul corridor from isis/daesh control. isis/daesh has imposed a brutal regime in mosul, and residents who recently managed to flee the city report that people in the city are starving and desperate for liberation. according to the office of the united nations high commissioner for refugees (unhcr), since 2014, some 3.3 million iraqis have been forced to flee their homes because of the war. in mosul, more than 1.5 million people are at risk of imminent displacement as a direct result of the operation to retake the area. parliament supported the operation launched by iraq to liberate mosul from isis/daesh control and considered that this operation played a decisive role in the current global effort to defeat isis/daesh once and for all. following the liberation of mosul, it will be necessary to continue to combat the further spread of islamist-jihadist ideologies in the region and elsewhere, including salafist jihadism, through which isis/da'esh is theologically and politically driven to commit atrocities.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the motions for a resolution on the situation in northern iraq/mosul. the resolution calls on iraqi authorities to make every effort to protect civilians, hospitals and schools, as they progress towards mosul. it underlines that daesh atrocities and genocide against christians, yazidis and other minorities should be referred to international criminal court. the eu has provided eur 134 million to date in humanitarian aid in iraq, including eur 50 million for mosul where 1.5 million people are at imminent risk of displacement. the resolution urges all parties to the conflict to open humanitarian aid corridors and guarantee assistance, and also suggests setting up a un third-party monitoring mechanism. i voted in favour because i believe that it is of crucial importance to urge iraqi authorities to protect civilians and prevent civilian casualties and human rights violations during the ongoing operation.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the european parliament resolution of 27 october 2016 on the situation in northern iraq/mosul. on 4 february 2016, the european parliament found that isis/daesh is engaged in genocide against christians and yazidis and other religious and ethnic minorities. the atrocities committed by isis/da'esh against religious and ethnic minorities in iraq include war crimes, crimes against humanity and genocide. i therefore join in supporting the operation launched by iraq to liberate mosul from isis/daesh control, as this operation could play a decisive role in the current global effort to defeat isis/daesh once and for all. i believe it is essential that all parties to the conflict, in times of hostility and afterwards, respect international humanitarian law and, in times of conflict, the principles of proportionality, discrimination and precaution.

in writing. ‒ i supported the motion for a resolution on the situation of journalists in turkey. the situation of press freedom in turkey has deteriorated significantly over the past decade. turkey is ranked 151 out of 180 countries in the 2016 press freedom index published by reporters without borders, up from 98th in 2005. freedom of expression and freedom of the press are essential and fundamental components of any democracy, and turkey is still a candidate country for eu membership. according to reporters without borders, 89 journalists were arrested, 104 media houses were closed, more than 2,300 journalists lost their jobs and at least 330 journalists had their press cards revoked during the first six weeks of the state of emergency. the violations of media freedom in turkey have also affected citizens of european countries, such as german satirist jan böhmermann and dutch journalist ebru umar. parliament called on the turkish government to respect all the conditions of democracy and the rule of law and to end discrimination against citizens in relation to freedom of speech and other fundamental rights.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the motions for a resolution on the situation of journalists in turkey. the resolution urges the turkish authorities to release those journalists and media workers being held without compelling evidence of criminal activity following the coup attempt of 15 july 2016. at least 99 journalists and writers have been arrested, denied the right of access to a lawyer and kept in inhumane conditions in which they are threatened and mistreated. the offices of more than 100 broadcasters, newspapers, magazines, publishers and distribution companies have been closed. the resolution strongly condemns the attempted coup of 15 july 2016 and supports the legitimate institutions of turkey and their right to respond to the failed military take-over, but stress that this event cannot be used as an excuse to further stifle legitimate and peaceful opposition and to prevent journalists from exercising their freedom of expression. i voted in favour because i believe that a free and pluralistic press is an essential component of any democracy’ and open society.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the european parliament resolution of 27 october 2016 on the situation of journalists in turkey. according to the european union of journalists and the turkish journalists association, the turkish police arrested at least 99 journalists and writers after the coup attempt on 15 july 2016, and no charges have been brought against them to date. the imprisoned journalists are also denied access to a lawyer and are held in inhumane conditions and subjected to threats and ill-treatment. i therefore join the call that the turkish government, under the pretext of the failed military coup, must not further repress the legitimate and peaceful opposition or journalists and media by disproportionate and illegal acts and measures to prevent them from peacefully exercising their right to freedom of expression.
in writing. ‒ i support the resolution on nuclear security and non-proliferation. i agree with the fact that the global security environment and in particular the eu security environment has deteriorated significantly and become less predictable. nor has the deterioration of relations between nuclear-armed nations contributed to this. as a matter of priority, i agree to prevent terrorist organizations or states from gaining access to or using nuclear weapons. it is important that we continue to pursue the goal of reducing and eliminating all nuclear arsenals and to move towards a world without nuclear weapons. i welcome the fact that nuclear-weapon-free zones have already been established in some regions of the world, namely in latin america and the caribbean, the south pacific, south-east asia, africa and central asia. i am concerned that nuclear-armed nations that are signatories to the nuclear non-proliferation treaty are updating and strengthening their nuclear arsenals.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the joint motion for a resolution on nuclear security and non-proliferation. recently, we have witnessed a variety of events that have affected the deterioration of relations between the nuclear-armed states. the deterioration of the security situation in the european union and in the wider neighbourhood may be of concern in the light of the re-emergence of nuclear weapons as a means of active deterrence and their possible proliferation among state and non-state actors. i support the call for all nuclear-weapon states to take concrete interim measures to reduce the risk of nuclear weapon detonations, including by limiting its operational status and by stopping nuclear weapons already in place.
in writing. ‒ i supported the motion for a resolution on nuclear security and non-proliferation. the treaty on the non-proliferation of nuclear weapons is a landmark international treaty aimed at preventing the proliferation of nuclear weapons and weapons technology, promoting cooperation in the peaceful uses of nuclear energy and enhancing global nuclear disarmament. this treaty is the only binding commitment of the nuclear-weapon states in a multilateral treaty to the goal of disarmament. the convention on the physical protection of nuclear material is a legally binding international instrument in the field of physical protection of nuclear material, which provides for measures relating to the prevention, detection and punishment of offences relating to nuclear material. the amendment of the convention makes it legally binding on states parties to protect nuclear capacity and material during peaceful domestic use, storage and transport. parliament expressed concern at the recent nuclear tests carried out by the dprk and the risks they pose to regional stability and demanded that the dprk cease such tests in the future. parliament encouraged the continued application and strict implementation of the convention on the physical protection of nuclear material and called on those states which had not yet ratified the treaties to do so.
in writing. ‒ i abstained of voting on motions for a resolution on nuclear security and non-proliferation. the resolution notes that worsening relations between nuclear-armed states, such as russia and the us or india and pakistan, but also russia’s threats to use nuclear weapons or to deploy them to more territories in europe, are making the eu’s security environment ever more tense. moreover, it stresses the concern about nuclear threats arising from the russian attitude, its statements indicating an increased readiness to use nuclear weapons. it cites the examples of russian military exercises simulating the use of these weapons against poland, high-ranking russian officials’ claims that russia has the right to deploy nuclear weapons in crimea and the deployment of the nuclear-capable iskander missile system to the kaliningrad region, neighbouring lithuania and poland. i abstained because i believe that this resolution is very one-sided and not balanced.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the european parliament resolution of 27 october 2016 on nuclear security and non-proliferation. the global security environment, and in particular the security environment of the eu, has deteriorated significantly and become more unstable and uncertain and less predictable. security threats are created by both state and non-state actors, regional and global. the deterioration of the security situation in the european union and in the wider neighbourhood is a cause for concern, which could lead to the re-emergence of nuclear weapons as a means of active deterrence and their possible proliferation among state and non-state actors. i therefore join the call for the european external action service to update and extend the 2003 eu strategy against proliferation of weapons of mass destruction and the new 2009 guidelines for action as an accompanying measure, thereby making the eu a driving force in strengthening and continuing multilateral nuclear disarmament and non-proliferation agreements.
in writing. ‒ i support the motion for a resolution on european voluntary service. through practice in the home country, we can see that volunteering plays an important role in expressing solidarity, freedom and responsibility, and helps to strengthen active citizenship and personal development. it is an important tool for social inclusion, training, education and intercultural dialogue. if we succeed in transferring these values to the european area, we will be able to create a european identity more easily and more effectively, and thus contribute to the spread of european values. in doing so, it is important to provide a european framework for voluntary activities that defines rights and responsibilities and promotes mobility and recognition of skills and competences. it is therefore a good proposal to support and implement the idea of co-financing voluntary work with eu grants, as recently proposed by the commission in its proposal for a new financial regulation.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the joint motion for a resolution on european voluntary service and the promotion of volunteering in europe. according to statistics, almost 100 million citizens in europe are engaged in voluntary activities, and their work generates about 5% of its gdp. this makes it all the more important to provide a european framework for volunteering activities in the sense of a legal framework defining the status of volunteers, their rights and responsibilities, and promoting mobility and the recognition of skills and competences. in this light, the resolution rightly encourages member states to define the legal environment for volunteers and to apply the recommendations of the agenda for a voluntary policy in europe and the european charter on the rights and responsibilities of volunteers.
in writing. ‒ i supported the motion for a resolution on european voluntary service and the promotion of volunteering in europe. in 2016, the european voluntary service celebrates its 20th anniversary and has supported 100,000 volunteers in its 20 years of existence. volunteering has value and significance as one of the most visible expressions of solidarity, which promotes and facilitates social inclusion, creates social capital and enables the transformation of society, and contributes to the development of an active civil society able to offer creative and innovative solutions to common challenges, and to economic growth, which should therefore be judged by specific criteria, in terms of economic and social capital. volunteering requires a combination of support mechanisms and/or appropriate organisational structures, which should be further strengthened by an appropriate legal framework defining the rights and obligations of volunteers and volunteering. parliament encourages the member states to promote the european voluntary service in their education and university systems as a tool for educating the younger generation in solidarity and civic engagement. the european voluntary service should provide quick and easy access to this programme and it is therefore necessary to simplify the current application system.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the motions for a resolution on the european voluntary service. almost 100 million eu citizens have taken part as volunteers in education, culture or arts, sport events, humanitarian and development aid work. young people should take advantage of volunteering schemes to develop skills and acquire experience that helps them to find jobs afterwards. the report stresses out that despite the real social and economic benefits of volunteering for individuals and organisations, participation in the european volunteering service remains modest and many barriers still have to be removed. to encourage volunteering, a more supportive environment is essential, including a legal framework with clear rights and responsibilities for programme managers and volunteers, as well as fair funding. i voted in favour because i believe that the eu needs a better coordinated policy on volunteering, to give volunteers a proper legal status and help them join programmes.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the european parliament resolution on european voluntary service and the promotion of volunteering in europe. the european voluntary service is a great service with clear frameworks. for example, the organisations that operate in it sign the quality charter. the participating volunteers, aged between 17 and 30, shall be dedicated exclusively to volunteering activities for a period of between two weeks and one year. it is known that the esf covers travel and subsistence expenses, insurance and allowances for participants. volunteering is an expression of solidarity and responsibility, as it contributes to greater involvement of citizens, personal development and, in our case, strengthening european values. it is an important tool for informal learning and training.

in writing. ‒ the vote in question is a recommendation for the second reading of the adoption of a regulation of the european parliament and of the council amending council regulation (ec) no 1342/2008 establishing a long-term plan for cod stocks and the fisheries exploiting those stocks. the purpose of that regulation is to amend and clarify certain articles of the regulation and thus to improve it. therefore, on 12 september 2012, the european commission published a proposal to revise the existing regulation. unfortunately, in adopting that regulation, the european council did not follow the co-decision procedure between the european parliament and the european council and adopted the regulation under its competence on the basis of article 43 (3) tfeu. neither the european parliament nor the european commission agreed with this. that is why the case was referred to the european court of justice. the latter annulled the council regulation in december 2015, which meant that the court ruled in favour of the european parliament and the european commission. this was a major victory for the european parliament, which will now be a co-legislator on the regulation. the european parliament and the european council reached agreement on the regulation at a trialogue in june this year, which mainly implements the principles of the new common fisheries policies while supporting the implementation of the regulation in the member states. on the basis of the above, i therefore voted in favour of adopting the recommendation in plenary.

in writing. ‒ i supported the draft legislative resolution of the european parliament on the council position at first reading with a view to adopting a regulation of the eu parliament and of the council amending council regulation (ec) no 1342/2008 establishing a long-term plan for cod stocks and the fisheries exploiting those stocks. the purpose of this proposal is to bring the regulation establishing a long-term plan for cod stocks and the fisheries exploiting those stocks ('the cod plan') into line with the new rules of the tfeu. the powers now conferred on the commission by that regulation have been reclassified into delegated and implementing measures. the main objective of the plan is to ensure the sustainable exploitation of cod stocks in the geographical area of the kattegat, the north sea, the west of scotland and the irish sea on the basis of the maximum sustainable yield.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the recommendation for second reading on the council position at first reading with a view to the adoption of a regulation of the european parliament and of the council amending council regulation (ec) no 1342/2008 establishing a long-term plan for cod stocks and the fisheries exploiting those stocks. the goal of the updated regulation is to allow north sea cod fishermen to land every catch more easily. the regulation removes limits on the number of days a vessel can spend in a fishing area and thus removes all obstacles to complying with the landing obligation in full. i voted in favour because i believe that this update of the 2008 regulation establishing a long-term-plan for cod stocks will make it fully compatible with the new common fisheries policy (cfp).

in writing. ‒ i agree with the report adopted and have supported it, as past media revelations have shown the flow of money into offshore tax havens and it has become clear that tax authorities need more powers and greater access to information on who the beneficial owners of these companies are. it is also important to give tax authorities the appropriate tools to properly access this data and to cooperate within the framework of european legislation.
in writing. ‒ disclosures in cases such as luxleaks and the panama papers show that the european union urgently needs better tax transparency to successfully tackle the challenges of money laundering, tax evasion and tax avoidance. directive 2011/16/eu provides tax authorities with access to information, procedures, documents and mechanisms for the performance of their anti-money laundering tasks. this ensures that information about financial account holders is communicated to the member states in which the account holder is resident. the commission proposal to amend this directive rightly notes, in essence, that without adequate access to information on the prevention of money laundering, tax authorities cannot assess whether financial institutions correctly identify and report beneficial owners. the parliament's report goes one step further and proposes that the rapid, permanent, mandatory and, above all, automatic exchange of information between member states is essential to prevent money laundering. in addition, the global nature of anti-money laundering activities makes cooperation between tax authorities essential, making the most of the integration at national, european and international levels. since the parliament's report confirms and in some respects strengthens the commission's proposal, i voted in favour of it.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a council directive amending directive 2011/16/eu as regards access to information by tax authorities for the prevention of money laundering. the rapid, transparent and automatic exchange of financial account data for tax purposes is essential for the effective fight against tax evasion. the scandals surrounding the concealment of offshore assets go hand in hand with tax evasion as well as money laundering, corruption, terrorist financing and other criminal activities. the access to data by tax administrations varies widely across the eu, and i welcome the establishment of a central register that will be accessible to tax administrations in all member states. the financial institutions will now be able to identify beneficial owners in cases where the account holder is an intermediary structure.
in writing. ‒ i supported the draft legislative resolution of the european parliament on the proposal for a council directive amending directive 2011/16/eu as regards access to information by tax authorities for the prevention of money laundering. in order to combat tax evasion and avoid problems such as those highlighted by the panama papers, and taking into account the need to improve tax transparency, the commission proposed that tax authorities in the eu be given access to national information concerning money laundering. in order to combat this, the eu tax authorities decided to do so by means of directive 2011/16/eu. the directive provides for measures and established procedures to improve (cooperation) (such as exchange of information, control and mutual information). the improvements include the commission's efforts to speed up transparency, to give tax authorities greater access to business owner data and to enable the verification of people involved in certain financial takeovers.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a council directive amending directive 2011/16/eu as regards access to anti-money-laundering information by tax authorities. the new rules will enable and oblige tax authorities with anti-money laundering responsibilities in any eu country to share automatically information such as bank account balances, interest income and dividends, with their counterparts in other member states. i voted in favour because i believe that efforts made in transparency are the only way to fight against tax evasion. moreover, links between money laundering, the funding of terrorism, organised crime and tax evasion highlight the need for close cooperation and coordination among eu countries.
in writing. ‒ the revelations of swissleaks, luxleaks, the panama papers and the bahamas, which are just a few examples of a global phenomenon, have confirmed the urgent need for greater tax transparency and closer coordination and cooperation between judicial authorities. the new rules thus provide for the mandatory automatic exchange of information on bank account balances, interest and dividend income between the authorities responsible for preventing money laundering and tax evasion in the member states. the resolution also stresses that the links between money laundering, terrorist financing, organised crime and tax evasion call for close cooperation and coordination between eu member states. i believe that the proposed directive brings effective and proportionate measures against tax evasion and therefore i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a council directive amending directive 2011/16/eu as regards access to information by tax authorities on the prevention of money laundering.

in writing. ‒ the parliament's report on the european central bank's annual report 2015 notes that the high level of public debt and the large number of bad loans in the banking sector continue to weaken the euro area financial market, while highlighting some important facts about the current situation in the financial area. the report also highlights the worrying practice of the ecb, which, by providing liquidity to banks at negative interest rates and removing the requirement to repay assets if the loans fall short of their benchmark, reduces the link between providing liquidity to central banks and lending to the real economy. it also stresses that banks with very low costs can access funds to subsidize their balance sheet, while the effects on the real economy would be minimal and these subsidies are not subject to strict conditions regarding the execution and purpose of the investments. despite many important findings, the report does not address some other topical issues, such as the need to promote a more sustainable economy, and does not include a requirement to establish mechanisms to channel funds into investments with a long-term positive impact on society and the environment, so i abstained from voting on this report.

in writing. ‒ retail financial services, which include personal bank accounts, payments, personal loans, mortgages and savings accounts, are part of the daily lives of european citizens. however, inefficient competition, particularly in the area of payments and banking, has led to large differences in the access of consumers to high-quality services at the same level of benefit between member states. the european union has made little progress in creating a single market for retail financial services in the past and this green paper provides the necessary impetus to remove cross-border barriers and connect financial actors from all member states with consumers across the european union, to ensure choice, value and quality for all consumers, thereby strengthening their trust in providers and making the right decisions in the light of their individual financial circumstances. the parliament's report welcomes the commission's initiative as it responds appropriately to the rapidly changing market environment by promoting integration and the cross-border provision of financial services. the report, which stresses, inter alia, the need for a high level of consumer protection legislation and its consistent implementation in the eu, calls on the commission to investigate misleading practices faced by consumers in card payments and currency conversion atm withdrawals, and i voted in favour of it.

in writing. ‒ the proposal for a directive under consideration in this report ensures that the existing air pollutant emission ceilings in directive 2001/81/ec will apply until 2020, while setting new national emission reduction commitments until 2030. national emission ceilings are intended to reduce air pollution and its harmful effects on public health and the environment throughout the european union. as air pollution is of a transboundary nature, this issue requires a multi-level approach, with some responsibility to be taken on at european as well as national, regional and local levels. pollution reduction will only be possible through an integrated approach that takes into account the responsibility of polluters, jurisdiction and fair sharing of costs. the commission proposal is unfortunately too lax in several respects, for example by failing to impose binding interim (2025) targets on member states to encourage them to reduce emissions continuously and evenly and to meet the 2030 targets, by completely excluding harmful methane from the list of pollutants, and by failing to take into account parliament's calls for legislative amendments that take greater account of the importance of clean air and other environmental objectives. the parliament's report does not address these shortcomings, nor does it propose any appropriate amendments to the commission's proposal, which is why i did not support it in the vote.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a directive of the european parliament and of the council on the reduction of national emissions of certain air pollutants and amending directive 2003/35/ec. air pollution, which in figures represents €330940 billion per year in the total cost to society of air pollution, must remain an important issue to be addressed at the level of the european union as a whole. i support the commission's proposal to introduce a new directive setting new emission ceilings for certain chemical compounds. we are faced with the problem that many member states are still not meeting the agreed standards.
in writing. ‒ i supported the draft legislative resolution of the european parliament on the proposal for a directive of the eu parliament and of the council on the reduction of national emissions of certain air pollutants and amending directive 2003/35/ec. eu legislation must be based on evidence-based policy making. the commission's proposal is clear on air quality, which is a major cross-border issue and affects both human health and the environment. low air quality contributes to premature mortality, sickness absence from work, high healthcare costs, reduced productivity, lost crops and damage to buildings. in europe, the total external costs to society related to health resulting from air pollution are estimated at around eur 330-940 billion per year. in addition, there is increasing evidence that the deposition of atmospheric nitrogen particles in the atmosphere causes changes in the natural environment, such as reduced diversity of native vegetation, reduced plant growth and an unbalanced nutritional status due to eutrophication and acidification. the commission proposal repeals and replaces the current national emission ceilings directive and sets new emission ceilings for sulphur dioxide, nitrogen oxides, ammonia and volatile organic compounds for the period from 2020 and from 2030.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a directive of the european parliament and of the council on the reduction of national emissions of certain atmospheric pollutants and amending directive 2003/35/ec. close to half a million europeans die every year from diseases linked to the millions of tons of gases and particulates human activity releases into the atmosphere. the aim of the new directive is to set tougher emission limits for key air pollutants. i voted in favour because i believe that the directive would set national targets to reduce emissions from five key air pollutants by 2030 compared to 2005.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a directive of the european parliament and of the council on the reduction of national emissions of certain atmospheric pollutants and amending directive 2003/35/ec. efforts to achieve high air quality that does not have major negative impacts on human health and the environment and does not seriously threaten human health and the environment are one of the essential elements of sustainable development to which the eu is committed. since i believe that the measures of the proposed directive will contribute to the progressive reduction of air pollution and to the provision of a high level of protection of human health and the environment, i supported it.

in writing. ‒ a sustainable and well-capitalised banking system and strong global standards and principles are key to maintaining financial stability and providing credit to the real economy. the basel committee on banking supervision brings together central banks and supervisors of major banking institutions around the world to develop internationally agreed minimum standards for prudent and sound banking and to address the negative consequences of the global economic and financial crisis that countries in the european union and elsewhere continue to face. the parliament's report does indeed provide some good starting points for the future, such as preventing the negative effects of an unreliable financial system on the real economy and withdrawing the right to use standard banking practices where these have already proved unsuccessful, giving supervisors the power to require banks to accurately calculate the risk of traditional banking instruments, and parliament's commitment to continue to advocate for the prevention of a new wave of bad bank rescues. however, given the lack of ambition and the weakness of the basel committee on banking supervision's recommendations, the fact that the promises of world leaders to stop taxpayers paying for irresponsible bank behaviour have not been fulfilled to date, and the strong possibility that we will see even negative deregulation in this area in the future, i did not support the report in my vote.

in writing. ‒ i agree with the intention to adopt additional anti-fraud measures and to support the further development of the existing value added tax system, and therefore i fully support these proposals in the european parliament. this important improvement requires fundamental reforms to eliminate or at least significantly reduce the problems of vat collection in the eu. i believe that an agreement on the final vat arrangements requires a joint effort by the member states, which can lead to an agreement on a better functioning vat system. i also see the call for a clearer vision of a simpler system with fewer exceptions and in conjunction with a pragmatic approach that respects the interests of the rapidly evolving digital economy as justified.
in writing. ‒ i supported the motion for a european parliament resolution on the efforts to achieve a definitive vat system and to combat vat fraud. the vat system was introduced in the eu in 1993 as a transitional arrangement. it was envisaged that the definitive solution would be postponed and replaced by interim solutions. vat is a consumption tax which is borne by the final consumer. it brought almost €1 trillion to the eu's coffers in 2014, making it an important and growing source of eu revenue. the poorly regulated system of vat interpretation within eu member states has led to money laundering and a grey economy. it was therefore all the more important to find a solution as soon as possible to the vat valuation between eu member states. the current system is prone to fraud and needs to be remedied. it is necessary to specify within which member states set the vat rates (more freedom, less litigation). reliable and high-quality impact assessments need to be carried out in cooperation with researchers and tax administrations and eu companies in order to reduce bureaucratic problems. a permanent tax system could be created by extending the system of general reverse charge to all intra-eu transactions. this would make the vat refund and invoicing redundant, reducing the possibility of fraud.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report ‘towards a definitive vat system and fighting vat fraud’. vat is a major and growing source of revenue in the member states and contributes to eu own resources, the eu’s total revenue from the vat own resource standing at eur 17 667 million and accounting for 12.27% of the total revenue of the eu in 2014. however, member states differ in the effectiveness with which they are able to address vat fraud and vat avoidance, since the vat gap is estimated to vary from less than 5% to over 40% depending on the country considered. the report emphasises that it is the responsibility of the tax authorities in the individual member states to ensure that vat is paid in a proper and simple way. it equally notes that the lack of comparable data and of adequate relevant indicators to measure member states’ performance affects the effectiveness of the eu system in tackling intra-eu vat fraud. i voted in favour because i believe that national tax administrations must take greater responsibility for ensuring tax compliance and reducing opportunities for evasion in the general implementation of the country-of-destination principle.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the road to a definitive vat system and the fight against vat fraud. the report is a response to the commission's communication of 7 april 2016 and its intention to adopt additional anti-fraud measures and to support the further development of the existing value added tax system. the commission intends to prepare a legislative proposal in the action plan to finalise the vat system based on the principle of taxation in the country of destination of goods and services. this marks a decisive shift away from the originally envisaged principle of taxation in the country of origin, which proved unworkable due to numerous instances of distortion of competition. as i believe that the commission's action plan will contribute to promoting fair taxation, sustainable consumption, employment, growth, investment and competitiveness, while limiting the scope for vat fraud, i supported the report.

in writing. ‒ i support the proposal to amend regulation no 952/2013, as some shortcomings have been identified in the existing regime. this change will now allow customs to more easily and correctly calculate import and other duties, apply non-fiscal measures such as sanitary controls and identify risks for goods arriving at their ports or airports. the current proposal to amend article 136 will fill this gap, thus ensuring equal treatment for goods and restoring the legal basis that already existed under the old customs code.
in writing. ‒ the commission proposal aims to amend article 136 of the union customs code in order to ensure the effective application of other provisions of the union customs code, in particular in the area of customs supervision. article 136 states, inter alia, that certain provisions, such as the obligation to present goods to customs upon unloading, do not apply to non-union goods temporarily leaving the customs territory of the union while moving by sea or air between two places in the customs territory of the union. in its proposal, the commission notes that the non-application of these provisions could jeopardise the effective customs control of non-union goods, as there is no clear legal basis in the current text of article 136 requiring the presentation of these goods to customs authorities. they may therefore have control problems, as this deprives them of the possibility to fully and correctly account for import and other duties or to identify risks. in its proposal, the commission seeks to ensure the correct application of other provisions of the union customs code by, inter alia, specifying precisely those provisions which do not apply when non-union goods re-enter the customs territory of the union and those provisions which do not apply to union goods which have retained their status despite having temporarily left the customs territory of the union. the parliament's report welcomes the commission's conclusions and proposals, and i therefore voted in favour of it.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council amending the regulation establishing the union customs code as regards goods temporarily leaving the customs territory of the union by sea or air. the amendment to the regulation will clarify the legal dilemmas regarding the presentation of goods to customs authorities, which leads to the incorrect calculation of various duties, the incorrect application of non-fiscal measures such as sanitary controls, and the risks for goods arriving at their ports or airports. the amendment of the regulation will thus ensure equal treatment for goods.
in writing. ‒ i supported the draft legislative resolution of the european parliament on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council amending regulation (eu) no 952/2013 laying down the union customs code as regards goods temporarily leaving the customs territory of the union by sea or air. the competent authorities in the member states do not currently have a legal basis for applying the provisions relating to the lodging of an entry summary declaration, the notification of arrival of a sea or air vessel, the transport of goods to customs and their presentation to customs on unloading or transhipment, the waiting for authorisation before unloading or transhipment of goods and the provisions on temporary storage. the absence of a proper legal basis makes customs controls difficult and therefore prevents them from correctly accounting for import duties and other charges, from properly applying non-fiscal measures such as sanitary controls and from identifying risks for goods arriving at their ports or airports. the current proposal will change that.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council amending regulation (eu) no 952/2013 laying down the union customs code, as regards goods that have temporarily left the customs territory of the union by sea or air. the relevant authorities in the member states do not have a legal basis, under the current article 136, on which to apply provisions related to lodging the entry summary declaration, notifying the arrival of a sea-going vessel or an aircraft, conveying and presenting the goods to customs upon unloading or transhipment, waiting for authorisation before unloading or transhipping the goods, as well as for the provisions on temporary storage. in the absence of a clear legal basis on which to require presentation of these goods to the customs authorities, they see their effective customs supervision duties hampered. i voted in favour because i believe that the current proposal to amend article 136 will close this gap and thereby ensure equal treatment of goods, providing again the legal basis that was already established through the old customs code.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council amending regulation (eu) no 952/2013 establishing the union customs code as regards goods temporarily leaving the customs territory of the union by sea or air. the proposed regulation will provide a legal basis for the exercise of certain customs control tasks on goods temporarily leaving the customs territory of the union while moving by sea or air between two places in that territory, directly and without a stop outside the union. this will allow for effective customs controls on the goods concerned, the correct accounting of import duties and other charges and the proper implementation of non-fiscal measures such as veterinary and phytosanitary controls.

in writing. ‒ the partnership agreement between the members of the african, caribbean and pacific group of states, of the one part, and the european union and its member states, of the other part, or the so-called cotonou agreement, governs relations between the eu and the republic of kiribati, while the agreement on the short-stay visa waiver further strengthens these relations and further strengthens economic and cultural links and deepens political dialogue, particularly in the areas of human rights and fundamental freedoms. according to the agreement, the republic of kiribati is one of the countries whose nationals are exempt from the visa requirement when crossing the external borders of the member states. all citizens of the republic of kiribati, irrespective of the purpose of the trip, except for paid employment, may travel without a visa to the territory of the contracting state for a maximum of 92 days in any 180-day period. the parliament's recommendation notes that such an agreement can have a positive impact on bringing european and pacific nations closer together, by, inter alia, simplifying travel conditions for entrepreneurs and encouraging investment and tourism. in addition, the republic of kiribati has made progress in the area of human rights (e.g. adoption of an action plan to eliminate sexual violence) and this agreement allows for further in-depth political dialogue on these issues, which is why i supported the recommendation in the vote.

in writing. ‒ i agree with the report on the european union solidarity fund, as it is an important source of funding for local and regional governments and mitigates the effects of natural disasters across europe. it can be used in a range of natural disasters, from floods to earthquakes and forest fires, to show european solidarity with the affected areas. it should also be stressed that investments in natural disaster prevention are of paramount importance in responding to climate change.
in writing. ‒ following the tragic floods of 2002, the eu set up an instrument to provide immediate financial assistance to countries affected by severe natural disasters. all member states and candidate countries may apply for assistance from the fund if their combined losses exceed eur 3 billion or 0,6% of gross national income. in this evaluation of the solidarity fund, the rapporteur stresses that it is not possible to anticipate all emergencies, but it is possible to improve the management of their consequences. to this end, the rapporteur addresses in his own-initiative report several aspects of the management of the fund, in particular its response time and the need for preventive measures, which is strongly linked to the need to coordinate the solidarity fund with other financial instruments. as the report strongly emphasises the crucial importance of rapid response by member states, which must deal with applications as soon as possible so that victims of accidents do not feel left behind in the time between the accident and the acquisition of funds, i voted in favour of it. it is also important to me that the rapporteur emphasises the positive effects of preventive measures, which must be a mandatory part of the post-disaster phase, and reminds member states to submit their risk prevention and management strategies in advance.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the european union solidarity fund: an assessment. over the years, it has often been shown that the european union solidarity fund is needed when natural disasters occur in the member states and that the priority is to help people in need as quickly as possible. but there's still a lot of room for improvement. the main consideration is to increase the flexibility with which we can respond more quickly and efficiently to disasters. however, from the point of view of budgetary control and the transparent management of taxpayers' money, we can be satisfied that significant improvements have been made in recent years towards better financial management.
in writing. ‒ proposal for a european parliament resolution on the european union solidarity fund: i voted in favour of the evaluation. following the tragic accidents of 2002, the european union established the european union solidarity fund (for the member states as well as the candidate countries). member states may apply for assistance from the fund if the total damage caused directly by a natural disaster exceeds eur 3 billion or 0,6% of gni (provisions also exist for minor disasters). natural disasters are difficult to prevent, so how quickly and how we respond after a disaster is important. emergency situations call for emergency procedures. the commission notes that the aid is granted to the beneficiaries of the measure, which are the beneficiaries of the measure, and that the aid is granted to the beneficiaries of the measure. disaster management and recovery are something we can influence, and the european union solidarity fund is one of the important levers of aid.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the european union solidarity fund: an assessment. following the tragic flooding of 2002, the european union introduced the european union solidarity fund. it was an immediate demonstration of the union’s solidarity with countries affected by major natural disasters. due to their unpredictable nature, natural disasters not only cause distress to the people affected but also raise the issue of response times from governments that have to meet unforeseen costs. when a disaster occurs, it is often too late for prevention but it should be an integral part of the next stage. i voted in favour because i believe it is important to seize the opportunity to comply with standards when rebuilding structures that have been destroyed or carrying out repairs on infrastructure.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the european union solidarity fund: an assessment. the european union solidarity fund is an instrument established to enable the eu to respond to major natural and regional disasters in the union and in the countries negotiating accession. the solidarity fund has been very useful since its creation, and its resources have been used for a total of eur 3.8 billion for 70 natural disasters in 24 eligible member states and accession countries. since the establishment of the fund, the number of natural disasters in the european union has increased significantly, and they have also become more severe and intense as a result of climate change. it is therefore important that in future, the allocation, management and implementation of the solidarity fund should ensure the greatest possible transparency and oversight of the use of the subsidies of the solidarity fund in order to ensure that the aid is effective and is directed to the right hands.

in writing. ‒ i support the conclusion of the agreement in question, as this agreement between the european union and the united states of america will significantly contribute to increasing the security of citizens. it thus addresses the protection of personal data in the context of transfers and processing intended for the prevention, investigation, detection or prosecution of criminal offences, including terrorism, which is currently on the rise.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the recommendation on the draft council decision on the conclusion, on behalf of the european union, of the agreement between the united states of america and the european union on the protection of personal data in the prevention, investigation, detection and prosecution of criminal offences. we need a broad set of safeguards and protections to be applied when personal data is exchanged between the united states of america and the european union for law enforcement purposes. the signed agreement does just that and contributes sufficiently to legal certainty, thus complementing the safeguards for data protection under existing and future agreements.
in writing. ‒ i supported, on behalf of the european union, the draft legislative resolution of the european parliament on the draft council decision on the conclusion of the agreement between the united states of america and the european union on the protection of personal data in the prevention, investigation, detection and prosecution of criminal offences. the agreement aims to ensure a high level of protection of the fundamental rights and freedoms of individuals, in particular the right to privacy with regard to the processing of personal data, when personal data are transferred to the competent authorities of the european union and its member states and the united states for these purposes (also referred to as the umbrella agreement). the umbrella agreement does not provide a legal basis for the transfer of personal data the basis for this is in some previous agreements (which it merely complements, harmonises). the agreement contains restrictions on the purpose and use of the transfer of personal data in order to prevent misuse of the release of personal data. the agreement represents a major advance in the protection of personal data when transferred between the eu and the us in the context of law enforcement activities. it may not be the best agreement that can be envisaged, but it is certainly the best possible in the present circumstances. the legal affairs committee gave its opinion on the draft and concluded that the envisaged agreement is based on an appropriate legal basis, ensures a high level of protection of fundamental rights to personal data and contributes to legal certainty and will enhance law enforcement cooperation with the united states.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the recommendation on the draft council decision on the conclusion, on behalf of the european union, of the agreement between the united states of america and the european union on the protection of personal information relating to the prevention, investigation, detection, and prosecution of criminal offenses. the purpose of the agreement is to ensure a high level of protection of personal information and enhance cooperation between the united states and the european union and its member states, in relation to the prevention, investigation, detection or prosecution of criminal offences, including terrorism. the envisaged agreement is mainly devoted to establishing a wide set of protections and safeguards, which will apply to the transfers of personal data for criminal law enforcement purposes between the united states, on the one hand, and the european union or its member states, on the other. i voted in favour because i believe that the envisaged agreement creates a framework for the protection of personal data that contributes to legal certainty. the agreement will supplement, where necessary, data protection safeguards in existing and future data transfer agreements or national provisions authorising such transfers.
in writing. ‒ i voted to approve the agreement between the united states of america and the european union on the protection of personal data in the prevention, investigation, detection and prosecution of criminal offences, on behalf of the european union. i support the agreement as it seeks to ensure a high level of protection of the fundamental rights and freedoms of individuals, in particular the right to privacy with regard to the processing of personal data when personal data are transferred to the competent authorities of the european union and its member states and the united states for the purposes of the prevention, investigation, detection and prosecution of criminal offences.
in writing. ‒ i agree with the eu-ghana interim agreement, as ghana and the eu are partners in various fields. the agreement is also important in promoting regional economic integration and investment. ghana is one of the main exporters of agri-food products to the economic community of west african states region, exporting cocoa, fruit, nuts and fish and importing rice, sugar and meat. all these raw materials are important for european citizens.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a council decision on the conclusion of an interim economic partnership agreement between the european community and its member states, of the one part, and ghana, of the other part. the interim agreement will be provisionally applied until the entry into force of the comprehensive economic partnership agreement between the european union and ghana. during this period, ghana has been granted duty-free access to the eu market. as the final negotiations on the regional economic partnership agreement are slow, we need to renew the interim agreement.
in writing. ‒ i supported the draft legislative resolution of the european parliament on the draft council decision on the conclusion of an interim economic partnership agreement between ghana, of the one part, and the european community and its member states, of the other part. the eu-west africa economic partnership is still a long way off, and ghana has therefore decided to proceed with the ratification of the interim economic cooperation agreement with the eu. in 2015, the total value of bilateral trade between ghana and the eu was eur 5,4 billion, representing more than 20% of total external trade. about one third of ghana's timber exports go to european markets (an agreement has been signed allowing legal timber trade with the eu). the 2007 agreement clearly does not fully correspond to the reality in 2016 and the interim agreement should be renewed. the interim agreement provides ghana, a lower middle-income country, with 100% market access based on a long-term contractual relationship, thereby providing the stability needed for new investment and job creation.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the recommendation on the draft council decision on the conclusion of the stepping stone economic partnership agreement between ghana, of the one part, and the european community and its member states, of the other part. ghana and the eu are partners across different areas, including that of fostering regional economic integration and investment. in 2015, the total two-way trade between ghana and the eu was worth 5.4 billion euros, comprising over 20% of ghana’s external trade. as soon as the regional epa enters into force, it will replace the two existing interim epas within the region. i voted in favour because i believe that the iepa ensures to ghana, a lower middle-income country, a 100% market access offer based on a long-term contractual relationship, which will ensure stability needed for new investments and job creation.
in writing. ‒ voted in favour of the conclusion of the economic partnership agreement between ghana, of the one part, and the european community and its member states, of the other part. i support the conclusion of the interim agreement as it will help to prevent trade disruptions for ghana, while also serving as a basis for a future regional economic partnership agreement. the interim agreement thus provides ghana, a lower middle-income country, with 100% market access on the basis of a long-term contractual relationship, thus providing the stability needed for new investment and job creation.
