in writing. ‒ i agree to use the eu solidarity fund to provide assistance to germany. the purpose is to respond quickly, efficiently and flexibly to emergencies. it is also a show of solidarity with the people of the affected areas. on 19 august 2016, germany submitted an application to mobilise the fund, following a series of short-term, exceptionally intense floods that affected the region of lower bavaria in may and june 2016. however, since the scale of the natural disaster meets all the conditions for the use of the fund, i consider that there are no reservations about its use.
in writing. ‒ this report addresses the decision of the parliament and the council on the mobilisation of the european union solidarity fund to provide assistance to germany following the floods that affected lower bavaria in may and june 2016. the floods destroyed public and private infrastructure and agricultural land, killing 7 people and affecting a total of 47 000 people. some communities have been without water for weeks, and have also had to deal with plumbing failures and electrical grid disruptions. the german authorities estimated the total direct damage at approximately eur 1,2 billion, which is well above the threshold of 1,5% of regional gdp, and therefore the accident can be considered a regional disaster under the provisions of the eu solidarity fund regulation. the commission therefore considers that the aid is compatible with the internal market. this report welcomes the decision of the parliament and the council confirming the mobilisation of the solidarity fund to assist germany. and since the solidarity fund is essentially a quick and effective emergency aid instrument by which the european union shows solidarity with the population of the affected areas, i voted in favour of it.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a decision of the european parliament and of the council on the mobilisation of the european union solidarity fund to provide assistance to germany. germany has been affected by a number of short-term intense floods in may and june this year and has therefore submitted an application to mobilise the solidarity fund. germany will thus receive a good eur 31 million in commitment and payment appropriations. i voted in favour of the report because germany's contribution was complete and fully met the criteria for using the european union solidarity fund.
in writing. ‒ i supported the motion for a european parliament resolution on the proposal for a decision of the european parliament and of the council on the mobilisation of the european union solidarity fund to provide assistance to germany. the european union solidarity fund (the 'fund') aims to enable the union to respond quickly, efficiently and flexibly to emergencies, thus demonstrating its solidarity with the population of areas affected by natural disasters. germany was affected by intense short-term flooding in may and june 2016 and therefore applied for the use of the fund in august. the floods have destroyed public and private infrastructure, private homes and agricultural land. seven people died, and more than 47 000 people were affected in lower bavaria, with more than 2000 unable to return to their homes for two months after the floods. we need to make a decision as soon as possible to help people.

in writing. ‒ the parliament's report addresses the decision of the parliament and the council to use the flexibility instrument to finance immediate budgetary measures to address the current migration, refugee and security crisis, which notes that an additional eur 530 million is needed to finance measures under the flexibility instrument to mitigate this crisis. the flexibility instrument finances expenditure which cannot be financed within the limits of the budget line ceilings. in this case, the 2017 ceilings for the 'security and citizenship' section do not allow for adequate funding of emergency measures in the area of migration, refugees and security. on this basis, the report agrees to the use of the flexibility instrument of eur 530 million, which is why i voted in favour of it. however, i would like to draw attention to the fact, as also noted by the committee on civil liberties, justice and home affairs, that the total amount available for this instrument in 2017 is eur 530 million, and that this is only a short-term solution to the issues to be addressed in the context of the ordinary budgetary procedure, and that this amount is unlikely to be sufficient to address the growing challenges in this area.

in writing. ‒ the solidarity fund enables the european union to respond quickly, efficiently and flexibly to emergencies, thus demonstrating its solidarity with the population of regions affected by natural disasters. the report on the use of the solidarity fund for the payment of advances under the general budget for 2017 welcomes the decision of the parliament and the council to conclude that the use of the fund for the payment of advances should amount to eur 50 million in order to ensure sufficient funds in the general budget of the european union for 2017 in a timely manner. this is the maximum amount of use of the fund that can be granted in cases where rapid action is required and budgetary resources must be made available in good time. this proposal is not linked to a specific disaster but provides for the entry of emergency funds into the general budget of the union so that they can be made available immediately in the event of future disasters. i voted in favour of the parliament's report, as it contains an important message, in addition to supporting the parliament and council decision, that the solidarity fund is not just one form of eu financial support, but above all a clear political expression of solidarity with citizens in need.

in writing. ‒ i support the resolution which notes the seriousness of the earthquakes in central italy. on 24 august 2016, central italy was struck by a devastating earthquake which caused significant material damage and destroyed towns, severely damaged local and regional infrastructure, destroyed historical and cultural heritage and damaged the economy. the earthquake and subsequent aftershocks injured more than 400 people, killed 290 and displaced up to 100,000.
in writing. ‒ the earthquake in italy on 30 october, with a magnitude of 6.5, is considered one of the strongest earthquakes to hit the apennines since the 1980s. three consecutive earthquakes left more than 100,000 residents in the quake zone homeless. cities, towns and villages are destroyed, local and regional infrastructure is damaged, historical and cultural buildings are destroyed, all of which have a negative impact on tourism and the economy. in the current situation, it is most important to offer financial as well as humanitarian assistance to the affected areas. the reconstruction of the affected areas and buildings must begin as soon as possible so that the local population can return to their homes and resume their normal lives. in view of the gravity of the situation and the large number of persons affected, the european commission should take all necessary measures to examine italy's request for financial assistance from the european solidarity fund as soon as possible. it is necessary to grant italy the requested financial assistance, while ensuring that the necessary synergies between the different financial instruments are established for the purpose of rapid recovery and that the funds are used efficiently and transparently. i therefore voted in favour of the resolution.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the joint motion for a resolution on the situation in italy following the earthquakes. this year, italy has been struck by earthquakes followed by aftershocks that have devastated entire villages, leaving many in these and surrounding areas on the verge of despair. more than 400 people were injured, and 290 died. i therefore support the call on the commission to consider, in the light of the exceptional and very serious situation, the possibility of excluding sustainable reconstruction and all earthquake-resistant investments, including those co-financed by the european structural and investment funds, from the national deficit calculation under the stability and growth pact.
in writing. ‒ i supported the european parliament resolution on the situation in italy after the earthquakes. italy was struck by a devastating earthquake in august 2016, followed by three more powerful quakes in late october. entire villages were completely destroyed, bringing many residents of the affected areas to the brink of despair and causing significant indirect damage to the surrounding areas. there was a displacement of 100,000 people. the recent earthquakes have devastated towns, seriously damaged local and regional infrastructure, destroyed historical and cultural heritage and damaged economic activities, in particular small and medium-sized enterprises, agriculture, landscapes, as well as tourism and hospitality capacities. it is necessary to offer immediate assistance and to take measures to ensure that the problems are alleviated before the coming winter.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the motion for a resolution on the situation in italy after the earthquakes. between august and october 2016 three devastating earthquakes hit the central apennines region of italy, killing 290 people, injuring more than 400 and displacing tens of thousands. the most recent quake, which occurred on 30 october, is the strongest to have been recorded in italy since the 1980 irpinia earthquake. the territories concerned suffer from a deformation that extends over an area of about 130 square km, with a maximum displacement of at least 70 cm. the earthquakes caused serious damage to towns, infrastructure and historic, artistic and cultural heritage assets. in order to cover reconstruction costs, italy may be obliged to submit a request for the amendment of its national and regional operational programmes under article 30 of regulation (eu) no 1303/2013 in order to be able to allocate more resources to thematic objective 5. the resolution underlines the serious economic effects of the successive earthquakes and the destruction left in their wake. i voted in favour because i believe that we have to show our deepest solidarity and empathy with all the individuals affected by the earthquakes and their families.

in writing. ‒ i voted for the report on the commissioners' declarations of interests guidelines. i support the report which recalls, inter alia, that the purpose of the review of commissioners' declarations of financial interests is to ensure the ability of commissioners-designate to act with complete independence and to ensure the greatest possible transparency and accountability of the commission. the assessment of a possible conflict of interest must also be based on convincing, objective and relevant facts and be linked to the area of activity of the commissioner-designate. we must therefore give the legal affairs committee sufficient time to examine the whole area in depth and to make an appropriate assessment.
in writing. ‒ motion for a european parliament resolution on commissioners' declarations of interests - i supported the guidelines. annex xvi to parliament's rules of procedure on the guidelines for the confirmation of the commission provides that parliament may seek all information relevant to its decision on the suitability of a candidate for commissioner. expects full disclosure of information relating to their financial interests. declarations of interests of candidate commissioners shall be forwarded to the committee responsible for legal affairs for examination. unfortunately, that provision does not define precisely the scope of the review by the committee on legal affairs. therefore, an additional substantive review is necessary. it is necessary to specify the scope of the review of declarations of financial interests by the committee on legal affairs. the role of the committee on legal affairs shall be to assess the existence of possible conflicts of interest and, where appropriate, to make recommendations for their elimination. the control of declarations of financial interests and, more generally, of possible conflicts of interest relating to members of the commission should not be limited to the commission's appointment procedure.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on commissioners’ declarations of interests – guidelines. the aim of scrutinising commissioners’ declarations of financial interests is to ensure that the commissioners-designate are able to fulfil their mandates completely independently and to ensure maximum transparency and accountability on the part of the commission. the report points out that a conflict of interests is defined as ‘any interference situation between a public interest and public and private interests that is likely to affect or that appears likely to affect the independent, impartial and objective exercise of a duty’. it equally underlines that the committee on legal affairs observes the strictest confidentiality when examining questions relating to the declarations of interests of the commissioners-designate, but also ensures, in accordance with the principle of transparency, that its conclusions are published as soon as they are available. i voted in favour because i believe that beyond the time allocated for questions that the committee on legal affairs wishes to put to the commissioner-designate, should it note a possible conflict of interests, it should be granted the right to continue with the hearing and obtain the required clarifications.
in writing. ‒ i voted for the report on the commissioners' declarations of interests guidelines. i support calls on the commission to urgently revise the 2011 code of conduct for commissioners to take account of the recommendations made by the european parliament in its recent resolutions and the general development of ethics and transparency standards applicable to all eu institutions. i believe that full disclosure of information relating to the financial interests of commissioners-designate contributes to the personal integrity of the candidates and strengthens the trust of eu citizens in the independent functioning of the eu institutions.
in writing. ‒ i agree that further improvements are needed in the maritime safety directive, which complements directive 2004/35/ec on environmental liability and directive 2011/92/eu on environmental impact assessment, and the ratification of the protocol on maritime activities to the barcelona convention in the council. these are the right steps to protect the environment, regulate human activities and ensure the safety of workers. it is important to be aware of the scale of oil and gas extraction in the north sea, which will in future extend to the southern mediterranean. however, the increased volume certainly increases the potential for accidents and therefore adequate safety must be ensured.
in writing. ‒ in order to establish minimum requirements for preventing and limiting the consequences of major accidents in offshore oil and gas operations, the european union adopted a directive on safety at sea in response to the major explosion on the deepwater horizon platform. the parliament's report calls for the full implementation and enforcement of this directive and stresses the need to establish an appropriate legal framework to regulate all maritime activities before the next major maritime disaster occurs. i voted in favour of the report because it highlights two very important aspects. first, the report expresses concern that the maritime safety directive defines an accident as 'major' only if it results in fatalities or serious bodily injury, but does not include possible serious consequences for the environment, for example when the accident seriously affects protected areas or protected species. secondly, the report rightly points out that the effective application of the 'polluter pays' principle for offshore oil and gas activities in line with the principle of sustainable development should not only cover the cost of remediating environmental damage, but also the settlement of compensation claims. the report also stresses the need to introduce strict liability rules for accidents at sea, which would make it easier for victims to access justice.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on liability, compensation and financial security for offshore oil and gas activities. i support the report which calls on member states which have not yet transposed the environmental liability and environmental impact assessment directives to do so without delay, while ensuring the independence of the competent authorities, and on the commission to assess whether it is appropriate to introduce additional harmonised rules on liability, compensation and financial security. it is the only way to prevent any further accidents with cross-border consequences.
in writing. ‒ i supported the motion for a european parliament resolution on liability, compensation and financial security for offshore oil and gas activities. offshore oil and gas activities are increasingly carried out further from land and often in much deeper water than before. some of the activities take place in very harsh environments, like the arctic. in april 2010, an explosion occurred on the deep water platform, causing a spill. this made it clear that minimum requirements were needed to prevent major accidents in offshore oil and gas operations in the eu and to limit the consequences of such accidents (the safety at sea directive was adopted after the accident). it is necessary to update the existing liability systems in member states in order to ensure that incidents in member states' waters do not adversely affect offshore oil and gas activities. the commission should work closely with member states to ensure that the system of compensation and financial guarantees for offshore oil and gas activities in the eu is updated, in particular to allow third parties to claim compensation for traditional damage caused by offshore oil and gas activities. this also requires the establishment of an effective compensation system.
in writing. ‒ i voted on the report on liability, compensation and financial security for offshore oil and gas operations. offshore oil and gas operations are being carried out further from land and often in much deeper waters than has previously been the case. some operations are taking place in harsh environments and in locations that depend on tourism for a large part of their income. following the explosion and oil spill from deepwater horizon on 20 april 2010, the offshore safety directive was adopted with the aim of establishing minimum requirements for preventing major accidents in offshore oil and gas operations in the eu and to limit the consequences of such accidents. member states had until 19 july to update their national legislative frameworks for offshore oil and gas operations to be in line with the offshore safety directive. i voted in favour because i believe that it is of utmost importance to update the existing liability systems in the member states to ensure that if an incident occurs in the waters of these states, it would not adversely affect the future of offshore oil and gas operations nor that of the entire eu.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on liability, compensation and financial security for offshore oil and gas activities. according to estimates from various studies, there have been thousands of accidents in the oil and gas sector in the european union, with serious and lasting consequences for the marine environment. i therefore consider it important that there are effective and appropriate compensation mechanisms and appropriate mechanisms for the rapid handling of claims in the event of damage caused by oil and gas activities to humans, animals and the environment. at the same time, the mechanisms for the mandatory financial guarantee for the payment of compensation in the event of accidents should not impose a disproportionate financial burden on the companies in the gas and oil industry and thus place them in a non-competitive position.

in writing. ‒ i agree with the implementation of the european order for payment procedure and welcome its successful functioning in all member states as a procedure applicable in civil and commercial matters in relation to the execution of uncontested claims. its main objective is to simplify and speed up the procedure for the cross-border recognition and enforcement of creditors' rights in the european union, thereby enabling the economy to function smoothly.
in writing. ‒ the european order for payment procedure is an action in the field of judicial cooperation in civil matters with cross-border elements. it is intended to facilitate the recovery of sums by creditors in cross-border judicial proceedings by allowing them to obtain an order for the recovery of undisputed civil and commercial claims easily. small and medium-sized enterprises have recently been facing increased delays in payments, which seriously threatens their survival and the loss of many jobs. according to the commission, there are approximately 12 000 applications for european payment orders submitted each year, with a wide variation in use between member states. this shows that there is a need to increase the information of citizens, businesses and legal professionals on the existence, operation and benefits of this procedure. the parliament's report welcomes the successful operation of the procedure to date and supports the commission's future efforts to optimise it. as the report points out, among other things, some essential facts, such as the practice of member states preferring to use national legislation instead of the european order for payment procedure, which prevents citizens from exercising their rights at cross-border level and thus reduces trust in eu legislation, i voted in favour of it. it is also a good report, calling for the simplification and acceleration of this procedure and for the reduction of the cost of crossborder cases.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the implementation of the european order for payment procedure. the main objective of the european order for payment, which is applicable in civil and commercial matters relating to the enforcement of uncontested claims, is to simplify and accelerate the procedure for the cross-border recognition and enforcement of creditors' rights in the european union. i support the report which considers that practical measures should be taken to further inform citizens, businesses, legal professionals and all other relevant parties about the existence, operation, use and advantages of the european order for payment procedure in cross-border cases;
in writing. ‒ i supported the motion for a european parliament resolution on the implementation of the european order for payment procedure. the purpose of the european order for payment procedure is to facilitate the recovery of sums in cross-border judicial proceedings. the procedure allows creditors to easily obtain a recovery order for uncontested civil and commercial claims. it can be requested by post, and often by electronic means - no lawyer is required. some countries have a low rate of use, so more needs to be done to inform businesses and legal professionals about the existence of the procedure and its benefits. the successful use of the procedure requires a rapid (30 day) issuance, the ability to submit the relevant forms online and the acceptance of applications in foreign languages. the commission should adopt new versions of certain standard forms in order to take account of the various changes that have taken place in recent years and to improve the clarity of those parts of the text where the payment of interest is concerned.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the application of the european order for payment procedure. the purpose of the european order for payment procedure is to allow for the easier recovery of sums in cross-border proceedings. the procedure is optional, meaning that it is available in cross-border cases as an alternative to the various equivalent national procedures. the procedure allows creditors to easily obtain an order to recover uncontested civil and commercial claims. it can be applied for by correspondence or, often, electronically, does not require the assistance of a lawyer, and is enforceable in other member states without any need for additional formalities. the commission states that some 12 000 applications for european orders for payment are made each year. where the defendant opposes the application, the procedure cannot continue. i voted in favour because i believe that the commission should adopt new versions of the standard forms in order to take into account various changes that have occurred over the years.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the implementation of the european order for payment procedure. the procedure was introduced to enable the recovery, quickly, simply and cheaply, of amounts arising from debts fixed in a fixed amount and due, which are not contested by the defendant. the data show that the procedure is generally implemented satisfactorily, but it is operating significantly below its full capacity. since i consider that the report gives a good presentation of the implementation of the european order for payment procedure, points out the key shortcomings in the implementation and makes reasoned suggestions for improving the procedure, i supported it.

in writing. the european commission presented a new package of measures at the end of november this year, entitled 'clean energy for all europeans'. the commission wants europe not only to adapt to the clean energy transition, but to take a leading role in this area, but unfortunately, given the contents of the package, this seems all the more unrealistic. what is of great concern to us is that the package is unfortunately a long way from the commitments made under the paris climate agreement, as many ngos and environmentalists have also pointed out. the increase in the energy efficiency improvement target from 27% to 30% is far too low and well below the request of the european parliament, which has already called for a binding 40% target by 2030. the package is also weak in the area of renewable energy sources, as maintaining the 27% renewable energy target is not ambitious enough and does not include binding national targets either. the continuation of fossil fuel subsidies is also a cause for concern. the package thus falls far short of the commission's promises and could even jeopardise eu action to combat climate change. i hope this is not another missed opportunity to take a step towards a greener, more sustainable and environmentally friendly future that we owe to our planet and future generations.

in writing. ‒ i support the european parliament's legislative resolution confirming the council's position at first reading. the agreement achieves the key objective of ensuring the sustainable management and exploitation of deep-sea species, while minimising the impact of deep-sea fishing activities on the highly sensitive marine environment. it is essential to stress that the european union will freeze its fishing footprint by defining the area where deep-sea fishing will be allowed. this zone also includes the area in eu waters of the north-east atlantic where directed fishing took place between 2009 and 2011. this territorial limitation will apply to vessels fishing for deep-sea species, i.e. those where the catch of deep-sea species represents more than 8% of the total catch on at least one fishing trip per year. a depth limit of 800 metres is also established, which is important for the effective protection of sensitive deep-sea ecosystems. however, it is also important to agree that vessels caught fishing in sensitive marine ecosystems at a depth of more than 400 metres will have to cease their activities and set sail at least five nautical miles from the fishing area concerned. in order to ensure the collection of scientific data, 20% of the vessels will need to have a scientific observer on board. i hope that the content will now be followed by effective implementation in practice.
in writing. ‒ i voted against the proposal of the efdd group that the european parliament reject the council's position at first reading on the establishment of specific conditions for fishing for deep-sea stocks in the north-east atlantic and provisions on fishing in international waters of the north-east atlantic and repeal the council regulation. i support the compromises reached in the trilogue, such as the european union freezing its fishing footprint by defining the area where deep-sea fishing will be allowed. i also support the compromise to introduce specific penalties for vessels that violate the rules on deep-sea fishing and that no exceptions to certain rules will be possible.
in writing. ‒ i did not support the draft legislative resolution of the european parliament on the council position at first reading with a view to adopting a regulation of the european parliament and of the council laying down special conditions for fishing for deep-sea stocks in the north-east atlantic and provisions on fishing in international waters of the north-east atlantic and repealing council regulation (ec) no 2347/2002. the proposal aims to establish specific conditions for fishing for deep-sea stocks in the north-east atlantic and provisions for fishing in international waters of the north-east atlantic. deep-sea fishing is dominated by traditional coastal countries such as portugal and by large-scale trawlers from france and spain. together they account for 1% of landings from the north-east atlantic. they hunt mainly species that are slow to grow and are vulnerable to overexploitation (sea sword, eel, etc.). the european union will freeze its fishing footprint by defining an area where deep-sea fishing will be allowed. this new measure aims to improve the protection of sensitive deep-sea ecosystems.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the recommendation for second reading on the council position at first reading in view of the adoption of a regulation of the european parliament and of the council establishing specific conditions for fishing for deep-sea stocks in the north-east atlantic and provisions for fishing in international waters of the north-east atlantic and repealing council regulation (ec) no 2347/2002. according to the regulation, the european union is going to freeze its fishing footprint by specifying the area in which deep-sea fishing will be allowed. that area includes the area in which targeted fishing took place between 2009 and 2011 in eu waters in the north-east atlantic. parliament has secured specific penalties for vessels breaching the regulation on deep-sea fishing and a stipulation that no exemptions will be granted to certain rules. i voted in favour because i believe that, through this regulation, parliament has introduced new, stricter transparency rules by including obligations to make information available to the public on european vessels targeting deep-sea species and to report all catches.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the european parliament legislative resolution on the council position at first reading with a view to adopting a regulation of the european parliament and of the council laying down special conditions for fishing for deep-sea stocks in the north-east atlantic and provisions for fishing in international waters of the north-east atlantic and repealing council regulation (ec) no 2347/2002. i support the adoption of the council's position at first reading without further amendments, as it is in line with the agreement reached in the trilogues. the purpose of the proposal is to establish specific conditions for fishing for deep-sea stocks in the north-east atlantic and provisions for fishing in international waters of the north-east atlantic in order to enable sustainable fishing.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the general revision of parliament’s rules of procedure. the report underlines that those amendments to the rules have taken due account of the provisions of the interinstitutional agreement of 13 april 2016 on better law-making. moreover, it draws attention to the need to reorganise the annexes to the rules of procedure so that they contain only texts that have the same legal value and are subject to the same procedural majority as the rules themselves, and annex vi which, although it requires a different procedure and a different majority for its adoption, consists of implementing measures of the rules. i voted in favour because the report requests that the other existing annexes and any additional texts which could be relevant for the work of the members, be re-grouped into a compendium which will accompany the rules.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on a coherent eu policy for the cultural and creative industries. in the current age of digitalisation, the existing cultural and creative industries face a major challenge to adapt to the significant developments in the field of digitalisation, while at the same time offering new opportunities for the development of new business models and market expansion. i therefore support the call in the report for the european commission to develop a comprehensive, coherent and long-term industrial policy framework for the cultural and creative sectors, while defining specific indicators for monitoring and analysing cultural, economic and social impact.
in writing. ‒ i supported the european parliament's motion for a resolution on a coherent eu policy for the cultural and creative industries. culture, art and creativity are shaping the image of europe. in europe in the 21st century, at the time of the transition to the digital economy, cultural and creative industries are increasingly replacing traditional production processes and value chains. the cultural and creative industries are industries based on cultural values and on the creativity, skills and talents of individuals, and can generate wealth and jobs by creating value from intellectual property (european culture has a history of more than 3000 years). around the world, the cultural and creative industries are considered to be a large and growing part of the global economy and create opportunities for new jobs. however, a genuine and coordinated industrial policy at eu level has not yet been established and a comprehensive industrial strategy is needed. the concept of 'cultural and creative industries' should be defined to ensure that it functions better. good international cooperation can also be achieved through culture. the cultural and creative industries play a key role in the reindustrialisation of europe, to drive growth and are strategically positioned to generate innovative spill-overs to other industrial sectors such as tourism, retail and digital technologies. europe could play a leading role in this.

in writing. ‒ the report stresses that overall political stability and respect for human rights are essential conditions for strengthening women's rights and improving their situation in individual countries. the eastern partnership countries should take immediate action to increase gender equality in society, including through the adoption of national action plans and through cooperation with international organisations and civil society stakeholders. they should also work to close the gaps in their anti-discrimination frameworks and to apply more legislation to combat gender-based discrimination, taking into account international standards. this is very important, as the statistics reflect a very worrying situation. in the eastern partnership countries, women occupied only 17 out of 136 senior ministerial positions in 2015, their share of elected parliamentarians averaged 16%, and they occupied only 17% of senior public administration positions. it is also important that the report also addresses the fight against trafficking in human beings, where women are the most frequent victims. in this context, there is a need to strengthen cooperation between the eastern partnership countries on the one hand and eu agencies and member states' law enforcement authorities on the other. i also supported the report because i considered that it contained very important aspects.

in writing. ‒ i supported the european parliament's motion for a resolution on women's rights in the eastern partnership countries. stabilising neighbourhood countries is one of the key objectives of the european union's external policy and the european neighbourhood policy to ensure security, peace, stability and prosperity for all, and women have an important role to play in this. the eastern partnership was established in 2009 at the initiative of the eu (it comprises the countries of ukraine, belarus, azerbaijan, moldova, georgia and armenia). women are still neglected in these countries. they are under-represented in the political structural areas, the gender pay gap remains wide and all too often they are victims of violence or trafficking. the aim of this report is not to list shortcomings and failures in the protection of women's rights, but to highlight the obstacles to women's empowerment and how greater gender equality could contribute to the achievement of the objectives of the eastern partnership and the european neighbourhood policy. gender equality is an area where great progress could be made through enhanced cooperation between the eu and the eastern partnership countries.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the rights of women in the eastern partnership states. stabilisation of its neighbourhood is one of the key objectives of the european union’s foreign policy and of the european neighbourhood policy (enp) in order to ensure the security, peace, stability and prosperity of all. women play a crucial role towards it. the eastern partnership was launched in 2009 with the prague declaration, as a joint initiative between the eu, its member states and six eastern european and south caucasus partner countries: armenia, azerbaijan, belarus, georgia, the republic of moldova and ukraine. because the eastern partnership is based on the commitment to the principles of international law, fundamental values of democracy, the rule of law and human rights, one should not forget the importance of gender equality and women rights. however, women remain remarkably absent from the political structures of power, be it in the executive or in the parliamentary branch, mainly due to discriminatory practices. i voted in favour because the report does not aim at listing the lacks and failures in protecting women’s rights but rather at highlighting the barriers to women’s empowerment and how greater gender equality would help reaching the eap and enp objectives.

respected. the report on the state of human rights in the world, or more precisely on the violation of human rights in the world, was introduced in the european parliament as a potentially powerful tool of our common foreign and security policy. if the helsinki conference four decades ago, by shining a spotlight on human rights abusers, paved the way for a world-changing epoch, today we must self-critically acknowledge that in using this tool of soft political power, we are falling short of the possibilities and expectations. thus, despite its size, this report does not capture the dramatic moment our planet is in. we invoke human rights when they are violated by others, we refuse to declare peace as a fundamental value, we leave people alone when they fear the present and the future. the european union, when it comes to the sources of crises, wars, human rights violations, is caught in its own fragmentation, history and geostrategy. so our conditional generosity in the humanitarian field is not enough. colleagues, we will have to talk about human rights more concretely, with reference to international and humanitarian law. we must be on the side of the weak and the humiliated, not on the side of power and its abuse. thank you so much.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the recommendation on the draft council decision on the conclusion of the agreement between the european union and the kingdom of norway on reciprocal access to fishing in the skagerrak for vessels flying the flag of denmark, norway and sweden. i support a new agreement between the eu and norway, replacing the old agreement from which norway withdrew. the new agreement will continue to give denmark, norway and sweden exclusive access to the waters of all three countries, and at the same time all member states will have reciprocal access to the respective waters of the other parties in the skagerrak and kattegat.
in writing. ‒ i supported the draft legislative resolution of the european parliament on the draft council decision on the conclusion of the agreement between the european union and the kingdom of norway on reciprocal access to fishing in the skagerrak for vessels flying the flag of denmark, norway and sweden. swedish, danish and norwegian fishermen have been fishing together in these waters for the same stock since at least the middle ages. the fishing tradition is older than the founding of the state and it is important to respect the historical fishing rights. the agreement between denmark, norway and sweden on mutual access to the skagerrak and kattegat fisheries entered into force on 7 august 1967 and was extended in 2002 until 2012. the new agreement continues to grant danish, norwegian and swedish vessels exclusive access to the waters of all three countries beyond four nautical miles from the baselines. it shall ensure permanent mutual access of both member states and norway to the relevant waters of the other parties in the skagerrak and kattegat, as well as prudent measures for the conservation and management of fisheries in the area. in addition, it allows for control measures in accordance with the principles of the normal jurisdiction of coastal states, which already apply to fisheries in the north sea.

in writing. ‒ the european commission has proposed to repeal regulation (eec) no 1192/69 on common rules for the normalisation of the accounts of railway undertakings, which allows member states to compensate railway undertakings for the payment of liabilities which are not covered by undertakings in other modes of transport. these obligations relate, for example, to special payments in the event of accidents at work, which railway undertakings are obliged to pay, whereas for other modes of transport they are paid by the state, to pensions for railway workers who perform heavy work and usually retire early, or to payments of costs for road-railway crossing facilities. the regulation was adopted before the liberalisation of the rail services market, when rail transport in europe was developing mainly within national borders, with integrated undertakings providing rail services and also managing rail infrastructure. the regulation on the numerous railway packages that have transformed the railway sector is no longer compatible with the current legal environment, as it differentiates between railway undertakings that are listed (and thus entitled to compensation) and undertakings that are not listed. i agree that the regulation is outdated and its wording is discriminatory, as only 40 companies listed in the annexes to the regulation have the possibility of being compensated, and i therefore support the proposal.
in writing. ‒ i voted against the amendment to reject the council's first reading position on common rules for the normalisation of railway company accounts. the proposal to repeal the regulation on common rules for the standardisation of accounts of railway undertakings is part of the market pillar of the fourth railway package. this will enable member states to compensate railway undertakings for the payment of liabilities which other transport undertakings do not have to cover. the regulation is no longer compatible with the current legal environment.
in writing. ‒ i supported the draft legislative resolution of the european parliament on the council's position at first reading with a view to adopting a regulation of the european parliament and of the council repealing council regulation (eec) no 1192/69 on common rules for the normalisation of the accounts of railway undertakings. as the commission states in its proposal, the regulation is no longer compatible with the current legal environment and has submitted a proposal for its repeal. the report agrees with that. it also agrees that the current text of the regulation is discriminatory, since only 40 companies listed in the annexes to the regulation are eligible for compensation. therefore, this regulation cannot be maintained unless the list of railway undertakings is kept up to date. negotiations were under way to resolve the problem. member states should respect all prior acts and implement the measures provided for in the directive without delay.
in writing. ‒ i supported the recommendation for second reading on the council's position at first reading with a view to adopting a regulation of the european parliament and of the council repealing council regulation (eec) no 1192/69 on common rules for the normalisation of the accounts of railway undertakings. regulation (eec) no 1192/69 is no longer compatible with the current legal environment following the numerous railway packages that have transformed the railway sector, as it discriminates between railway undertakings which are listed (and thus entitled to compensation) and undertakings which are not listed.
in writing. ‒ the proposed amendments seek to improve the quality of rail passenger services and increase their operational efficiency. this should mean a greater competitiveness and attractiveness of the railway sector compared to other modes of transport and a step forward in the development of the single european railway area. but unfortunately, the report contains too many flaws to support it on my own. the proposed new rules provide that public service contracts in railway transport must be awarded on the basis of competitive tendering procedures. however, the regulation contains a number of exceptions to this principle and allows contracts to be concluded directly or by a simplified procedure in a number of cases, which means that member states will be able to maintain their national systems over time. i also find it problematic that the regulation does not include a provision on the establishment of binding criteria in public service contracts, when it comes to strengthening environmental and social aspects, as well as on the establishment of a minimum quality of public services. we also wanted a stronger text on passenger rights, social and employment conditions and accessibility, but this was not achieved. for all the reasons i have mentioned, i voted against.

in writing. ‒ the so-called 'management' directive aimed to open up the internal rail passenger services market to increase competitive pressure on internal rail services markets in order to increase the volume and improve the quality of passenger services and to improve the management by the infrastructure manager to ensure equal access to the infrastructure. i regret to say that the directive contains too many shortcomings to be able to support it myself. a european network of infrastructure managers is established to exchange best practices, monitor implementation and address cross-border bottlenecks. unfortunately, this is all that remains of our proposal to set up a european regulatory authority with the power to deal with the many cross-border issues and problems. the directive also provides for the development of common information and ticketing systems to enable more efficient multimodal and cross-border passenger transport, with the commission monitoring developments and preparing a report to parliament and the council by 2022 and, if necessary, accompanying it with legislative proposals, for which no deadline is provided. the european parliament called for the establishment of such a system by 2019 for all public passengers on railways at first reading, but unfortunately this is not taken into account here. so there are too many flaws.

in writing. ‒ the annual report on human rights and democracy in the world and the european union's policy on human rights and democracy for 2015 expresses serious concern at the threat to the protection of human rights and democratic values worldwide and the undermining of the universality of human rights in many parts of the world, including under authoritarian regimes and through the activities of terrorist groups such as daesh. it calls on all eu institutions and member states to fulfil their commitments to promote democracy and the rule of law, and to protect and uphold human rights and fundamental freedoms. it is also important to condemn the attacks on journalists, judges, prosecutors, as well as environmental and human rights activists around the world, which we unfortunately still see very frequently. the report also takes the clear view that the european union must give human rights a central place in its relations with all third countries, including strategic partners, and it is important that the same commitment is shown in both internal and external policies. i am also pleased that the report is sufficiently progressive and includes strong parts on areas such as lgbti rights, combating all forms of discrimination, trafficking in human beings, migration, sexual and reproductive rights, environmental migration, freedom of expression online, support for human rights defenders, etc. for all that, i also supported the report.

in writing. ‒ in recent years, the european union has faced unprecedented internal and external challenges, including interstate conflicts, state collapse, terrorism, hybrid threats, cyber and energy insecurity, organised crime and climate change. the eu will only be able to respond effectively to all these new challenges if its structures and member states engage in a joint and truly coordinated effort within the framework of a common foreign and security policy, which must be clearly defined if it is to be successful. while i welcome the report's view that no member state can overcome the current challenges on its own and that member states must show a sufficient level of unity, political will and mutual trust, i am critical of the fact that the text of the resolution is unfortunately still too weakly worded. the strategy of the common foreign and security policy reflected in the resolution is not sufficiently clear, and the resolution contains several controversial and flawed parts. it calls, inter alia, on member states to increase their defence spending in order to meet nato's capability objectives, which require that at least 2% of gdp be devoted to defence, which would of course have an impact on member states' public finances. since the text of the resolution simply contains more questions than answers, i did not support the resolution.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the implementation of the common foreign and security policy. as we agreed in the opinion of the committee on budgets, we can all be concerned that less than one third of all available funds were spent on the common foreign and security policy in 2015, which is unusual given the scale of international conflicts that also threaten the european union. i also support the opinion of the committee on budgets, which calls on the member states to meet the 2% of gdp criteria for national defence spending, as slovenia does, and at the same time to invest more thoughtfully in their defence capabilities in order to improve their ability to operate in nato and the eu.
in writing. ‒ i supported the motion for a european parliament resolution on the implementation of the common foreign and security policy. the european union is facing unprecedented internal and external challenges, including interstate conflicts, state collapse, terrorism, hybrid threats, cyber and energy insecurity, organised crime and climate change. he's facing terrorist threats even on his own turf. europe can only respond effectively if its structures and member states work together. it is a wise intention to draw up an operational plan for security and defence. we are surrounded by unstable hotspots (middle east, africa, russia) with direct consequences for the well-being and security of eu citizens. this is now an opportunity for the eu to improve its action and cooperation (common foreign policy, combating disinformation, strengthening defence...). the eu needs to strengthen its security and defence capabilities, as it will only be able to realise its full potential as a global power if it accompanies its unrivalled soft power with hard power as part of the eu's comprehensive approach. sustainable development is one of the three pillars on which eu foreign policy must operate, alongside defence and diplomacy, and it is difficult to strengthen the market without security and stability. a solution to the conflict in syria must be found as soon as possible, including with the help of turkey as a partner.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the implementation of the common foreign and security policy. the eu is now surrounded by a series of hotbeds of instability, with much of the middle east and north africa engulfed in ethnic and religious conflicts and wars involving the larger powers indirectly, and terrorist groups spreading throughout the region. the report i supported analyses comprehensively the current state and challenges of international affairs and the role of the eu. the internal and external security challenges are complex. an effective security policy is only possible with the cooperation and political will of all member states.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the instruments of the common agricultural policy to reduce price volatility on agricultural markets. i support the initiatives of the committee on budgets, which in its opinion calls, inter alia, for better synergies between the common agricultural policy and other eu policies, in particular those relating to energy, water supply, land use, biodiversity and ecosystems, and the development of remote and mountainous areas, while also calling for greater transparency of agricultural markets, making price information available to all stakeholders, including consumers.
in writing. ‒ i supported the motion for a european parliament resolution on the instruments of the common agricultural policy to reduce price volatility on agricultural markets. european farmers are increasingly exposed to a variety of risks, as they are dependent on biological processes, climate change and the various impacts of plant and animal diseases (natural processes that cannot be controlled). the volatility of market prices is a major problem for farmers. the original instrument included price regulation, i.e. farmers would receive a guaranteed minimum price despite the crisis. the third cycle began in agriculture with the 2013 reform which defined the common agricultural policy for the period 2014-2020 (cycle i. starting with the 1992 agenda 2000, cycle ii. starting with the 2003 fischler reform). these reforms have gradually brought the cap closer to the market. the volatility of agricultural product prices is one of the main reasons for the catastrophic situation faced by many european farmers at the moment.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the instruments of the common agricultural policy to reduce price volatility on agricultural markets. the agricultural sector is increasingly exposed to price volatility, due to a variety of causes, such as the instability and imperfection of agricultural markets, the increasing globalisation and development of agricultural markets, the increased volatility of supply due to climate unpredictability, the increased health risks and the uncertain balance of food supply. the report i supported therefore advocates a more determined and coordinated policy with targeted instruments at eu and national level to ensure multi-purpose, sustainable agricultural production throughout the union at fair and profitable prices.

on behalf of the s&d group. thank you, mr president, and first of all, thank you to the rapporteur, mr de mery, for the excellent negotiations that have safeguarded the interests of the european parliament and all european citizens. and it also opened the door for georgians and ukrainians to get visa-free travel soon. ladies and gentlemen, the union's visa policy is one of the most tangible and concrete instruments of european foreign policy. at least, that's how it was in the past. i remember the tremendous emotion of the people of the western balkans when we were able to get their visas lifted. today, this same visa policy is losing its appeal as a result of continuous tightening. on the one hand, additional criteria, including political ones, for visa waiver and new measures such as the introduction of smart borders or etias. on the other hand, the continuing threat of visa reintroduction has made it possible to re-introduce the suspension mechanism. my dear commissioner! the second key aspect of the european visa policy is reciprocity. the european union must also have the courage to act when it comes to the question of reciprocity. today, the commission still allows the second-class citizens of as many as five eu member states to deliberately violate its own rules. in parliament, we will monitor closely the implementation of the new rules and take decisive action in the event of abuse.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council amending the regulation on the list of third countries whose nationals must be in possession of visas when crossing the external borders and those whose nationals are exempt from that requirement (amendment of the detention mechanism). i support the amendment that the commission should monitor the situation in these third countries and report regularly to the european parliament and the council. we will thus ensure the continuous fulfilment of specific criteria relating, inter alia, to illegal immigration, public order and security, economic benefits, in particular in the field of tourism and external trade.
in writing. ‒ i supported the draft legislative resolution of the european parliament on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council amending regulation (ec) no 539/2001 listing the third countries whose nationals must be in possession of visas when crossing the external borders and those whose nationals are exempt from that requirement (change of detention mechanism). visa policy is one of the key eu issues, affecting external action as well as internal security. it is important to this extent that its management is clearly defined as a shared competence of the co-legislators under the ordinary procedure. the evolution of the political and migration situation, in particular following the successive visa liberalisation procedures, requires a revision of the detention mechanism in order to make it more effective and flexible. it is necessary to introduce elements that will enable the eu to respond rapidly to sudden increases in the number of irregular migrants from third countries, unfounded asylum applications, refused readmission applications and security threats on european territory.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council amending regulation (ec) no 539/2001 listing the third countries whose nationals must be in possession of visas when crossing the external borders and those whose nationals are exempt from that requirement (amendment of the detention mechanism). visa policy is one of the key eu issues, affecting external action as well as internal security. the evolution of the political and migration situation, in particular following the successive visa liberalisation procedures, requires a revision of the detention mechanism in order to make it more effective and flexible. such flexibility must, of course, be accompanied by a robust set of human rights safeguards and measures, and by reports and statistics provided by european agencies and competent law enforcement bodies.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the draft motion for a resolution on the draft commission implementing directive amending annexes i to v to the council directive on protective measures against the introduction into the community of organisms harmful to plants or plant products and against their spread within the community. i agree that the draft commission implementing directive is not in line with union law, as it is not in line with the objective of the regulation. it states, inter alia, that the phytosanitary risks posed by any species, variety or biotype of pathogenic organisms, animals or parasitic plants which cause harm to plants or plant products should be identified. in addition, measures to reduce risks to acceptable levels should be laid down.
in writing. ‒ i supported the draft motion for a resolution of the european parliament on the draft commission implementing directive amending annexes i to v to council directive 2000/29/ec on protective measures against the introduction into the community of organisms harmful to plants or plant products and against their spread within the community. the draft commission implementing directive is not in accordance with union law as it is not consistent with the objective of regulation (eu) 2016/2031, namely to identify the phytosanitary risks posed by any species, variety or biotype of pathogenic organisms, animals or parasitic plants which cause harm to plants or plant products (harmful organisms) and the measures to reduce those risks to an acceptable level. in this respect, it would recall that regulation (eu) 2016/2031 will repeal and replace directive 2000/29/ec as soon as it enters into force (14 december 2019).
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the european parliament resolution of 15 december 2016 on the draft commission implementing directive amending annexes i to v to council directive 2000/29/ec on protective measures against the introduction into the community of organisms harmful to plants or plant products and against their spread within the community. the resolution concludes that the draft commission implementing directive is not in accordance with union law as it is not in line with the objective of regulation (eu) 2016/2031, namely to identify the phytosanitary risks posed by any species, variety or biotype of pathogenic organisms, animals or parasitic plants which cause harm to plants or plant products (harmful organisms) and the measures to reduce those risks to an acceptable level. i therefore consider that the proposals put forward by the commission to remedy this inconsistency are necessary.
in writing. ‒ thalidomide is a sedative and hypnotic drug that first appeared as a medicine in west germany in the 1950s. it was marketed as a safe drug to treat morning sickness, headache, cough, insomnia, and colds, but its use during pregnancy has caused the death and deformity of thousands of babies. documents from that time testify to the very poor pharmaceutical control in west germany. unfortunately, the evidence also confirms that the state intervened in the criminal proceedings against the german producer of thalidomide, which did not allow for a proper finding of its culpability for the consequences that had occurred, and also prevented civil proceedings, which therefore did not satisfy the right to a trial, and thus did not provide the survivors with adequate financial compensation. the resolution calls on the member states and the commission to coordinate activities and measures for the official recognition and compensation of survivors, thereby facilitating their healthcare and enabling a better quality of life. research shows that survivors require a lot of support due to specific health needs and have difficulty with mobility and independent living, as they have suffered many consequences that they face on a daily basis, and most of them have not had adequate care since birth. i myself supported the resolution for all these reasons.
in writing. - i voted for a joint resolution on aid to thalidomide victims. member states and the european commission should coordinate activities and measures to formally recognise and provide compensation to survivors. thalidomide was introduced in the 1950s as a safe and effective treatment for morning sickness in pregnant women. however, a number of adverse effects for pregnant women were soon observed, reflected in various deformities in the children of mothers taking thalidomide during pregnancy. i therefore also support the call on the commission to create a framework protocol at european level, whereby all european citizens affected by thalidomide will be entitled to appropriate compensation.
in writing. ‒ i supported the european parliament resolution on aid for thalidomide victims. thalidomide is a medicine that was marketed by chemie grünenthal gmbh in the late 1950s and early 1960s. it's supposed to cure morning sickness, pneumonia, colds and headaches. in pregnant women who took it, it caused a high number of newborn deaths and birth defects. recent reports in germany and the united kingdom indicate that survivors of thalidomide need to improve their quality of life, as their bodies are weakened and disabled by the drug's effects. in an open letter, the chairs of the european parliament's political groups supported the efforts to help thalidomide survivors. now is the ideal opportunity to mitigate and correct past wrongs.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the european parliament resolution on aid to victims of thalidomide. recently published independent reports in germany and the united kingdom conclude that thalidomide survivors need more support for their health needs, mobility and independent living, because their health is rapidly deteriorating due to the type of disability and because they have not received adequate support all the time since birth. i therefore support the call on the member states and the commission to coordinate action and measures for the formal recognition and compensation of surviving victims of thalidomide as soon as possible.
in writing. ‒ the paediatric medicines regulation came into force in 2007 and its aim was to improve children's health in europe by promoting the development and increased accessibility of medicines for children up to the age of 17. the regulation has made some progress, but it is still too slow and inadequate in many areas, especially in the field of paediatric oncology and neonatology. cancer remains the number one cause of death by disease in children over one year of age, and about 6000 children and young people die of cancer every year in europe. the regulation also provided for several incentives to enable the pharmaceutical industry to invest more in research and development, but these incentives were often abused by pharmaceutical companies and therefore did not produce the results expected. the resolution therefore calls on the commission to submit a report on the implementation and application of the paediatric medicines regulation by january 2017, as also provided for in article 50 of this regulation. this report should provide a comprehensive identification and in-depth analysis of the barriers currently hampering innovation in paediatric medicinal products. in the light of these findings, the commission should examine possible amendments, including a legislative review of the regulation, which appears to be necessary. for all these reasons, i supported the resolution in plenary.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the motion for a resolution on the question for oral answer on the regulation on paediatric medicinal products. the resolution rightly calls on the commission to consider introducing changes, including a legislative revision of the paediatric medicines regulation, which will take into account paediatric development plans, disease and drug priority models, earlier and more feasible paediatric investigation plans, better incentives for research that more effectively serves the needs of the paediatric population, while ensuring an assessment of the cost of research and development and full transparency of clinical outcomes, and strategies to prevent the misuse of medicines in the field of paediatric treatment, where there are already approved paediatric medicines. however, although the regulation has helped to improve the overall situation, unfortunately, in many areas, not enough progress has been made.
in writing. ‒ i supported the european parliament resolution on paediatric medicines. the paediatric regulation has had a significant impact on paediatric drug development, as most pharmaceutical companies consider paediatric development to be an essential part of overall product development. but there is still a lack of progress in the field of oncology, because cancer is still the leading cause of death in children. many cancers occur only in children and not in adults. and so far, only two innovative cancer drugs have been approved based on pediatric research, targeting malignancies in pediatric patients. new drug trials and new medicines could have life-saving benefits and it is therefore necessary to ensure the best available treatment methods and thus to allow the optimal use of research funds. the commission should consider introducing amendments, including a legislative review of the paediatric medicines regulation, on the basis of the findings of the report. it would be prudent to renew the provisions in horizon 2020 on funding designed to support high-quality paediatric clinical research. the role of european networking for paediatric clinical research should be strengthened and it should be ensured that member states implement measures to support the research, development and availability of medicinal products for paediatric use.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the european parliament resolution on the regulation on paediatric medicines. research in paediatrics to develop effective medicines is very limited and scanty. i therefore support calls on the commission to strengthen the role of the european paediatric clinical research network and to provide funding sources to support the research, development and availability of paediatric medicines in the areas where they are most needed, in particular in the field of paediatric oncology and neonatology.
in writing. ‒ the right to petition is one of the fundamental rights of european citizens and residents and is enshrined in the treaty and the charter of fundamental rights of the union. the purpose of the annual activity report of the committee on petitions is to present an analysis of the petitions received in 2015 and of the relations with the other institutions and to provide an overview of the objectives achieved in 2015. in 2015, 1431 petitions were received, 943 of which were admissible, of which 424 were swiftly examined and closed. unfortunately, it appears that the vast majority of eu citizens are still not familiar with this tool, which can help the european institutions and the member states to raise awareness of issues and pressing problems that concern them and fall within the eu's sphere of action, and more needs to be done to promote it. i also welcome the part of the report which stresses that petitions are an alternative and independent means of investigation and verification of compliance with eu law and that this procedure is not excluded from proceedings before national courts, which is very important for citizens. the report also recognises the important role of petitions for the legislative process, as they allow the identification of existing gaps and shortcomings in the transposition of eu legislation and there is more to be done. i supported the report because of all the above.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the activities of the committee on petitions in 2015. the right to petition, which was introduced to make it easier for european citizens to address petitions or complaints to the institutions of the european union, is an important instrument that we know in the eu. it can contribute to better legislation and thus also have a significant impact on people's daily lives. especially in these times, when the eu seems far away to many citizens because of various crises, we need this bridge between citizens and institutions even more.
in writing. ‒ i supported the motion for a resolution of the european parliament on the activities of the committee on petitions for 2015. the 2015 annual report is an overview of the work of the committee on petitions. the committee's programme of activities is not linked to the european commission's legislative programme but is shaped by citizens who, by exercising their right to petition the european parliament, express concerns about issues in the various political and legislative areas of the union. the 2015 statistics show that the majority of citizens turn to the european parliament for assistance on matters relating to the environment, justice, the internal market and fundamental rights. in 2015, 1431 petitions were received, which is 47% less than in 2014. spain was the country with the highest number of petitions in 2015, followed by italy and germany. analysis of the statistics on petitions shows that the main reasons for the inadmissibility of petitions are the fact that petitioners still confuse the competences of the eu and the member states and do not distinguish between the eu institutions. the european commission remains the committee's primary partner in dealing with petitions, as it is responsible for monitoring the application and compliance with eu law. the key topics of the committee on petitions in 2015 were mortgage legislation and risky financial instruments, the environment and disability.
in writing. ‒ the european parliament's resolution on international aviation agreements stresses that, if parliament is to take a decision on the approval of international aviation agreements at the end of the negotiations, it must monitor the entire process of negotiating and agreeing agreements from the outset. the framework agreement specifically provides that the european parliament is to be kept regularly and, if necessary, confidentially informed of all the details of the ongoing procedure at all stages of the negotiations from the very beginning. the resolution also stresses that parliament expects the commission to provide information to parliament's competent committee on its intention to propose the opening of negotiations on the conclusion and amendment of international air transport agreements, to arrange with the council and the negotiating partners for access by meps to all relevant documents, including negotiating directives and consolidated texts, at the same time and on an equal footing with the council. all these provisions of the resolution are very important, as the commission is currently negotiating 20 such agreements in a very non-transparent way, and this resolution is therefore very important, as it calls for greater involvement of parliament in the procedures and better access to information. all this is a precondition for greater transparency, which is why i myself supported the resolution.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the motion for a resolution on international air transport agreements by mr cramer, on behalf of the committee on transport and tourism. i support a greater role for parliament in the process of adopting the various agreements, particularly in view of the various concerns and proposals that may arise at an early stage and are also relevant for the final approval of the agreements. the resolution of the committee on transport and tourism rightly points out that the framework agreement specifically provides that the european parliament is to be informed regularly and, if necessary, confidentially from the outset of all the details of the ongoing procedure at all stages of the negotiations.
in writing. ‒ i supported the european parliament resolution on international air agreements. in the aviation strategy for europe, the commission proposed the opening of negotiations on civil aviation safety with japan and china and on eu-level air transport agreements with china, turkey, mexico, the six gulf cooperation council member states, armenia and asean (association of southeast asian nations). if parliament has to take a decision at the end of the negotiations, it must monitor the process from the very beginning. the european parliament should be kept regularly and, where necessary, confidentially informed of all the details of the ongoing procedure at all stages of the negotiations from the very beginning. parliament guarantees the complete confidentiality of the information obtained.
on behalf of the verts/ale group. this regulation of the european parliament and of the council on the union customs code therefore entered into force on 30 october 2013, and with it all the provisions empowering the commission to draw up implementing acts, including delegated acts. the code itself came into force in may of this year. but, as my colleagues have already said, it is part of a project to modernise european customs in the sense of a complete paperless operation of all the entities involved in these customs procedures. we naturally want these procedures to be as bureaucratic as possible, in short, to be completely paperless, to simplify certain conditions for the issuing of permits, while also ensuring that appropriate controls are in place in these areas, because paperlessness also promotes opportunities for abuse. and given that the european union is also financially dependent on customs duties and the revenue they generate, there is a need to make an additional effort in terms of checks and inspections. so i think this is a step in the right direction, that this information and the law itself are welcome support for the unification of the customs area of the european union. i hope, of course, that the member states will not have too many problems in doing so and that they can implement them as soon as possible. and finally, of course, to the esteemed colleagues in the audience, and to all of you on the balconies, a merry christmas and a happy new year, and we'll see you next time.
